Comprehensive v3 security audit — applied fixes

findings.title: docker-compose.yml pins an image tag that has never existed in GHCR: the publish workflow only ever pushes v-prefixed tags, so the documented `docker compose up -d` quick start fails with manifest unknown
findings.description: docker-compose.yml:53 sets `image: ghcr.io/vulnradar/vulnradar:3.0.0`. The only thing that ever pushes to that registry is .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml, which fires on `push: tags: v*` (lines 5-6), sets `VERSION=${GITHUB_REF_NAME}` (line 40), and pushes `$IMAGE:${VERSION}` and `$IMAGE:latest` (lines 53-54). GITHUB_REF_NAME for a tag push is the literal tag, so every published tag carries the leading `v`. I queried the public GHCR tag list anonymously (ghcr.io/v2/vulnradar/vulnradar/tags/list): it contains v1.9.2 through v3.7.2 plus `latest` plus the cosign `sha256-...` signature tags, and no bare `3.0.0`. README.md:79 and app/docs/setup/page.tsx:640 (Step 4) both instruct the operator to run `docker compose up -d` against this file, and app/docs/setup/page.tsx:684 gives `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d` as the Update operation. The compose comment at lines 48-51 also tells the operator to run `docker pull ghcr.io/vulnradar/vulnradar:3.0.0` to fetch a digest. All of these reference a tag the registry does not have.
findings.impact: A self-hoster following the README or the setup docs never gets a running container. `docker compose up -d` aborts on the app service with `manifest unknown` before anything else in AUDIT-014#host-01 or #host-03 is even reached. This is upstream of every other self-host finding: the documented path stops at the image pull. AUDIT-013#deps-06 and AUDIT-014#host-05 both noticed the pin is stale or a no-op; neither noticed the tag does not exist at all.
findings.recommendation: Either change docker-compose.yml:53 to `ghcr.io/vulnradar/vulnradar:v3.7.2` (matching what docker-publish.yml actually pushes) or strip the `v` at publish time in docker-publish.yml:40 (`VERSION=${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}`) and push both `v`-prefixed and bare tags. Fix the pull command in the comment at docker-compose.yml:49 to match. Then add a CI step that asserts the tag referenced by docker-compose.yml resolves in the registry, so the next drift is caught before release.

findings.title: VERDICT: the documented self-host does not work. On an empty database instrumentation.ts exits 1 before creating a single table, and nothing in the running app ever writes the schema-meta row it demands
findings.description: Static trace only (docker and psql are not installed on this machine, nothing was executed). Boot path for a container started against an empty Postgres: Dockerfile:114-115 ENTRYPOINT tini + CMD npm start -> next start -> instrumentation.ts register() (instrumentation.ts:28). At instrumentation.ts:91 it runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS vulnradar_schema_meta, at :99 it SELECTs the single row, and at :105 `if (metaRes.rows.length === 0)` it prints the SCHEMA VERSION NOT SET box and calls process.exit(1) at :144. The 2,900 lines of CREATE TABLE statements start at :279, after that gate, so they never run. A repo-wide grep for vulnradar_schema_meta finds exactly two writers: scripts/create-fresh-db/create-fresh-db.mjs:302 and scripts/migrate/_meta.mjs:69 (writeMeta). Neither is the app. The app never inserts that row under any code path, so the gate can never be satisfied by booting. The two commands the error box offers are also both dead ends on an empty DB: scripts/migrate/_detect.mjs:56 returns version:null when no fingerprint tables are present, and migrate.mjs:355 then aborts with "Could not detect a known schema version"; there is no empty-to-1.0.0 step in scripts/migrate/versions/. Only npm run db:create can bootstrap, and it is a side-by-side clone tool (scripts/create-fresh-db/create-fresh-db.mjs:6-18) that creates a DIFFERENTLY NAMED database ("default ends in _v3", :725) and reads its DDL from resolve(ROOT, "instrumentation.ts") (:69), so it needs the source checkout, not the image. docker-compose.yml:100 sets restart: unless-stopped, so the app container crash-loops forever. Four separate docs assert the opposite: README.md:79-82, app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:259-264 ("instrumentation.ts runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS for every table ... Look for Database schema verified successfully"), app/docs/setup/page.tsx:652-654, app/docs/config/page.tsx:1144-1147 ("Schema auto-creates on first boot; meta row is written on first scan via db:migrate"). The log line they tell the operator to look for exists at instrumentation.ts:3199, unreachable past the :144 exit.
findings.impact: A new self-hoster who follows README.md exactly gets a Postgres container that comes up healthy and an app container that restart-loops with a red box telling them to run one of two commands, one of which cannot work on an empty database and the other of which is not present in the image (see host-02). There is no documented path from a fresh checkout plus a Postgres string to a running instance. This is the headline claim of the project's Self-Hosting section and it is false as written.
findings.recommendation: In instrumentation.ts, split the metaRes.rows.length === 0 branch at :105 into two cases. If the public schema contains no application tables at all (query information_schema.tables for 'users'), treat it as a fresh install: fall through to the CREATE TABLE sequence at :279 and INSERT the meta row with schema_version = MIN_SCHEMA_VERSION at the end, next to the existing success log at :3199. Keep the current exit(1) only for the genuinely ambiguous case of a populated database with no meta row. Then correct README.md:78-82 and the three docs pages to describe whichever behaviour ships.

findings.title: The Dockerfile runtime stage copies five paths and never copies scripts/, so db:create, db:migrate, the admin Backup button and the self-updater's migrate step are all unrunnable inside the published image
findings.description: Static trace. The runner stage (Dockerfile:62) copies exactly five paths from the builder: public, .next, node_modules, package.json, next.config.mjs (Dockerfile:75-79). scripts/, instrumentation.ts and the rest of the source tree are not copied. Every npm script in package.json:29-40 resolves to node scripts/<something>.mjs, so inside the container all of them fail with a module-not-found on a path that does not exist. Concretely: (1) README.md:82 tells the operator to run `docker compose exec app npm run db:create`, which runs node scripts/create-fresh-db/create-fresh-db.mjs (package.json:31), absent; and because of host-01 the container is not even running, so `docker compose exec` fails first with a container-not-running error. (2) app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:545-548 tells the operator to run npm run db:migrate "inside the app container" after a schema change; same absence. (3) The admin panel Backup button, documented at app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:407-414 and promoted in .env.example's DATABASE BACKUPS block, goes POST /api/v3/admin/backup -> lib/backup/run-backup.ts:33, which spawns join(appRoot, "scripts", "backup-db.mjs"); absent, so the job always fails. (4) The self-updater runs npm run db:migrate -- --yes at lib/updater/apply.ts:353; absent. Dockerfile:88-92 installs postgresql-client specifically so that "scripts/migrate/migrate.mjs backs up the database to databases/ before applying any schema changes", a package installed for a script the image does not contain. AUDIT-013#deps-05 already noted a different Dockerfile comment describing something that does not exist; this is the same class of drift but with functional consequences.
findings.impact: Every documented in-container maintenance operation fails: initialise the database, migrate after an upgrade, take a backup from the admin panel, and self-update. Combined with host-01 there is no way to recover a self-hosted instance from inside the container at all, and the operator must have a separate Node + source checkout with network access to the same Postgres.
findings.recommendation: Add `COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/scripts ./scripts` and `COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/instrumentation.ts ./instrumentation.ts` to the runner stage after Dockerfile:79 (create-fresh-db.mjs:69 reads instrumentation.ts as its v3 schema source, so both are needed). Also copy lib/ if any script imports from it. Then re-verify that `docker compose exec app npm run db:create` resolves before README.md:82 is left pointing at it.

findings.title: A 1 MB response body of plain word characters pins the Node event loop for tens of minutes: maskPlaceholderSecrets runs a quadratic regex over the whole body once per each of the 74 secrets-extended detectors, reachable unauthenticated via /api/v3/demo-scan
findings.description:
maskPlaceholderSecrets (lib/scanner/checks/secrets-extended.ts:35-41) runs `body.replace(/[A-Za-z0-9_-]*(?:example|your_|xxxx|0000|placeholder|test_|dummy)[A-Za-z0-9_-]*/gi, ' ')` over the entire response body. The leading unbounded `[A-Za-z0-9_-]*` makes the match attempt at every start position O(n) work, so the whole pass is O(n^2) on any long unbroken run of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` characters with no literal alternative present. Measured on this machine (Node 22, exact regex copied out of the file): n=25,000 -> 1.22 s; 50,000 -> 5.99 s; 100,000 -> 25.1 s; 200,000 -> 97.5 s; 400,000 -> 396 s. Clean quadratic (4x time per 2x input), extrapolating to about 41 minutes at the 1,000,000-character body cap.

The cost is then multiplied: lib/scanner/checks/secrets-extended.ts:1272-1281 wraps EVERY detector in the module with `((url, headers, body) => fn(url, headers, maskPlaceholderSecrets(stripExampleContent(body))))`, and that module exports 74 detectors, so the mask runs 74 times per scanned page, not once. stripExampleContent (lib/scanner/_helpers.ts:200) leaves a body with no tags untouched, so nothing shrinks the input first.

The execution path is fully synchronous with no budget: lib/scanner/engine.ts:168-173 loops `for (const check of catLegacyChecks) { const result = check(url, headers, body); }` and its own doc comment at :126 states it does not enforce a size limit. The scan-job watchdog (lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts:165) and the cancel timer (lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:171) are both setTimeout-based, so neither can fire while a synchronous regex holds the event loop.

The cheapest reach is unauthenticated: app/api/v3/demo-scan/route.ts has no getSession() call, is gated only by FEATURE_DEMO_MODE (default true, lib/config/config-values.ts:1117) and a per-IP rate limit, reads the target body up to SCAN_RESPONSE_BODY_MAX_BYTES = 1 MiB (lib/config/config-values.ts:569) at route.ts:179, slices to 1,000,000 chars at :190, and then runs `for (const check of allChecks) check(url, headers, bodyForChecks)` at :193-199. `allChecks` includes the wrapped secrets-extended detectors (lib/scanner/registry.ts:55). safeFetch only blocks private/internal targets, so an attacker's own public host is a valid demo target.
findings.impact: One unauthenticated HTTP POST to /api/v3/demo-scan naming an attacker-controlled URL that returns 1 MB of `aaaa...` blocks the single Node event loop of the whole Next.js process. Every other request (login, dashboard, scans, Stripe webhooks, health checks) stalls behind it for the duration; measured scaling puts that in the tens of minutes to hours. Nothing in the app can recover it because every timeout in the scan path is a setTimeout. This is a full-instance denial of service from a single request, and it also directly falsifies the product's central 'under 3 seconds' claim for any page that happens to contain a long word-character run.
findings.recommendation: Two independent fixes, both in lib/scanner/checks/secrets-extended.ts. (1) Hoist the masking out of the per-detector wrapper at :1272-1281: compute `maskPlaceholderSecrets(stripExampleContent(body))` once per body (memoize on the body reference, or change the registry to pass a pre-masked body) instead of once per detector, removing the 74x multiplier. (2) Bound the quadratic regex itself: change the two `[A-Za-z0-9_-]*` runs in maskPlaceholderSecrets to `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,120}` (no real credential token is longer than that, and the file's own doc comment only claims to erase 'the contiguous identifier/token run'), which makes each start-position attempt O(1) and the pass linear. Separately, add a hard body-length guard in lib/scanner/engine.ts's runSyncChecks and in app/api/v3/demo-scan/route.ts, and prefer a real budget check between checks rather than relying on setTimeout watchdogs that a synchronous regex can never let run.

findings.title: Admin row actions including Delete are invisible on touch but still hit-testable, in four list panels
findings.description: Four panels use `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100` as the only rendering condition for their row action buttons: components/admin/notifications/notifications-manager.tsx:625, components/admin/features/mass-email-manager.tsx:573, components/admin/features/security-alerts-manager.tsx:367 and :382, and components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:1834. Touch devices have no hover state, so the buttons are permanently invisible while remaining fully hit-testable. Six sibling admin panels pair `hidden md:block` with an `md:hidden` card list; these four did not. The same class of bug exists at components/teams/team-members-list.tsx:146, where the member kebab (View Scans / Remove) has no sm: prefix, while components/shares/shares-row.tsx:118 does it correctly with `sm:opacity-0 sm:group-hover:opacity-100 sm:group-focus-within:opacity-100`.
findings.impact: An admin on a phone cannot see row actions at all, and can fire a destructive one, including Delete, by tapping apparently blank space.
findings.recommendation: Change to `md:opacity-0 md:group-hover:opacity-100` in all four admin panels so the actions are unconditionally visible below md. Bring components/teams/team-members-list.tsx:146 in line with components/shares/shares-row.tsx:118.

findings.title: The 'send the verification email again' button is dead: it checks a success field the API envelope never sets
findings.description: The handler branches on `if (res.ok && data.success)` then `else if (!res.ok)`. lib/api/api-utils.ts:15 defines ApiResponse.success as `NextResponse.json(data, { status })`, which adds no success field. app/api/v3/auth/resend-verification/route.ts returns ApiResponse.success({ message: ... }) at lines 44, 54 and 64, so the body is a bare {message}. On a 200 response data.success is undefined, so the first branch is false and `!res.ok` is also false. Neither branch executes. components/auth/signup-success.tsx:45 and components/auth/verify-email-expired.tsx:46 check res.ok alone and work correctly.
findings.impact: An unverified user is told to check their email, clicks 'send again', watches the button spin and reset, and sees nothing change. They click repeatedly until the rate limit trips, at which point they finally get an error, which reads as the resend being broken rather than throttled. This is the terminal step of the signup funnel.
findings.recommendation: Delete `&& data.success` from the condition at components/auth/login-form.tsx:54. Match the two sibling components that already do this correctly.

findings.title: Checkout reads meData.data on an endpoint that returns flat, so every existing subscriber gets the wrong upgrade flow
findings.description: app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx:60-66 reads `meData.data?.subscriptionStatus` and `meData.data?.role`. app/api/v3/auth/me/route.ts returns ApiResponse.success({...}) at lines 47 and 133, and lib/api/api-utils.ts:15 confirms ApiResponse.success returns the object flat with no data wrapper. So meData.data is undefined and both reads are permanently undefined.
findings.impact: hasActiveSubscription is permanently false, so an existing subscriber upgrading is shown the full card-entry form instead of SwitchPlanPanel. They type card details that the server action then ignores, because it prorates against the card already on file. A large share will abandon the flow believing they are about to be charged twice. isStaffAccount is likewise permanently false, making the staff guard at :96-114 dead code. This is on the money path.
findings.recommendation: Drop the .data hop: use meData?.subscriptionStatus and meData?.role.

findings.title: scan_history.team_id is never written by any scan path, so team scan sharing is dead end to end while shipping a full UI for it
findings.description: PATCH /api/v3/history/[id] destructures teamId at :267, authorizes it at :313-326 and writes it at :349-352. That is the only write path to scan_history.team_id (instrumentation.ts:928) in the entire codebase. Every INSERT INTO scan_history omits the column: app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:368, scan/crawl/route.ts:440, scan/bulk/route.ts:278, scan/authenticated/route.ts:469, scan/github/route.ts:252, lib/scanner/scheduled-scans-worker.ts:280, lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:633. No UI ever sends teamId: the only PATCH bodies sent are {notes} (app/history/page.tsx:394) and {isPublic} (components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:339); a repo-wide grep for 'share to team' / 'share with team' across .tsx returns zero. The sibling columns webhooks.team_id (instrumentation.ts:934) and scheduled_scans.team_id (:937) have the same shape: PATCH accepts teamId (webhooks/[id]/route.ts:201, schedules/route.ts:308) and no UI sends it.
findings.impact: GET /api/v3/teams/member-scans queries WHERE user_id = $1 AND team_id = $2 (app/api/v3/teams/member-scans/route.ts:53-60) and can only ever return an empty array, yet the product ships a complete viewer for it with pagination (app/teams/page.tsx:469, components/teams/team-member-scans.tsx). Every getTeamResourceAccess team branch across history, share and report is unreachable. The feature is documented and sold at app/docs/teams/page.tsx:374-380. A paying team customer sees an empty panel with no explanation.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Share with team' control to components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx beside the existing 'Make private' item at :590, populated from getAssignableTeamIds with a 'Personal (private)' null option, plus a team column and filter on History. Add the same selector to the webhook and schedule rows on Profile > Developer. Alternatively decide the feature is not wanted and remove the columns, the read paths and the docs section.

findings.title: The findings toolbar overflows the viewport and horizontally scrolls the whole page, which is what makes /history read as broken on mobile
findings.description: components/scanner/results-list.tsx:398 is `<div className="flex items-center gap-2">` with no flex-wrap and no overflow wrapper, containing three buttons each marked shrink-0 at :408, :425 and :448. Measured: 'Most severe first' about 146px, 'Group by severity' about 146px, 'Select' about 82px, plus two gap-2 gaps, totalling roughly 390px. Content width on /history is 375 - 32 = 343px (app/history/page.tsx:443, max-w-6xl mx-auto px-4). No ancestor has overflow-x-hidden, so the row spills into body. The reason this reads as a /history-specific bug is that the 'Select' button only renders when selectable = Boolean(scanUrl) (:126), which is set only on the two owner surfaces, /history and /dashboard. On /shared, /host and /demo the row is about 300px and fits. /demo is additionally immune because components/demo/demo-shell.tsx:9 carries overflow-x-hidden.
findings.impact: The entire page scrolls sideways on any phone. This is the single most visible mobile defect in the product and the one the owner reported.
findings.recommendation: Change line 398 to `flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2` and drop shrink-0 from lines 408, 425 and 448. Alternatively keep one row and wrap each label in `<span className="hidden sm:inline">`, leaving the icons.

findings.title: /profile is the last page on the retired horizontal icon strip, and below 640px it has no accessible name on any tab
findings.description: app/profile/page.tsx:722-741 is inline JSX rendering eight buttons, each `{tab.icon}` plus `{tab.label}`. The replacement components are AdminMobileSectionTrigger and AdminMobileToc (components/admin/shared/admin-mobile-toc.tsx:68 and :123), consumed at app/admin/page.tsx:1034-1057, whose own docstring at :59-62 reads 'Lives at the top of the mobile sidebar in place of the old horizontal icon strip.' The docs equivalent is DocsMobileNavTrigger / DocsMobileNav (components/docs/docs-mobile-nav.tsx:19 and :43). Four defects verified: (1) lucide auto-applies aria-hidden="true" when a component carries no a11y prop (node_modules/lucide-react/dist/cjs/lucide-react.js:92) and the TABS array at :625-664 passes none, so at 375px each button holds one aria-hidden SVG plus one display:none span; (2) eight buttons at px-3.5 plus a 16px icon is 44px each, 366px against 343px available, and scrollbar-hide (app/globals.css:37) removes the only signal that the row scrolls; (3) the strip is lg:hidden, so between 640px and 1023px labels return and it grows to ~910px against 736px, hiding two tabs; (4) missing type="button" and aria-current, both of which the new pattern supplies at admin-mobile-toc.tsx:187,190.
findings.impact: On a phone, account settings navigation is eight unlabeled icons with one cut in half and no indication the row scrolls. A screen reader announces 'button' eight times with no way to distinguish them, so a screen-reader user cannot navigate /profile at all.
findings.recommendation: Replace lines 722-741 with AdminMobileSectionTrigger plus AdminMobileToc, passing the eight TABS entries as AdminTocItem[] with active and onSelect, grouped the way app/admin/page.tsx:997-1009 builds mobileSectionItems from NAV_GROUPS. Note that /profile's own Developer sub-tabs at components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:663-696 are already the correct version of this strip (labels never hidden, type="button", aria-current, explicit aria-hidden) - the page header is an older, worse copy of its own child.

findings.title: Automatic subdomain discovery is awaited on the scan critical path with a hardcoded 15s cap, and nothing on screen needs it
findings.description: executeScan starts automatic subdomain discovery at lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:544 and then awaits it at :793. lib/scanner/subdomain-auto.ts:52 caps that work at DEFAULT_AUTO_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000. The clock starts after the target fetch, so total wall clock is fetch + 15s. discoverSubdomainsForRoot (lib/scanner/subdomain-discovery-engine.ts:315) runs four sequential stages: nine passive sources (crt.sh alone has a 15s fetch timeout at :441), a 191-prefix DNS brute force in batches of 50, DNS resolution of up to 1000 passive entries, and HTTP reachability probing of every host at concurrency 25. On a cache miss it cannot finish inside the cap, so it reliably burns the whole 15s. Nobody opts in; it runs on every HTTP scan. The result view does not need it: components/scanner/subdomain-discovery.tsx already renders from initialResult with a click-to-discover fallback, so null is a supported state. Regression introduced at 8e5e11b5 (2026-08-18) with a 10s cap, raised to 15s at a233e0bb (2026-08-19). The same pattern exists at lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:698.
findings.impact: Every scan takes 15-20 seconds instead of 2-5. This is the product's headline speed claim being contradicted on the primary flow, in front of the user, on every single scan. Since commit 3a242f89 the server-reported duration also includes the wait, so the 'Scan duration' stat shows ~17s too. The only surface where the under-3-seconds claim still holds is the landing demo, and only because app/api/v3/demo-scan/route.ts:209 passes cacheOnly: true and skips subdomain discovery, software inventory, CVE enrichment, ports and screenshots entirely.
findings.recommendation: Drop the await at lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:792-796 and the readSubdomains call at :797-802. Let discovery keep running in the background; it already warms the DB cache via subdomain-discovery-engine.ts:418. Have the subdomain panel read that cache lazily. Roughly a 10-line change. Apply the same fix at lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:698. Do this BEFORE removing the timer (scan-05): once the scan actually takes 3s the number stops being a liability and becomes the proof.

findings.title: Badge global scope leaked other users' private/authenticated scans, bypassing is_public entirely
findings.description: app/api/v3/badge/[token]/route.ts and app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.ts joined host_badges to scan_history on (hb.scope = 'global' OR sh.user_id = hb.user_id) with no is_public filter, unlike every other privacy-gated path in the codebase (getExactUrlReputation's AND is_public = true). Any user could set a badge to scope='global' on a URL, then whenever anyone else scanned that exact URL -- including a private or authenticated dashboard scan -- the attacker's badge/share endpoint would return the victim's full findings, headers, and metadata with no consent or is_public=true required. Found by the audit's security-review agent; verified against the real code and fixed before this ever shipped (the global-scope toggle feature was built and audited in the same session, never released).
findings.recommendation: Changed the JOIN condition in both routes to (sh.user_id = hb.user_id OR (hb.scope = 'global' AND sh.is_public = true)) -- the owner's own scans still match unconditionally (unchanged behavior), but a foreign scan can only be surfaced via a global-scope badge when its own owner marked it public. The existing notes/identity redaction for foreign-but-public scans (Community scan / no avatar / no notes) is unaffected and still applies.

findings.title: No database backup or disaster-recovery mechanism anywhere in the codebase
findings.description: There is no backup script, no scheduled pg_dump/pg_basebackup job, no documented restore procedure, and no mention of backups in README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.dev.yml, or scripts/. The production Docker Compose file stores all data in a bare local Docker volume (postgres_data, driver: local) with no snapshot, replication, or offsite-copy story. This is a SaaS with user accounts, password hashes, Stripe billing history, API keys, scan history, and team data all in one Postgres instance -- a lost/corrupted volume, a bad migration, a `docker volume rm`, or host disk failure is unrecoverable data loss for every customer, with no tested restore path even claimed to exist. Evidence: docker-compose.yml lines 17-44, 114-116 (postgres service, named local volume, no backup sidecar/cron); README.md has no backup/DR section; grep for 'backup'/'pg_dump' across README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docker-compose*.yml, and scripts/ returns nothing related to database backups (only unrelated 2FA 'backup codes').
findings.recommendation: NOT YET APPLIED -- reported for review. Recommendation: Add a scheduled pg_dump (or WAL-archiving/pg_basebackup) job -- even a simple cron container in docker-compose.yml pushing encrypted dumps to object storage -- document the restore procedure, and actually perform a test restore before calling this production-ready. For the hosted/managed deployment, confirm the managed Postgres provider's backup retention and verify a restore has been rehearsed, not assumed.

findings.title: code-cmdi-exec: code-cmdi-exec JSON metadata belongs to a different check entirely (Media Device Access, severity info) while its detector implements real command-injection detection
findings.description: In lib/scanner/checks/code.ts, the `code-cmdi-exec` detector matches `exec("..." + userInput)` — i.e. child_process.exec called with a shell command built via string concatenation, a genuine shell-injection sink (same class as the sibling code-cmdi-* checks, which are all severity high/critical). But the JSON entry the registry pairs it with (lib/scanner/checks-data/code.json, `_idx: 27`) has title "Media Device Access", description "Camera/microphone API access detected.", evidence "Media device access found.", riskImpact "Privacy concern - ensure user consent.", and severity "info" — metadata that belongs to getUserMedia/camera-mic detection (which is actually implemented correctly, under its own id, in lib/scanner/checks-data/content.json's `webcam-microphone-access` entry). Only the entry's `codeExamples` field was updated to match command injection (execFile with argument arrays); everything else was left as the old media-device content. Verified against lib/scanner/registry.ts's resolveDetector: since `code-cmdi-exec`'s def.category is "code" and code.ts owns and implements that id directly, the registry pairs the real command-injection detector with this mislabeled metadata every time it runs — there is no shadowing/fallback involved. Trigger: Any page whose inline script contains a pattern like `exec("ls " + userPath)` (a real, exploitable command-injection sink) gets reported to the user as an "info"-severity "Media Device Access" finding with fix steps about camera/microphone consent, instead of a high/critical command-injection alert.
findings.recommendation: In lib/scanner/checks-data/code.json, replace the `code-cmdi-exec` entry's title/description/evidence/riskImpact/explanation/fixSteps/severity to describe child_process.exec with a concatenated command string (shell metacharacter injection), using severity "high" to match the sibling code-cmdi-process-spawn/code-cmdi-popen entries (or "critical" to match code-cmdi-spawn-shell-true/code-cmdi-os-exec/code-cmdi-bin-sh-concat, whichever tier the team judges exec()+concat belongs to). The `codeExamples` field is already correct for command injection and can be left as-is.

findings.title: Badge 'global' scope leaks other users' PRIVATE (and always-private authenticated) scans, bypassing scan_history.is_public entirely
findings.description:
Both the badge-image endpoint and the full-detail shared endpoint resolve an auto-updating (host_badges) token to 'whichever completed scan of that exact URL is newest, by anyone' when the badge owner has set scope='global' -- with NO `is_public` filter on the resolved scan_history row. Query in app/api/v3/badge/[token]/route.ts lines 60-73:
```
FROM host_badges hb
JOIN scan_history sh
  ON sh.url = hb.url AND (hb.scope = 'global' OR sh.user_id = hb.user_id)
WHERE hb.badge_token_hash = $1 AND hb.revoked_at IS NULL AND sh.status = 'completed'
ORDER BY sh.scanned_at DESC LIMIT 1
```
The identical join (no is_public filter) is repeated in app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.ts lines 47-60, which returns the FULL scan JSON (findings array with all evidence, response_headers, authenticated flag, result_meta) rather than just a badge SVG.

This directly breaks an invariant enforced everywhere else in the codebase: lib/scanner/host-reputation.ts's getExactUrlReputation explicitly scopes `WHERE url = $1 AND is_public = true` with a comment stating 'a scan its owner explicitly kept private must never be exposed through it'; lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts only calls upsertHostReputation `if (applied && url && isPublic)`; and app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts makes authenticated scans (which capture logged-in dashboard/account content) private-by-default *regardless* of any account setting, specifically because that content is more sensitive than a logged-out scan. The badge 'global' feature ignores both of these established privacy boundaries.

Attack: Attacker (any registered user) scans a target URL they don't need to own (e.g. https://saas.example.com/dashboard), issues POST /api/v3/badge/site with that scanId, then PATCH .../badge/site {url, scope:'global'} to flip the badge to global scope. Attacker now polls the unauthenticated GET /api/v3/shared/{badge_token} endpoint. Whenever ANY other VulnRadar user later scans that exact same URL -- including a strictly-private authenticated scan that peeks at their own logged-in dashboard/account/billing page, which app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts's own comments describe as 'account settings, billing details, internal dashboards, anything behind the login' -- that other user's full findings, response headers, and scan metadata become readable to the attacker, who never needed the victim's consent, a share link, or is_public=true. The victim never opted into anything; only the attacker's own badge configuration (which the victim has no visibility into) determines exposure. The UI's own copy in components/badge/badge-preview.tsx ('Their notes and identity stay private, only the findings summary shows') confirms this is not the intended behavior even for a knowingly-public scan -- yet the implementation exposes full findings, not a summary, and applies no privacy gate at all.

Confirmed via tests too: tests/app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.test.ts and tests/app/api/v3/badge/[token]/route.test.ts assert the exact `(hb.scope = 'global' OR sh.user_id = hb.user_id)` SQL fragment and test identity/notes redaction for a foreign scan, but neither test asserts an is_public check exists -- the privacy gate was simply never wired in. Evidence: app/api/v3/badge/[token]/route.ts:60-73 and app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.ts:47-60 (host_badges fallback JOIN, no is_public/authenticated filter); contrast with lib/scanner/host-reputation.ts:271 (`WHERE url = $1 AND is_public = true`) and app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts:314-327 (authenticated scans always private unless explicitly opted in); components/badge/badge-preview.tsx:76-77 (UI's stated intent is 'only the findings summary shows', not full detail with no privacy check).
findings.recommendation: NOT YET APPLIED -- reported for review. Recommendation: Add `AND sh.is_public = true` to the global-scope branch of the JOIN in both app/api/v3/badge/[token]/route.ts and app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.ts, e.g. `ON sh.url = hb.url AND (sh.user_id = hb.user_id OR (hb.scope = 'global' AND sh.is_public = true))`. Since authenticated scans are is_public=false unless the scanning user explicitly opted in, this alone closes the authenticated-scan leak too. Separately, tighten /api/v3/shared/[token]'s foreign-scan branch to actually match the UI's promised 'findings summary' rather than the full findings/response_headers/result_meta payload, since a stranger's scan being picked up by someone else's global badge was never an explicit share action by that scan's owner. Add a regression test asserting a private (is_public=false) or authenticated scan is never resolvable through a global-scope badge token.

findings.title: Versioned v3.0.0 upgrade path is missing 4 tables and ~25 columns that instrumentation.ts creates
findings.description: Live-verified: built a true v2.0.0-shaped scratch DB (34 tables, from the frozen instrumentation-v2.ts snapshot) with seed data, ran the real db:migrate engine to 3.0.0 (41/41 steps succeeded), then diffed the result against instrumentation.ts. Missing tables: processed_stripe_events, user_ai_configs, cve_kev_cache, webhook_deliveries. Missing columns include api_keys.scopes; users.ai_chat_banned/google_id/google_email/google_name/google_avatar_url/github_id/github_email/github_name/github_avatar_url/discord_username/discord_avatar_url/discord_email/scans_private_by_default; scan_history.share_expires_at/is_public; broadcast_messages.sent_by; scheduled_scans.preferred_hour_utc/preferred_day_of_week/preferred_day_of_month; webhooks.secret; host_reputation.findings/response_headers/result_meta/authenticated/scanned_url; plus idx_scan_history_url_public_completed. db:migrate against real production tonight will write schema_version=3.0.0 to vulnradar_schema_meta while these remain absent -- it only flips a version flag, it does not fully upgrade the schema.
findings.recommendation: Add the missing addTables/addColumns entries to 2.0.0-to-3.0.0.mjs, the matching table/column names to _registry.mjs's v3.0.0 fingerprint, and the 4 new table names to create-fresh-db.mjs's MIGRATE_TABLES v3.0.0-only list. Re-run the scratch-DB round-trip to confirm zero drift before trusting db:migrate against production.

findings.title: Admin password gate structurally unreachable — all gated action handlers dead code
findings.description: The password re-auth gate in PATCH /api/v3/admin lived inside the switch as fallthrough cases ending with break. After break, the switch exits; the actual action handlers (update_email, disable, reset_password, delete, revoke_all_sessions, remove_admin) appeared as duplicate case labels below the gate — code that the JS engine never reaches. Every GATED_ACTION ran without any password check. Additionally make_admin and set_role were not gated at all, and userId was compared with strict equality against the numeric literal 1 while the client sends a string.
findings.recommendation: Moved password gate entirely before the switch using a Set<string>. Added make_admin and set_role to GATED_ACTIONS. Fixed userId coercion to Number() with integer + positive validation. Added missing update_password and revoke_all_sessions handlers (they were in the gate set but had no handler in the switch).

findings.title: Moderator can change any regular user's email without re-auth
findings.description: update_email is in modActions; a moderator can target any regular user, change the email to attacker@evil.com, then trigger forgot-password. reset-password doesn't re-check email_verified_at, so the attacker receives the reset link at the new address and takes over the account.
findings.recommendation: Require the moderator to re-authenticate (password or TOTP) before update_email; send email verification to the new address and only apply the change after the user confirms via token. Block the forgot-password flow until email_verified_at IS NOT NULL for the new address.

findings.title: safeFetch followed 3xx redirects without re-validating each hop
findings.description: Node's built-in fetch follows Location: blindly. A target that 302s to 169.254.169.254 (or any private IP) bypassed validateScanTarget after the first hop.
findings.recommendation: Manual redirect loop with per-hop validateScanTarget; cross-host redirects rejected outright; same-host redirects capped at 5 hops.

findings.title: The only focus indicator is an inset ring in exactly the same colour as the primary button fill, so keyboard focus is invisible on every primary CTA in both themes
findings.description: app/globals.css:370 is the single source of the visible focus indicator for the whole product: `:focus-visible:not([tabindex="-1"]):not([data-radix-collection-item]) { @apply outline-hidden ring-2 ring-ring ring-inset; }`. It removes the native outline and replaces it with a 2px ring drawn INSIDE the element's own border box (the comment at :349 says ring-inset was chosen deliberately over the previous ring-offset-2 pair). The ring colour is `hsl(var(--ring))`, and `--ring` is defined identically to `--primary` in both themes: globals.css:178 `--primary: 213 94% 68%` / :196 `--ring: 213 94% 68%` (light) and :230 / :242 (dark). components/ui/button.tsx:12 gives the default Button variant `bg-primary`, and its own base class only sets `focus-visible:outline-hidden` with no replacement, so the base rule is the only indicator it gets. An inset ring in hsl(213 94% 68%) drawn on top of a fill of hsl(213 94% 68%) has a contrast ratio of exactly 1.00:1. Nothing anywhere restores the outline: `ring-offset` appears only in the comment at globals.css:349 and in one Radix toast class (components/ui/toast.tsx:80). lib/ui/animations.ts:92 `focus.ring` and the three per-component FOCUS_RING constants (components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:79, inline-auth-form.tsx:46, crawl-url-selector.tsx:19) all use the same `ring-ring` colour and do not set --tw-ring-inset back, so they inherit the inset the base rule sets on the same element. app/legal/accessibility/page.tsx:76-79 publishes: "Focus Indicators: Visible focus indicators help users navigate with keyboards."
findings.impact: A keyboard-only user tabbing through Sign in, Sign up, Start scan, Save, Confirm, or any other default-variant Button sees no change at all: the ring is the same blue as the button. On the auth screens the submit button is the last stop in the form, so the user tabs off the password field and has no way to tell whether focus landed on the button or moved past it. WCAG 2.1 AA SC 2.4.7 Focus Visible fails on the single most-used control in the product, and the published accessibility statement asserts the opposite.
findings.recommendation: In app/globals.css, give --ring a value distinct from --primary (a light-theme value near hsl(213 60% 35%) clears 3:1 on every surface in the light palette, and a near-white value clears it on bg-primary), or drop `ring-inset` from the rule at :370 and pair `ring-2 ring-ring` with `ring-offset-2 ring-offset-background` so the ring is drawn against the page rather than the control's own fill. If ring-inset must stay for the clipping reason documented at :349, add a `[&.bg-primary]`-style override, or set `focus-visible:ring-primary-foreground` on the default variant in components/ui/button.tsx:12.

findings.title: The API reference's headline request field `probes` was deleted from the scan routes in commit d0c815f7 and is now a silent no-op in every code sample
findings.description: app/docs/api/page.tsx:43 makes `"probes": ["ssh:22", "smtp:587"]` the request-body example for POST /scan, :40 says "Service probes are opt-in via the probes field", :52 and :56 describe the six services in detail, and the curl (:938) and JavaScript (:958) code samples both send it. app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:232 destructures only `{ url, scanners, isPublic }` plus body.captureScreenshot (:236) and body.portScan (:241); `probes` appears nowhere in the route, in lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts's ExecuteScanParams (:207-251), or anywhere else in app/ or lib/ (verified by grep). Commit d0c815f7 "refactor: remove Service probes (consolidated into Scan common ports)" removed "the `probes` payload field, the API `probes` parse in scan/crawl/authenticated routes, the runServiceProbes executor path" and deleted lib/scanner/service-probes.ts, but touched no docs file. The same dead field is still in lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:706-712 (so the playground prefills it), app/docs/page.tsx:119/143, app/docs/architecture/page.tsx:448-457, and lib/ai/docs-knowledge.md:1027/1892, which is what the in-product AI assistant answers from.
findings.impact: A developer following the first example on the API reference sends a body whose main feature flag is silently discarded: no error, no probes, no way to tell it did nothing. The replacement capability (body.portScan, gated on verified domain ownership, app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:241/310-324) is documented nowhere, so the feature is unreachable from the docs in both directions. The in-product AI assistant repeats the dead field verbatim.
findings.recommendation: Delete the `probes` field from the POST /scan endpoint card (app/docs/api/page.tsx:41-44, notes :52 and :56), from both code samples (:938, :958), and from the ScanRequest schema in lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:706-712. Add `portScan: boolean` and `captureScreenshot: boolean` to the request body and notes, stating that portScan is held to the same verified-domain gate as active-probes and returns 403 DOMAIN_NOT_VERIFIED. Then re-run `node scripts/compile-docs-knowledge.mjs` so lib/ai/docs-knowledge.md stops teaching it.

findings.title: The API playground prefills POST /scan and POST /scan/crawl with `"scanners": [""]`, which selects zero check categories and burns a real quota unit on an empty scan
findings.description: lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:713-718 declares ScanRequest.scanners as `{ type: "array", items: { type: "string" } }` with no `example` on either the array or its items. lib/api/playground.ts's buildExample falls through to `case "array": return s.items ? [buildExample(spec, s.items)] : []` and then `case "string": return ""`, producing `[""]`. app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx:83-91 stringifies that into the request-body textarea and :284 seeds the editable body with it, so the prefilled POST /scan body is `{"url":"example.com","probes":["ssh:22"],"scanners":[""]}`. app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:242-243 treats a non-empty array as an explicit selection (`selectedScanners = [""]`), and lib/scanner/engine.ts:104-119's getPlannedSyncCategories builds `new Set([""])` and filters ALL_CATEGORIES against it, yielding zero categories. POST /scan/crawl reuses the same ScanRequest schema (openapi-spec.ts:102).
findings.impact: The first thing a developer does on the playground page ("pick an endpoint, paste a key, and read the live response", app/docs/api/page.tsx:1187) starts a real scan that runs almost no checks, still charges one dailyScans unit and one API-key request, and returns a summary of zero findings. That reads as "the scanner found nothing" rather than "you sent an invalid selector", because the route never validates the category strings.
findings.recommendation: Add `example: ["headers", "ssl"]` (or omit the field from the example by giving the whole ScanRequest an object-level `example`) in lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:713-718, and defensively drop empty/unknown entries in app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:242-243 so `[""]` normalizes to null rather than to "run nothing".

findings.title: Every API code sample and the OpenAPI `servers` URL hardcode https://vulnradar.dev on any build without NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, including the published Docker image
findings.description: lib/config/constants.ts:191 resolves `APP_URL = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL || CONFIG_APP_URL`, and lib/config/config-values.ts:141 sets CONFIG_APP_URL to "https://vulnradar.dev". NEXT_PUBLIC_* is inlined by Next at build time, and .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:49-51 runs `docker build -t $IMAGE:${VERSION} -t $IMAGE:latest .` with no `--build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, even though Dockerfile:16/32 declares the ARG. So the published GHCR image bakes vulnradar.dev into APP_URL. app/api/v3/openapi.json/route.ts:11 calls `buildOpenApiSpec(APP_URL)`, which lands in lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:25 as `servers: [{ url: "https://vulnradar.dev/api/v3" }]` (its own docstring at :12-13 claims "baseUrl is the deployment's origin so a self-hosted instance advertises its own server"). app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx:62 reads `spec.servers[0].url` as its baseUrl and :298/:316 fetch that absolute URL. Every curl/JS sample on app/docs/api/page.tsx:935-984, the rate-limits backoff samples (app/docs/rate-limits/page.tsx:379/413), and the reports curl samples (app/docs/reports/page.tsx:296/449) interpolate the same APP_URL.
findings.impact: On a self-hosted instance run from the official image, every documented curl command targets the public SaaS instead of the operator's own deployment, and the playground's "Send request" button issues a cross-origin request to vulnradar.dev that fails CORS with the opaque message "Request failed (network, CORS, or an invalid URL)". The playground's own setup text ("the key ... is sent only to https://vulnradar.dev/api/v3") then tells the operator their key goes to someone else's server.
findings.recommendation: Pass `--build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` in .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:49, or (better, since the image is shared) make app/api/v3/openapi.json/route.ts call resolveAppUrl(request) from lib/config/runtime-config.ts instead of the compiled APP_URL, and have app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx:62 fall back to `window.location.origin + "/api/v3"` when the spec's server host does not match the current origin.

findings.title: Crawl scans are documented as capped at 15 pages in three places; the real cap is a per-plan 25/50/100/250 and unlimited when billing is off
findings.description: app/docs/api/page.tsx:322 says "Up to 15 pages per crawl" and :332 cites "Max 15 pages (MAX_PAGES in app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts)". No `MAX_PAGES` identifier exists in that file (verified by grep). app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:256-272 resolves `crawlPageLimit = BILLING_ENABLED ? getCrawlPageSelectionLimit(await getUserPlan(userId)) : -1`, and lib/billing/crawl-page-limits.ts:19-24 defines CRAWL_PAGE_SELECTION_LIMITS as free 25, core_supporter 50, pro_supporter 100, elite_supporter 250; the engine-side ceiling is CONFIG_CRAWL_SCAN_MAX_PAGES = 500 (lib/config/config-values.ts:603). The same wrong number is in lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:96 ("Crawl and scan up to 15 pages of a site") and in the CLI help/docs (cli/lib.mjs:126, app/docs/cli/page.tsx:135).
findings.impact: A user reading the docs caps their own crawl at 15 pages and never discovers they are entitled to 25 on the free plan or 250 on Elite, which is the single largest per-plan difference in the crawl feature. Self-hosters, for whom the cap is removed entirely, are told a limit that does not exist on their deployment.
findings.recommendation: Replace the fixed 15 in app/docs/api/page.tsx:322 and :332 and in lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:96 with the per-plan table from lib/billing/crawl-page-limits.ts, note that billing-disabled deployments are unlimited, add the 403 CRAWL_PAGE_LIMIT error (app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:265-271) to the endpoint card's error list, and fix the same string in cli/lib.mjs:126 and app/docs/cli/page.tsx:135.

findings.title: The rate-limits page publishes a 100/hour per-IP limit on "any /api/v3/*" that is enforced on only five routes
findings.description: app/docs/rate-limits/page.tsx:230-234 lists a row "API requests per IP (any /api/v3/*)" with 100 attempts / 60 minutes, under a heading (:189-196) that presents the whole table as IP-based limits enforced from CONFIG_RATE_LIMIT_*_ATTEMPTS pairs. The named limit is RATE_LIMITS.api (lib/rate-limiting/rate-limit.ts:254, CONFIG_RATE_LIMIT_API_REQUESTS = 100 / _WINDOW_MINUTES = 60). Grepping every consumer of `RATE_LIMITS.api` finds exactly five call sites: app/api/v3/auth/update/route.ts:44, app/api/v3/contact/route.ts:36, app/api/v3/landing-contact/route.ts:28, app/api/v3/scan/reputation/route.ts:138, app/api/v3/support-tickets/[id]/route.ts:177. middleware.ts contains no rate-limit call at all. Two of the five are not even per-IP: scan/reputation keys on `scan-reputation:${userId}` and auth/update keys on `${userId}:${clientIp}`. The row below it, "POST /api/v3/scan (and friends) 100/60", is likewise keyed per user (`scan:${session.userId}`, app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:165) and is skipped entirely on the Bearer-API-key branch (the checkGlobalRL call sits inside the session-cookie `else` at :150-176).
findings.impact: The published contract says any /api/v3 endpoint is capped at 100 requests/hour per IP. It is not: 150 of the 155 routes have no such gate, and API-key callers have no scan burst limit at all. An operator sizing capacity, or a security reviewer reading the page, is given a guarantee the code does not make. AUDIT-013 already recorded unmetered paths; this is the doc side of the same gap.
findings.recommendation: Either apply RATE_LIMITS.api in middleware.ts for the whole /api/v3 tree, or rewrite the two rows in app/docs/rate-limits/page.tsx:230-239 to name the five routes that actually carry it, mark which limits are keyed per user rather than per IP, and state that the scan burst limit applies to session auth only.

findings.title: The `main` branch has no branch protection and no ruleset, so not one CI job is a required check and every ci.yml comment claiming a step blocks merges is false
findings.description: I queried the public GitHub API for this repository. `GET /repos/VulnRadar/vulnradar.dev/branches/main` returns `protected: false` with `protection.required_status_checks.enforcement_level: "off"` and empty `contexts` and `checks` arrays; `GET /repos/VulnRadar/vulnradar.dev/rules/branches/main` returns an empty array, so no repository ruleset applies either. ci.yml runs five jobs on `pull_request: branches: [main]` (lint, typecheck, test, extension, build) and its comments assert they gate merges: line 43 "format drift should block merges", lines 65-66 "removed `continue-on-error: true`. Typecheck must block merges", line 70 "block merges on high/critical CVEs in runtime deps". None of these are required checks, so a red CI run is advisory only and the merge button stays green. The same absence means .github/CODEOWNERS is decorative: CODEOWNERS auto-requests reviewers but only enforces review when "Require review from Code Owners" is set in branch protection, and it is not. Direct pushes to main are also unrestricted.
findings.impact: The entire CI investment (SHA-pinned actions, a Prettier gate, a hard typecheck, an `npm audit` gate on 71 runtime dependencies, an extension build, a Next.js build) enforces nothing. Broken TypeScript, a failing test suite, or a high-severity CVE in a production dependency can be merged or pushed straight to main with a single click, and the next `v*` tag turns that into a published image and a GitHub release. It also means the two-person review flow the CODEOWNERS file describes is not actually required for lib/auth, lib/billing, or .github.
findings.recommendation: Add a ruleset (or classic branch protection) on `main` that requires the Lint, Typecheck, Test, Extension, and Build check names, requires at least one approving review, requires review from code owners, and blocks force pushes and direct pushes. Commit the ruleset JSON under .github/ so the configuration is reviewable in-repo rather than living only in the web UI.

findings.title: Dependabot auto-merge calls `gh pr merge --auto` into an unprotected main, so with zero required checks a dependency bump merges the instant it opens, before CI has run
findings.description: .github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml:32 runs `gh pr merge --auto --squash "$PR_URL"` for any dependabot PR whose `update-type` is `version-update:semver-patch` (line 30) and which lacks the `dependabot-merge-ignore` label. The workflow header at line 3 states the guarantee: "Auto-merge patch and minor dependabot updates after CI passes." `--auto` does not wait for CI; it waits for the PR to become mergeable under the branch's protection rules. Per ci-02, `main` has `protected: false`, `required_status_checks.enforcement_level: "off"`, empty `contexts`, and no ruleset, so a dependabot PR is mergeable at the moment it opens and auto-merge fires immediately, with lint, typecheck, test and build still queued or running. The workflow grants itself `contents: write` and `pull-requests: write` at lines 11-13. Separately, ci.yml's `npm ci` steps (lines 37, 62, 101, 138, 193) run with no `--ignore-scripts` and .npmrc contains only `audit-level=high`, `fund=false`, `update-notifier=false`, so package lifecycle scripts execute in CI. (If the repository's "Allow auto-merge" setting happens to be off, `gh pr merge --auto` errors instead and the entire workflow is dead on every dependabot PR; that is the alternative reading and is also a finding.)
findings.impact: A compromised patch release of any of the 71 runtime dependencies is merged to main with no human review and without a single CI job having passed, and its install scripts then run in every subsequent CI job. The next `v*` tag builds that main into the published GHCR image and the signed release tarball, so the compromise propagates to every self-hosted install through the in-app updater. The `npm audit --audit-level=high` gate at ci.yml:71 only catches advisories that already exist, which by definition a fresh malicious release does not have. The stated safety property ("after CI passes") is not enforced anywhere in the repository.
findings.recommendation: Fix ci-02 first: `--auto` is only meaningful once required status checks exist. Then either require Lint/Typecheck/Test/Build as checks on main, or replace `--auto` with an explicit gate in this workflow (a `needs:` on a job that re-runs the suite, or `gh pr checks --watch` before merging). Also restrict auto-merge to devDependencies, or add a cooldown so a package released in the last N days is never auto-merged.

findings.title: No CI job ever builds the Dockerfile, runs docker compose, or boots the app against a Postgres, which is exactly how the two critical self-host breaks reached a published release
findings.description: .github/workflows/ci.yml defines five jobs and contains no occurrence of `docker`, `compose`, `hadolint`, or `trivy`, and declares no `services:` block, so there is no Postgres in CI. The only place the Dockerfile is ever built is .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:49, which fires on `push: tags: v*`, that is, after a release has already been cut. Two consequences are already realised in this audit: AUDIT-014#host-01 (instrumentation.ts:105 exits 1 on an empty database before creating a table) requires a real Postgres to observe and nothing in CI has one; AUDIT-014#host-02 (Dockerfile:75-79 never copies scripts/) requires building and inspecting the runtime stage and nothing in CI does. There is also an install-mode divergence: ci.yml's build job runs plain `npm ci` (line 193) while Dockerfile:24 runs `npm ci --silent --ignore-scripts`, so a green CI build does not prove that the image's dependency install produces a working tree.
findings.impact: The self-hostable half of the product, which is the entire open-source value proposition, has zero automated verification. Two critical breaks shipped to a signed, published release without any job failing. Every future change to the Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, instrumentation.ts boot DDL, or the scripts/migrate runner is unverified until a self-hoster hits it.
findings.recommendation: Add a `selfhost` job to ci.yml that (1) builds the image with `docker build .`, (2) brings up `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d` against a real postgres:16.4-alpine, (3) polls `/api/v3/health` until it reports the database is reachable, and (4) runs `docker compose exec app npm run db:create` so the documented init command is exercised. Make it a required check per ci-02. A hadolint step on the Dockerfile and `docker compose config -q` on both compose files are cheap additions in the same job.

findings.title: Self-hosting is the differentiator that beats six of the eight commercial peers, it is asserted in six separate marketing surfaces, and AUDIT-014#host-01 proves it does not currently work
findings.category: competitive positioning: list (b), the load-bearing advantage
findings.description: Of the eight commercial DAST vendors researched (Detectify, Intruder, Probely/Snyk, Pentest-Tools.com, Acunetix/Invicti, Burp Suite DAST, Snyk, Astra), only Burp Suite DAST and Acunetix/Invicti offer real self-hosting; the other six are SaaS with at most an internal-scanning agent (audits/AUDIT-014/research-competitors-commercial.md, "Deployment" section). GPL-3.0 plus a working self-host is therefore the single structural advantage that no amount of engineering by a small team could otherwise buy. The product asserts it in six places: components/landing/landing-open-source.tsx:39 ("Self-hosting is one Dockerfile and a Postgres connection string"), app/landing/page.tsx:82 (FAQ: "Yes. The whole thing is GPL-3.0 and runs on your own infrastructure"), app/landing/page.tsx:57 (the definitional FAQ answer), components/landing/landing-use-cases.tsx:21 ("a self-host path if the SaaS is a non-starter"), lib/seo/alternatives.ts:46 (the shared VR.hosting string reused on all five /alternatives pages), and lib/seo/alternatives.ts:103, :250, :317 (per-competitor FAQ answers repeating it). AUDIT-014#host-01 (critical) found that on an empty database instrumentation.ts exits 1 before creating a single table, and AUDIT-014#host-02 found the Dockerfile runtime stage never copies scripts/, so db:create and db:migrate are unrunnable inside the published image. Merged from mkt-03, which filed the same fact from the marketing surface. Its point stands and is folded in here: the recommendation is to keep the self-hosting copy rather than weaken it, because the marketing surface is itself the argument for prioritising the host-01 and host-02 fixes. If they cannot be fixed quickly, the copy has to change instead, since it is currently false on the landing page and in the README.
findings.impact: Every competitive claim on the site rests on a capability that a new self-hoster cannot currently exercise. A developer who reaches /alternatives/detectify, reads "self-host it yourself with no plan limits", clones the repo and fails at first boot does not file a bug: they conclude the open-source claim is decorative and leave. This is the one advantage the eight commercial peers structurally cannot copy, and it is the one that does not work.
findings.recommendation: Treat AUDIT-014#host-01 and #host-02 as competitive-blocking, not just deploy bugs: fix them before any further marketing or SEO work in section 19. Then add a CI job that runs the documented self-host path end to end (fresh Postgres container, docker compose up, assert /api/v3/health returns healthy) so the claim cannot silently rot again. Only once that job is green, promote self-hosting from a paragraph in components/landing/landing-open-source.tsx to a named comparison row in lib/seo/alternatives.ts's shared VR object, phrased against the verified fact: "Self-host it. Six of the eight commercial web scanners cannot be run on your own infrastructure at any price."

findings.title: Four docs pages tell a fresh self-hoster to run SQL that demotes the auto-provisioned super_admin to admin, and no UI path can ever restore it
findings.description: lib/auth/auth.ts:284 (and the two sibling insert paths at :365 and :384) assign the role with `CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM users) THEN 'super_admin' ELSE 'user' END`, so the very first account created on a fresh instance is already super_admin (level 50 in STAFF_ROLE_HIERARCHY, lib/config/client-constants.ts:39-48). Four docs pages nonetheless tell the operator to sign up the first user and then promote it with `UPDATE users SET role = 'admin'`: app/docs/setup/page.tsx:428, app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:281, app/docs/config/page.tsx:1155 and app/docs/developers/page.tsx:501. That statement is a demotion, not a promotion: super_admin (50) becomes admin (40). app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:642-647 then filters SUPER_ADMIN out of validRoles for the set_role action, with the comment 'super_admin is un-assignable through this endpoint (or any UI path)'. No docs page mentions the automatic bootstrap or how to undo the demotion.
findings.impact: Every operator who follows the documented install to the letter silently gives up the god-mode role on their own instance. hasGodMode (lib/auth/permissions-client.ts:293) protection, the super-admin-only guards at app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:431/544/549, and the un-deletable-account property are all lost, and the only way back is raw SQL that no document describes.
findings.recommendation: Delete the promote-to-admin SQL step from all four pages and replace it with one sentence: the first account created on a fresh instance is automatically super_admin, sign up and open /admin. If a manual promotion step is still wanted for a non-first account, use `role = 'admin'` only with an explicit warning never to run it against the bootstrap account, and document `UPDATE users SET role = 'super_admin' WHERE id = 1` as the only recovery.

findings.title: README and five docs sites still describe the lib/types/config.ts + lib/config/config.ts layer that commit 2cee4042 deleted nine days ago, including a typecheck safety net that no longer exists
findings.description: Commit 2cee4042 (2026-08-20) removed 'lib/config/config.ts + lib/types/config.ts (the dead loadConfig/getConfigValue/DEFAULT_CONFIG layer, superseded by the registry/getSetting resolver)'. There is no lib/types/ directory in the tree at all, and grepping lib/ for loadConfig or getConfigValue returns nothing. Six doc sites still describe it as live: README.md:99 ('lib/types/config.ts derives the typed DEFAULT_CONFIG from them') in the paragraph headed 'Single source of truth'; app/docs/config/page.tsx:125-136 renders a lib/config/ directory tree that lists config.ts and lib/types/config.ts while omitting registry.ts, runtime-config.ts, env.ts and brand.ts, the four files that actually drive configuration today; app/docs/config/page.tsx:1173-1178 promises 'Build time: npm run typecheck exercises every CONFIG_* through the typed DEFAULT_CONFIG in lib/types/config.ts. Renaming or removing a constant fails typecheck'; app/docs/architecture/page.tsx:176-184 lists both deleted files as steps 2 and 3 of the config chain; app/docs/developers/page.tsx:769-773 warns against 'Editing lib/types/config.ts defaults'; and app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:578-581 offers a troubleshooting row whose stated cause is 'Renamed a CONFIG_* constant without updating the typed DEFAULT_CONFIG'.
findings.impact: A self-hoster or contributor reading the canonical explanation of how configuration works is sent to two files that do not exist and told about two exported functions that do not exist. Worse, app/docs/config/page.tsx:1173-1178 advertises a compile-time guarantee that was deleted with the file: renaming or deleting a CONFIG_* constant no longer fails typecheck through any DEFAULT_CONFIG, so someone who trusts that safety net can ship a broken rename. The docs also never name registry.ts or runtime-config.ts, which is where configuration actually lives now.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the config chain in all six places as config-values.ts -> registry.ts (SETTINGS_REGISTRY) -> runtime-config.ts (database ?? env ?? default) -> constants.ts / client-constants.ts, with env.ts as the boot-time validator. Redraw the tree in app/docs/config/page.tsx:125-136 from the real ls of lib/config/. Delete the DEFAULT_CONFIG typecheck claim at :1173-1178 and the self-hosting troubleshooting row at :578-581, or replace them with whatever real gate exists.

findings.title: .github/SUPPORT.md instructs bug reporters to delete package-lock.json and reinstall, the one operation that strips the 28 Linux native-binding entries and breaks CI and the Docker build
findings.description: package-lock.json contains 58 platform-scoped optional packages, 28 of them Linux: @next/swc-linux-{x64,arm64}-{gnu,musl}, @rolldown/binding-linux-*, @img/sharp-linux-* and @img/sharp-libvips-linux-*. Every CI job installs with `npm ci` on ubuntu-latest (.github/workflows/ci.yml:37, :62, :101, :137, :193) and Dockerfile builds on a Linux base, so all of them resolve those entries out of the committed lockfile. .github/SUPPORT.md:19 tells anyone about to file a bug to 'Delete node_modules and package-lock.json, then npm install from scratch'. Run on Windows, that regenerates the lockfile without the Linux entries and additionally re-resolves every version away from the pinned set. Nothing in CONTRIBUTING.md, README.md or app/docs/setup/page.tsx warns about this: app/docs/setup/page.tsx:129 warns only 'Use npm, not pnpm or yarn', which is the adjacent hazard, not this one.
findings.impact: A contributor or maintainer who follows the official support instructions on a Windows or macOS machine and commits the regenerated lockfile breaks `npm ci` on every CI job and the Docker image build with a 'Cannot find native binding' failure for next/font, and the breakage looks like a code problem rather than a lockfile problem. The repo has hit this before.
findings.recommendation: Change .github/SUPPORT.md:19 to `rm -rf node_modules && npm ci` (which never rewrites the lockfile). Add a short 'Lockfile' section to CONTRIBUTING.md stating that package-lock.json must only ever be regenerated on Linux, that a lockfile diff removing any *-linux-* entry must be rejected in review, and that npm ci is the only supported install for reproducing a bug. Optionally add a CI step that fails when the diff drops a linux optional dependency.

findings.title: The self-hosting troubleshooting table tells an operator locked out by broken SMTP to call POST /api/v3/auth/2fa/disable, which requires the session they cannot obtain
findings.description: app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:593-596 documents the symptom 'Login succeeds but 2FA code never arrives', cause 'SMTP not configured', fix 'Set SMTP_HOST/PORT/USER/PASS/FROM in .env and restart, or disable 2FA via /api/v3/auth/2fa/disable'. app/api/v3/auth/2fa/disable/route.ts:17-19 calls getSession() and returns 401 when there is none, then at :38-52 requires the account password in the body. A user stopped at the second factor has not completed login: the interim state is a separate signed token handled by lib/auth/pending-2fa.ts, not a session cookie, so getSession() returns null and the call is a guaranteed 401. The second half of the fix is therefore unusable in exactly the situation the row describes, and the first half (configure SMTP) is the same instruction the operator already could not satisfy.
findings.impact: An operator who self-hosts without SMTP and enabled email 2FA is permanently locked out of their own instance, and the only recovery the documentation offers cannot be executed. This compounds AUDIT-014#host-04. The repo does ship a database-side escape (npm run db:repair-2fa) but it only touches rows proven corrupt by scripts/_lib/_lib.2fa-diagnostics.mjs, so it does not help a healthy-but-unreachable email 2FA row, and it is documented nowhere.
findings.recommendation: Replace the second clause of the fix in app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:596 with a database recovery that actually works from outside the app: `UPDATE users SET totp_enabled = false, two_factor_method = NULL, totp_secret = NULL, backup_codes = NULL WHERE email = '...';` run through psql, with a note that this is the only path when no session can be established. Add the same recovery to a new troubleshooting section, and document npm run db:repair-2fa and npm run db:diagnose-2fa alongside it.

findings.title: Every semantic colour used as text fails WCAG AA in light mode, including the severity badge at 1.66:1, while /legal/accessibility publishes a WCAG 2.1 AA conformance claim
findings.description: The light and dark themes share one value for every accent token. app/globals.css:178 sets --primary: 213 94% 68% and the .dark block at :230 repeats the identical triplet. The same is true of --severity-critical/high/medium/low (:204-207 vs :249-252, identical) and --warning (:219 vs :264). Those values were tuned for a near-black ground, and the in-app idiom is to paint the colour as TEXT on a 10 to 15 percent tint of itself: components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:37-78 pairs tone.text with tone.surface, and SeverityBadge at :106-114 applies both to the same span. I computed the sRGB contrast ratios directly from the token triplets in globals.css against --card (light 213 22% 95%, dark 224 18% 9%). Light mode: severity medium 1.66:1, high 2.15:1, low 2.67:1, critical 2.79:1, info 3.40:1. Dark mode the same badges are 7.77, 5.34, 4.88, 4.17 and 4.20:1. The same split hits the rest of the accent layer in light mode: text-primary on bg-card is 2.25:1 and on the bg-primary/10 active-nav pill used by app/admin/page.tsx:1078 and app/profile/page.tsx:757 it is 2.08:1; text-[hsl(var(--warning))] on its own /10 tint (app/browser/[id]/page.tsx:377, components/teams/teams-types.ts:64) is 1.90:1; text-[hsl(var(--success))] on card (components/history/history-stats.tsx:77, components/assets/assets-stats.tsx, app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:224) is 2.98:1; text-destructive on card is 3.37:1 and on destructive/10 is 2.97:1. Only the neutral layer is safe: muted-foreground is 5.02:1 on card and foreground is 15.86:1. globals.css:179-185 shows the team already reasoned about contrast in the opposite direction (they darkened --primary-foreground because white on the primary fill measured about 2.5:1) but never checked colour-as-text on a light surface. app/legal/accessibility/page.tsx:54 states conformance with WCAG 2.1 Level AA and :73 says "We maintain sufficient color contrast ratios between text and backgrounds". Merged from a11y-02 and a11y-03, which an independent agent derived with its own contrast calculator and reached the identical 1.66:1 for the medium severity badge. Their additional specifics: text-primary measures 1.99:1 against the light page background across 478 usages including the links inside the accessibility statement itself, and the severity tokens are used as TEXT colour 83 times via text-[hsl(var(--severity-*))]. Only --severity-info differs between the two theme blocks; every other accent token is byte-identical. Verified during the merge: app/globals.css:178 and :230 both read `--primary: 213 94% 68%`.
findings.impact: A user on the light theme cannot read the single most important visual encoding in the product. The MEDIUM severity chip on a finding row is 1.66:1, roughly the contrast of pale yellow on white, so the word disappears and only the 6px dot survives, which is exactly the colour-alone encoding the severity-badge docblock at :30-34 says it exists to avoid. Every link, every active sidebar item, every SSL-grade cell and every success or warning count on /dashboard, /history, /assets, /shares and /browser is in the same state. The published accessibility statement is measurably false, which matters for a security product sold to teams who ask for a VPAT.
findings.recommendation: Split the accent tokens into a fill value and a foreground value instead of retuning the fills (retuning --primary would move every bg-primary button and the focus ring). In app/globals.css add to :root only: --primary-text: 213 94% 43%; --destructive-text: 0 84% 43%; --success-text: 142 76% 26%; --warning-text: 38 92% 29%; --severity-critical-text: 0 84% 41%; --severity-high-text: 25 95% 33%; --severity-medium-text: 45 93% 27%; --severity-low-text: 210 90% 40%. Each of those lightness values is the first one that clears 4.5:1 against its own existing 10 to 15 percent tint on --card. In the .dark block define the same eight names as aliases of the current fills so dark mode is byte-identical to today. Then change components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:41,49,57,65,73 so `text` reads text-[hsl(var(--severity-X-text))] while `solid` (dots, rails, SeverityDistribution segments) keeps the current fill, and add the four new utilities to the tailwind.config.mjs colour map so text-primary-text and friends exist. Finally sweep the literal token uses: text-primary in app/admin/page.tsx:1078, app/profile/page.tsx:757, text-[hsl(var(--success))] in components/history/history-stats.tsx, assets-stats.tsx, shares-stats.tsx and app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:224, and text-[hsl(var(--warning))] in app/browser/[id]/page.tsx:377 and components/teams/teams-types.ts:64.

findings.title: The skip link in the root layout targets #main-content, which the three shared page shells never render, so it is inert on the docs, the SEO pages, /host, /shared and /public-scans
findings.description: app/layout.tsx:171-176 renders a single skip link with href="#main-content" on every route. Only 19 page files define that id: app/dashboard, /history, /profile, /admin, /teams, /repos, /shares, /assets, /attack-surface, /badge, /pricing, /landing, /browser/[id], the four /checkout pages and app/admin/ai-chats/[id]. The three shared shells that render the remaining pages do not. components/shared/public-page-shell.tsx:60-62 opens <main className={...}> with no id and no tabIndex, and it is the shell for app/changelog, app/compare, app/contact, app/host/[hostname], app/public-scans, app/security and app/shared/[token]. lib/seo/seo-ui.tsx:19 is <main className="flex-1">{children}</main>, also with no id, and it is the shell for app/checks, app/checks/[id] (about 750 generated pages), app/checks/category/[category], app/alternatives, app/alternatives/[competitor], app/tools, app/tools/api-scanner and app/tools/link-checker. components/docs/docs-shell.tsx:76-78 names its main id="docs-content", not main-content, covering all 20 docs pages. app/donate/page.tsx:24 has no <main> element at all. Both counterexamples that do work, components/auth/auth-layout.tsx:25-28 and components/auth/auth-split-layout.tsx:95-98, set id="main-content" and tabIndex={-1} together, which is the correct pattern. app/legal/accessibility/page.tsx:93 states "Skip navigation links allow users to bypass repetitive content". Merged from a11y-04, which additionally names the changelog shell among the surfaces whose skip-link target does not exist.
findings.impact: A keyboard or screen-reader user pressing Tab on the site's whole public and documentation surface, including the two shareable report pages (/host/[hostname] and /shared/[token]) that are the product's main outbound link, activates the skip link and the focus does not move. They then tab through the full nav on every page. The pages where this works are almost entirely the signed-in ones, so the visitors most likely to be evaluating the product are the ones it fails for. The accessibility statement claims otherwise.
findings.recommendation: Three one-line edits. components/shared/public-page-shell.tsx:60: add id="main-content" tabIndex={-1} to the <main>. lib/seo/seo-ui.tsx:19: same, <main id="main-content" tabIndex={-1} className="flex-1">. components/docs/docs-shell.tsx:77: rename id="docs-content" to id="main-content" and add tabIndex={-1}, then update any in-page anchor that referenced docs-content (grep shows the docs TOC does not, so this is safe). Wrap app/donate/page.tsx:24's content div in <main id="main-content" tabIndex={-1}>. Then add a test in tests/ that renders each shell and asserts one element with id="main-content", so a fourth shell cannot regress it.

findings.title: Every arrow and section sign in a PDF report renders as mojibake, because the Helvetica fonts are declared with no /Encoding while UTF-8 bytes are written straight into the content stream
findings.description: generatePdfReport declares its two fonts as `<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /Helvetica >>` and `/Helvetica-Bold` (lib/reports/pdf-report.ts:449-452) with no `/Encoding` entry, so a viewer falls back to the font's built-in single-byte StandardEncoding. Text reaches the content stream unchanged: escPdf (:50-52) escapes only backslash and parentheses, addText writes the raw JS string into a literal at :86, and the whole document is emitted with `new TextEncoder().encode(pdf)` at :513, which is UTF-8. Every multi-byte character therefore arrives as N separate single-byte glyph codes. Non-ASCII characters are not hypothetical in this data: lib/scanner/checks-data holds 96 of them, and they sit in exactly the fields the PDF prints. secrets-extended.json entry [5] fixSteps[0] is "Revoke the token immediately via GitHub Settings → Developer Settings → Personal Access Tokens", and at least ten more fixSteps in that file use U+2192 (PyPI, Cloudflare, Tailscale, Algolia, Mapbox, PagerDuty, Datadog, Supabase). email.json[11].explanation contains "RFC 5321 §5.1". headers.json[96].codeExamples[0].code contains two arrows. Those fields are printed at pdf-report.ts:372 (fixSteps), :364 (explanation) and :386 (codeExamples). U+2192 is E2 86 92 in UTF-8, so one arrow becomes three glyphs. Note the /Length values are byte-correct (:460), and the xref byte-offset fix documented at :486-490 already exists, so the file is structurally valid: this is purely a rendering defect. Neither the Markdown (lib/reports/markdown-report.ts) nor the SARIF (lib/reports/sarif-report.ts) export has this problem, so the PDF is the only format that corrupts the text.
