findings.impact: The PDF is the artifact a user forwards to a manager or a client, and /docs/reports/page.tsx:134 sells it as exactly that ("hand a PDF to a stakeholder"). The garbling lands on the remediation steps of secret-exposure findings, which are the highest-stakes instructions the scanner produces. A leaked-GitHub-token finding tells the reader to go to "GitHub Settings a†' Developer Settings", which reads as a broken tool and undermines the report's credibility at the exact moment it is being used to argue for a fix.
findings.recommendation: Two-line fix plus one guard. In lib/reports/pdf-report.ts:449-452 add `/Encoding /WinAnsiEncoding` to both font objects, then transcode text to CP1252 bytes before writing it: extend escPdf (:50) to map each code point through a small WinAnsi table and emit anything unmappable as a PDF octal escape (\\NNN), falling back to an ASCII transliteration for characters WinAnsi has no slot for (U+2192 -> "->", U+2018/2019 -> "'", U+201C/201D -> '"', U+2026 -> "..."). Because the string is then single-byte, also change line 460 and 470 to compute /Length over the transcoded bytes. Add a test in tests/lib/reports/ that renders a finding whose fixSteps contain U+2192 and U+00A7 and asserts the emitted stream contains no byte above 0x7F outside an escape.

findings.title: All 29 "Build" tier admin settings (APP_NAME, APP_URL, LOGO_URL, FOOTER_TEXT, every SEO_*) are written to system_settings and then read by nothing, while the admin banner and /docs/config both promise the change applies on the next build
findings.description: lib/config/registry.ts declares 267 settings; 29 carry `tier: "build"` (APP_NAME, APP_SLUG, APP_DESCRIPTION, TOTAL_CHECKS_LABEL, APP_URL, APP_REPO, DISCORD_INVITE_URL, CHROME_WEB_STORE_URL, FIREFOX_ADDON_URL, LOGO_URL, PRIMARY_COLOR, BACKGROUND_COLOR_DARK/LIGHT, FOOTER_TEXT, the 13 SEO_* keys, BULK_SCAN_CLIENT_URL_LIMIT, MAX_AVATAR_UPLOAD_BYTES). The admin write path accepts every key that passes isSettingKey and upserts it (app/api/v3/admin/features/route.ts:316-341). Reading them back is the problem. I enumerated every getSetting/getSettings call site across app/, lib/ and components/ with a Node scan: 157 distinct keys are resolved through lib/config/runtime-config.ts, and not one of them is a build-tier key. The only reader of any build-tier row is resolveAppUrl (lib/config/runtime-config.ts:143), which does `values.get("APP_URL")` for OAuth redirect_uri and is called by exactly 7 sign-in routes. Everything else reads the synchronous constants in lib/config/constants.ts:170-231, which resolve from process.env or the CONFIG_ literal and never touch Postgres. No build step reads the table either: package.json's prebuild runs only the four knowledge compilers, and `system_settings` appears nowhere under scripts/ except the schema DDL. So the banner at components/admin/features/system-settings-manager.tsx:515-518 ("Saving here updates the database immediately, but the change only shows up after the next build and deploy"), the identical claim at app/docs/config/page.tsx:596-603, and the APP_URL help text at lib/config/registry.ts:377 are all false: the next build reads NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL or the CONFIG_ literal, never the row that was saved. The registry's documented `database value ?? environment override ?? shipped default` chain (runtime-config.ts:3, repeated at app/docs/config/page.tsx:607) is also inert for these keys in both of its first two steps, because resolve() is only reachable through getSetting/getSettings.
findings.impact: A self-hoster follows /docs/self-hosting, creates the first admin, opens /admin > Settings > Branding, types their own product name, logo and footer line, saves, sees a success toast and an explicit banner telling them it will appear on the next deploy, rebuilds, and gets VulnRadar's branding back. There is no error and no way to tell the write did nothing. The same is true of the APP_URL field, which is the single most load-bearing deployment value in the product: an operator who sets it there and rebuilds still ships canonical tags, sitemap entries, robots host, OG/Twitter URLs, JSON-LD @id, badge embed snippets and every transactional email link pointing at vulnradar.dev. Combined with AUDIT-014#host-05 (the compose app service has no build context, so the documented Docker path can never rebuild at all), the admin panel is the only branding surface a Docker self-hoster has, and it is a no-op.
findings.recommendation: Two options, pick one and make the UI match it. (a) Make them real: give every build-tier key a server-side read path through getSetting in the server components that render it (app/layout.tsx metadata, components/seo/structured-data.tsx, app/sitemap.ts, app/robots.ts, app/manifest.ts, lib/email/email.ts), accept that client components still need NEXT_PUBLIC_ inlining, and drop the tier distinction for the server-rendered half. (b) Make them honest: stop persisting build-tier keys. Have the PATCH handler in app/api/v3/admin/features/route.ts reject any key whose registry tier is "build" with a 400 naming lib/config/config-values.ts as the place to change it, render those fields read-only in system-settings-manager.tsx, and rewrite the banner at :515 and app/docs/config/page.tsx:596-603 to say "edit lib/config/config-values.ts and rebuild; this page cannot change them". Either way, delete the false "next build and deploy" wording from all three places.

findings.title: The browser extension is compiled against a literal https://vulnradar.dev with no build arg, no setting and manifest host_permissions to match, so a self-hoster cannot point it at their own instance at all
findings.description: extension/src/lib/constants.ts:3 sets `apiHost: "https://vulnradar.dev"` as a plain `as const` literal. Every network call, every deep link and every privacy statement derives from it: extension/src/lib/api.ts:93 and :167 build request URLs, service-worker.ts:180 and :183 open history/dashboard tabs, content/reputation-card.ts:271 and :348 render links, onboarding/welcome.ts:41-86 prints it three times, options/options.ts:365 and :1123 print it again. Nothing overrides it: extension/vite.config.ts defines no `define` block and no env plumbing, extension/scripts/build.mjs references no VITE_ or process.env variable, and the options page has no host field (options.ts:1123 states as fact "The extension talks to https://vulnradar.dev only"). Both manifests pin it a second time: extension/manifest/chrome.json:42 and extension/manifest/firefox.json:52 are `"host_permissions": ["https://vulnradar.dev/*"]`, so even patching constants.ts alone leaves every request blocked by the browser. A third copy exists at service-worker.ts:418-421, where EXCLUDED_HOSTS is a literal list of sandbox.vulnradar.dev / vulnradar.dev / www.vulnradar.dev rather than being derived from apiHost, so a repointed build would auto-scan its own instance and still skip vulnradar.dev. /docs/extension never mentions self-hosting; it links only to the two public store listings (app/docs/extension/page.tsx:113 and :139), which install the vulnradar.dev-locked build.
findings.impact: The extension is advertised on a self-hosted instance's own /docs/extension page, and installing it from either store gives the operator's users a tool that sends their scan targets to vulnradar.dev, authenticated with an API key from vulnradar.dev, that will never work against the instance they actually run. A self-hoster who wants it has to fork the extension, edit four files, rebuild, and side-load an unsigned unpacked extension on every machine, which Chrome disables on restart for non-store extensions in managed environments. There is no documentation for any of that. Compare the CLI (cli/lib.mjs:57, `--api-base`) and the GitHub Action (.github/actions/scan-gate/action.yml:15-18, `api-base-url`), which both take the repoint as a first-class input; the extension is the only client that does not.
findings.recommendation: Add a `VULNRADAR_API_HOST` build-time define in extension/vite.config.ts and extension/scripts/build.mjs (`define: { __API_HOST__: JSON.stringify(process.env.VULNRADAR_API_HOST || "https://vulnradar.dev") }`), read it in extension/src/lib/constants.ts:3, and template the same value into `host_permissions` in a small step in extension/scripts/build.mjs the way `__VERSION__` is already templated. Derive EXCLUDED_HOSTS at service-worker.ts:418 from `new URL(VULNRADAR.apiHost).hostname` plus its `www.` form instead of the literal list. For the no-rebuild case, add an optional "Instance URL" field to the options page backed by `optional_host_permissions: ["https://*/*"]` plus a browser.permissions.request() prompt, and note the whole mechanism in app/docs/extension/page.tsx so a self-hoster does not have to read the source to discover it does not work.

findings.title: SUPPORT_EMAIL is documented as an env override and registered as a runtime admin setting, but 8 of its 9 call sites read the build-time constant, and in the 4 client components the env read is compiled out so the footer permanently shows support@vulnradar.dev
findings.description: Three surfaces promise SUPPORT_EMAIL is configurable: .env.example:87-88 ("Falls back to CONFIG_SUPPORT_EMAIL in lib/config/config-values.ts"), app/docs/config/page.tsx:987-994 ("CONTACT_EMAIL, SUPPORT_EMAIL: override the addresses used by contact/support emails"), and lib/config/registry.ts:432-438, which registers it `tier: "runtime"` with the explicitly UI-facing help text "Address shown to users who need help and used as the reply-to on support mail". Exactly one call site honours the runtime setting: app/legal/accessibility/page.tsx:23-24 uses getSettings(["SUPPORT_EMAIL", ...]). The other eight read the build-time export at lib/config/constants.ts:638 (`process.env.SUPPORT_EMAIL || CONFIG_SUPPORT_EMAIL`): lib/email/email.ts:167, :287, :801, :816, :830, :840 (every transactional email footer and every security-alert "email us" line), lib/support/ticket-notify.ts:39 (the To: address for support tickets), components/seo/structured-data.tsx:98 (JSON-LD contactPoint), components/contact/contact-quick-links.tsx:17-18, plus four "use client" components: components/scanner/footer.tsx:244 (sitewide), components/scanner/dashboard-error-state.tsx:293, components/demo/demo-error.tsx:46 and app/checkout/success/checkout-success-content.tsx:72. In a client bundle Next.js only inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_-prefixed variables, so `process.env.SUPPORT_EMAIL` becomes a falsy constant and the `||` folds away at build time. I confirmed this in the checked-in build output: .next/static/chunks/9711-3989d97c24edd68e.js contains `O="support@vulnradar.dev",R="legal@vulnradar.dev",I="security@vu...` with no process.env reference left. LEGAL_EMAIL, SECURITY_EMAIL and ENTERPRISE_EMAIL (constants.ts:639-641) have no env path at all and are baked into that same chunk, although their runtime settings do reach the /legal/* pages and /api/security-txt via getSetting.
findings.impact: A self-hoster sets SUPPORT_EMAIL in .env exactly as documented and gets a split-brain instance: outgoing email, support-ticket routing and the JSON-LD contact point use their address, while the footer on every single page, the dashboard error state, the demo error and the checkout success page keep telling their users to email support@vulnradar.dev. Those users then email a third party about a product they do not run, which is a support-load and privacy problem for both sides and reads as a phishing-shaped inconsistency. The admin-panel SUPPORT_EMAIL field makes it worse: it is labelled runtime tier, so it saves with no build warning at all, and changes precisely one page out of nine.
findings.recommendation: Two fixes. (1) For server-rendered surfaces, switch to the runtime setting so the admin field means something: lib/email/email.ts should take the support address as a parameter resolved by its callers via getSetting("SUPPORT_EMAIL"), and components/seo/structured-data.tsx, components/contact/contact-quick-links.tsx and lib/support/ticket-notify.ts should call getSetting directly (all three are server components/modules already). (2) For the four client components, the address has to be inlined at build time, so rename the env var to NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPPORT_EMAIL in lib/config/constants.ts:638 and .env.example:88 (keeping SUPPORT_EMAIL as a server-only fallback), or pass the address down from a server parent as a prop. Whichever is chosen, correct app/docs/config/page.tsx:989-993 so it does not claim a plain SUPPORT_EMAIL override reaches the UI.

findings.title: The AI assistant reads its five knowledge files from process.cwd()/lib/ai/, but the Dockerfile runner stage never copies lib/, so /docs, /changelog, /checks and /legal are empty in every published image and tell the operator to run a command the image does not contain
findings.description: app/api/v3/ai/context/route.ts:18-26 defines readKnowledgeFile(...segments) as `readFileSync(join(process.cwd(), ...segments))` guarded by existsSync, returning "" on a miss. Five call sites use it: :61 lib/ai/docs-knowledge.md, :74 lib/ai/changelog-knowledge.md, :87 lib/ai/checks-index.md with :89 falling back to checks-knowledge.md, :102 lib/ai/legal-knowledge.md, and :284-287 checks-knowledge.md for the /finding explainer. Those files exist in the repo (lib/ai/*.md, 244 KB to 975 KB each) and are regenerated by the prebuild compilers in package.json. They are not JS imports, so nothing bundles them into .next. The runner stage of the Dockerfile copies exactly five paths: /app/public (:75), /app/.next (:76), /app/node_modules (:77), /app/package.json (:78) and /app/next.config.mjs (:79). lib/ is not among them, and next.config.mjs:4 explicitly disables `output: "standalone"`, so Next.js output file tracing is not copying them either. In the published image every one of those five reads misses and the route returns the failure summary written at :66 and :80: "Documentation not available. Run `npm run build:knowledge` to generate it." Per AUDIT-014#host-02 scripts/ is not copied into the image either, so that npm script cannot run there: it invokes node scripts/compile-docs-knowledge.mjs.
findings.impact: Four of the AI assistant's slash commands and the per-finding explainer silently return nothing on every Docker deployment, which is the deployment path the docs recommend. The user sees a confident "not available" message pointing at a remediation command that fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND inside the container, so the operator burns time on a fix that cannot work. This is also a hosted-instance risk if production ever moves to this image: the /changelog context block alone is 250 KB of product knowledge the assistant is designed around, and its absence degrades quietly rather than erroring. Extends AUDIT-014#host-02, which found the same missing-scripts root cause for db:create, db:migrate and the Backup button; this is a second, user-facing consequence of the same COPY list.
findings.recommendation: Add `COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/lib/ai/*.md ./lib/ai/` to the Dockerfile after line 79 (a narrow copy, roughly 1.4 MB, not the whole lib/ tree, which is already compiled into .next). Then change the fallback summaries at app/api/v3/ai/context/route.ts:66, :80, :95 and :107 to a message that does not name an npm script, since the container cannot run one: "Knowledge base not available on this instance." If a broader fix is preferred, have scripts/compile-*-knowledge.mjs emit a .ts module exporting the string instead of a .md file so the content is bundled into .next and the runtime filesystem read disappears entirely.

findings.title: docker-compose.yml has no env_file, so 11 of the 48 environment variables the app reads are forwarded and the rest of .env is silently ignored, while the self-hosting docs state the app reads .env via env_file
findings.description: Static analysis, measured with a Node script over `git ls-files` (48 distinct process.env.* names in app/, lib/, components/, scripts/, middleware.ts, instrumentation.ts, excluding NODE_ENV/PORT/HOSTNAME/NEXT_RUNTIME and test-only names). The app service at docker-compose.yml:52 declares only an `environment:` map (:55-72) and no `env_file:` key. Compose reads the project .env file for ${VAR} substitution INSIDE the compose file, but only the keys listed in that map are actually placed in the container's environment. The map forwards 11 app variables: DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_SSL, NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY, SMTP_HOST/PORT/USER/PASS/FROM, NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY, TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY (plus CONTACT_EMAIL and NODE_ENV). Not forwarded, despite all being documented in .env.example and read in source: AI_PROVIDER, AI_BASE_URL, AI_MODEL, AI_API_KEY (lib/ai/provider.ts), STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, AUTH_SECRET, DISCORD_CLIENT_ID/CLIENT_SECRET/BOT_TOKEN/GUILD_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET, GITHUB_CLIENT_ID/SECRET, TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDR, DATABASE_SSL_CA, AVATAR_STORAGE_DIR, BACKUP_DIR, BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY, BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS, BACKUP_OFFSITE_UPLOAD_URL, NVD_API_KEY, WEB_RISK_API_KEY, URLHAUS_AUTH_KEY, LOGO_URL, SUPPORT_EMAIL, DISABLE_CSP, SECURITY_ALLOW_NON_BROWSER_API, and the four NEXT_PUBLIC SEO/verification vars. app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:243-244 states flatly "The app reads .env via env_file", and the same page then instructs the operator to put AI_BASE_URL / AI_MODEL / AI_API_KEY in .env (:213-217) and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in .env followed by `docker compose restart app` (:372-377). Neither reaches the process. docker-compose.dev.yml:46-61 has the identical map and the identical gap. This is the mechanism behind AUDIT-012#obs-08's "Invalid signature" symptom: on the shipped compose the webhook secret cannot be set at all.
findings.impact: A self-hoster who configures AI, Stripe, Discord/Google/GitHub OAuth, a trusted proxy CIDR, a custom backup directory or a threat-intel API key in .env exactly as the docs say gets no error and no effect. Features silently stay off, and the failure looks like a bug in the feature rather than in the plumbing. OAuth being unreachable also removes the only sign-in path that works without SMTP (see host-04).
findings.recommendation: Add `env_file: [.env]` to the app service in both docker-compose.yml (after :54) and docker-compose.dev.yml, keeping the explicit `environment:` map for the values that are composed rather than passed through (DATABASE_URL, NODE_ENV). If passing the whole file is undesirable, extend the map to cover every key in .env.example and correct app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:243-244.

findings.title: Without SMTP a self-hoster can create an account but can never log in: signup leaves email_verified_at NULL, the verification email throws in production, and login refuses unverified accounts
findings.description: Static trace. lib/email/email.ts:81 builds the SMTP transport only when SMTP_HOST && SMTP_USER && SMTP_PASS are all set, otherwise `transporter` is null. sendEmail then logs a warning and, when process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production", returns successfully (:407-418); in production it throws `new Error("Email service not configured")` at :427. Both Dockerfile:106 and docker-compose.yml:56 set NODE_ENV=production, so the production branch is the one self-hosters hit. app/api/v3/auth/signup/route.ts:215-222 sends the verification email inside a background catch that only console.errors, so signup returns 200 and the user row is created with email_verified_at NULL (the signup INSERT never sets it; grep across app/api/v3/auth/ shows the only setters are the OAuth callback, the staff-invite route, and app/api/v3/auth/verify-email/route.ts:77, which needs the token from the email). app/api/v3/auth/login/route.ts:164 then blocks the login with `unverified: true`. app/api/v3/auth/resend-verification/route.ts calls the same sendEmail and throws the same way. The two escape hatches are both closed on the default compose: OAuth sign-in sets email_verified_at immediately but its credentials are not forwarded to the container (host-03), and there is no admin setting to disable verification (grep for REQUIRE_EMAIL/EMAIL_VERIFICATION over lib/config finds only CONFIG_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_HOURS, a TTL). Every doc labels SMTP optional: app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:185 "# Optional: SMTP", docker-compose.yml:62 "# SMTP (optional, for emails)", app/docs/config/page.tsx:1160 "(Optional) Configure SMTP". The First Admin User procedure at app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:268-284 tells the operator to sign up and then run one SQL statement (UPDATE users SET role = 'admin'), and omits the UPDATE users SET email_verified_at = NOW() that is actually required to log in at all.
findings.impact: The most likely self-hoster profile, someone with a Postgres string and no mail server, reaches a working signup form, creates the account the docs tell them to create, and is then locked out with a message about an email that was never sent and cannot be resent. There is no in-app recovery. The instance is unusable and the cause is not discoverable from the UI.
findings.recommendation: Either mark the account verified at signup when no SMTP transport is configured (check the same SMTP_HOST/USER/PASS triple lib/email/email.ts:81 uses and set email_verified_at = NOW() in the signup INSERT), or add an explicit setting that skips verification. At minimum, add `UPDATE users SET email_verified_at = NOW() WHERE email = '...';` alongside the role UPDATE at app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:280 and stop calling SMTP optional there and in docker-compose.yml:62.

findings.title: The documented self-host upgrade path is a no-op: the app service declares no build context, so `git pull && docker compose build app && docker compose up -d` re-pulls the same pinned 3.0.0 image
findings.description: Static analysis. The app service in docker-compose.yml:52-53 declares `image: ghcr.io/vulnradar/vulnradar:3.0.0` and no `build:` key, unlike docker-compose.dev.yml:40-44 which does. app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:535-541 documents the upgrade as `cd vulnradar.dev; git pull; docker compose build app; docker compose up -d`. With no build context, `docker compose build app` cannot build anything from the pulled source, and the subsequent `up -d` reconciles against the pinned image tag, so the freshly pulled source has no effect whatsoever on what runs. The same shape breaks README.md:78-79, which labels `docker compose up -d` as "# 3. Build and run" immediately after a `git clone` at :70: the clone is only used for .env and lib/config/config-values.ts edits, and config-values.ts is baked into the image at build time (README.md:95 "Edit and rebuild"), so those edits also never take effect on the prod compose path. app/docs/setup/page.tsx:607-613 makes the same promise, offering `git clone` as the "Or build from source locally" alternative to curling the compose file, when both branches land on the same non-building compose. This extends AUDIT-013#deps-06, which recorded the 3.0.0-vs-3.7.2 pin: the new part is that the documented mechanism for getting off that pinned version does not build and the fork-customisation workflow the README sells is unreachable from the shipped compose.
findings.impact: A self-hoster who forks and rebrands the app per README.md:88-102 sees none of their config-values.ts edits, and an operator following the documented upgrade steps believes they have upgraded while still running the 3.0.0 image. Neither failure produces an error message.
findings.recommendation: Give the app service in docker-compose.yml a `build:` section alongside `image:` (context ., dockerfile Dockerfile, args NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL) so `docker compose build app` works and `up -d` prefers the local build, or change app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:535-541 and README.md:78 to the pull-only path (`docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`) and point fork customisation at docker-compose.dev.yml explicitly.

findings.title: NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL is inlined at build time and the published image is built without the build-arg, so every self-hosted instance renders vulnradar.dev in 15 client components regardless of the runtime env var
findings.description: Static analysis. lib/config/constants.ts:191 is `export const APP_URL = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL || CONFIG_APP_URL;`, with CONFIG_APP_URL = "https://vulnradar.dev" (lib/config/config-values.ts:141). Next.js replaces NEXT_PUBLIC_* with a literal at build time in any module that reaches the client bundle. A scan of every "use client" file under app/, components/, lib/ and hooks/ finds 15 that reference APP_URL, including components/landing/landing-api-example.tsx, components/demo/demo-hero.tsx, components/scanner/footer.tsx, components/admin/features/mass-email-manager.tsx and ten /docs pages. Dockerfile:16 declares ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL and :32 forwards it to ENV, but .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml passes no build-args at all, so the published ghcr.io image, which is the image docker-compose.yml:53 pulls, has the fallback literal baked into those bundles. Setting NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL in docker-compose.yml:59 changes only server-side reads. The comment at lib/config/constants.ts:177-184 states "Self-hosters set NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL (see the Dockerfile's build ARG ...)" and lists the consumers as emails, sitemap.xml, robots.txt and canonical/OG tags, which is accurate for the server half but does not cover the 15 client files. .env.example:19 describes the variable as "Used in emails, redirects, and client-side code", which is the part that does not work on the prebuilt image.
findings.impact: On a self-hosted deployment at scanner.example.com, the docs pages, API examples, demo hero and footer shown to that operator's own users all print https://vulnradar.dev, so copied curl commands and links point at the upstream SaaS rather than the operator's instance. For a rebranded GPL fork this is a functional and a branding failure, and it is invisible in the logs.
findings.recommendation: Either pass `build-args: NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` in .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml and tell self-hosters that the prebuilt image is hard-coded to the upstream URL (so they must build locally), or make APP_URL runtime-resolvable for client code: expose it through a server-rendered value in the root layout or an existing runtime-config endpoint and have the 15 client components read that instead of the compile-time constant.

findings.title: About 30 per-probe scanner timeouts are bare 3000/4000/5000/6000 literals with no config entry, and a timed-out probe returns an empty finding array so a slow target silently reports clean
findings.description: lib/scanner/async-checks.ts contains 30 hardcoded per-probe deadlines, counted by pattern: 11 x setTimeout(reject, 4000), 5 x setTimeout(reject, 3000), 1 x setTimeout(reject, 6000), 6 x AbortSignal.timeout(5000), 4 x AbortSignal.timeout(4000), 1 x AbortSignal.timeout(6000), plus timeout: 5000 (:2005) and timeout: 4500 (:2277). lib/scanner/subdomain-discovery-engine.ts adds 11 more (:441 15000, :476-:670 seven at 10000, :708 12000, :858 4000, :869 3000), lib/scanner/checks/tls.ts three more (:136 5000, :268 and :382 4500), lib/scanner/checks/content.ts one (:2287 6000). None of these resolve through lib/config/registry.ts, even though the registry already carries ten scanner deadline settings (SCAN_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS, SCAN_ASYNC_CHECKS_TIMEOUT_MS, SCANNER_ASYNC_BRANCH_TIMEOUT_MS, SCANNER_THREAT_INTEL_API_TIMEOUT_MS, CRAWL_PAGE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS, and friends, registry.ts:1769-1959) that an operator can already edit. The failure mode is the important half: checkMTASTS races dns.resolveTxt against setTimeout(reject, 3000) at :1133-1138, and its catch at :1147-1155 only returns a finding for ENODATA/ENOTFOUND/ENOENT, so the literal string 'timeout' falls through to `return []` at :1154. checkTLSRPT (:1293-1299) has the identical shape. A probe that times out therefore produces no finding and no warning, indistinguishable from a probe that ran and found nothing. Not the same as AUDIT-011#scan-01 (the 15s subdomain cap on the critical path), AUDIT-012#perf-01 (the 5s NVD/OSV calls and the 300s watchdog) or AUDIT-013#dup-01 (the duplicated 10s body-reader timeout); this is the remaining per-check inventory.
findings.impact: A self-hoster scanning a slow, geographically distant, or rate-limiting target loses DNS and TLS checks silently: the scan says the site has no MTA-STS finding rather than saying the check did not complete. That is a false negative on a security scan, presented with full confidence, and the operator has no setting anywhere in the admin panel that can widen the window.
findings.recommendation: Add two registry keys covering the families (a SCANNER_DNS_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS for the setTimeout(reject, N) races and a SCANNER_HTTP_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS for the AbortSignal.timeout(N) fetches), resolve them once per scan in lib/scanner/async-checks.ts and thread them into each probe, and change the catch blocks (async-checks.ts:1147, :1301 and their siblings) to distinguish a timeout from a clean negative so the result carries an explicit 'check did not complete' marker instead of an empty array.

findings.title: The 'delete all scan history' confirmation states a count that is the display cap, not the row count, so a user with 400 scans is told 100 will be deleted and 400 are
findings.description: GET /api/v3/history caps its result with the admin setting HISTORY_LIST_MAX_ROWS (app/api/v3/history/route.ts:111, :128, :139; default CONFIG_HISTORY_LIST_MAX_ROWS = 100 at lib/config/config-values.ts:640) and returns no total count alongside it. app/history/page.tsx:224 fetches that endpoint into `scans` and never learns a row was dropped. Three surfaces then present scans.length as the account total: the page subtitle at :580 ('{scans.length} scans on record'), the summary at :661-:663, and HistoryStats at :588. The worst of the three is the destructive confirmation at :659-:664, which reads 'This deletes all {scans.length} scans on this account, findings and notes included. This cannot be undone.' The DELETE handler it triggers has no LIMIT at all (app/api/v3/history/route.ts:220-222, `DELETE FROM scan_history WHERE user_id = $1 AND (scan_type IS NULL OR scan_type != 'github')`), so it removes every row. The same shape sits on /assets: app/assets/page.tsx:153-:154 renders '{assets.length} distinct hosts you've scanned' over a list built from the same HISTORY_LIST_MAX_ROWS-capped scan query (app/api/v3/assets/route.ts:197-:206), with a second bare literal ALL_HOSTS_MAX = 500 (:105) capping the public scope. Client pagination compounds it: components/ui/pagination-control.tsx:11 offers page sizes up to 100 and app/history/page.tsx:633 passes totalItems={filtered.length}, so the control reports the cap as the truth.
findings.impact: A user on an unlimited-retention plan reads 'This deletes all 100 scans' and loses 400. The number in a one-way destructive confirmation understates its blast radius, which is the one place a number must not be approximate. Separately the Assets inventory, sold as a host inventory, silently omits every host whose last scan is older than the newest 100 scans.
findings.recommendation: Return a `total` (a COUNT(*) over the same WHERE clause, without the LIMIT) from GET /api/v3/history and GET /api/v3/assets, render that in the subtitle and the delete dialog, and pass it as totalItems to PaginationControl. Where the list is genuinely truncated, say so ('showing the 100 most recent of 412') rather than reporting the cap as the total.

findings.title: No visitor can ever scan their own URL without an account: the demo hardcodes window.location.origin, and all ~780 SEO pages funnel their only CTA into it
findings.description: app/demo/page.tsx:30-43 defines handleSelfScan(), which reads `const siteUrl = window.location.origin` at :38 and POSTs that to API.DEMO_SCAN. There is no URL input anywhere in the demo: components/demo/demo-hero.tsx:22-28 resolves the same origin after mount purely to display it as a read-only Target row (:69-72), and the only control is a single Run scan button (:44-53). The server does not impose this. app/api/v3/demo-scan/route.ts:114-133 reads `url` from the request body, accepts any http/https URL, and gates it with checkAccessRules (:136-149), safeFetch with a single-hostname redirect allowlist (:156-166), and an IP rate limit of DEMO_SCAN_LIMIT=5 per DEMO_WINDOW_HOURS=12 (config-values.ts:1029-1030). So the restriction to VulnRadar's own site is a UI decision, not a security control. Meanwhile every organic entry point funnels here: lib/seo/seo-ui.tsx:107-137 ScanCta renders a primary button labelled "Run a free scan" pointing at ROUTES.DEMO, and it is used by app/checks/[id]/page.tsx:343, app/checks/category/[category]/page.tsx, app/checks/page.tsx, app/alternatives/page.tsx, app/alternatives/[competitor]/page.tsx, app/tools/page.tsx, app/tools/api-scanner/page.tsx:148 and app/tools/link-checker/page.tsx, which is roughly 780 pages. app/tools/page.tsx:14 titles that surface "Free Online Security Tools, No Signup" and app/tools/api-scanner/page.tsx:38 answers its own FAQ with "Yes. Paste the API URL and VulnRadar runs the checks", yet neither page contains a single <input> or <form> (verified: zero matches for <input|<form|<Input in both files). The demo's own closing CTA states the problem out loud at components/demo/demo-cta.tsx:21 with the heading "That was our site. Try yours.", and the only button under it is Create a free account. Signup is not a short path either: app/signup/page.tsx:46 tells the user "You get a verification email, then the scanner", so the hosted flow is signup, leave the site, open mail, click, log in, then scan.
findings.impact: This is the single biggest conversion gap in the product. A visitor who arrives from a query like "online api security scanner" reads a page that promises pasting a URL, clicks the one primary button, and lands on a page whose only possible action is scanning vulnradar.dev. The intent that brought them is unserviceable without an email address and an out-of-band verification click, and the free single-URL scanners this product competes with (Security Headers, Mozilla Observatory, SSL Labs) all serve it in one field with no account. Roughly 780 pages of deliberate SEO investment terminate in a dead end.
findings.recommendation: Add a URL field to the demo and keep the self-scan as the secondary story. In components/demo/demo-hero.tsx, replace the read-only Target row with a controlled input plus an authorization checkbox, and in app/demo/page.tsx replace handleSelfScan's `window.location.origin` at :38 with the field value. The server needs no change. Gate abuse with the Turnstile the app already ships plus the existing 5-per-12h IP limit, and satisfy app/legal/acceptable-use/page.tsx:53-55 with a required checkbox rather than by removing the feature. Copy to ship, hero H1: "Scan a URL. No account." Lead: "Paste any URL you are authorized to scan. The full check set runs against it from our servers and the whole report comes back, evidence and fixes included. Five runs per connection, then an account keeps the history." Field label: "URL to scan", placeholder "https://example.com". Checkbox: "I own this site or have written permission to scan it." Secondary button under the field: "Or scan VulnRadar itself", which preserves the existing dogfood flow. Keep components/demo/demo-info.tsx verbatim, it is the strongest trust copy in the repo, and retitle its H2 from "Why we let you scan us" to "We are a target on this page too" so it still reads correctly when the primary target is the visitor's URL. Then change the hero CTA order at components/landing/landing-hero.tsx:83-104: primary becomes "Scan a URL, no account" pointing at ROUTES.DEMO, secondary outline becomes "Create a free account" pointing at ROUTES.SIGNUP.

findings.title: Four marketing surfaces claim scans finish in under 3 seconds while the shipped scan path still awaits a 15s subdomain discovery, so the visitor watches the claim fail on the first scan
findings.description: The under-3-seconds claim is published in five places: app/landing/page.tsx:31 (the page meta description, "get a security report in under 3 seconds"), app/landing/page.tsx:77 (the FAQ answer "Under 3 seconds for a standard scan", which is also emitted as FAQPage structured data via FaqStructuredData at :110), components/landing/landing-hero.tsx:61 (the stat strip entry ["<3s", "per scan"]), components/landing/landing-how-it-works.tsx:46 ("Most scans are done in under three seconds"), and README.md:8. components/landing/landing-api-example.tsx:23 also ships a sample response with "duration": 2841. AUDIT-011#scan-01 established the engine does not meet that on the signed-in path, and the cause is still present: lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:791-795 still awaits autoSubdomainsPromise, capped at 15000ms by lib/scanner/subdomain-auto.ts, and components/scanner/scanning-indicator.tsx:118 still starts the client stopwatch that AUDIT-011#scan-05 measured at 15 to 20 seconds. Verified at those exact lines in the current tree. The only surface where the claim holds is the demo, and only because app/api/v3/demo-scan/route.ts skips subdomain discovery entirely, which means the visitor sees 3 seconds in the demo and 17 seconds on their first real scan.
findings.impact: The product's headline differentiator is contradicted by the product roughly thirty seconds after the visitor reads it, on the first scan they run as a signed-up user. A specific number that turns out to be wrong by 5x is worse than no number, because it teaches the reader that the rest of the page's very specific claims (stable IDs, deterministic severities, real evidence) may be equally decorative. The FAQ answer is also syndicated as FAQPage structured data, so the false number is what an answer engine quotes.
findings.recommendation: Fix the engine, do not soften the copy: AUDIT-011#scan-01 specifies a roughly 10-line change at lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:791-802 and lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:698 that makes every one of these five claims true again. If that will not ship this cycle, remove the number rather than publish a false one. Interim copy: app/landing/page.tsx:31 becomes "Paste a URL and get ${TOTAL_CHECKS_LABEL} deterministic checks back across headers, TLS, cookies, DNS, and secrets. Same URL, same finding IDs, every run. No agent to install." app/landing/page.tsx:75-78 FAQ becomes question "How long does a scan take?" answer "Checks run in parallel rather than in sequence, and the report shows the exact duration for your target. Slow DNS or a long certificate chain is what moves the number." components/landing/landing-hero.tsx:58-63 drops the speed stat and becomes [[checkCount, "checks"], [categoryCount, "categories"], ["0", "models in the detection path"], ["GPL-3.0", "licensed"]], which keeps the mono tabular-nums idiom and swaps the one number the product cannot back for the one differentiator it can. components/landing/landing-how-it-works.tsx:45-49 becomes "Everything runs in parallel, so the wall clock is the slowest module, not the sum of them. The report tells you exactly how long yours took."

findings.title: History search, tag filter, pagination and the "N scans on record" count all operate on a hard 100-row window, so a scan that is still inside retention is unfindable
findings.description: GET /api/v3/history returns at most HISTORY_LIST_MAX_ROWS rows (app/api/v3/history/route.ts:128 and :138, ORDER BY sh.scanned_at DESC LIMIT), and that setting defaults to 100 (lib/config/config-values.ts:640, CONFIG_HISTORY_LIST_MAX_ROWS = 100). app/history/page.tsx:222-236 fetches that one capped page into `scans`, and every user-facing operation then runs client-side over it: the URL search box at :406, the tag filter at :408, usePagination(filtered, pageSize) at :423, and the header count at :580 which renders `{scans.length} scans on record`. The same capped call feeds the Compare host picker (app/compare/page.tsx:40-52), so hosts older than the newest 100 scans never appear there either. Free plan allows 25 scans a day and elite 500, so the window fills in days or hours. Merged from qols-15, filed independently while auditing information hierarchy. Its additional detail: /dashboard shows the true COUNT(*) from the same session, so the two pages disagree with each other about how many scans the account has.
findings.impact: A user who scanned staging.example.com three weeks ago and has run 150 scans since types "staging" into the history search and is told nothing matches, for a scan that exists and is inside their retention window. No message explains that only part of their history was loaded. The count under the History heading also plateaus at 100 permanently and reads as the account's true scan total, so paid users see a number that contradicts their usage. Compare silently cannot diff older hosts for the same reason.
findings.recommendation: Move search, tag filter and pagination server-side. Add `search`, `tag`, `page` and `limit` query params to app/api/v3/history/route.ts and push the substring match into the SQL WHERE clause alongside the existing retention predicate, returning `{ scans, total }`. In app/history/page.tsx replace the client `filtered` computation at :404-410 with a debounced fetch keyed on the filter state, drive usePagination from the server `total`, and source the :580 count from `total` rather than `scans.length`. Do the same for Compare: add GET /api/v3/history/hosts returning host plus scan-count rows so app/compare/page.tsx:40 stops pulling the full list. Until that lands, at minimum render "showing the most recent 100 scans" above the filter row so an empty result is explainable.

findings.title: Rescan in history starts a background job and then shows nothing at all: no progress, no result, no error, and the menu item is never disabled
findings.description: handleRescan (app/history/page.tsx:267-278) POSTs to /api/v3/scan and on res.ok awaits fetchHistory() then clears `rescanning`. But POST /api/v3/scan is a background job that returns { scanId, status: "running" } immediately (app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:443 and :454), so the history refetch fires milliseconds after the job is queued and cannot contain the finished scan. Nothing here polls /api/v3/scan/status/[id], unlike the dashboard which does at app/dashboard/page.tsx:597. The trigger (components/history/history-scan-row.tsx:221-231) is a DropdownMenuItem with no `disabled`, so it stays clickable while `rescanning` is set. Failure is invisible too: there is no !res.ok branch and the bare catch at :276 swallows everything.
findings.impact: The user opens the row menu, clicks Rescan, sees a spinning icon for about a quarter of a second, and the list is identical. Nothing says a scan started, nothing says when it finished, nothing says if it was refused. The rational reaction is to click again, which burns another scan against the daily cap with no warning, and a rate-limit or plan-cap 429 produces exactly the same visible outcome as success.
findings.recommendation: Make Rescan behave like the dashboard's own scan. After the POST, put the returned `scanId` into state and reuse the poll loop from app/dashboard/page.tsx:128-165 (extract pollScanStatus into lib/scanner/poll-scan-status.ts and import it from both), showing the row in a scanning state driven by the server's categoriesCompleted / categoriesTotal, then replace the row in place on completion. Add disabled={rescanning === scan.id} to the DropdownMenuItem at components/history/history-scan-row.tsx:221. Add a !res.ok branch that surfaces data.error, routing the daily-limit case into the PremiumUpgradeModal the dashboard already mounts at app/dashboard/page.tsx:972. The cheaper interim fix is to navigate to /dashboard?scan=<url> on click and let the existing scanning UI own the whole thing.

findings.title: On a phone a history row has no actions at all: rescan, open-URL and view-details are desktop-only, and on desktop the trigger is invisible until hover
findings.description: The entire row action cluster is wrapped in a div classed `hidden sm:flex items-center justify-end w-12 shrink-0` (components/history/history-scan-row.tsx:199), so below 640px the DropdownMenu at :200-242 containing View details, Rescan and Open URL is not rendered at all. The only remaining affordance on a phone is tapping the row body at :80. The severity breakdown (:152) and the source badge (:145) are `hidden sm:flex` too. Above 640px the trigger is `h-8 w-8 p-0 opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100` (:206), so it is invisible until the pointer enters the row, and a touch device never produces a hover.
findings.impact: Rescanning a URL you scanned last week, the most common repeat action in this product, is impossible from a phone. There is no fallback: the mobile row shows no URL-open link and no per-scan menu. Phone users can read history but never act on it. The mobile meta strip at :246 also drops the per-severity counts in favour of a bare findings total, which removes the one signal that decides whether a row is worth opening.
findings.recommendation: Below sm, render a trailing chevron button at h-11 w-11 on each row that opens a Sheet (components/ui/sheet.tsx already exists and today has exactly one consumer, components/scanner/header.tsx:215) listing View details, Rescan, Open URL and Copy URL as full-width 44px rows. Above sm, change :206 from `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100` to `sm:opacity-0 sm:group-hover:opacity-100` so the button is always present on touch, matching what components/shares/shares-row.tsx:118 already gets right. Also surface the worst-severity count on the mobile meta strip so the row still tells you what it found.

findings.title: Every share and privacy mutation fails silently, so a failed "revoke share link" or "make private" is indistinguishable from a successful one
findings.description: Four mutations that change who can see a scan all discard failure. app/shares/page.tsx:121-143 (revoke share link) calls setConfirmRevoke(null) at :124 before the request fires, has no !res.ok branch, and logs to console at :140, so the dialog closes either way and the failure path looks exactly like success minus the row disappearing. app/shares/page.tsx:99-119 (toggle publicly-listed) is console.error only at :117, so on failure the Switch at components/shares/shares-row.tsx:162 silently snaps back. components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:331-349 (make public/private) has no !res.ok branch and a catch commented "Silently fail" at :345. components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:282-307 (create share link) guards on `if (res.ok && data.token)` at :297 with no else, and its catch at :302 is also commented "Silently fail".
findings.impact: A user who clicks Revoke on a share link, confirms, and sees the dialog close believes a public report URL is dead. If the DELETE 500s or 403s the link is still live and still serving their scan. Same shape for Make private: the menu item returns to its previous label with no explanation, so the user cannot tell whether the scan is still feeding the public /host page. A failed share creation looks like a broken button: the item says "Sharing...", reverts to "Share this scan", and no modal appears.
findings.recommendation: Give all four a real failure path: an !res.ok branch that reads data.error, and a catch that surfaces it. The cheapest consistent vehicle is the toast already mounted at app/layout.tsx:195 (see qolf-06). For the revoke specifically, move setConfirmRevoke(null) at app/shares/page.tsx:124 to after a successful response and keep the dialog open showing the error on failure, exactly as app/history/page.tsx:288-290 already does for Clear history. Delete both "Silently fail" comments rather than propagating them: the one at components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:303 cites the old ShareButton as precedent for the behaviour.

findings.title: Saving scan notes and renaming a team both discard the user's text on failure while closing the editor as if it saved
findings.description: handleSaveNotes (app/history/page.tsx:389-397) PATCHes /api/v3/history/{id} and does `if (res.ok) setScanNotes(notes)` with no else and no try/catch anywhere in the chain, so a network failure is an unhandled promise rejection. Its caller components/history/history-notes.tsx:22-27 awaits it then unconditionally runs setSaving(false) and setEditing(false), collapsing the editor. The dashboard copy at app/dashboard/page.tsx:375-387 is the same shape with an explicit `catch { /* ignore */ }`. app/teams/page.tsx:428-456 (rename team) is the only handler on that page with no !res.ok branch, an empty catch at :451, and a finally at :453-456 that closes the name editor regardless.
findings.impact: A user types a paragraph of remediation notes on a scan, clicks Save, the editor closes, and the notes are gone with no message. Because the editor closed, the natural read is that it worked. The team rename case is worse in one respect: on failure the heading snaps back to the old name with no explanation, so a rejected rename (duplicate name, insufficient role) reads as the UI having eaten the edit.
findings.recommendation: Change onSave in components/history/history-notes.tsx to return a boolean and only close the editor on true, keeping the textarea populated and rendering the server error inline underneath on false. In app/history/page.tsx:389 and app/dashboard/page.tsx:375 add the !res.ok branch reading data.error plus a real catch. In app/teams/page.tsx:428 move setEditingName(false) out of the finally into the res.ok branch and route the error into the page's existing actionError banner (declared :78, rendered :515-532), which every other handler on that page already uses.

findings.title: Admin "Run Cleanup Now" deletes rows across the whole database with no confirmation, while resetting a single setting in the same file opens a dialog
findings.description: runCleanup (components/admin/features/system-settings-manager.tsx:371-383) POSTs to /api/v3/admin/cleanup directly from the button's onClick at :605, with no dialog of any kind. The adjacent copy at :597-599 states what it does: it deletes expired keys, old scan history per plan retention, audit logs older than 365 days, and other stale database rows, across every account. In the same component, resetting one system setting back to its default (an action that is undone by simply re-entering the value) does get a full ConfirmDialog at :756, reached from components/admin/features/settings-field.tsx:268. Every other destructive admin action in the repo is gated by either AdminPasswordConfirmDialog or SaveConfirmationModal; this and the staff-invite revoke at components/admin/staff/staff-list.tsx:186 are the only two holes.
findings.impact: The single most destructive control in the product, a database-wide purge affecting every user's scan history, is one mis-click on an unremarkable outline button in a settings panel, and there is no undo (qolf-09). An operator scrolling the system settings page and clicking what looks like a maintenance utility deletes other people's data. The inconsistency makes it worse: because trivial actions on the same page open dialogs, the absence of one here reads as a signal that this button is safe.
findings.recommendation: Wrap runCleanup in the AdminPasswordConfirmDialog (components/admin/shared/admin-password-confirm-dialog.tsx) that already gates delete_scans and delete_user, and have the dialog body render a dry-run count first: add a GET mode to /api/v3/admin/cleanup that returns the row counts it would delete per table, so the operator confirms against real numbers rather than a description. Add the same gate to the staff-invite revoke at components/admin/staff/staff-list.tsx:186. Then remove the ConfirmDialog on reset-to-default at :756, which is buying nothing.

findings.title: /admin is 20 tabs grouped by data model inside one 1,683-line client component, so the three tasks an operator actually performs each cross three to seven of them
findings.description:
The whole admin surface is one client component. `VALID_TABS` (app/admin/page.tsx:112-133) declares 20 destinations, `ActiveTab` (:152-172) repeats the same 20 as a union, and `NAV_GROUPS_RAW` (:689-835) sorts them into 6 groups: User Management (users, teams, admins), Security (access-rules, blocked-data, security-alerts, audit), Communications (broadcast, notifications, ai-chats, support-tickets), Content (content), Billing (billing-overview), System (settings, updater, backup, queue-status, error-logs, email-logs, engine-feedback). Every group name is a data-model noun, not a job. The System group alone holds 7 unrelated destinations that share nothing except not fitting elsewhere: an update installer, a backup runner, a scanner-queue gauge, two log viewers, a settings editor and a detection-tuning tool. Content is a group of one. Billing is a group of one. The panel body is 20 sibling `{activeTab === X && <Manager/>}` lines (:1182-1674) with no route split, and AUDIT-012#fe-11 already measured the cost: 22 eagerly imported managers in one 1,333 KB route. The growth is visible in the leftovers: a 31-entry toast-label map inlined at :530-562, a stale 5-tab table still exported from components/admin/config.ts:7-17 (AUDIT-013#dead-01), and an empty app/api/v3/admin/bulk directory (AUDIT-011#bulk-06).

Measured click cost of the three most common operator tasks today.

A) Resolve a support ticket that needs the requester's account state. 1 click Support in the nav, 2 click the ticket, 3 select and copy the requester email (support-inbox.tsx:253 renders `owner_email` as plain text, no link), 4 click Users in the nav (handleTabChange at :869-876 calls setSelectedUser(null) and rewrites the URL, so the open ticket is gone), 5 click the search box and paste, wait the 300 ms debounce at :599, 6 click the user row, 7 click Support again, 8 click the ticket again to re-read it. Seven clicks plus a copy-paste, and the ticket view is rebuilt from scratch twice.

B) The morning check, is anything wrong right now. The panel lands on `activeTab = "users"` (:203). Scanner Queue is 1 click, Error Logs 2, Security Alerts 3, Backups 4, Email Logs 5, Support 6. Six clicks, six panels that each refetch on mount with their own poll interval, and the operator does the staleness arithmetic on the backup date themselves. Only one of the 20 nav items carries any status indicator at all (the updater dot, :1087-1092).

C) Apply a support fix to one user, for example reset a daily scan limit. Type in the search box, 1 click the row, then scroll past Overview, Account Management, Staff Role and Badges and Admin Notes to reach Support Actions (user-detail-panel.tsx:1872), 2 click the right card out of 21 laid out in a `grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3` (:1894), 3 confirm. Three clicks, but the cost is scanning 21 near-identical cards, not the clicks.
findings.impact: An operator cannot form a mental model of the panel from its navigation, because the navigation describes the database rather than the work. Cross-referencing is the normal case in support and the panel makes it the expensive case: task A costs seven clicks and destroys the operator's place twice. Task B, the one that protects the service, costs six clicks and is therefore skipped, which is how the failures AUDIT-012#obs-02 and AUDIT-012#obs-03 found stay invisible. New destinations get appended to whichever group is least wrong, so the drift compounds.
findings.recommendation:
Regroup by operator job and split the route. Seven sections, 17 destinations, one home.

1. Operations (new default landing, replaces users as the initial tab at app/admin/page.tsx:203). Home view described in qols-02. Children: Scanner Queue, Error Logs, Email Logs, Backups, Updater. This merges the five System-group destinations that are all one question, is the machine healthy.
2. People. Users (search-first, see below), Teams, Staff and Invites (today's Active Staff plus the invite modal from staff-list.tsx).
3. Support. Tickets, AI Chats. Moves ai-chats out of Communications: reading a user's conversation is support and moderation work, not messaging.
4. Trust and Safety. Security Alerts, Access Rules, Blocked Data, Hosts and Shares (today's single-item Content group). Merges four scattered destinations into the one job, deciding what a user or an IP is allowed to do.
5. Billing. Billing Overview, plus a gifted-subscriptions list (today gifts are only visible per-user through user-detail-panel.tsx:2251).
6. Messaging. Broadcast, Notifications. Both are tell users something; today they sit in Communications next to two support tools.
7. Configuration. Settings, Engine Feedback, Audit Log.

Searchable rather than browsable: Users, Audit Log, Error Logs, Email Logs, AI Chats are all logs you query. Users should open on a search field with recent-activity results underneath, not a paginated directory of every account.

Mechanics: give each destination its own route segment under app/admin/(section)/, which deletes the 20-branch conditional at :1182-1674 and fixes AUDIT-012#fe-11 for free. Move the tab table out of app/admin/page.tsx into a single exported ADMIN_SECTIONS in components/admin/config.ts (replacing the stale ADMIN_TABS at config.ts:7-17), keyed by permission exactly as NAV_GROUPS_RAW already does, and derive VALID_TABS, ActiveTab and the mobile TOC from it.

After the restructure: task A becomes 1 click (the requester name in the ticket header opens an inline account panel, see qols-03) with zero navigation. Task B becomes 0 clicks, the home view is the landing page, and a click only to drill into whatever is red. Task C stays 3 clicks; the win there is time-to-find, addressed separately in qols-06.

findings.title: The admin landing view is ten headcount aggregates, none of which can go red, so there is no screen anywhere that answers whether anything is wrong right now
findings.description:
The panel opens on the users tab (app/admin/page.tsx:203) and the only thing above the user table is two StatBar rows of five counters each (:1108-1179): Total Users, Total Scans, Scans 24h, 2FA Enabled, Disabled, New Users 7d, Active API Keys, Active Webhooks, Schedules, Shared Scans. Every one is a plain COUNT from the stats query at app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:329-338. Not one can indicate a fault, and the code comment at app/admin/page.tsx:1103-1107 concedes they are not even clickable because the admin API takes only page, limit and search.

The signals that could go red exist but are each one nav click away and none is summarised anywhere. Scanner backlog: components/admin/features/queue-status-manager.tsx:72 computes `backedUp` and renders a destructive badge at :108-116, but only while that tab is mounted. Backup freshness: backup-manager.tsx:199-201 prints the newest file's mtime as plain text with no expected-interval comparison, so a backup that stopped running three weeks ago looks identical to one that ran this morning apart from a date the operator has to reason about. Security alerts, error logs, email delivery failures and support tickets are the same shape. Of the 20 nav items rendered at :1059-1094 exactly one carries a status indicator: the updater dot at :1087-1092.

This matters because AUDIT-012 found two failures that are silent by construction: #obs-02, a scheduled database backup that fails on every run still reports success to the failure escalator and writes no log line; #obs-03, worker failure escalation only sees pass-level throws, so a worker where every item failed resets its streak to zero and never alerts. Both are precisely the class of fault a health view exists to catch, and neither has any surface in the panel today.
findings.impact: Nobody finds out the service is degraded from the admin panel. Backups can be dead for weeks (obs-02) and the Backups tab will show a stale date that reads as normal. A worker where every item errors (obs-03) shows no signal at all. The scanner queue can be backed up and the operator only learns when a user complains. On a service with about 50 real users and no on-call rotation, the admin panel is the whole monitoring story, and its front page is a vanity dashboard.
findings.recommendation:
Add app/admin/(operations)/page.tsx as the panel's default landing view and change the initial activeTab at app/admin/page.tsx:203 to it. Render one status list, not a card grid: rows of `label / value / state`, each row green, amber or red, ordered worst-first, following the divided-list idiom in design-language.md D4 rather than adding a ninth stat strip. Rows to include, all buildable from endpoints that already exist:

- Scanner queue: reuse computeBackedUp and the stale-age thresholds already in components/admin/features/queue-status-utils.ts (STALE_PENDING_MS, STALE_RUNNING_MS). Red when backed up, amber when the oldest pending scan exceeds the stale threshold.
- Failed scans in the last 24 h: `counts.failedLast24h` from GET /api/v3/admin/queue-status. Amber above zero, red above a configurable share of completed.
- Backup age: from GET /api/v3/admin/backup's lastBackupAt, compared against the configured schedule interval rather than printed raw. Red when older than two intervals. This is the row that would have surfaced AUDIT-012#obs-02.
- Worker last success: add a per-worker last-success timestamp read and show age. This is the row that would have surfaced AUDIT-012#obs-03.
- Unresolved security alerts, error-log volume in the last hour, bounced or failed emails in the last 24 h, open support tickets, outstanding staff invites, update available.

Each row links to the tab that owns it. Mirror the worst state onto the nav item as a coloured dot, reusing the exact markup already at app/admin/page.tsx:1087-1092 so the operator sees a fault from any tab. Keep the ten headcount counters, but demote them to a collapsed Growth strip below the status list or move them to Billing Overview; they answer a business question, not an operational one.

findings.title: Delete the elapsed-seconds clock from the scanning card, and with it the 500ms re-render loop and the fake timer-driven progress it secretly also feeds
findings.description:
This is the executable removal spec for AUDIT-011#scan-05, which filed the problem but conditioned the fix on AUDIT-011#scan-01 landing first. The section brief overrides that: remove the timer regardless. New material below is the full dependency set that scan-05 did not trace.

The clock is four pieces, all still at the lines scan-05 cited. components/scanner/scanning-indicator.tsx:118 seeds `const [startedAt] = useState(() => Date.now())`. :119 holds `elapsed`. :148-151 runs `setInterval(() => setElapsed(Date.now() - startedAt), 500)` for the whole life of the component, forcing a full re-render of the card and its 18-to-20-row checklist twice a second purely to repaint one string. :271-273 renders it through `formatElapsed` (:77-81), which floors to whole seconds, so a displayed `17s` means at least 17.0 real seconds. `formatElapsed` has exactly one call site (verified by grep across app/, components/, lib/, tests/).

The part scan-05 missed: `elapsed` is not only the readout. :157-161 derives `simulatedStep = Math.floor(elapsed / STEP_MS)` and `simulatedSettling`, and :189-193 uses both whenever `hasRealProgress` is false. So deleting only the render at :271-273 leaves a dead 500ms interval and a fabricated progress bar behind it.

`hasRealProgress` (:153) is `categoriesTotal > 0`, which comes from the poll. Two windows where it is false and the bar is therefore pure fiction at STEP_MS = 1200ms per step: (a) every scan's first 0 to 2000ms, because app/api/v3/scan/route.ts computes `categoriesTotal` at :339 and then throws it away, returning only `{ scanId, status: "running" }` at :454, so the client cannot know the denominator until the first poll lands; (b) the entire authenticated-scan path, because app/dashboard/page.tsx:585 gates polling on `if (!auth)`, so `setScanProgress` is never called for a POST to API.SCAN_AUTHENTICATED and `categoriesTotal` stays 0 for the whole run.

On a slow or stalled connection the two failure modes compound: see scanui-05. The bar freezes at its last polled step while the clock keeps counting, which is the worst possible combination of the two signals.
findings.impact: The product's headline claim is speed, and the single number a user watches on every scan contradicts it. Removing the readout alone is not enough: it leaves a twice-a-second re-render of a 20-row list running for the length of every scan, and leaves a progress bar that is honest during a polled scan and invented during the first two seconds of it and for the whole of every authenticated scan, with nothing on screen distinguishing the two.
findings.recommendation:
In components/scanner/scanning-indicator.tsx delete, in this order: the render block at :271-273, `formatElapsed` at :77-81, the `elapsed` state at :119, the interval at :148-151, `startedAt` at :118, and `STEP_MS` at :42 together with `simulatedStep`/`simulatedSettling` at :157-161 and the `else` branch at :189-193.

That leaves `hasRealProgress` needing to be true from the first frame. Make it so with a one-line server change: `app/api/v3/scan/route.ts` already has `categoriesTotal` in hand at :339, so include it in both returns at :442 and :454 (`{ scanId, status: "running", categoriesTotal }`). In app/dashboard/page.tsx `runScan`, seed `setScanProgress({ currentCategory: null, categoriesCompleted: 0, categoriesTotal: data.categoriesTotal ?? 0 })` immediately after `setRunningScanId(scanId)` at :594. Do the same in app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts if it returns the same shape.

The authenticated path has no progress source at all, so do not fake one: pass a new `indeterminate` prop when `auth` is set, and render the family list with no per-row state and the bar as a single `motion-safe:animate-pulse motion-reduce:opacity-100` track, with the line "Signing in, then running every family". An honest indeterminate state is better than a 1200ms-per-step fiction.

Do not replace the clock with the server-reported engine duration on this screen either. `result.duration` already lands on the completed view as the "Scan duration" stat (components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx:303-310), which is the right place for it: a number that appears after the fact reads as a measurement, the same number ticking up during the wait reads as a countdown. What goes in its place is scanui-02.

findings.title: robots.txt Disallows /shared/ and /host/ for every user agent, so Twitter, Facebook and Slack refuse to fetch a shared scan report and it unfurls with no preview at all
findings.description: lib/seo/routes.ts:107 defines DISALLOWED_PATHS, which includes "/shared/" (line 121) and "/host/" (line 122). app/robots.ts:60 spreads that list into the `User-agent: *` group, so the published robots.txt contains `Disallow: /shared/` and `Disallow: /host/` with no exception group. The three biggest link unfurlers all document that they obey robots.txt: X's card crawler (Twitterbot), Facebook's facebookexternalhit, and Slack's Slackbot-LinkExpanding. LinkedInBot and Discordbot behave the same way. The result is that the two URL shapes the product exists to have people share are the exact two shapes those fetchers are told not to touch. Indexing is already prevented independently: app/shared/[token]/layout.tsx:7 and app/host/[hostname]/layout.tsx:8 both call privatePageMetadata(), which emits `noindex, nofollow, nocache` (lib/seo/metadata.ts:85). So the robots.txt Disallow is doing a job the meta tag already does, and paying for it with the previews. The correct split is the standard one: robots.txt governs crawling, the robots meta tag governs indexing.
findings.impact: Sharing a scan report is a core, documented feature (app/docs/sharing/page.tsx) and the primary way this product could spread. Today a user pastes a /shared/<token> or /host/<hostname> link into Slack, X, LinkedIn or Facebook and gets a bare blue link with no title, no image and no description, because the fetcher reads robots.txt first and stops. Not a weak preview: no preview. Every share is a link that looks broken, which suppresses click-through on exactly the traffic the product gets for free.
findings.recommendation: In app/robots.ts, add a fourth rule group before the wildcard group for the link unfurlers: `{ userAgent: ["Twitterbot", "facebookexternalhit", "Slackbot-LinkExpanding", "Slackbot", "Discordbot", "LinkedInBot", "TelegramBot", "WhatsApp", "redditbot", "Iframely"], allow: "/", disallow: [...DISALLOWED_PATHS.filter(p => p !== "/shared/" && p !== "/host/"), ...QUERY_DISALLOW] }`. Keep /shared/ and /host/ in the wildcard group's Disallow and keep the noindex meta on both pages: indexing stays blocked by the meta tag, which is the mechanism that actually controls it. Pair this with seo-02 so the preview that now renders is worth rendering.

findings.title: ScanResult.incomplete is captured, persisted and typed on every surface but rendered by nothing, so a scan whose DNS/TLS/live-fetch branch timed out tells the user "every enabled check ran and none of them fired"
findings.description: The scanner records which async branches did not finish. lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:4651-4656 builds `incomplete[]` from every branch whose `timedOut` flag is set; lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:746 reads it and :846 writes `...(incomplete.length > 0 ? { incomplete } : {})` into scan_history.result_meta. It survives the whole read path: lib/scanner/types.ts:258 declares it on ScanResult, lib/scanner/history-detail.ts:21 declares it on the API response and :71 maps it back onto ScanResult, app/api/v3/host/[hostname]/route.ts:41 returns it, and app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:113 explicitly threads it into the ScanResult it builds. Grepping `incomplete` across app/, components/, lib/ and extension/src returns not one JSX or template reference: no component reads the field. The declaration's own doc comment (lib/scanner/types.ts:251-257) states the contract it is violating verbatim: "A category listed here means 'not checked', not 'checked and clean': the UI should say so rather than treat a missing finding from that area as a clean result." What the user gets instead, when for example the DNS and TLS branches both time out on a slow resolver: components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx:197 calls getSafetyRating(result.findings), zero remaining findings resolves to VERDICT.safe, and :45-52 prints "Nothing exploitable found". Below it, components/scanner/scan-result-detail.tsx:220 sees findings.length === 0 and renders :228-235, "Nothing found on this scan / Every enabled check ran against this host and none of them fired." On the dashboard the override at components/scanner/dashboard-results.tsx:268-287 says the same thing louder: "Zero findings on this host / Every enabled check ran and none of them fired." The only trace of the truth anywhere on screen is the "Engine confidence" stat (scan-summary.tsx:295-302) dropping from 97% to 94% (lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts:368), an unexplained three-point difference in an unlabelled number.
findings.impact: This is the single most damaging failure in this class for a security scanner: a partially failed scan is presented as a clean bill of health, with an explicit sentence asserting that every check ran. A user whose TLS branch timed out reads "Nothing exploitable found" and ships. The same result feeds the public /host/[hostname] page and read-only /shared/[token] links, so the false all-clear is what a third party sees too, and the danger score and severity distribution are computed from the same truncated finding set. The data needed to prevent this is already in the database on every affected scan.
findings.recommendation: Render `result.incomplete` in components/scanner/scan-result-detail.tsx, above ScanSummary (:142) so it is read before the verdict, using the same warning block already built for `result.redirect` at :120-140 (border-[hsl(var(--warning))]/25 bg-[hsl(var(--warning))]/5, AlertTriangle, title plus reason plus mono detail line). Copy in the house voice: title "Part of this scan did not finish", body "The DNS and TLS checks ran out of time, so nothing from those areas was checked. This report is not a clean result for them, it is a gap. Rescan to fill it in." with the branch labels rendered as the mono detail line. Then gate the zero-findings block: when `incomplete` is non-empty, replace both empty-state copies (scan-result-detail.tsx:228-235 and dashboard-results.tsx:268-287) with "No findings from the checks that completed" and drop the "Every enabled check ran" sentence, which is false in that case. Suppress VERDICT.safe's "Nothing exploitable found" headline the same way in components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx:197, since getSafetyRating cannot distinguish a clean scan from a truncated one.

findings.title: An async check branch that throws is recorded as complete, so a crashed DNS or TLS branch produces zero findings, an empty incomplete[] and full engine confidence
findings.description: boundedBranch (lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:4428-4458) wraps each of the three async branches. Its success handler at :4441 returns `{ label, findings, timedOut: false }`; its rejection handler at :4442 returns `{ label, findings: NO_FINDINGS, timedOut: false }`. The timeout racer at :4453 is the only path that sets `timedOut: true`. runAsyncChecksDetailed then builds the incompleteness report from that flag alone (:4652-4655: `if (r.value.timedOut) incomplete.push(r.value.label)`). So a branch that rejects, a DNS resolver error, a TLS socket error, an unhandled exception anywhere inside the branch, is indistinguishable at that layer from a branch that ran to completion and found nothing. The in-code comment at :4438-4439 states the intent as "A rejecting branch contributes no findings, same as a timed-out one", but a timed-out one at least sets the flag and a rejecting one does not. Downstream that means lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:746-750 computes `getEngineConfidence(findings, asyncTimedOut || incomplete.length > 0)` with both operands false, so lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts:368 uses the full base of 97 rather than 94, and :846 writes no `incomplete` key at all. This is the same bug class AUDIT-012#obs-01 filed for per-check exceptions inside runSyncChecks (lib/scanner/engine.ts:172), but at whole-branch granularity and with the extra bite that the mechanism specifically built to report incompleteness is bypassed rather than merely unlogged.
findings.impact: A permanently broken or transiently failing DNS/TLS/live-fetch branch reports the strongest possible result the product can produce: no findings from that area, no incompleteness marker, and 97% engine confidence. On a self-host with no outbound DNS, or an instance where one branch throws on a particular input shape, every scan reads as a clean TLS and DNS posture forever. Because the failure sets no flag, even the fix in state-01 would not surface it, and there is no log line either (obs-01), so nobody can find out from either side.
findings.recommendation: Change the rejection handler at lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:4442 to `() => ({ label, findings: NO_FINDINGS, timedOut: true })`, or better, add a distinct `failed: true` field and push the label into `incomplete` for both cases, so "timed out" and "crashed" are separable in result_meta while both reaching the UI as "not checked". Log the rejection reason with the branch label at the same point, which is what obs-01 asks for. The UI change is then free: the block proposed in state-01 already renders whatever is in `incomplete`.

findings.title: Deep (crawl) scans structurally cannot report incompleteness: the async layer is raced against a 15s timer that resolves to an empty array, and engine confidence is hardcoded to the complete value
findings.description: The crawl executor takes the bookkeeping-free path everywhere. lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:17 imports `runAsyncChecks`, not `runAsyncChecksDetailed`, whose own doc comment at lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:4617-4620 says "Use this from a route that surfaces scan completeness to the user; runAsyncChecks below is the same work without that bookkeeping". The crawl result is surfaced to the user through the exact same components as a single scan (app/dashboard/page.tsx:640-649 maps crawl.pages[0] straight into the ScanResult that DashboardResults renders). Then :203-217 races that call against `new Promise(resolve => { asyncTimeoutHandle = setTimeout(() => resolve([]), 15000) })`, so when the 15 second ceiling wins, every DNS, TLS and live-fetch finding for that page is silently replaced by an empty array with no record that it happened. Finally :747 hardcodes `engineConfidence: getEngineConfidence(allFindings, false)`, passing `false` for asyncTimedOut unconditionally, and the crawl's result_meta (:747-757) never writes an `incomplete` key at any point. Grepping `incomplete` in execute-crawl-scan.ts returns nothing.
findings.impact: Deep scan is the paid, slower, more thorough mode, and it is the one mode that cannot tell the user when it came back short. A crawl of a site with slow DNS or a slow TLS handshake reports zero TLS and DNS findings alongside "97%" engine confidence and the "Nothing exploitable found" verdict, with no timeout marker anywhere in the stored record. Because the 15 second ceiling is per page, a multi-page crawl silently drops a different subset of checks on each page, so the same crawl re-run produces different findings with no explanation, which breaks the product's headline promise that the same URL produces the same result.
findings.recommendation: In lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts switch line 17 and 206 to `runAsyncChecksDetailed`, collect the per-page `incomplete` labels alongside `findings`, union them across pages, pass the union's non-emptiness as the second argument to getEngineConfidence at :747 instead of the literal `false`, and write `...(incomplete.length > 0 ? { incomplete } : {})` into the result_meta at :747-757 exactly as lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:846 does. The outer 15s race at :203-217 should resolve to a sentinel that marks the page incomplete rather than to `[]`, so a timed-out page is never mistaken for a page with nothing to report. The UI then needs no further change once state-01 lands.

findings.title: Two loaders in the repo detail view skip setLoading(false) on the non-ok branch, so an API error leaves a permanent skeleton and makes the correctly written error and empty states unreachable
findings.description: components/repos/repo-detail.tsx has the best state ladder in the repo, :242-255 renders skeleton, then loadError, then empty, then data, and both of its loaders defeat it. `loadScans` (:85-102) sets `setLoadingScans(true)` at :86, parses the body at :92, and on `!res.ok` at :93-96 sets loadError and `return`s. There is no `finally`; `setLoadingScans(false)` is at :101, after the try/catch, so the early return skips it. `loadingScans` stays true forever, and the render at :242 checks `loadingScans` before `loadError`, so the error message that was just set can never be shown: the three Skeleton bars at :243-247 render indefinitely. `loadScanDetail` (:113-129) repeats it exactly: `setDetailLoading(true)` at :116, `if (!res.ok) { setScanDetail(null); return; }` at :119-122, and `setDetailLoading(false)` at :128 after the try/catch.
