findings.description: app/docs/api/page.tsx:1299 publishes the CI/CD integration snippet as `- uses: ${APP_REPO}/.github/actions/scan-gate@main`, and lib/ai/system-prompt.ts:397 gives the AI assistant the same snippet to hand out, with `api-key: ${{ secrets.VULNRADAR_TOKEN }}` right underneath. .github/actions/scan-gate/action.yml is a composite action whose only step is a `shell: bash` block (lines 76-183), so every consumer runs shell from VulnRadar's default branch at job time. That branch has no protection and no required checks (ci-02) and accepts unreviewed auto-merged dependency bumps (ci-03). Meanwhile every third-party action in this repo's own workflows is pinned by commit SHA (verified: all 23 `uses:` lines carry a 40-hex SHA), so the project applies to itself the standard it does not publish to its users. There is also no ref a consumer could safely pin to instead: all 65 tags are `vX.Y.Z` application releases whose content moves under the action, and no workflow in this repo ever calls the action, so it is entirely untested.
findings.impact: A single push to VulnRadar's main runs immediately in every downstream consumer's CI job, with that job's full secret set and write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN, not merely their VulnRadar API key. For a security vendor shipping a supply-chain-relevant action this is the exact misconfiguration the product is sold to detect. The action being untested also means a change to POST /api/v3/scan's response shape breaks every consumer's pipeline with no signal here.
findings.recommendation: Cut a dedicated moving major tag for the action (`v1`) that only advances after review, update app/docs/api/page.tsx:1299 and lib/ai/system-prompt.ts:397 to `scan-gate@v1` with a note that a SHA pin is stronger, and add a job to ci.yml that runs the action against a known target so its contract is exercised. Fixing ci-02 is a prerequisite for `@main` or `@v1` being trustworthy at all.

findings.title: There is no deploy pipeline, no migration step ordered ahead of new code, and no rollback procedure documented anywhere
findings.description: No workflow in .github/workflows/ deploys anything: ci.yml validates, docker-publish.yml pushes an image on a tag, release.yml attaches artifacts, and the remaining three are housekeeping. The documented upgrade for a self-hoster is app/docs/setup/page.tsx:684, `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`, with no migration step at all. Schema changes are applied by instrumentation.ts at process boot, which is after the new image is already the running container and is serving traffic, so there is no point at which the schema is advanced while the old code is still live. `npm run db:migrate` is mentioned once at app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:547 and again inside an error remediation string at line 570, and per AUDIT-014#host-02 the migrate script is not even present in the published image. Grepping app/docs/, README.md and SECURITY.md for `rollback`, `roll back`, `revert` and `previous version` returns nothing: there is no documented way back. AUDIT-013#migrate-01 established the versioned upgrade path is already missing 11 tables and 8 columns relative to what instrumentation.ts creates, and AUDIT-013#migrate-04 that `db:restore` pipes into psql without `ON_ERROR_STOP`, so the recovery tooling is itself unreliable.
findings.impact: An operator whose upgrade fails at boot (which per AUDIT-014#host-01 is the default on a fresh database) has a crash-looping container, a database that may have been partially altered by the new image's boot DDL, no migrate script inside the image to inspect or re-run, and no documented rollback. Reverting the compose tag is not obviously safe because the old code may not tolerate whatever schema the new boot already applied, and nothing tells the operator that.
findings.recommendation: Add an Upgrading section to app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx that (1) tells the operator to run `npm run db:backup` before pulling, (2) documents `db:migrate` as a distinct step run before the new container takes traffic, and (3) states plainly which schema changes are backward compatible and how to pin back to the previous version tag. Ship scripts/ in the image (AUDIT-014#host-02) so the documented commands are runnable, and state the supported downgrade window.

findings.title: The GitHub Action gate stops at severity counts and never uploads the SARIF the API already produces, so findings never reach the Security tab that ZAP, Nuclei and Snyk actions all populate
findings.description: The composite action at .github/actions/scan-gate/action.yml is complete and correct: it starts a scan, polls GET /scan/status, and at :152 to :176 reads only summary.critical/high/medium/low/total, writes a step summary table, and exits 1 on threshold breach. It never fetches SARIF. A full SARIF 2.1.0 generator already exists at lib/reports/sarif-report.ts:1 and is exposed as GET /api/v3/history/[id]/report?format=sarif (app/api/v3/history/[id]/report/route.ts:174), and app/docs/reports/page.tsx:310 to :319 already publishes the exact two-step recipe (curl the SARIF, then github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3) as something the user must hand-assemble. The action already emits scan-id as an output (.github/actions/scan-gate/action.yml:45), so the two halves are one curl apart. Separately, the action lives at .github/actions/scan-gate/ inside the app repo, which is not a GitHub Marketplace-publishable location: Marketplace requires action.yml at the root of its own repository plus a tagged release. ZAP ships official Marketplace actions, Nuclei ships one, and Snyk and Burp both list Actions integrations (audits/AUDIT-014/research-competitors.md, ZAP and Nuclei sections).
findings.impact: A developer wiring VulnRadar into CI gets a red X and a markdown table, while the equivalent ZAP or Nuclei action gets them annotated Code Scanning alerts inline on the pull-request diff, with dismissal and tracking handled by GitHub. That is the difference between a gate people keep and a gate people delete after the second false alarm. And because the action is not on the Marketplace, the highest-intent discovery channel for this product (a developer searching the Actions marketplace for "security scan") returns nothing.
findings.recommendation: Two changes, both small. First, in .github/actions/scan-gate/action.yml add an optional `sarif-file` input (default `vulnradar.sarif`); after the poll loop succeeds, curl `$VR_API_BASE/history/$scan_id/report?format=sarif` to that path and add a `sarif-file` output, then document the follow-on `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif` step in app/docs/api/page.tsx:1299's snippet so the published example is the complete one. Second, mirror the action into a dedicated `VulnRadar/scan-gate-action` repo with action.yml at the root and a v1 tag, publish it to the Marketplace, and change the `uses:` in app/docs/api/page.tsx:1299 from the current `${APP_REPO}/.github/actions/scan-gate@main` (an unpinned branch reference) to `VulnRadar/scan-gate-action@v1`.

findings.title: There is no overall A+ to F grade, so the badge and public host report speak safe/caution/unsafe and cannot occupy the vocabulary SecurityHeaders.com just vacated
findings.category: list (a) gap rank 3: the grading vocabulary and the badge flywheel
findings.description: Four of the free peers grade a whole site on one A+ to F scale: MDN HTTP Observatory (A+ down to F, ten header tests), SecurityHeaders.com (A+ to F on response headers), Qualys SSL Labs (A+ to F plus T and M), and ImmuniWeb (grade-gated PDF certificate plus installable badge). VulnRadar has the scoring machinery but not the vocabulary. lib/scanner/ssl-grade.ts:1 already computes a real SSL-Labs-style A+/A/B/C/D/F letter, but only for the TLS handshake. The whole-scan verdict is a three-state safety rating (lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts:19, "safe" | "caution" | "unsafe") plus a 0-10 danger score (:306), and the embeddable badge renders exactly that three-state label (app/api/v3/badge/[token]/route.ts:99 to :115). Confirmed live this session: Snyk shut down the securityheaders.com API in April 2026 (announced January 2026), leaving only the free web scanner; the replacements ranking for "securityheaders alternative" are unknown micro-vendors (WebAudit, Guardr, detectzestack, myssl.info, sitesecurityscore). SSL Labs v4 requires an organizational email and forbids commercial use by default, and MDN Observatory dropped TLS entirely in October 2024. The auto-updating badge infrastructure already exists and is idempotent per (user, url) so an embed never breaks (app/api/v3/badge/site/route.ts:8).
findings.impact: A README badge that says "caution" is a liability the owner removes; a badge that says "A" is a trophy the owner keeps and that links back. ImmuniWeb built 380M+ scans on exactly that mechanic and gates the certificate on the grade so people work to earn it. VulnRadar has the badge, the public host page, the API, and TLS plus DNS plus header coverage that the vacated SecurityHeaders niche wants, and cannot be compared against the incumbent because it does not speak the incumbent's scale.
findings.recommendation: Add `getSiteGrade(findings): "A+"|"A"|"B"|"C"|"D"|"F"` to lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts, derived from the existing danger score and severity weights so it stays deterministic and needs no new detection work, and document the exact deduction table on a public page the way lib/scanner/ssl-grade.ts:20 already documents its own. Render the grade as the primary label in app/api/v3/badge/[token]/route.ts:99 (keep safe/caution/unsafe as the badge's secondary colour semantics), lead with it on app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx, and gate the shareable badge on B or better, matching ImmuniWeb. Then publish a keyless or free-key-tier grading endpoint documented in app/docs/api as the drop-in for the dead securityheaders.com API, using the existing demo-scan rate-limit shape (app/api/v3/demo-scan/route.ts:97) rather than the account-gated /api/v3/scan.

findings.title: The /alternatives set names five competitors, one of which stopped existing as a standalone product in November 2024, and omits every free-tool and open-source peer the product actually competes with
findings.description: lib/seo/alternatives.ts:53 defines exactly five entries: intelliradar (:55), detectify (:108), intruder (:162), probely (:215) and qualys (:268). Each renders a public page at /alternatives/<slug> (app/alternatives/[competitor]/page.tsx:18) and is listed in lib/seo/routes.ts:72. Two problems. First, the Probely entry at :215 to :266 describes Probely in the present tense as an independent commercial vendor; Probely was acquired by Snyk on 12 November 2024 and relaunched as "Snyk API and Web" on 22 April 2025, with help.probely.com now titled "Snyk API and Web Help Center" (audits/AUDIT-014/research-competitors-commercial.md, Probely section, verified live). Second, the set is aimed entirely at commercial DAST vendors the product does not realistically win against on features, and contains none of the peers it actually shares a shape with: SecurityHeaders.com, MDN HTTP Observatory, SSL Labs, ImmuniWeb, OWASP ZAP, Nuclei, or the cheapest credible paid entries (Pentest-Tools.com from $95/mo, Astra from $69/mo). The one entry with no real competitor behind it, "IntelliRadar" (:55), is filler whose comparison rows all say "Varies by product" (:66, :72, :76, :81, :87).
findings.impact: A live public page tells visitors to compare VulnRadar against a product that no longer sells under that name, which is the kind of staleness that gets screenshotted and undermines the page's own stated ground rule at lib/seo/alternatives.ts:1 to :13 that only defensible facts appear. Meanwhile the highest-intent search terms available right now, "securityheaders.com alternative" and "securityheaders api alternative" (a well-known free API that died four months ago, with only unknown micro-vendors ranking), have no page at all.
findings.recommendation: In lib/seo/alternatives.ts: rename the probely entry to slug "snyk" / name "Snyk API and Web", note the Probely lineage in one sentence of `summary`, and keep /alternatives/probely alive as a redirect so existing links and sitemap entries do not 404. Delete or replace the intelliradar entry, whose rows carry no information. Add entries for securityheaders (lead with: the API shut down in April 2026, VulnRadar's covers headers plus TLS plus DNS plus cookies in one call), mozilla-observatory (lead with: dropped TLS entirely in October 2024), ssl-labs (lead with: v4 requires a corporate email and forbids commercial use, VulnRadar computes its own grade in lib/scanner/ssl-grade.ts), owasp-zap and nuclei (be honest: they send deeper payloads, VulnRadar is the hosted zero-setup path with a public check catalog), and pentest-tools (the closest analogue in shape, and the cheapest credible paid rival at $95/mo against VulnRadar's $5 to $20).

findings.title: Authenticated scanning ships form, header and cookie login but no recorded multi-step sequence, no TOTP, no SSO/OIDC login, and no re-authentication when the target drops the session mid-scan
findings.category: list (a) gap rank 5: authenticated scanning, narrowed against the code
findings.description: The research called authenticated scanning the single biggest gap and flagged it for verification. Verified in code, the gap is much narrower than that. lib/scanner/auth/types.ts:13 declares `ScanAuthType = "form" | "header" | "cookie"`, all three are implemented (lib/scanner/auth/login.ts, lib/scanner/auth/browser-login.ts), and the form path is better than a naive implementation: it opens a real headless browser session to render a client-side login form before parsing it (lib/scanner/auth/browser-login.ts:1 to :27). POST /api/v3/scan/authenticated exists (app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts:56), the session is origin-bound with a logout guard (lib/scanner/auth/scan-session.ts:104 to :113), and the crawl engine reports the auth state back. What is genuinely absent: (1) multi-step or recorded login sequences, a browser-recorder capture of the click path (Detectify ships a Chrome recorder, Astra uses Chrome DevTools Recorder, Pentest-Tools and Acunetix both ship a login sequence recorder, Snyk supports recorded sequences); (2) TOTP or OTP second factor, which Astra and Snyk both handle and Acunetix explicitly claims for MFA and CAPTCHA; (3) SSO or OpenID Connect login flows, which only Snyk supports; (4) automatic re-authentication when the session dies mid-scan. On (4), lib/scanner/auth/scan-session.ts:86 `markLost()` records the loss and :116 to :154 detects all three loss signals (cleared session cookie, 401/403, redirect back to the login path), but nothing ever calls establishScanSession again: a grep for re-auth, reauth, relogin across lib/scanner/ and app/api/v3/scan/ returns zero hits. Snyk is the only one of the eight with automatic re-auth mid-scan.
findings.impact: For this product's users (developers scanning their own staging app behind a login) the practical bite is ordered opposite to the market's marketing. Item (4) costs users today: a long crawl of a session-expiring app silently degrades to an anonymous scan partway through and reports status "lost", so the user pays a scan against their daily quota and gets a partial result they must re-run by hand. Items (1) to (3) cost the product a specific class of prospect (SPAs with a multi-screen login, any team with 2FA enforced on staging) but each is expensive to build and none is a same-day fix.
findings.recommendation: Build (4) first, alone: it is the smallest change and the only one costing users today. In lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts, when the binding reports `lost`, call `establishScanSession` once more with the same EphemeralAuthInput held in memory for that request, cap re-auth at two attempts per scan, and record the count in ScanAuthReport (lib/scanner/auth/types.ts:85) so the result says "re-authenticated once" rather than "lost". Then add TOTP as (2): it is a `totpSecret` field on EphemeralFormAuth (lib/scanner/auth/types.ts:21), an otpauth-style code generator, and one extra form submit in lib/scanner/auth/browser-login.ts, and it unlocks every target with authenticator-app 2FA. Defer (1) recorded sequences and (3) SSO: a recorder needs a browser extension capture format, a step-replay engine on top of the BrowserBase CDP path, and stored (not ephemeral) sequence definitions, which contradicts the deliberate never-persisted credential model documented at lib/scanner/auth/types.ts:1 to :10. That model is itself an advantage worth keeping; see comp-10.

findings.title: SARIF ships but nothing connects it to DefectDojo or Faraday, the two open-source vulnerability managers this product's self-hosting users already run
findings.category: list (a) gap rank 6: OSS ecosystem interop
findings.description: DefectDojo (4,911 stars, BSD-3-Clause, 500+ report parsers, actively pushed 2026-08-29) is the layer OSS-first teams aggregate scanners into, and it already parses ZAP, Nuclei, Trivy, Nikto, Burp, SSL Labs and Wapiti; Faraday (6,697 stars, GPL-3.0, 80+ tool plugins) is the same shape (audits/AUDIT-014/research-competitors.md, DefectDojo and Faraday sections, both verified live). VulnRadar already emits everything such a parser needs: a complete SARIF 2.1.0 report with per-rule descriptors, security-severity, tags and helpUri (lib/reports/sarif-report.ts:1 to :253), reachable over the API at GET /api/v3/history/[id]/report?format=sarif (app/api/v3/history/[id]/report/route.ts:174). Nothing in the repo, the docs (app/docs/reports/page.tsx), or .github/ mentions DefectDojo, Faraday, or any vulnerability-management destination. The word appears nowhere in the codebase.
findings.impact: The self-hosting, GPL, small-security-team audience is precisely the DefectDojo audience, and it is also the audience most likely to install a second scanner rather than switch. Being absent from the 500-parser list means VulnRadar is the one tool in their stack whose findings have to be moved by hand, which is how a tool gets dropped at the next cleanup.
findings.recommendation: Two cheap moves. First, add a "Send findings to DefectDojo" subsection to app/docs/reports/page.tsx next to the existing SARIF and CI section (:279), showing the curl that pulls SARIF and POSTs it to DefectDojo's /api/v2/import-scan/ endpoint with scan_type=SARIF, which already works today with zero code change. Second, open a parser PR upstream to DefectDojo (a ~150-line Python parser plus fixtures) that reads VulnRadar's native JSON export so the tool is named in their supported list; that listing is a durable discovery channel that costs one afternoon.

findings.title: The 750 public check pages have no contribute-a-check path, leaving the one moat a GPL scanner can actually build (the nuclei-templates model) unstarted
findings.category: list (a) gap rank 7 and list (b): the community check catalog
findings.description: nuclei-templates carries roughly 11,997 template files across 873 directories with daily commits, a formal Pioneers program, and template bounties; that community, not the binary, is the moat none of the commercial eight have (audits/AUDIT-014/research-competitors.md, Nuclei section, verified live). VulnRadar has the raw material: a per-category registry with static JSON check definitions (lib/scanner/registry.ts:23 to :40, 18 categories), a public page per check, and an index at app/checks/page.tsx:75 whose own copy says "Not a marketing number: every one is a real page that tells you what it catches". It also already has a well-designed Scanner Detector Proposal issue template (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/detector.md:1) asking for threat model, detection strategy, false-positive risk and test fixtures. None of that is connected: grep for "detector.md", "Propose" or "contribute" across app/checks/ and components/checks/ returns zero hits, so no visitor to any of the ~750 pages is ever told a check can be proposed. AGENTS.md:140 to :167 documents the add-a-check procedure for maintainers only, and CONTRIBUTING.md (56 lines) never mentions checks at all.
findings.impact: The check catalog is simultaneously the main organic SEO surface and the only asset that compounds without headcount, and it currently converts zero readers into contributors. A security-minded reader who lands on a check page from a search, spots a gap, and finds no way in leaves. Every commercial peer's detection set is closed; VulnRadar's is open and unadvertised, which is the worst of both.
findings.recommendation: Add a persistent block to app/checks/page.tsx below the category accordion (:140) and to the bottom of app/checks/[id]/page.tsx: a two-line pitch plus a direct link to the prefilled issue template at https://github.com/{APP_REPO}/issues/new?template=detector.md, and a link to a new app/docs/developers section that walks the actual change (add a def to lib/scanner/checks-data/<category>.json, add a detector to lib/scanner/checks/<category>.ts, run scripts/find-duplicate-ids.mjs). Add a `contributor` field to the CheckDef schema at lib/scanner/registry.ts:82 and credit it on the check page, which is what makes a first contribution feel worth the pull request. Then put the live count on the landing page as a growth number rather than a static one: "{N} checks, {M} contributed by people who are not us."

findings.title: Ticketing stops at one one-way GitHub issue holding up to 50 findings, with no per-finding issue, no close-the-loop retest, and no Jira or Linear
findings.category: list (a) gap rank 8: issue tracker integration
findings.description: Jira is universal across all eight commercial vendors, Slack near-universal, and the real differentiator is two-way sync: Detectify's Jira integration updates the finding when the ticket is resolved, and Probely/Snyk goes further, marking the Jira issue Done automatically triggers a retest of that finding. Linear appears only at Intruder (audits/AUDIT-014/research-competitors-commercial.md, "Table stakes" item 2). VulnRadar's entire ticketing surface is POST /api/v3/scan/github-issue (app/api/v3/scan/github-issue/route.ts:11), which files one issue per scan into one repo, listing at most 50 findings in the body (`MAX_FINDINGS_LISTED = 50`, :26). It is one-way and one-shot: nothing reads the issue's state back, nothing closes it when a rescan shows the finding gone, and there is no per-finding issue so no finding has its own trackable ticket. Notification delivery is limited to Discord, Slack and generic webhooks (lib/webhooks/detect-type.ts:7 to :14) plus email; there is no Jira, Linear, ServiceNow or Teams destination anywhere in lib/.
findings.impact: For the developer this product targets, a single 50-item issue is a dump, not a workflow: it cannot be assigned, prioritised, or closed piecemeal, and once one finding is fixed the issue is stale but still open. For the small security team, the absence of any close-the-loop mechanism means the remediation state lives only inside VulnRadar (lib/scanner/remediation-store.ts) and inside the tracker separately, and the two drift.
findings.recommendation: Do not start with Jira. The GitHub connection already exists, is already authorised for issue writes (lib/github/github-connections.ts), and the finding IDs are already stable across runs (lib/scanner/_helpers.ts generateId, `<checkId>--<urlHash>`), which is exactly what a close-the-loop integration needs and what Jira would still need built. Extend app/api/v3/scan/github-issue/route.ts with a per-finding mode: one issue per finding, titled with the check id, labelled by severity, and stamped with the stable finding id in the body. Then in lib/scanner/regression-alert.ts, which already diffs a completed scan against the previous scan of the same URL by that same id, close any tracked issue whose finding is absent from the new scan and post a one-line comment saying which scan proved it fixed. That is the Probely/Snyk retest loop, built on machinery that already exists. Add Jira only if a paying user asks for it by name.

findings.title: SARIF export and the six-framework compliance crosswalk are shipped, complete, and free on every tier, and neither is mentioned anywhere on the landing page or in any /alternatives comparison row
findings.category: list (b): the strongest shipped feature nobody is told about
findings.description: Two features exist in full and are invisible in marketing. (1) SARIF 2.1.0 export: lib/reports/sarif-report.ts:1 to :253, wired into both the client export menu (components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:556) and the API (app/api/v3/history/[id]/report/route.ts:174). (2) A compliance crosswalk mapping findings to PCI DSS 4.0, SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A, OWASP ASVS 4.0, HIPAA and GDPR, built on a documented OWASP-Top-10 backbone with an explicit "Unmapped findings" honesty section rather than force-fitting (lib/reports/compliance-mappings.ts:1 to :80, rendered by lib/reports/compliance-report.ts). Against the researched set this is genuinely differentiated: Burp Suite DAST has no compliance framework mapping at all, which the research calls a real hole in the strongest-in-class product; Snyk paywalls DAST entirely to the Ignite tier at roughly $1,260/yr per developer; compliance views are otherwise standard only at Intruder, Astra, Snyk and Invicti, all of which are enterprise-priced. Yet the shared VulnRadar answers used by every /alternatives table (lib/seo/alternatives.ts:44 to :51) list only licensing, hosting, pricing, onboarding and engine parity, and the API-and-CI row at :240 says only "REST API, webhooks, and CI-friendly scans on every tier". The landing page never uses the words SARIF, PCI, SOC 2 or ISO 27001: app/landing/page.tsx's FAQ and all eleven components/landing/*.tsx files omit them entirely.
findings.impact: The product ships, at $0, two of the exact artifacts that make an enterprise scanner purchasable, and asks visitors to infer them. "I need a SOC 2 evidence artifact" and "I need findings in the GitHub Security tab" are two of the highest-intent reasons anyone shops for a scanner at all, and neither search term has anywhere to land on this site outside the docs.
findings.recommendation: Add two rows to the shared VR object in lib/seo/alternatives.ts:44: `reports: "SARIF 2.1.0, PDF, Markdown, and a PCI DSS / SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / ASVS / HIPAA / GDPR crosswalk. Free tier included."` and `ci: "SARIF straight into GitHub Code Scanning, plus a GitHub Action and a GitLab template."`, and give every entry a matching `them` value (Burp's honest answer is "no compliance mapping"; Snyk's is "DAST is Ignite tier and above"). On the landing page, replace one of the three items in components/landing/landing-features.tsx's SUPPORTING array (:1 to :14) with "The report an auditor asks for": one sentence on the crosswalk, one on SARIF, linking /docs/reports. Keep the voice concrete, for example "Export the same scan as SARIF for the Security tab or as a PCI DSS and SOC 2 crosswalk for the auditor. Both on the free tier."

findings.title: Authenticated scanning here never stores a credential and the product ships zero telemetry, a privacy posture no SaaS peer can match, and it is stated nowhere outside a source-file comment
findings.description: lib/scanner/auth/types.ts:1 to :10 documents a deliberate design: "There is no stored credential anywhere in this codebase: a caller supplies login material directly in a single scan request, it lives in memory for the length of that one request, and it is never written to a table, a log line, an audit record, or the persisted scan result." The route enforces it (app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts:56 to :68: logAction records only the non-secret outcome), and the session object reports counts rather than contents (lib/scanner/auth/scan-session.ts:157 to :172). Every one of the eight commercial vendors stores your target credentials in their SaaS by construction, because all of them offer saved recorded login sequences. Separately, components/landing/landing-open-source.tsx:6 to :13 already lists "Telemetry: None" and "Third-party trackers: None" as bare facts in a definition list. The privacy argument is never made anywhere: neither claim appears in any /alternatives comparison row (lib/seo/alternatives.ts:44 has no privacy or data-handling row), in any landing FAQ answer (app/landing/page.tsx), or on the pricing page.
findings.impact: "Do I have to give a third-party SaaS a working login to my staging environment" is the objection that kills authenticated-scanning trials, and it is the one objection this product has an unusually good answer to. Burying that answer in a TypeScript file comment means it never reaches the person deciding.
findings.recommendation: Add a `privacy` row to the shared VR object in lib/seo/alternatives.ts:44: "Login material is sent in one request and held in memory for that request only. Never stored, logged, or written to a scan result." and give each competitor an accurate neutral `them` ("Saved login sequences, stored vendor-side"). Add it to the authenticated-scanning UI as a one-line reassurance above the credential fields, and to app/docs/ wherever authenticated scanning is documented. Pair it with the two existing facts from components/landing/landing-open-source.tsx:10 to :11 into a short "What we never keep" block on the landing page, which is a genuinely different section shape from the icon grids CLAUDE.md's design rules ban.

findings.title: Active probing is nine reflection-and-error-based probes with no out-of-band channel, so blind injection, stored XSS and second-order flaws are structurally undetectable and the marketing should say so
findings.category: list (a) gap rank 11: depth of active testing
findings.description: The research called active injection testing the defining line and ranked it gap number one. Verified in code, VulnRadar is further along than that implies but structurally capped. lib/scanner/active-probe-catalog.ts:46 to :101 defines nine opt-in probes, gated behind verified domain ownership (:117): reflected XSS canary, error-based SQLi, SSTI, OS command injection, confirmed open redirect, GraphQL introspection, active CORS reflection, dangerous HTTP methods, and X-Forwarded-Host injection, implemented in lib/scanner/active-probes/ (five modules, roughly 700 lines). Every one of them decides from the immediate response body or status. There is no out-of-band interaction server anywhere in the repo (grep for oast, collaborator, interactsh across lib/scanner/ returns only unrelated matches in port-scan.ts and two checks-data JSON files), which means blind and time-based SQLi, blind SSRF, blind XXE, out-of-band command injection and Log4Shell-class flaws cannot be confirmed by construction. There is also no second request-cycle verification, so stored XSS is out of reach. By contrast ZAP and Wapiti send full active-scan payloads across 30+ module families including XXE, path traversal, file upload and CSRF, Nuclei adds fuzzing with -dast, Burp ships OAST via Collaborator, Pentest-Tools ships actual auto-exploiters, and Invicti claims runtime proof-based verification at 99.98%.
findings.impact: Two-sided. Against ZAP and Wapiti, VulnRadar genuinely finds less, and a security engineer who assumes "active probing" means ZAP-equivalent coverage will conclude the scanner missed things it never claimed to look for. Against the free graders (Observatory, SecurityHeaders, SSL Labs), VulnRadar finds far more, which is the comparison that actually matters for its funnel. The cost today is not missed findings so much as an unstated ceiling.
findings.recommendation: Do not build an OAST server. It needs a public wildcard DNS zone plus an always-on HTTP collector, it breaks in every self-hosted deployment (which is the differentiator in comp-01), and it is the single most expensive item on this list. If out-of-band detection is ever wanted, integrate the public interactsh server as an optional, off-by-default setting rather than operating one. What is worth doing now is cheap and honest: state the ceiling. Add one line to the active-probes description surface (lib/scanner/active-probe-catalog.ts:44's rendered panel and app/checks/category/active-probes) saying these probes confirm what the response itself proves and do not attempt blind or time-based detection, and add an /alternatives entry for OWASP ZAP that says plainly that ZAP sends deeper payloads while VulnRadar is the hosted, zero-setup, public-catalog path. Being the tool that documents its own limits is a positioning asset for a scanner whose core pitch is determinism.

findings.title: One free scan already covers headers plus TLS plus DNS and email plus cookies at exactly the moment every free peer narrowed, and the hero copy actively undersells it to headers-only
findings.description: The free grading market contracted sharply and in one direction. MDN HTTP Observatory runs ten tests on HTTP headers only and sunset its TLS/SSH Observatory in October 2024. SecurityHeaders.com covers response headers only and its API was shut down by Snyk in April 2026 (confirmed live this session). SSL Labs covers TLS only, its v4 API rejects free email providers, and commercial use is prohibited by default. Hardenize went enterprise-only under Red Sift. ImmuniWeb is the only broad free option left and caps its free API at eight tests a day. VulnRadar covers all of it in one call: 18 check categories including headers, ssl, tls, dns, email, cookies, configuration, information-disclosure, api, code, secrets-extended, client-side, supply-chain and reputation (lib/scanner/registry.ts:23 to :40), plus port scanning (lib/scanner/port-scan.ts), software inventory with OSV/CVE correlation (lib/scanner/software-inventory.ts, osv-check.ts, cve-enrichment.ts), subdomain discovery, and a self-computed SSL-Labs-style letter grade that depends on no third-party API (lib/scanner/ssl-grade.ts:1). The landing hero shows a six-row readout of security headers and nothing else, and its caption at components/landing/landing-hero.tsx:132 to :136 says "Every header, cookie, and config gets read the same way: no rendering, no screenshot, just the response", which describes a headers scanner and is also inaccurate, since the product does take page screenshots (lib/scanner/page-screenshot.ts) and does render pages in a real browser for authenticated login (lib/scanner/auth/browser-login.ts). Relatedly, components/landing/landing-features.tsx:4 claims "no browser extension" while extension/ ships one to the Chrome store.
findings.impact: The single strongest, most defensible, most timely claim available to this product, that it is now the only free tool covering headers and TLS and DNS together, is not made anywhere, and the hero actively frames the product as the narrower category the incumbents just abandoned. Visitors arriving from a "security headers" search have no reason to learn the scan also graded their certificate and checked their SPF and DMARC records.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the hero caption at components/landing/landing-hero.tsx:132 to name the breadth, for example: "One request, one report: headers, certificate and TLS, cookies, DNS and mail records, exposed secrets. Observatory dropped TLS in 2024 and SSL Labs will not grade a site for you commercially. This does both." Extend HERO_READOUT_ROWS (:25) beyond six header rows to include one TLS row and one DNS or DMARC row so the visual matches the claim. Fix components/landing/landing-features.tsx:4's "no browser extension" to "nothing you have to install" so it stops contradicting the shipped extension. Then add the /alternatives entries from comp-04, since the comparison pages are where this argument converts.

findings.title: CONTRIBUTING.md's pre-PR checklist covers two of the seven CI gates and never mentions that the repository has tests
findings.description: CONTRIBUTING.md:55 says 'Ensure npm run build and npm run lint pass locally', and its script table at :17-24 lists dev, build, lint, lint:fix, typecheck and format. .github/workflows/ci.yml gates a PR on seven things: npm run lint (:40), npm run format:check (:44), npx tsc --noEmit (:67), npm audit --audit-level=high --omit=dev (:71), a regenerate-and-diff of the AI knowledge files (:73-82, which runs npm run build:knowledge and then `git diff --exit-code -- lib/ai lib/config/check-stats.generated.ts`), npm run test (:107), node --test in cli/ (:112), plus the extension's own typecheck, format:check and both builds (:141-149) and finally npm run build (:196). CONTRIBUTING never mentions tests, formatting checks, the extension jobs, or the knowledge regeneration, and the repo's own AGENTS.md 'Before every commit' list (:173-205) also omits format:check, the CLI test, the extension gates and the knowledge diff.
findings.impact: The knowledge-file gate is the trap: any PR that edits a docs page, the changelog data, a check definition or a legal page fails CI with a `git diff --exit-code` error unless the contributor ran npm run build:knowledge and committed the regenerated lib/ai/*.md. Nothing in CONTRIBUTING or AGENTS tells them that. A contributor who follows CONTRIBUTING exactly still gets a red build, on the one step that is least self-explanatory.
findings.recommendation: Replace CONTRIBUTING.md:55 with the full local equivalent of CI: `npm run lint && npm run format:check && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build`, plus `npm run build:knowledge` and commit the result whenever docs, changelog, checks or legal pages change, plus `cd cli && node --test` and `cd extension && npm run typecheck && npm run format:check` when those directories change. Add the same four missing steps to AGENTS.md:173-205 so both the human and the agent checklist match ci.yml.

findings.title: AGENTS.md lists 12 of the scanner's 18 categories, so an automated contributor is told six live categories do not exist
findings.description: AGENTS.md:140-153 gives the authoritative category list an agent must consult 'Before adding a scanner' and names 12: headers, ssl, tls, content, cookies, configuration, information-disclosure, dns, email, api, code, secrets-extended. The Category union at lib/scanner/types.ts:22-39 has 18, adding vibe-code, client-side, supply-chain, host-validation, reputation and active-probes. lib/config/check-stats.generated.ts:7 records EXACT_CHECK_CATEGORY_COUNT = 18, README.md:12 and :30 say 18, and the browser extension's own list at extension/src/lib/categories.ts has all 18. AGENTS.md is the only surface that disagrees, and it has a matching lib/scanner/checks-data/<category>.json for each of the six it omits.
findings.impact: An automated contributor following AGENTS.md sees no vibe-code, client-side, supply-chain, host-validation, reputation or active-probes category and will either refuse to place a check there or invent a new category rather than using the existing one. active-probes matters most: it is the only opt-in, writes-to-the-target category (lib/scanner/types.ts:41-50 explains why it is excluded from ALL_CATEGORIES) and an agent that does not know it exists cannot honour that contract.
findings.recommendation: Replace the hand-written list in AGENTS.md:140-153 with the 18 names from lib/scanner/types.ts, or better, replace it with an instruction to read the Category union directly so it cannot drift again. Add a line stating that active-probes never runs by default and must be named explicitly.

findings.title: The docs nav bills /docs/config as 'Every CONFIG_* value and every environment variable'; the page names 76 of 308 constants and 206 of 267 runtime settings are never named anywhere
findings.description: components/docs/docs-nav.ts:82-85 gives /docs/config the summary 'Every CONFIG_* value and every environment variable'. lib/config/config-values.ts defines 308 `export const CONFIG_*` constants; app/docs/config/page.tsx names 76 of them. lib/config/registry.ts defines 267 SETTINGS_REGISTRY entries, and lib/config/runtime-config.ts:81-94 resolves each one as `database value ?? process.env[key] ?? shipped default`, which means every one of those 267 keys is a valid environment variable name. Only 61 of the 267 appear anywhere on the config page, and almost all of those appear only in their CONFIG_-prefixed form, so the page never tells the reader that the bare key is the environment variable. app/docs/config/page.tsx:605-627 does document the resolution order correctly but never lists which keys participate.
findings.impact: A self-hoster who wants to pin a rate limit, a scan timeout or a billing limit through the environment (the documented way for a container to override without a database write) has no way to learn the variable name short of reading lib/config/registry.ts. The nav summary promises completeness the page does not deliver, so the reader stops looking after not finding their value.
findings.recommendation: Generate the reference rather than hand-writing it: emit a table from SETTINGS_REGISTRY (key, tier, type, default, group, help, all of which the registry already carries) at build time the way scripts/compile-checks-knowledge.mjs already generates check-stats, and render it on /docs/config. Until then, change the nav summary at components/docs/docs-nav.ts:84 to something honest such as 'How configuration resolves, and the values you are most likely to change'.

findings.title: README describes two configuration layers and says the static layer requires an edit and a rebuild; there are three layers and 239 of 268 settings are runtime-editable with no rebuild
findings.description: README.md:88-102 states VulnRadar has 'two configuration layers', describes lib/config/config-values.ts as 'Static app config ... App name, URL, emails, SEO metadata, rate limits, feature flags, billing plans. Edit and rebuild', and closes with 'Self-hosters edit config-values.ts and nothing else'. .env.example:329-330 repeats it: 'These values are NOT in .env. Edit lib/config/config-values.ts directly and rebuild'. In reality lib/config/registry.ts carries 267 SETTINGS_REGISTRY entries of which 239 are `tier: "runtime"` and 29 are `tier: "build"`, lib/config/runtime-config.ts:81-94 resolves each as database ?? env ?? default with a 30 second cache, and components/admin/features/system-settings-manager.tsx renders the whole registry as an editable admin Settings page. Rate limits, feature flags, billing limits, scan timeouts and AI budgets, the very examples the README puts in the 'edit and rebuild' row, are all runtime tier. app/docs/config/page.tsx:580-627 documents this correctly, so the README and .env.example contradict the docs page they link to.
findings.impact: A self-hoster rebuilds and redeploys an image to change a rate limit or a feature flag that they could have changed in the admin panel in five seconds, or sets an environment variable and concludes it does not work because the README told them the value is compiled in. The database layer, which is the one the admin panel writes and the one that wins, is not mentioned in the README at all.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite README.md:88-106 as three layers: database (admin Settings, wins, no restart), environment (a variable named exactly like the SETTINGS_REGISTRY key), and the shipped CONFIG_* default in config-values.ts (edit and rebuild, and required only for the 29 build-tier values). Delete 'Self-hosters edit config-values.ts and nothing else' at :102 and fix the same claim at .env.example:329-330.

findings.title: The crawl page caps are documented as 15 and 20 in six places; the real caps are per-plan 25 to 250 and 500 for discovery, and the MAX_PAGES constant the docs cite no longer exists
findings.description: The real caps: lib/billing/crawl-page-limits.ts:19-24 sets CRAWL_PAGE_SELECTION_LIMITS to free 25, core_supporter 50, pro_supporter 100, elite_supporter 250, and app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:257-268 enforces it, treating a billing-disabled (self-hosted) caller as unlimited. Discovery is capped by CONFIG_CRAWL_DISCOVER_MAX_PAGES = 500 (lib/config/config-values.ts:594), read at app/api/v3/scan/crawl/discover/route.ts:74-79. Neither route defines a MAX_PAGES symbol any more. Six surfaces still say 15 or 20: cli/README.md:34 and cli/lib.mjs:126 ('Crawl and scan up to 15 pages'), app/docs/cli/page.tsx:135, app/docs/developers/page.tsx:64, lib/ai/system-prompt.ts:210 ('Crawl + scan up to 15 pages'), and lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:96. The API reference repeats it at app/docs/api/page.tsx:322, :332 ('Max 15 pages (MAX_PAGES in app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts)') and :364 ('Returns up to 20 URLs (MAX_PAGES in app/api/v3/scan/crawl/discover/route.ts)'); those three belong to the API-reference agent's surface and are noted here only so the fix is done in one pass. lib/changelog/data.ts:793 already records the change to 500 discovered and per-plan selection, so the docs are behind their own changelog.
findings.impact: Paying users are told their crawl covers 15 pages when an elite plan covers 250, so they under-use what they paid for and may buy a competitor for site-wide coverage. Self-hosters, who are uncapped, are told they are capped at 15. The AI assistant repeats the wrong number because lib/ai/system-prompt.ts:210 carries it. Two doc lines also cite a constant name that a reader will grep for and not find.
findings.recommendation: Import the numbers instead of writing them. On app/docs/cli/page.tsx and app/docs/developers/page.tsx render CRAWL_PAGE_SELECTION_LIMITS from lib/billing/crawl-page-limits.ts and CONFIG_CRAWL_DISCOVER_MAX_PAGES, the same way app/docs/developers/page.tsx:117 already renders ALL_CATEGORIES. Reword cli/README.md:34 and cli/lib.mjs:126 to 'Crawl and scan the pages your plan allows (self-hosted: unlimited)'. Update lib/ai/system-prompt.ts:210 and recompile the knowledge files.

findings.title: SECURITY.md points reporters at a PGP key and an Acknowledgments list that security.txt does not contain, and scopes out deployments that ignore a hardening guide that does not exist
findings.description: public/.well-known/security.txt has exactly six fields: Contact, Expires (2028-06-18, in the future, correct), Preferred-Languages, Canonical, Policy and Acknowledgments (pointing at https://vulnradar.dev/changelog). SECURITY.md:16 says to email security@vulnradar.dev '(PGP key below)'; SECURITY.md:64-68 then says 'We accept reports encrypted to the PGP key published in public/.well-known/security.txt'. There is no Encryption: field and no key in that file, so a reporter who wants to encrypt has nothing to encrypt to and is told to ask for the fingerprint by unencrypted email. SECURITY.md:26 offers credit 'in the Acknowledgments section of public/.well-known/security.txt' and :62 says 'See public/.well-known/security.txt for the latest list'; the file has no list, only a URL to the changelog. Separately, SECURITY.md:57 puts 'Self-hosted deployments that don't follow our hardening guide' out of scope, and no self-hosting hardening guide exists: grepping for 'harden' across app/docs/ and the root markdown returns only SECURITY-POSTURE.md, which is a checklist for vulnradar.dev's own Cloudflare and ProtonMail records and is not linked from SECURITY.md, README.md or any docs page.
findings.impact: A researcher who follows the published policy cannot encrypt a report, cannot see who has been credited, and is told their self-host finding may be rejected against a document they cannot read. The address itself is real and consistent (CONFIG_SECURITY_EMAIL at lib/config/config-values.ts:155), so the process fails only on the parts SECURITY.md invented.
findings.recommendation: Either publish a key and add `Encryption: https://vulnradar.dev/.well-known/pgp-key.txt` to security.txt, or delete the PGP claims at SECURITY.md:16 and :64-68. Point the Acknowledgments claims at whatever page actually lists credited researchers, or drop them. Either write a self-hosting hardening guide and link it from SECURITY.md:57, or narrow that exclusion to something checkable such as 'deployments running with DISABLE_CSP=1 or without TLS'.

findings.title: The architecture doc's permissions section cites a deleted lib/auth/permissions.ts, three symbols that do not exist, and a role ladder missing 5 of the 9 real roles with every level number wrong
findings.description: app/docs/architecture/page.tsx:540-556 documents the role hierarchy as `user (0) -> support (1) -> moderator (2) -> admin (3)` and lists 'lib/auth/permissions.ts: server-safe role + permission maps (ROLES, ROLE_PERMISSIONS, userHasPermission, canManageRole)'. lib/auth/permissions.ts was removed by commit 4b8d6e71 ('fix: remove dead legacy permission system, fix stale role-name lists'); the file is gone and ROLES, ROLE_PERMISSIONS and userHasPermission do not appear anywhere in lib/. The real model is lib/config/client-constants.ts:12-49, which defines nine roles (user, support, billing, security_analyst, content_manager, ops, moderator, admin, super_admin) with STAFF_ROLE_HIERARCHY levels 0, 10, 20, 20, 20, 20, 30, 40, 50, plus lib/auth/permissions-client.ts (STAFF_PERMISSIONS, hasStaffPermission, canManageRole, getRoleLevel, hasGodMode) and lib/auth/authorization.ts (requireStaff, requireModerator, requireAdmin, requirePermission). The doc omits the four lateral specialist roles and super_admin, and all four level numbers it does give are wrong.
findings.impact: A contributor reading the architecture doc to understand authorization opens a path that does not exist, greps for three symbols that do not exist, and comes away believing there are four roles when there are nine. Missing super_admin from the doc is the material part: it is the god-mode tier, it is auto-assigned to the first account, and app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:642-647 refuses to assign it through any UI, so anyone reasoning about admin security from this page reasons about the wrong model.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite app/docs/architecture/page.tsx:540-556 against lib/config/client-constants.ts:12-49: render STAFF_ROLE_HIERARCHY rather than hand-typing it, note that the four level-20 roles are lateral specialists rather than a rung, and note that super_admin is bootstrap-only and un-assignable. Point the file list at lib/auth/permissions-client.ts and lib/auth/authorization.ts.

findings.title: Two 'every script' inventories list 15 and 9 of the 35 npm scripts, omitting every database diagnostic, repair, backup and restore command the repo ships
findings.description: app/docs/developers/page.tsx:504 says 'Every npm script and what it does. Defined in package.json' and then tables 15 of the 35 scripts in package.json. scripts/README.md:49 heads a table 'Available scripts' with 9. Between them they never mention db:diagnose, db:diagnose-2fa, db:repair, db:repair-2fa, db:repair-sequences, db:migrate-avatars, db:backup, db:restore, docs:compile, changelog:compile, checks:compile, legal:compile or build:knowledge. scripts/README.md's directory tree at :10-46 is separately stale: it lists 9 of the 25 files in scripts/_lib/, omits all 12 root-level scripts (backup-db.mjs, restore-db.mjs, build-og-image.mjs, the four compile-*-knowledge.mjs, db-diagnose.mjs, db-diagnose-2fa.mjs, db-repair.mjs, db-repair-2fa.mjs, db-repair-sequences.mjs, migrate-avatars-to-files.mjs) and omits create-fresh-db/schemas/instrumentation-v2.ts. This extends AUDIT-013#dead-04 (which found the archived migrator entry in the same tree) and AUDIT-013#dead-10 (which found the find-duplicate-ids.mjs 'CI gate' claim at :20 and :63 that no workflow runs).
findings.impact: An operator whose database is in a bad state has five purpose-built diagnostic and repair tools in the repo and no document that mentions any of them. That is the direct cause of the impossible recovery advice in doc-05 and it compounds AUDIT-013#migrate-15, which found that nothing documents what to do when a migration fails. db:backup and db:restore are undocumented in these two inventories even though app/docs/config/page.tsx:999-1002 refers to them as if they were.
findings.recommendation: Generate both tables from package.json rather than maintaining them by hand, or at minimum add the 20 missing entries to app/docs/developers/page.tsx:504 and the 8 missing db:* commands to scripts/README.md:49. Regenerate the scripts/README.md tree from an actual listing of scripts/. Add a short 'when something is wrong with the database' section that names db:diagnose, db:diagnose-2fa, db:repair, db:repair-2fa and db:repair-sequences with their dry-run defaults.

findings.title: The published accessibility statement claims automated accessibility testing and accessibility testing in the development process; the repo has neither a tool nor a CI job
findings.description: app/legal/accessibility/page.tsx:183-191 states the assessment approach as 'Self-evaluation using automated accessibility testing tools', 'Manual testing with screen readers and keyboard navigation' and 'Review against WCAG 2.1 success criteria', and :194-199 states 'we incorporate accessibility testing into our development process'. Neither package.json nor extension/package.json depends on axe, jest-axe, pa11y, lighthouse, jsdom, happy-dom or any testing-library package, and no workflow in .github/workflows/ references axe, a11y, accessibility or lighthouse. AUDIT-013#cov-09 already established that vitest.config.ts runs environment: node with no DOM, so no component can be rendered in a test at all, let alone audited. Two of the page's specific feature claims are checkable and split: the Skip Links claim at :92-95 is true (app/layout.tsx:175), while the Form Labels claim at :88-91 is already contradicted by AUDIT-011#docs-07 on the API playground.
findings.impact: This is a published legal accessibility statement, the document a regulator, a procurement reviewer or a complainant reads first. Two of its claims describe a process that provably does not exist in the repository, which turns a good-faith statement into an unsupported one and undermines the parts that are true.
findings.recommendation: Either make the claim true or narrow it. Adding jsdom plus @axe-core/react or a pa11y-ci pass over the main routes and one CI job is a day of work and would make both sentences accurate. If that is not on the roadmap, rewrite app/legal/accessibility/page.tsx:183-191 to describe what is actually done (manual keyboard and screen-reader passes, review against WCAG 2.1 AA) and delete the automated-tooling and 'incorporate accessibility testing into our development process' claims.

findings.title: HOST_BIND exists only as a comment inside docker-compose.yml, and the troubleshooting row for the exact symptom it causes points at APP_PORT instead
findings.description: docker-compose.yml:78 publishes the app as `"${HOST_BIND:-127.0.0.1}:${APP_PORT:-3000}:3000"`, so out of the box the container is reachable only from the docker host itself. The only mention of the variable anywhere in the repository is the comment two lines above it at :76 ('Override with HOST_BIND=0.0.0.0 to expose'), repeated in docker-compose.dev.yml:68. HOST_BIND is not in .env.example, not in app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx, not in app/docs/setup/page.tsx, not in app/docs/config/page.tsx and not in README.md. app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:583-587 documents the symptom '502 from reverse proxy', cause 'App not listening on the expected port', fix 'Check APP_PORT (default 3000); confirm the app container is up via docker compose ps' and never mentions the bind address.
findings.impact: An operator whose reverse proxy, load balancer or LAN client is not on the docker host gets connection refused, follows the one troubleshooting row that matches the symptom, checks APP_PORT and `docker compose ps`, finds both correct, and has no documented next step. The variable that fixes it is discoverable only by reading the compose file.
findings.recommendation: Add HOST_BIND to .env.example beside APP_PORT with the 127.0.0.1 default and the 0.0.0.0 override spelled out, add it to the environment table on app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx, and extend the troubleshooting row at :583-587 to read 'Check HOST_BIND (default 127.0.0.1, set 0.0.0.0 if the proxy is not on this host) and APP_PORT (default 3000)'.

findings.title: Five product surfaces the README advertises have no documentation page: billing and subscription management, bulk scanning, notifications, admin operations, and what to do when a scan fails or reports nothing
findings.description: DOCS_NAV (components/docs/docs-nav.ts:13-140) has 19 entries across six sections. Cross-checking them against the shipped surface: (1) Billing. app/pricing, app/checkout, app/api/v3/billing/route.ts, app/api/v3/billing/subscription/cancel/route.ts and .../reactivate/route.ts exist, four paid plans are defined in lib/billing/catalog.ts, and three separate credit products have checkout components under components/billing/. No docs page explains plans, upgrading, cancelling, reactivating, credits, or what happens at the end of a trial; grepping app/docs for 'cancel' returns only API and team contexts and 'refund' returns one line on the AI page. (2) Bulk scanning. README.md:34 advertises it, app/api/v3/scan/bulk and components/scanner/dashboard-bulk-result.tsx implement it, and 'bulk scan' appears in app/docs only inside the API reference. (3) Notifications. app/api/v3/notifications exists and is referenced from eight docs pages in passing, with no page of its own. (4) Admin. app/admin plus 267 SETTINGS_REGISTRY entries, the audit log, impersonation, broadcasts, the Backup button and IP rules have no operator page; 'audit log' appears in app/docs only in the API reference and 'activity log' nowhere. (5) Troubleshooting a scan. Nothing anywhere covers a scan that fails, times out, or returns zero findings, which is the single most common support question for a scanner.
findings.impact: Every one of these lands in support instead of self-service, and the project has in-app support tickets (app/docs/triage covers them) so the cost is real. Billing is the sharpest: a paying user who wants to cancel has no documentation and must find the button, which is a chargeback and trust risk on a service with a real subscriber base.
findings.recommendation: Add three pages first, in this order: 'Plans and Billing' under Using VulnRadar (what each plan includes rendered from lib/billing/catalog.ts, how to upgrade, cancel and reactivate, how the three credit types work, what happens when a subscription lapses); 'Troubleshooting Scans' (timeouts, blocked targets, zero-finding results, robots.txt exclusions, what each terminal scan status means); and 'Administration' under Running your own (the /admin tabs, the settings registry, the audit log, backups, IP rules, impersonation). Fold bulk scanning into the scheduled-scans page or give it a section, and give notifications a section on the account-security page rather than a page of its own.

findings.title: The product ships two mutually exclusive corner-radius conventions, so the scan result view and /profile are visibly different products sitting one nav item apart
findings.description: audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md section C5 records the ladder: rounded-2xl for one flagship block, rounded-xl for content cards, code blocks, tables and the readout, rounded-lg for small cards and chip links, rounded-md for buttons. I counted every rounded-* literal per directory. components/scanner: 83 rounded-md, 4 rounded-lg, 0 rounded-xl. components/history: 21 rounded-md, 3 rounded-lg. components/shares, components/assets, components/host, components/teams and components/billing are the same shape (6, 6, 1, 10 and 36 rounded-md respectively). Against that, components/profile is 72 rounded-lg + 24 rounded-xl + 14 rounded-md, and components/admin is 132 rounded-lg + 19 rounded-xl + 26 rounded-md. These are not buttons: filtering to bordered card containers, the scanner family draws its panels at rounded-md (components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:608,719,837,862, dashboard.tsx:260,342,417,453, response-headers.tsx:46, dns-records-panel.tsx:207, port-scan-panel.tsx:126, threat-intel-panel.tsx, software-inventory-panel.tsx, results-list.tsx:463), while components/profile and components/admin draw the equivalent panels at rounded-lg or rounded-xl (18 and 9 of them respectively), and components/ui/card.tsx:12 (the shared primitive, used by 42 files) is rounded-lg. The landing page, the documented yardstick, uses rounded-xl for content cards. So the same nav bar leads to a 6px-radius scan report and a 12px-radius billing card.
findings.impact: Radius is one of the two or three cues a person uses to decide whether two screens belong to the same application. A user who scans a site and then opens Profile crosses a visible seam. It also makes every new component a coin flip for the author, which is how the split got to 83 versus 132 in the first place.
findings.recommendation: Adopt the landing ladder as written in design-language.md C5 and move the scanner family up, not the profile family down, because the shared primitive components/ui/card.tsx and 42 of its consumers are already on rounded-lg. Concretely: in components/scanner, change the bordered panel containers (issue-detail.tsx:608,719,837,862; dashboard.tsx:172,260,342,417,453; response-headers.tsx:46; dns-records-panel.tsx:207; port-scan-panel.tsx:126; results-list.tsx:463,598; scan-result-detail.tsx:228; crawl-pages-info.tsx:54; dashboard-error-state.tsx:182; scan-summary.tsx) from rounded-md to rounded-xl, and the same in components/history, components/shares, components/assets, components/host and components/teams. Leave rounded-md on the actual controls (inputs at results-list.tsx:379, buttons at :408,615) where it is correct. Then write the three-rung ladder into CLAUDE.md's spacing section so it is reviewable: rounded-xl = panel, rounded-lg = small card or chip, rounded-md = control, rounded-full = pill, rounded-2xl = one flagship block per page.

findings.title: Seven different page-H1 treatments across 71 pages, and the documented Page H1 scale appears on no signed-in page at all
findings.description: design-language.md B2 records the Page H1 (non-hero) as `text-3xl sm:text-4xl font-semibold tracking-tight mb-5 text-balance`, cited from app/pricing/page.tsx:77. I extracted the className of every <h1> in app/ and components/. Seven distinct treatments ship: (1) the documented one, on app/pricing/page.tsx:77, app/checks/page.tsx:75, app/checks/category/[category]/page.tsx:126, app/alternatives/page.tsx:40, app/alternatives/[competitor]/page.tsx:85, app/tools/page.tsx:56, app/tools/api-scanner/page.tsx:79, app/tools/link-checker/page.tsx:80, all of them public SEO pages; (2) `text-xl sm:text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight text-foreground` on app/history/page.tsx:576, app/assets/page.tsx:148, app/shares/page.tsx:160, app/repos/page.tsx:360,465 and app/public-scans/page.tsx:118; (3) `text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight` on app/profile/page.tsx:679, app/admin/page.tsx:1021, app/attack-surface/page.tsx:30, app/legal/page.tsx:57 and app/teams/join/page.tsx:29; (4) `text-2xl sm:text-3xl font-semibold tracking-tight` on app/badge/page.tsx:101, app/changelog/page.tsx:22, app/compare/page.tsx:212, app/contact/page.tsx:56 and app/donate/page.tsx:32; (5) `text-lg font-semibold` with no tracking-tight on app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:144,161,218 and app/shared/[token]/page.tsx:143,251; (6) `font-bold` variants on app/checkout/credits/page.tsx:52,82,145 and its three sibling checkout pages, app/checkout/success/checkout-success-content.tsx:98 and app/security/page.tsx:48; (7) `text-2xl sm:text-4xl` (skipping the 3xl step) on app/checks/[id]/page.tsx:195. Only the SEO family matches the spec. Every page a paying user actually works in is on one of the other six. text-balance, which design-language.md B3 says goes on every heading, is present only on the SEO family, checks/[id] and two modal titles.
findings.impact: A user moving Dashboard to History to Profile to Admin sees the page title change size three times for no reason, so nothing tells them what a page title is. Two of the seven treatments use font-bold, a weight design-language.md B3 records as appearing nowhere in the reference work.
findings.recommendation: Two tiers, written down, then applied. Tier A (marketing, docs, SEO, legal, pricing): keep the documented `text-3xl sm:text-4xl font-semibold tracking-tight mb-5 text-balance`. Tier B (in-app working pages, where the H1 sits above a dense table and must not eat the fold): standardise on `text-xl sm:text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight text-balance text-foreground`, which treatment (2) already uses on five pages and which is the largest existing cluster. Change app/profile/page.tsx:679, app/admin/page.tsx:1021, app/attack-surface/page.tsx:30, app/badge/page.tsx:101, app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:218 and app/shared/[token]/page.tsx:251 to Tier B, and app/security/page.tsx:48, app/legal/page.tsx:57, app/changelog/page.tsx:22, app/contact/page.tsx:56 and app/donate/page.tsx:32 to Tier A. Delete every font-bold in an <h1> (checkout pages are covered separately in dsn-05). Add both strings to CLAUDE.md under a Typography heading next to the existing Button and Spacing conventions, which is the only reason the button geometry stayed consistent and the heading scale did not.

findings.title: The four checkout pages are the least spec-conformant surface in the product and they are the revenue path: container mx-auto, py-8 md:py-12, font-bold headings and md: breakpoints, all four times over
findings.description: app/checkout/credits/page.tsx, app/checkout/github-credits/page.tsx, app/checkout/browser-credits/page.tsx and app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx (plus components/billing/checkout-skeleton.tsx) fail four of the fourteen tell-tale checks in design-language.md G simultaneously, and they are the only files in app/ that do. Check 2 (container): they are the only five files in the repo using Tailwind's `container` class, at credits:119,142, github-credits:121,140, browser-credits:123,142, [productId]:168,192 and checkout-skeleton:13,24, always as `container max-w-4xl mx-auto px-4`, where the documented default is `max-w-6xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6` and the responsive px step is missing. Check 1 (section rhythm): `py-8 md:py-12` at credits:142 and its three siblings, against the documented `py-16 sm:py-20`; md: rather than sm: is used for every breakpoint on these pages while the rest of app/ uses sm:. Check 7 (heading scale): `text-2xl font-bold mb-2` at credits:52,82, `text-2xl md:text-3xl font-bold mb-2` at :145, `text-lg font-bold` at :190 and `text-2xl font-bold` at :226, with the same lines in all three credit pages and [productId]:81,100,120,150,198,257. design-language.md B3 records that font-bold appears nowhere in the reference work. The three credit pages are otherwise near-identical files, which AUDIT-013#dup-06 already filed from the code-duplication angle (roughly 1,900 duplicated lines across the three checkout components and three pages); the design consequence is that a single fix has to be made three or four times and has not been.
findings.impact: This is the screen where a user hands over a card. It is visibly heavier and more cramped than the pricing page they arrived from: a bolder title, half the vertical room, a narrower measure and no sm: padding step, so on a 640px phone the page has 16px gutters where /pricing has 24px. It reads as a different, older product at the exact moment trust matters most, and the same four defects have to be fixed four times because the pages were copied.
findings.recommendation: Fix this together with AUDIT-013#dup-06's collapse rather than separately. When the three credit pages fold into one parameterised CreditCheckout page, give the surviving page: `<main id="main-content" tabIndex={-1} className="w-full max-w-4xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6 py-12 sm:py-16">` (max-w-4xl is defensible for a single-task form; drop the `container` class, which does nothing here but add Tailwind's own padding), the Tier A page H1 from dsn-04 (`text-3xl sm:text-4xl font-semibold tracking-tight mb-5 text-balance`), `text-lg font-semibold` for the tier price at credits:190, and `text-2xl font-semibold tabular-nums` for the Total today figure at :226. Change every md: breakpoint on these pages to sm: to match the rest of app/. Apply the same to app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx and components/billing/checkout-skeleton.tsx so the skeleton and the loaded page still line up.

findings.title: Six implementations of one inline stat strip, at three different value type sizes and two container geometries, and two byte-identical copies of the STAT_ICON_TONES table
findings.description: Extends AUDIT-013#dup-12, which caught the Cell duplication between components/assets/assets-stats.tsx:9 and components/shares/shares-stats.tsx:17 and the three identical stats skeletons, from the code angle. It missed four more copies and did not record the visual result. The full set: components/history/history-stats.tsx:18 defines a third byte-identical Cell; components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:94 defines StatCell (the same markup with items-start instead of items-center and no textTone); components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx:75 defines Stat (same again at StatIcon size="sm" with a text-sm value and flex-1 basis-24 instead of a grid); components/admin/shared/stat-card.tsx:52 defines StatBar, a sixth. The value type size differs three ways for the same element: text-2xl in history-stats/assets-stats/shares-stats/dashboard.tsx:108, text-sm in scan-summary.tsx:88, text-lg in stat-card.tsx:82. The container differs two ways: `grid grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-4 gap-px bg-border overflow-hidden rounded-md border border-border` in the four app-side copies versus `flex flex-wrap rounded-lg border border-border/50 bg-border/50 gap-px overflow-hidden` at stat-card.tsx:62. On top of that, the STAT_ICON_TONES lookup is duplicated verbatim, nine keys and all their class strings, at components/shared/stat-icon.tsx:11-24 and components/admin/shared/stat-card.tsx:11-24; stat-icon.tsx's own docblock at :4-10 says it exists to stop each file inventing its own colours and then names stat-card.tsx as the pattern it is copying rather than importing from it.
findings.impact: This is the mechanism by which one product stops looking like one product, applied to the element a user meets first on five different pages. The counts row on /dashboard, /history, /assets and /shares is 24px tall type in a 6px-radius box; the same row on /admin is 18px type in an 8px-radius box with a half-opacity border; the same row inside a scan summary is 14px type in a flex strip. Nothing distinguishes them semantically, so a reader learns the pattern four times. Two copies of the tone table mean the next colour added lands in one of them.
findings.recommendation: Promote a single components/shared/stat-strip.tsx exporting `StatStrip({ items, size })` and reusing the existing StatIcon, with size="md" giving today's `text-2xl font-semibold leading-none tabular-nums tracking-tight` value and size="sm" giving `text-sm`, and one container: `flex flex-wrap gap-px overflow-hidden rounded-xl border border-border bg-border` (rounded-xl per dsn-03). Delete Cell from components/history/history-stats.tsx:18, components/assets/assets-stats.tsx:9 and components/shares/shares-stats.tsx:17, StatCell from components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:94, Stat from components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx:75, and rewrite components/admin/shared/stat-card.tsx's StatBar as a thin wrapper that adds only the onClick/aria-pressed filtering behaviour its docblock at :46-51 describes. Delete the STAT_ICON_TONES block at components/admin/shared/stat-card.tsx:11-26 and import StatTone and the tones from components/shared/stat-icon.tsx. Collapse the three stats skeletons AUDIT-013#dup-12 lists into one StatStripSkeleton beside it so the loading state cannot drift from the loaded state again.

findings.title: Five empty-state grammars, four of which are byte-identical wrappers around the same markup with a different icon and sentence
findings.description: Five distinct empty-state treatments ship. (1) The app family, `flex flex-col items-center gap-3 rounded-md border border-dashed border-border bg-card/50 px-4 py-14 text-center` with a 6x6 icon at text-muted-foreground/60, a text-sm font-semibold title, a max-w-xs text-xs body and an optional sm Button: components/history/history-empty-state.tsx:25 and :48, components/assets/assets-empty-state.tsx:20 and :41, components/shares/shares-empty-state.tsx:7, components/public-scans/public-scans-empty-state.tsx:5, components/teams/teams-list.tsx:56 and :72, components/scanner/results-list.tsx:598, components/scanner/dashboard-results.tsx:269 and components/scanner/scan-result-detail.tsx:228. The four standalone files are the same JSX with only the icon and copy swapped, and each is its own module. (2) The admin family, components/admin/shared/data-table.tsx:19-45 EmptyState: no dashed border and no card at all, a 12x12 rounded-full bg-muted/50 circle holding a 6x6 icon at text-muted-foreground/50, py-16 px-4, text-sm font-medium title, text-xs max-w-sm body. Used by roughly 14 admin panels plus app/admin/page.tsx:1301,1502. (3) components/badge/badge-empty-state.tsx:8, `rounded-xl border border-dashed border-border bg-card/30 py-14 px-6`. (4) components/repos/repo-detail.tsx:251, `rounded-lg border border-dashed border-border px-4 py-10` with no background at all. (5) components/profile/tabs/developer/api-keys-section.tsx:250, `rounded-xl border border-dashed border-border bg-muted/20 p-5 sm:p-6` left-aligned. Radius spans md, lg and xl; the surface spans bg-card/50, bg-card/30, bg-muted/20 and nothing; the icon is bare in one family and in a circle in the other.
findings.impact: Empty states are the first thing a new account sees on five pages in a row (/history, /assets, /shares, /teams, the results list) and they are the first thing an admin sees in fourteen panels. Two unrelated grammars for the same moment make the admin panel read as a bolted-on second application, which is exactly how it is built. Four separate one-file modules means a copy change or an a11y fix has to be made four times.
findings.recommendation: Add components/shared/empty-state.tsx exporting `EmptyState({ icon, title, description, action, variant })` with the app family's geometry as the default (`flex flex-col items-center gap-3 rounded-xl border border-dashed border-border bg-card/50 px-4 py-14 text-center`, rounded-xl per dsn-03) and variant="inline" dropping the border and background for use inside a card that already has one, which is what the admin EmptyState is really doing. Delete components/history/history-empty-state.tsx, components/assets/assets-empty-state.tsx, components/shares/shares-empty-state.tsx and components/public-scans/public-scans-empty-state.tsx and call the shared component from the four pages with their icon and copy inline; delete the inline copies at components/teams/teams-list.tsx:56,72, components/scanner/results-list.tsx:598, dashboard-results.tsx:269 and scan-result-detail.tsx:228; re-export the shared component from components/admin/shared/data-table.tsx as EmptyState with variant="inline" so the fourteen admin call sites need no edit, and delete its body at :19-45. Fold components/badge/badge-empty-state.tsx and components/repos/repo-detail.tsx:251 in too.

findings.title: Twenty-three distinct inline alert geometries across 53 files, with four radii, three border opacities and two off-scale background opacities, because there is no Alert primitive
findings.category: one-off components / inline alerts (53 files across app/ and components/, no primitive in components/ui/)
findings.description: components/ui/ has no alert.tsx. 53 files hand-roll the inline error banner. Extracting every className that pairs a destructive border with a destructive background and has padding and a radius gives 23 unique strings, including: `rounded-md border border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/10 px-3 py-2 text-sm text-destructive`, `rounded-lg border border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/10 px-3 py-2 ...`, `rounded-lg border border-destructive/25 bg-destructive/5 px-3.5 py-3 ...`, `rounded-lg border border-destructive/20 bg-destructive/5 px-3 py-2.5`, `flex items-start gap-3 p-4 rounded-xl border border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/10` (app/teams/page.tsx:518), `rounded-xl border border-destructive/25 bg-destructive/3 p-4 sm:p-5`, `p-4 rounded-2xl mb-5 bg-destructive/10 text-destructive` and `flex flex-col gap-3 rounded-lg border border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/6 p-4`. Radius spans rounded-md, rounded-lg, rounded-xl and rounded-2xl; border opacity spans /20, /25 and /30; background spans /3, /5, /6 and /10; padding spans p-3, p-4, px-3 py-2, px-3 py-2.5, px-3.5 py-3 and px-4 py-3. bg-destructive/3 and bg-destructive/6 are not steps on Tailwind's opacity scale, so they are one-off arbitrary values. The success side has the same problem plus a second syntax split: `bg-[hsl(var(--success)/0.1)]` and `bg-[hsl(var(--success))]/10` both appear for the same colour, and the success banner exists at rounded-md and rounded-lg with px-3 py-2, px-3 py-2.5 and px-3.5 py-3. AUDIT-013#dup-14 filed the state-management half of this (50 components hand-roll a useState banner pair while a full Radix toast stack serves one consumer); this is the visual half and it stands whichever way that decision goes.
findings.impact: Error and success feedback is the highest-stakes UI in the product because it appears when something has gone wrong, and it looks different on every screen it appears on. Nothing signals "this is the app telling you something" consistently. A designer changing the error treatment has to touch 53 files and will miss some, and the two off-scale opacities mean two of the banners are already a shade nobody chose deliberately.
findings.recommendation: Add components/shared/inline-alert.tsx exporting `InlineAlert({ tone, title, children, onDismiss })` with tone in error | success | warning | info. One geometry: `flex items-start gap-2.5 rounded-lg border px-3.5 py-3 text-sm`. One tone table using the dsn-01 foreground tokens: error `border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/10 text-[hsl(var(--destructive-text))]`, success `border-[hsl(var(--success))]/30 bg-[hsl(var(--success))]/10 text-[hsl(var(--success-text))]`, warning `border-[hsl(var(--warning))]/30 bg-[hsl(var(--warning))]/10 text-[hsl(var(--warning-text))]`, info `border-primary/25 bg-primary/5 text-foreground`. Include the leading lucide icon (AlertTriangle / Check / AlertTriangle / Info) and role="alert" so every call site gets the announcement free. Migrate in batches by directory, starting with components/profile (the setError/setSuccess tree at components/profile/types.ts already threads one pair everywhere, so it is the cheapest) and app/teams/page.tsx:518, app/profile/page.tsx:695, app/repos/page.tsx:333 and app/attack-surface/page.tsx:45. Standardise the token syntax on `bg-[hsl(var(--success))]/10` (Tailwind opacity modifier) rather than the two-syntax mix, and delete the bg-destructive/3 and bg-destructive/6 arbitrary values.

findings.title: Six modal scrims and five modal card geometries, and two of the scrims are opposite colours in light mode: bg-black/80 versus bg-background/80
findings.description: Extends AUDIT-013#dup-07, which inventoried the sixteen hand-rolled modals for missing focus trap, Escape and scroll lock. The visual half was not recorded.
