Six distinct scrims ship: `fixed inset-0 z-50 bg-black/80` (components/ui/dialog.tsx:23, alert-dialog.tsx:20, sheet.tsx:24); `bg-black/60 backdrop-blur-xs` (components/admin/features/engine-feedback-manager.tsx:838, ip-rules-manager.tsx:273, staff-list.tsx:290 and :634, teams-list.tsx:168, gift-subscription-modal.tsx:66); `bg-black/50 backdrop-blur-xs` (components/profile/tabs/profile-billing-tab.tsx:1534); `bg-background/80 backdrop-blur-xs` (components/shared/onboarding-tour.tsx:121, components/shared/notification-center.tsx and the scanner modals); `bg-background/95 backdrop-blur-xs` (the mobile nav drawers); and none at all (components/scanner/ai-choice-modal.tsx wrapper). In dark mode black/80 and background/80 look similar. In light mode --background is 213 25% 90%, so bg-black/80 dims the page to near-black while bg-background/80 washes it to near-white: two modals opened one after another invert the whole screen. The cards differ too: components/ui/dialog.tsx:39 is `border bg-background p-6 shadow-lg sm:rounded-lg max-w-lg`; the admin hand-rolls are `bg-card border border-border rounded-xl p-6 shadow-2xl`; components/scanner/ai-choice-modal.tsx:41 and crawl-url-selector.tsx:107 are `rounded-md border border-border bg-card shadow-lg`; components/shared/onboarding-tour.tsx:127 is `rounded-md shadow-2xl`; components/shared/notification-center.tsx:133 is `rounded-2xl shadow-2xl`. So the surface is bg-background or bg-card, the radius is lg, md or 2xl, and the shadow is lg or 2xl. design-language.md D1 records that shadows in this system are near-invisible (shadow-xs) and that rounded-2xl is reserved for one flagship block.
findings.impact: Opening two dialogs in a session, for example the AI choice modal on /dashboard and then the crop dialog on /profile, shows two different products, and in light mode the page behind them goes dark for one and light for the other, which reads as a rendering bug rather than a style choice. It also means the eleven hand-rolled modals AUDIT-013#dup-07 wants migrated onto Radix cannot be migrated without a visible change, which is a reason the migration keeps not happening.
findings.recommendation: Pick one scrim and put it in components/ui/dialog.tsx: `fixed inset-0 z-50 bg-background/80 backdrop-blur-xs` reads correctly in both themes, unlike bg-black/80, and it is already what the newer in-app modals use. Change dialog.tsx:23, alert-dialog.tsx:20 and sheet.tsx:24 to it. Set the card to `border border-border bg-card p-6 shadow-lg sm:rounded-xl max-h-[90vh] overflow-y-auto` (bg-card, not bg-background, so the panel separates from the scrim; rounded-xl per dsn-03) at dialog.tsx:39 and alert-dialog.tsx:37. Then migrate the eleven hand-rolled modals AUDIT-013#dup-07 lists onto it, starting with components/admin/users/gift-subscription-modal.tsx:66, which sits in the same directory as a Dialog-based sibling. Drop shadow-2xl everywhere; it appears nowhere in the reference work.

findings.title: Seven visual treatments for a row of tabs, only two of which use the Radix Tabs primitive, and /profile's sidebar is /admin's with the focus ring removed
findings.description: Extends AUDIT-011#prof-01 (which filed /profile's mobile tab strip for having no accessible name below 640px) with the rest of the class. Seven treatments: (1) components/ui/tabs.tsx:16-33, a segmented control on `bg-muted p-1` with an active `bg-background shadow-xs` at rounded-sm, h-10, px-3 py-1.5, imported by exactly two files (components/admin/features/ip-rules-manager.tsx:29 and system-settings-manager.tsx:12); (2) components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:896-916, the same idiom hand-rolled at a different size, `flex gap-1 rounded-md bg-muted p-1` with active `bg-card shadow-xs`, rounded, px-2.5 py-1, text-xs; (3) app/assets/page.tsx:160-183, a third segmented variant, `inline-flex rounded-md border border-border bg-card p-0.5` with active `bg-primary text-primary-foreground`, a solid brand fill where the other two use a neutral raise; (4) components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx:29-44, underline tabs, `flex gap-1 border-b border-border/50` with `-mb-px border-b-2 border-primary px-3 py-2`, and no role or aria-current at all since they are Links; (5) components/docs/docs-code-tabs.tsx:30-47, underline plus fill plus top radius, `rounded-t-lg` with active `bg-secondary/30 border-b-2 border-primary`, px-4 py-2; (6) app/profile/page.tsx:723-739, the mobile strip, underline again but at px-3.5 py-3 with a `border-b border-border/80` rail rather than /50; (7) app/profile/page.tsx:743-768 and app/admin/page.tsx:1052-1097, the desktop vertical sidebar, `bg-primary/10 text-primary font-medium` pills at rounded-lg. Treatment (7) is nearly the same code twice: admin uses px-2.5 py-2 and includes `focus-visible:outline-hidden focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring` at :1076; profile uses px-3 py-2.5 and has no focus classes at all, so on /profile the eight sidebar links receive no visible focus except whatever the global :focus-visible rule at app/globals.css:370 supplies, and the sidebar widths differ (lg:w-48 versus lg:w-52).
findings.impact: Tabs are the primary navigation idiom of the signed-in product and there is no such thing as "a tab" here. /assets renders its scope toggle as a solid blue pill, which under design-language.md's accent-restraint doctrine spends the page's one accent on a filter switch; two segmented controls that are visually the same are built two different ways so a keyboard fix lands on one; and the vertical sidebar that /profile and /admin share was copied rather than extracted, which is how /profile lost the explicit focus ring.
findings.recommendation: Two shared components, not seven. (a) components/shared/segmented-control.tsx wrapping Radix Tabs with the components/ui/tabs.tsx:16 geometry plus a size prop ("sm" giving px-2.5 py-1 text-xs for dense use); replace components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:896 and app/assets/page.tsx:160 with it, and change the assets active state from bg-primary to the neutral `bg-background shadow-xs` raise the primitive already uses. (b) components/shared/section-nav.tsx holding the vertical sidebar markup currently duplicated at app/profile/page.tsx:743 and app/admin/page.tsx:1052, taking `items`, `groups` and `width`, with admin's focus-visible classes and admin's px-2.5 py-2, and use it on both pages. Keep the underline treatment for cross-page navigation only (components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx), give it `aria-current="page"` on the active Link, and switch components/docs/docs-code-tabs.tsx to the same underline geometry (drop rounded-t-lg and bg-secondary/30) so there is one underline tab and one segmented tab in the whole product. AUDIT-011#docs-11's tabpanel/aria-controls fix should land on (a) once, not on each copy.

findings.title: The onboarding tour is the most AI-generated-looking surface in the product and it is the first thing every new account sees: a chart-ramp rainbow of icons, icon-in-a-rounded-square, font-bold and Title Case SaaS copy
findings.description: components/shared/onboarding-tour.tsx:24-79 defines eight steps and gives each one a colour off the chart ramp: step 2 text-[hsl(var(--chart-2))] (160 degrees, teal), step 3 --chart-3 (30, orange), step 4 --chart-4 (280, purple), step 5 --chart-5 (340, pink), then --chart-2 and --chart-3 again for steps 6 and 7. That fails tell-tale 4 (primary is blue and rationed, accent on at most two elements per section) and misuses the chart ramp, which app/globals.css:197-201 defines for data series, as UI decoration; the repetition at steps 6 and 7 proves the colours encode nothing. The icon is then set in a tinted rounded square at :215-221, `inline-flex p-2 rounded-md bg-muted/50` plus the step colour, which is the exact icon-in-a-rounded-square grammar CLAUDE.md and design-language.md E1 name as the giveaway; every one of the eight steps gets one, and the sidebar at :175-200 repeats the coloured icon a second time per step. :223 uses `text-lg font-bold`, a weight design-language.md B3 records as appearing nowhere in the reference work, and :127 uses shadow-2xl on a rounded-md card, failing tell-tales 7 and 10. The copy fails F1's voice rules outright: "Your all-in-one web vulnerability scanner. Let's walk you through the key features so you can get the most out of VulnRadar" (:28), "Scan Any Website" (:32), "Track Your History" (:39), "Team Collaboration" (:65), "You're All Set!" (:72), "Integrate VulnRadar into your CI/CD pipeline for continuous security monitoring" (:53), "Happy scanning with VulnRadar!" (:74). Every title is Title Case where the product's own headings are sentence-case declarative statements ("This is a finding, in full", "What actually happens when you hit scan"), and every description states a benefit rather than a mechanism.
findings.impact: This modal is the first VulnRadar interface a new user ever sees, before the dashboard. It sets the expectation for the whole product and it contradicts every rule the landing page follows, so a visitor who was sold by the landing copy meets a generic onboarding carousel one click later. The rainbow is also the only place in the app where four unrelated hues appear together, which undermines the accent restraint the rest of the product maintains.
findings.recommendation: Keep the structure, which is genuinely good (a named step list on the left rather than a dot pager, and the docblock at :143-145 says why), and fix the surface. Delete the `color` field from every entry in STEPS and render all icons at text-muted-foreground with the active one at text-primary, so the accent marks position and nothing else; that also removes the last two consumers of --chart-2 through --chart-5 outside a chart. Delete the `inline-flex p-2 rounded-md bg-muted/50` icon plate at :215 and put the icon inline before the title at h-4 w-4. Change :223 to `text-lg font-semibold tracking-tight text-balance` and :127 to `rounded-xl shadow-lg` (see dsn-09). Rewrite the eight titles as sentence-case statements and the bodies as mechanism, in the voice of design-language.md F1: for example step 2 "Paste a URL and hit Scan" / "310 checks run in parallel against the live response. Every finding comes back with a stable ID and a config snippet you can paste.", step 3 "Every scan is kept" / "Filter by URL or tag. Tag a scan production or staging and the tag survives a rescan.", step 4 "Diff two scans of the same URL" / "Same URL, same finding IDs, so the diff is the list of things that actually changed.", step 8 "Go run one" / "Nothing else to configure." Remove "all-in-one", "Happy scanning" and the CI/CD sentence.

findings.title: Two callout components with overlapping variant names map warning to two different colours and use border-2, a width used nowhere else in the system
findings.description:
components/docs/docs-callout.tsx:22-47 and components/legal/legal-callout.tsx:10-26 are two callout components with a `variant` prop whose vocabularies overlap but do not match: docs has info | warning | success | error, legal has warning | danger | info. `warning` exists in both and resolves to different colours: docs uses --warning (38 degrees) at :34-36, legal uses --severity-medium (45 degrees) at :12-14. `error` and `danger` are the same thing under two names. The geometry is unrelated too: docs is `rounded-r-lg border border-l-4 border-border/50 p-4` with a coloured left rule, a 3.5 icon and a text-xs font-semibold label, and its docblock at :14-19 explains the choice ("the left rule does the work; there is no icon-in-a-rounded-square, because four of those down a page is decoration"). Legal is `max-w-prose rounded-xl border-2 p-5` with no icon and a text-base font-semibold h3. border-2 appears on exactly one other non-decorative element in app/ and components/ (an avatar ring and a spinner), so it is a one-off width. Both are correct on tokens, so this is purely a grammar split. It also produces a heading-level inconsistency: the legal callout emits an

inside legal sections that already have their own h3s, while the docs callout emits a

.
findings.impact: A reader who goes from /docs/self-hosting (which uses the docs callout heavily) to /legal/acceptable-use sees the same kind of aside drawn with a different border weight, a different radius, no icon and no coloured rule, and the warning aside changes hue. The duplicated vocabulary also means a future "add a note about X" ticket gets two different implementations depending on which directory it lands in.
findings.recommendation:
Delete components/legal/legal-callout.tsx and re-export DocsCallout from components/shared/callout.tsx (moved out of components/docs/ since two sections use it), mapping the two legal call sites: app/legal/acceptable-use/page.tsx:51 variant="warning" stays warning, app/legal/dmca/page.tsx:62 variant="info" stays info, and app/security/page.tsx:63 variant="info" stays info. Keep the docs geometry and the four-variant vocabulary (info | warning | success | error), since it is the one with a written rationale and 60-odd call sites. Add an optional `as="h3"` prop if a legal callout genuinely needs to be a heading in the document outline; otherwise leave it as the

label the docs version uses. Retire the name `danger`.

findings.title: The profile Social tab and the two OAuth profile modals are a brand-chrome island: full-bleed vendor gradients, decorative white blobs, text-white and font-bold, unlike anything else in the app
findings.description: components/profile/tabs/profile-social-tab.tsx:604 opens the Discord card with `relative bg-linear-to-br from-[#5865F2] via-[#4752C4] to-[#3C45A5] px-6 py-5` and :777 opens the GitHub card with `relative bg-linear-to-br from-[#24292e] via-[#1b1f23] to-[#0d1117] px-6 py-5`, both with `titleClassName="text-white"` and `subtitleClassName="text-white/70"`, a `h-10 w-10 rounded-xl bg-white` icon plate at :154, a `bg-white/15 backdrop-blur-xs ring-1 ring-white/20` plate at :607 and a `bg-white/20 text-white border-white/30` badge at :622. components/modals/discord-profile-modal.tsx:90-125 and components/modals/github-profile-modal.tsx:97-125 go further: a full-bleed brand header, three absolutely positioned `rounded-full bg-white/20` decorative circles at :92-94 and :99-101, a `border-4 border-background ring-4` avatar at :120, `text-xl font-bold text-white` at :107 and `text-2xl font-bold` at :125. Nowhere else in app/ or components/ is there a gradient header, a decorative blob, a border-4 ring or text-white outside a scrim. The rest of the product paints on bg-card with a border and spends colour on one element per section. The literal hexes are legitimate third-party brand colours (design-language.md A3 permits them), so the problem is not the values, it is the composition: five nested branded surfaces to say "you can sign in with Discord".
findings.impact: /profile is one of the two or three most-visited signed-in pages, and its Social tab looks like a different design system dropped into a slot. The gradient headers also make the two cards the loudest thing on a page whose actual content (2FA, API keys, billing) is quieter, so visual weight is inverted against importance. The three floating white circles are pure decoration in a product whose illustration doctrine (design-language.md E2) is "the actual mechanism of the product, rendered as itself".
findings.recommendation: Bring both cards back to the house grammar and keep the brand colour as a single accent. Replace the gradient header at profile-social-tab.tsx:604 and :777 with the standard card header used elsewhere in the tab tree, `flex items-center gap-3 border-b border-border/60 px-5 py-4`, holding a `h-9 w-9 rounded-lg` plate filled with the vendor colour (bg-[#5865F2] / bg-[#181717]) and the vendor glyph in white, then `text-base font-semibold text-foreground` for the label and `text-xs text-muted-foreground` for the subtitle; that keeps the brand recognisable in exactly one element per card. Drop titleClassName / subtitleClassName / headerClassName from the OAuthIdentityCard props entirely once both callers stop overriding them. Keep the connect button's brand fill at :721 and :780 (it is the one action that should read as the vendor's) but drop shadow-xs. In components/modals/discord-profile-modal.tsx and github-profile-modal.tsx, delete the six decorative `bg-white/20` circles at :92-94 and :99-101, replace the gradient header with the same bordered header, change `text-xl font-bold text-white` to `text-lg font-semibold text-foreground` and `border-4 ... ring-4` to `ring-2 ring-border`.

findings.title: The AI chat renders code blocks and inline code on bg-black/30, which is a mid-grey slab on the light theme instead of the documented code surface
findings.description: components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:226 renders every markdown <pre> in an assistant reply as `bg-black/30 border border-border/30 rounded-md p-2.5 my-2 text-[11px] font-mono` and :241 renders inline code as `bg-black/30 px-1 py-0.5 rounded border border-border/20`. components/ai-chat/message-content.tsx:43 and :58 carry byte-identical copies (AUDIT-013#dup-11 filed the duplication; this is about the colour). bg-black/30 is a fixed 30 percent black regardless of theme. On the dark theme it composites over --card (224 18% 9%) to something marginally darker than the panel, which is roughly the intent. On the light theme it composites over --card (213 22% 95%) to about #A7AAAD, a mid-grey slab, and the surrounding message text is --foreground at 220 20% 10%. design-language.md B2 records the shipped code idioms: inline code is `font-mono text-xs px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded bg-background border border-border/60 text-foreground` and a code block is `rounded-xl border border-border/60 bg-muted/40`. Neither uses a fixed black. The same file has one more theme-blind value at :304, `hover:bg-black/20` on the copy button.
findings.impact: Anyone using the light theme sees the AI assistant answer questions in grey boxes that look like unloaded images, and a config snippet (the thing the assistant is most often asked for) is the least readable part of the reply. The AI chat is a supported, promoted feature on every page, so this is a per-page defect on the light theme rather than a corner case.
findings.recommendation: Change all four sites (components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:226,241 and components/ai-chat/message-content.tsx:43,58) to the documented code idiom: <pre> to `bg-muted/60 border border-border/60 rounded-lg p-2.5 my-2 text-[11px] font-mono text-foreground overflow-x-auto whitespace-pre`, inline <code> to `bg-background border border-border/60 px-1 py-0.5 rounded text-[0.82em] font-mono text-foreground`. Change :304's `hover:bg-black/20` to `hover:bg-muted`. Do this as part of AUDIT-013#dup-11's collapse (delete the chat-widget copies and import the message-content ones) so the fix cannot land on only one of the two.

findings.title: The PDF report is branded in the dead cyan brand: BRAND_COLOR is #1AB3CC at 189 degrees, not the shipped blue #60a5fa
findings.description: lib/reports/pdf-report.ts:26-27 hardcodes `BRAND_COLOR = [0.1, 0.7, 0.8]` (#1AB3CC, hue ~189) and `BRAND_DARK = [0.05, 0.35, 0.4]` (#0D5966, hue ~189). Those two constants carry the entire brand identity of the document: the 8pt cover accent bar (:145), the wordmark set in 28pt (:150), the 2pt rule under it (:155), the rule at the top of every findings page (:311, :409), and the "DETAILED FINDINGS" / "Remediation Steps" / "Code Examples" subheads (:318, :370, :379). The real brand is blue #60a5fa, agreed by app/globals.css:178, lib/config/config-values.ts:188, lib/config/brand.ts:19-21, public/og-image.svg and the store PNGs, and recorded in audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md section A2. This is the same class of defect as app/global-error.tsx:10's `BRAND_TEAL = "#0891b2"` and it extends AUDIT-011#design-01, which filed only the stale CLAUDE.md line and not the two code sites that still ship the old colour. lib/config/brand.ts already exists and describes itself (:1-13) as "the single source of truth for out-of-app surfaces", but pdf-report.ts does not import it.
findings.impact: The one document that leaves the product and gets forwarded to someone who has never seen the app is teal. A reader who then visits the site sees a blue product. Nothing on the PDF matches the OG card in a Slack unfurl, the extension, or the emails, so the brand reads as three unrelated tools.
findings.recommendation: Import BRAND from lib/config/brand.ts into lib/reports/pdf-report.ts and add a hex-to-PDF-rgb helper (`function rgb(hex: string): [number, number, number]`), then replace BRAND_COLOR with rgb(BRAND.primaryLight) (#60a5fa) and BRAND_DARK with rgb(BRAND.primary) (#3b82f6). Do the same for TEXT_PRIMARY / TEXT_SECONDARY / TEXT_MUTED, which are currently three more ad-hoc greys, mapping them to a light-surface equivalent of BRAND.text / textMuted / textFaint. While there, fix app/global-error.tsx:10 the same way (a literal "#60a5fa", since that file cannot import at runtime safely, with a comment pointing at brand.ts). Add a lint-visible comment in brand.ts naming pdf-report.ts as a consumer so the next colour change catches it.

findings.title: The extension declares its design tokens three separate times and the three copies disagree with each other and with the app
findings.description: The extension defines the same `--vr-*` token set in three places with no shared source. (1) extension/src/popup.css:5-66 declares it four times over: `:root`, a `prefers-color-scheme: dark` block, `[data-theme="light"]` and `[data-theme="dark"]`. (2) extension/src/options.css:5 `@import`s popup.css, so it inherits (1), which is correct. (3) extension/src/content/reputation-card.ts:454-500 redeclares the whole set inside CARD_CSS on `.card`, and it does not agree with (1): light `--vr-bg` is `#ffffff` there against `#dfe5ec` in popup.css, light `--vr-border` is `#e2e5ec` against `#c3cbd5`, dark `--vr-bg` is `#14171f` against `#0e111a`, and `--vr-primary-fg` is `#ffffff` against `#15192a` (popup.css:15-18 documents that white-on-primary was fixed for a 2.5:1 contrast failure, and CARD_CSS reintroduces exactly that pairing). Against the app the whole extension set is approximate rather than equal: app dark --background is 224 20% 6% = #0C0E12 vs #0e111a; dark --card 224 18% 9% = #13151B vs #13161f; dark --border 224 15% 16% = #23262F vs #232735; dark --foreground 210 20% 95% = #F0F2F5 vs #eaeef4; light --foreground 220 20% 10% = #14181F vs #15192a; light --border 213 16% 78% = #BEC6D0 vs #c3cbd5. --radius is 0.5rem (8px) in the app against --vr-radius 10px / --vr-radius-sm 6px. Only --vr-primary (#60a5fa) is exactly right. The extension is a separate npm package with its own package.json, package-lock.json and vite.config.ts, so it cannot import from lib/, which is why this drifted; audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md A3.3 already recorded the store PNGs as a fourth near-black navy, and this is the code behind it.
findings.impact: The reputation card is injected into arbitrary third-party pages and is the extension surface most people see first, and it does not match the popup they open next: a white card against the popup's blue-tinted #dfe5ec, and a lighter dark card against the popup's near-black. The white-on-#60a5fa primary button inside CARD_CSS reintroduces a contrast pairing the popup already fixed as sub-3:1. Any future retune of app/globals.css silently leaves the extension behind, and there is nothing in the build that would catch it.
findings.recommendation: Create the shared abstraction that is missing: a generated token file the extension owns but does not author. (a) Extend lib/config/brand.ts with a `light` half and a `metrics` block (radius 8px, radiusSm 6px, radiusPill 999px, the font and mono stacks) so it covers both themes, since it already calls itself the source of truth for out-of-app surfaces. (b) Add scripts/build-extension-tokens.mjs that reads brand.ts and writes extension/src/tokens.css containing exactly the four blocks popup.css:5-66 hand-writes today, with a `/* GENERATED - do not edit */` banner. (c) Wire it as a `pretest`/`prebuild` step in extension/package.json so a drifted checkout fails loudly, and add it to the repo's own build so the two cannot separate. (d) Replace popup.css:5-66 with `@import url("./tokens.css")`, and in reputation-card.ts delete the redeclaration at :458-464 and :496-500, inlining the generated values via a `TOKENS_CSS` string import instead (the content script is bundled IIFE by extension/scripts/build.mjs, so a string constant is fine where a CSS import is not). The card keeps its own elevation shadow, which is justified for a floating overlay, but nothing else.

findings.title: The extension renders severity as solid-fill marketing pills, the exact treatment the app's severity badge documents itself as avoiding, from a fourth and fifth hardcoded palette
findings.description: extension/src/popup.css:454-484 styles `.badge` as `border-radius: var(--vr-radius-pill)` with a fully saturated background and `color: #fff` per severity. components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx is the app's single source of truth and its own docblock (quoted in audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md D3) says the badge uses `rounded`, not `rounded-full`, "so it does not read as a marketing pill", and encodes severity as a tinted surface at /10-/15 with a matching text colour, a border at /30-/40, an h-1.5 dot, and a weight that varies with an `emphasis` field. The extension does the one thing that idiom exists to avoid. Separately the severity hexes are declared in four places inside the extension with no single source: extension/src/lib/types.ts:24-30 (SEVERITY_HEX, used for the finding row's left rail via format.ts:9), popup.css:464-484 (.badge.*), extension/src/content/reputation-card.ts:198-203 (SeverityChips), and extension/src/popup/popup.ts:313-322 (an inline score-colour ladder). Critical (#ef4444) and high (#f97316) match --severity-critical / --severity-high exactly; low is Tailwind blue-500 #3b82f6 against the token's 210 90% 56% = #2A8FF4, and info is Tailwind gray-500 #6b7280 against the dark token's 215 15% 55% = #7B899E. `.badge.medium` also hardcodes a text colour of `#1f1f1f`, which is not a token in either system.
findings.impact: A user who scans in the extension and then opens the same scan in the dashboard sees the same finding rated with a different visual grammar: a loud filled pill in one place, a quiet tinted chip in the other. Colour is also doing all the work in the extension, where the app deliberately encodes severity by weight as well as colour, so the extension's severity read is weaker for anyone with a colour vision deficiency. The four uncoordinated copies mean a severity retune has to be applied in four files by hand.
findings.recommendation: Collapse to one source and adopt the app's grammar. In extension/src/lib/types.ts extend SEVERITY_HEX into a `SEVERITY_TONE` record mirroring components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:37-78: `{ solid, text, surface, border, emphasis }`, with solid taken from the generated token file in dsnx-03 (so low becomes #2a8ff4 and info #7b899e). Restyle popup.css `.badge` as `border-radius: var(--vr-radius-sm); border: 1px solid <border>; background: <surface>; color: <text>; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.02em; font-size: 10px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` with a 6px dot in `solid`, driven by inline custom properties set from SEVERITY_TONE rather than five CSS rules. Delete the inline colour objects at reputation-card.ts:198-203 and popup.ts:313-322 and read SEVERITY_TONE instead. Keep the finding row's 3px left rail (popup.ts:508) as is: it already matches store_1.png and reads well.

findings.title: Transactional emails carry no List-Unsubscribe header, and the in-body unsubscribe button reaches only three of the roughly fifty-five templates
findings.description: sendEmail (lib/email/email.ts:387-441) calls transporter.sendMail with from, to, subject, text, html and replyTo only. There is no `headers` option anywhere in the file and no occurrence of List-Unsubscribe. The unsubscribe affordance exists purely as an HTML button in layout() at :118-126, and it renders only when an `unsubscribeToken` is threaded through. Grepping every caller, exactly three pass one: lib/notifications/notifications.ts:105-112, app/api/v3/teams/members/route.ts:257-264 and app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:52-56. The file exports roughly 55 template functions. Every other email, including scanCompleteEmail (:1299), criticalFindingsEmail (:1396), scheduledScanCompleteEmail (:1458) and postureDigestEmail (:1562) when sent outside the notifications helper, renders a footer with no unsubscribe control at all. Compounding it, that footer's own copy at :167 reads "Choose what we send you in your account settings" and does not link to account settings; the only link in the sentence is the mailto for SUPPORT_EMAIL.
findings.impact: Gmail and Yahoo's bulk sender rules require a one-click List-Unsubscribe (RFC 8058) on mail of this shape, and mailbox providers use its absence as a spam signal. With roughly 50 registered users the volume is below the hard enforcement threshold today, so this is a deliverability risk that grows silently rather than a live outage. The user-facing half is worse and is live now: a recipient of a scan-complete or digest email is told to change a setting and given no way to get there, so the only remaining exit is the spam button, which is the single worst outcome for sender reputation. Self-hosters inherit the same footer for their own users.
findings.recommendation: In lib/email/email.ts:433 add `headers` to the sendMail call: when unsubscribeToken is present, `{ "List-Unsubscribe": `<${unsubscribeUrl}>, <mailto:${SUPPORT_EMAIL}?subject=unsubscribe>`, "List-Unsubscribe-Post": "List-Unsubscribe=One-Click" }`, and make /unsubscribe accept POST as well as GET so the one-click path works. Build unsubscribeUrl once in sendEmail and pass it into layout() rather than deriving it there. Then make the token the default rather than the exception: give sendEmail an optional `userId` and have it look up users.unsubscribe_token itself (the query already exists at lib/notifications/notifications.ts:97-100), so every non-security template gets the footer control without each call site remembering. Keep security notices (password changed, 2FA, new login) exempt by an explicit `transactional: true` flag rather than by accident. Finally, change the footer sentence at :167 to link the words "account settings" to `${APP_URL}/profile#notifications`.

findings.title: No email has preheader text, so every VulnRadar message previews in the inbox as the wordmark plus the first words of the heading
findings.description: layout() (lib/email/email.ts:107-180) opens the body with the logo lockup at :151-156 and drops straight into the card at :159. There is no hidden preview span: the file contains zero `display: none` declarations. Gmail, Apple Mail, Outlook and every mobile client render the subject followed by the first visible text of the body, so the preview line for every one of the roughly 55 templates begins with "VulnRadar" (the wordmark at :154, which is real text, not an image) followed by whatever emailHeading() emitted. For scanCompleteEmail that means the inbox line is "VulnRadar Scan complete" rather than the finding counts, which are the only thing the recipient wants from the preview. The severity chip row (severityChipRow, :315-332) that carries those counts is well below the fold of the preview.
findings.impact: Inbox open rate on the scan-complete, critical-findings and posture-digest emails is decided by a preview line that currently repeats the sender name and the subject. A recipient scanning an inbox cannot tell a clean scan from one with two criticals without opening the mail, which is the exact judgement the digest exists to let them make at a glance.
findings.recommendation:
Give layout() a second content parameter and render a preheader immediately after ``, before the logo row: `
${escapeHtml(preheader)}
` followed by a run of ` ﻿` repeated about 30 times so the client does not pull body copy in behind it. Thread a `preheader` field through SendEmailOptions alongside subject/text/html. Then set it per template with the fact the recipient needs: scanCompleteEmail -> "2 critical, 5 high on example.com. Scanned 3 seconds ago."; criticalFindingsEmail -> the top finding title; emailVerificationEmail -> "The link works for 24 hours."; email2FACodeEmail -> "Expires in 10 minutes" and never the code itself; postureDigestEmail -> the week-over-week delta. Default to the first sentence of the plain-text body when a template does not set one, which is a one-line fallback and better than nothing.

findings.title: One static OG image serves every page on the site, so a shared scan, a check page and the pricing page all unfurl identically
findings.description: app/layout.tsx:69-84 is the only `openGraph` block in the entire app/ tree (verified by grep across app/ for both .ts and .tsx), and it points every page at the single static `/og-image.png` built by scripts/build-og-image.mjs from public/og-image.svg. There are zero `opengraph-image.tsx` or `twitter-image.tsx` route files anywhere under app/. That means /shared/[token], /host/[hostname], /compare, /pricing, all 20 /docs sections and the roughly 750 /checks SEO pages every unfurl with the same card, whose baked copy reads "Scan any website for security issues in seconds. Just a URL." over a mock result for "your-domain.com" showing a risk score of 2 and five invented findings. The card itself is strong work (audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md names it one of the three best artifacts in the repo) and it is right for the site root, but it is the only card that exists.
findings.impact: Sharing a scan is a core flow, and the share link is the product's main organic distribution: a user pastes /shared/<token> into a Slack channel or a ticket, and everyone who sees it gets a generic marketing card for a fictional domain instead of the hostname and the finding counts they were being shown. The same applies to the roughly 750 /checks pages, which are the main organic SEO surface: every one of them competes for the same unfurl, so nothing in a search or social preview distinguishes "Missing HSTS" from "Exposed .git directory". This compounds AUDIT-012#fe-01, which already found only 5 of 311 routes prerendered.
findings.recommendation: Add three `opengraph-image.tsx` route files using next/og ImageResponse, all rendering one shared layout so they read as a family with the existing SVG (bg #0a0e18 to #0e1526, card #141d30, stroke #26344d, mono wordmark top-left, headline in #ffffff with the accent clause in #60a5fa, severity dots straight from the --severity-* scale exactly as og-image.svg:93-101 already does). (1) app/shared/[token]/opengraph-image.tsx: the scanned hostname as the headline, the risk score chip, and one severity distribution bar with the real counts, all read from the same share query the page uses. (2) app/checks/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx: the check title, its severity chip, and its category, from the checks registry. (3) app/host/[hostname]/opengraph-image.tsx: the hostname and its current reputation score. Set `export const size = { width: 1200, height: 630 }` and `alt` on each. Keep the static PNG as the root and docs fallback. Because ImageResponse only supports a subset of CSS, build it as flex boxes with explicit widths, and load no external font: the site already ships in system-ui (AUDIT-011#design-02), so next/og's default is consistent with the product rather than a deviation.

findings.title: app/global-error.tsx is a different design from the other two error pages: different palette, no wordmark, no status numeral, no digest, and no light mode
findings.description: app/error.tsx and app/not-found.tsx are the same composition: a mono wordmark lockup with ThemedLogo, a `border-y border-border/50 py-8` band holding a `font-mono text-6xl font-semibold tabular-nums` status numeral (500 / 404), a short honest sentence, a two-up button row, and a row of three or two `text-primary` footer links, all on tokens and all with `focus.ring` (error.tsx:33-127, not-found.tsx:15-89). app/global-error.tsx shares none of it: it opens with a 6rem circle holding a warning icon at :51-60 (an icon-in-a-rounded-shape, which CLAUDE.md and design-language E1 name as an anti-pattern), has no wordmark at all, no numeral, no error.digest block despite error.digest being available in its props, and it hardcodes `#09090b` / `#fafafa` / `#a1a1aa` / `#71717a` / `#52525b`, which is the Tailwind zinc ramp, not the app's #0C0E12 / #F0F2F5 navy. Its two links are coloured `BRAND_TEAL = "#0891b2"` (:10), a brand the product no longer has. It is also dark-only: a light-mode user hitting the global boundary drops into a black page. Inline styles there are correct and the file's own comment (:6-9) explains why, but the values are wrong, and nothing forces the two files to stay in sync. Separately, both error.tsx:103 and not-found.tsx:47 label the secondary route back as "Go to Dashboard", which is the product's internal noun for what an anonymous visitor arriving on a 404 from a search engine experiences as the scan page.
findings.impact: The global boundary is the page a user sees when the app has failed hardest, and it is the one that looks least like the product: teal links on zinc, no logo, no error id to quote to support. A user who does reach it cannot copy a digest, so a support conversation starts with "it broke" and no correlation id. The publicly reachable and indexable 404 sends an anonymous visitor to a button labelled with a word that only means something to an existing user.
findings.recommendation: Rebuild app/global-error.tsx as a literal-hex mirror of app/error.tsx rather than a separate design. Keep the inline-style constraint, but source the values from lib/config/brand.ts by transcribing them with a comment pointing back: background #0b0e14, card #12151c, border #252a34, text #f1f5f9, muted #9aa6b8, link #60a5fa (delete BRAND_TEAL). Add a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light)` block via a small inline `<style>` element in the same file so the light palette (#dfe5ec / #eff2f5 / #14181f) is available without CSS variables. Replace the 6rem icon circle with the same structure error.tsx uses: an inline SVG VulnRadar mark plus the wordmark in `ui-monospace` at 20px/600, a 1px top and bottom rule at rgba(255,255,255,0.08), a monospace 60px "500", the heading "Something broke on our end", and the digest in a bordered mono block with a copy button (navigator.clipboard, guarded). Add a comment in both files naming the other as the sibling that must match. Separately, change the secondary CTA label in both error.tsx:105 and not-found.tsx:49 from "Go to Dashboard" to "Scan a URL", which is what the page actually does and matches the voice rule that copy names the mechanism.

findings.title: The PDF report draws its severity breakdown with ASCII hash characters even though the file has a rectangle primitive, and uses a sixth hand-rolled severity palette
findings.description: lib/reports/pdf-report.ts:269-279 renders the cover page's severity breakdown as five text rows of the form `CRITICAL     3 ###`, where the bar is `"#".repeat(Math.min(count, 30))` at :271 set in Helvetica. The file defines `addRect` at :124-134 and uses it exactly once, for the 8pt cover accent bar at :145, so the vector primitive needed to draw a real bar already exists and is not used. The app's canonical aggregate is SeverityDistribution (components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:129-190), whose own docblock says it "reads as one bar rather than five cards, and the segment widths carry the information". The PDF instead produces five rows whose widths are capped at 30 and therefore stop carrying information above 30 findings. The colours come from SEVERITY_COLORS at :18-24, a sixth independent severity palette in normalized RGB triplets: critical [0.84,0.15,0.15] = #D62626 against the token #EF4444, high [0.95,0.4,0.1] = #F26619 against #F97316, medium [0.85,0.65,0.1] = #D9A61A against #E7B008, low [0.2,0.5,0.9] = #3380E6 against #2A8FF4, info [0.5,0.5,0.55] = #80808C against #7B899E. Every one of the five is wrong. This is the export-format half of AUDIT-013#dup-02, which found severity ordering redeclared across nine tables; cite that finding for the ordering, this one is about the colour values and the rendering. Checked and clean: the ordering here is correct (critical to info, from SEVERITY_LEVELS at :262-268), the findings arrive already severity-sorted from lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:711, and the "Informational" label that lib/seo/seo-ui.tsx:30 uses on /checks does not reach any export, since the PDF prints `sev.toUpperCase()` (:273) and Markdown uses "Info" (lib/reports/markdown-report.ts:36).
findings.impact: The severity summary is the first thing anyone opening the report looks at, and it is rendered as terminal art in a vector document. A target with 40 criticals and 3 lows shows a 30-hash bar next to a 3-hash bar, understating the ratio by more than 4x. The five wrong colours mean the reader cannot match a bar in the PDF to a chip in the app by eye.
findings.recommendation: Delete SEVERITY_COLORS at :18-24 and derive it from BRAND.severity in lib/config/brand.ts via the hex-to-rgb helper added in dsnx-02, so all six surfaces share one set of values. Replace the loop at :269-279 with a real bar: one `addRect(margin, y, contentWidth, 10, [0.90,0.90,0.92])` track, then a left-to-right run of `addRect` segments each `contentWidth * count / total` wide in that severity's colour, then a legend row below it built from addText plus a small `addRect(x, y, 6, 6, colour)` dot per present severity, showing `3 critical  ·  5 high` and skipping zero counts exactly as severityChipRow does in lib/email/email.ts:315-332. That is the same information architecture as SeverityDistribution and the same one already shipping in the emails, so the three agree.

findings.title: PDF text wrapping breaks only on spaces, so any URL, header value or token longer than the line budget runs off the right edge of the page
findings.description: wrapText (lib/reports/pdf-report.ts:54-68) splits the input on " " and accumulates words until the running length would exceed maxChars. When a single word is itself longer than maxChars, the branch at :59-61 flushes the current line and assigns the oversized word to `current`; nothing ever splits it, so it is pushed whole at :66 and drawn as one line by addText at :86 starting at x = margin with no clipping and no right bound. The line budget is `Math.floor(contentWidth / (size * 0.5))` (:77), which at size 8 (the size used for Evidence at :355, Risk at :359 and fixSteps at :372) is 123 characters. Findings routinely carry longer unbroken strings in exactly those fields: a full Content-Security-Policy directive list, a redirect chain URL, a query string, a base64 script hash, or a JWT-shaped token in a secrets finding's evidence. Anything past roughly 123 characters is drawn past pageWidth - margin and is lost at the page boundary.
findings.impact: The evidence string is the product's stated differentiator ("every finding carries the raw evidence it was derived from, so you can check our work rather than take it on faith"), and in the PDF the longest and most specific evidence is the evidence that silently gets truncated at the paper edge with no ellipsis and no indication anything is missing. A reader checking the work on a forwarded report sees a sentence that stops mid-token.
findings.recommendation: In wrapText, after the flush at :60, add a hard-break loop for the oversized word: while `word.length > maxChars`, push `word.slice(0, maxChars)` and continue with the remainder, preferring a break after any of `/ ? & = ; , .` within the last 12 characters of the slice so URLs and CSP directives break at a readable point. Separately, render code and evidence in a monospace font rather than Helvetica: add a third font object `<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /Courier >>` next to :449, expose it as /F3, and use it for the Evidence line (:355) and the codeExamples block (:384-387), with maxCharsPerLine computed as `contentWidth / (size * 0.6)` for that font since Courier is fixed-width. That also preserves the indentation the current word-wrap destroys in code samples. While in the file, move the `addPageHeader()` call so it fires on any page break, not only between findings: the guard at :328 only runs before each finding, so a finding that spans a page leaves the continuation page with no header rule.

findings.title: middleware 301-redirects every request to https when X-Forwarded-Proto says http, with no environment opt-out, so a self-host behind a plain-HTTP reverse proxy is unreachable
findings.description: middleware.ts:219-229 reads the first value of X-Forwarded-Proto and, when it equals "http", rewrites the request URL's protocol to https: and returns a 301. There is no env flag guarding it: the only escape hatch in this file is DISABLE_CSP=1 (:252), which throws in production (:236-243) and in any case is checked after the redirect has already returned. The same assumption is baked into the security headers built at :131 and :161: `upgrade-insecure-requests` in the CSP and `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload`, both emitted unconditionally on every response. Meanwhile docker-compose.yml:78 documents the plain-HTTP LAN case as supported: `- "${HOST_BIND:-127.0.0.1}:${APP_PORT:-3000}:3000"` with the comment "Override with HOST_BIND=0.0.0.0 to expose the app port on all interfaces (e.g. bare metal LAN)", and app/docs/setup/page.tsx:283 tells operators to set NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://localhost:3000.
findings.impact: Direct access with no proxy is fine (no header, no redirect), so this only bites the configuration the self-hosting docs actually recommend: a reverse proxy in front. An operator running nginx or Traefik on an internal network, a Tailscale/VPN-only host, or a staging box without a certificate forwards X-Forwarded-Proto: http, the app 301s to https, the proxy has no TLS listener, and every request fails. The failure looks like a redirect loop or a connection refused with nothing in the app logs explaining it, and the operator has no supported way to turn it off short of editing middleware.ts and rebuilding, which the pinned-image Docker path (AUDIT-014#host-05) does not allow.
findings.recommendation: Gate the redirect on an explicit opt-out in middleware.ts:219: skip it when `process.env.ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP === "1"`, and skip the Strict-Transport-Security header and the CSP `upgrade-insecure-requests` directive in buildSecurityHeaders under the same flag. Document the variable in .env.example next to NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL and in app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx's TLS section, with an explicit warning that it is for trusted internal networks only. Keep the current behaviour as the default so nothing changes for the hosted instance.

findings.title: FOOTER_TEXT and BACKGROUND_COLOR_LIGHT are editable admin settings documented as branding knobs, but neither value is read by any rendering code: the footer prints a different literal and the light background colour is never emitted
findings.description: lib/config/registry.ts:515-523 registers FOOTER_TEXT with help "Short line rendered in the site footer", and :505-514 registers BACKGROUND_COLOR_LIGHT with help "Hex colour reported to the browser for light mode". Both have defaults from config-values.ts (CONFIG_FOOTER_TEXT at :191, CONFIG_BACKGROUND_COLOR_LIGHT at :190), and CONFIG_FOOTER_TEXT is listed to self-hosters as a branding value to edit at app/docs/config/page.tsx:249. Neither is exported from lib/config/constants.ts: greping app/, lib/ and components/ for FOOTER_TEXT and BACKGROUND_COLOR_LIGHT returns only lib/config/config-values.ts, lib/config/registry.ts, the docs page, and components/admin/features/settings-registry-utils.ts:149 (which gives FOOTER_TEXT a multiline textarea in the editor, so real UI work was done on a field nothing consumes). The actual footer line is a different literal built inline at components/scanner/footer.tsx:229-231: `{"\u00A9"} {new Date().getFullYear()} {APP_NAME}. For authorized security testing only.` The light background colour has no consumer either: app/layout.tsx:130 emits only `themeColor: BRANDING_PRIMARY_COLOR`, and app/manifest.ts:23 uses BRANDING_BACKGROUND_DARK for background_color, so nothing ever reads the light value.
findings.impact: Two settings that appear in the admin Branding tab, appear in the published configuration reference, validate their input (min/max length, a textarea affordance for one of them), save successfully, and do nothing at all. Unlike the rest of hc-01 these are not even fixable by editing config-values.ts and rebuilding, because no code path reads the constant either. An operator customising their fork's footer will change CONFIG_FOOTER_TEXT, rebuild, see the footer unchanged, and reasonably conclude the whole config system is broken.
findings.recommendation: Pick one direction per key. For FOOTER_TEXT: render it in components/scanner/footer.tsx:230 (export FOOTER_TEXT from lib/config/constants.ts alongside the other branding exports and use it in place of the hardcoded "For authorized ..." sentence, keeping the copyright line separate), or delete the registry entry at :515, the CONFIG_ constant at config-values.ts:191, the MULTILINE_SETTING_KEYS entry at settings-registry-utils.ts:149 and the docs bullet at app/docs/config/page.tsx:249. For BACKGROUND_COLOR_LIGHT: either emit it as a second themeColor entry with `media: "(prefers-color-scheme: light)"` in app/layout.tsx:130 (Next.js metadata supports an array of themeColor objects), or delete it the same way.

findings.title: NOREPLY_EMAIL is documented and registered as the From address on automated mail, but every outgoing email's From is SMTP_FROM || SMTP_USER and the NOREPLY_EMAIL constant is read by nothing
findings.description: lib/config/registry.ts:464-471 registers NOREPLY_EMAIL with help "From address on automated mail. Must be a domain your SMTP relay is allowed to send as." app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:153 tells self-hosters to set `export const CONFIG_NOREPLY_EMAIL = "noreply@yourdomain.com"` as part of the rebrand block, and app/docs/setup/page.tsx and app/docs/config/page.tsx:225 both list it. The actual From is built at lib/email/email.ts:430: `const from = `"${APP_NAME}" <${SMTP_FROM}>`;`, where SMTP_FROM is defined at lib/config/constants.ts:648-649 as `process.env.SMTP_FROM || process.env.SMTP_USER || SMTP_USER`. NOREPLY_EMAIL never appears in that path. The exported constant at lib/config/constants.ts:642 has zero readers anywhere in app/, lib/ or components/. The runtime setting has exactly two readers, and neither is a From address: app/api/v3/contact/route.ts:136 and app/api/v3/landing-contact/route.ts:101 use `await getSetting("NOREPLY_EMAIL")` as a reply-to fallback.
findings.impact: An operator who does exactly what /docs/self-hosting:153 tells them, or who edits the field in the admin Branding tab, changes nothing about who their users see mail from. Mail goes out as whatever SMTP_USER happens to be, which for a Gmail or SES relay is often a personal or IAM-shaped address rather than a no-reply alias. Worse, the registry help text specifically warns "Must be a domain your SMTP relay is allowed to send as", implying the operator can break delivery by getting it wrong, so someone debugging an SPF or DMARC rejection will spend time on a field that is not in the code path at all.
findings.recommendation: Make the From honour the setting: at lib/email/email.ts:430, resolve the address as `SMTP_FROM || (await getSetting("NOREPLY_EMAIL"))` (sendEmail is already async and server-only), so an explicit SMTP_FROM still wins for relays that require an exact envelope sender but the configured no-reply address is used otherwise. Then either delete the unused NOREPLY_EMAIL export at lib/config/constants.ts:642 or repoint it at the same resolution. If the SMTP_FROM-only behaviour is deliberate, instead rewrite the registry help at :470 and the two docs pages to say it is only used as a reply-to on contact-form acknowledgements.

findings.title: Five OpenRouter call sites hardcode https://vulnradar.dev in the HTTP-Referer header instead of importing APP_URL, and one also hardcodes the product name, so a self-hoster's AI spend is attributed to vulnradar.dev
findings.description: Five separate places build the OpenRouter attribution headers with a duplicated literal rather than the APP_URL export that already exists for exactly this: app/api/v3/ai/chat/route.ts:278, lib/ai/auto-tag-suggest.ts:277, lib/ai/review-source.ts:204, lib/ai/scan-summary.ts:144 and lib/ai/verify-findings.ts:365, each `headers["HTTP-Referer"] = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL ?? "https://vulnradar.dev"`. lib/config/constants.ts:191 already resolves this as `export const APP_URL = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL || CONFIG_APP_URL`, and four of these five files already import from that module. The duplication also drifts on the operator: `??` only falls through on null/undefined, so an operator who sets NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL to an empty string here gets an empty HTTP-Referer, whereas APP_URL's `||` would fall back. Separately, lib/ai/review-source.ts:205 sets `headers["X-Title"] = "VulnRadar"` as a bare literal while the other four use APP_NAME.
findings.impact: OpenRouter uses HTTP-Referer and X-Title for its public app rankings and for per-app spend attribution in the account dashboard. A self-hoster who configures AI_PROVIDER=openrouter with their own key has all of their traffic reported as coming from vulnradar.dev, and their GitHub repo-review traffic reported as the app "VulnRadar", so their own dashboard cannot distinguish their usage and a third party's product name appears on their bill's attribution. It also inflates vulnradar.dev's position on OpenRouter's rankings with traffic it did not generate. Small in money terms, wrong in every other sense, and it is the kind of thing a security-conscious self-hoster notices and files an issue about.
findings.recommendation: Replace all five with `APP_URL` imported from @/lib/config/constants (already imported in lib/ai/scan-summary.ts and lib/ai/verify-findings.ts; add the import in the other three), and replace the literal at lib/ai/review-source.ts:205 with APP_NAME to match its four siblings. Better still, extract one `openRouterAttributionHeaders()` helper into lib/ai/provider.ts, which already owns the per-provider base URL table at :113-114, and call it from all five so the sixth copy cannot be added.

findings.title: CHROME_WEB_STORE_URL and FIREFOX_ADDON_URL default to VulnRadar's own published listings despite a comment saying they are empty on a fork, so a fork's JSON-LD sameAs claims another organisation's store profiles
findings.description: lib/config/config-values.ts:144 carries the comment "Empty until a store listing is live for this fork/deployment" and is immediately followed at :145-146 by a non-empty Chrome Web Store URL for extension id nbmifpplhhejdfokaglpomdnbaifngfj, and at :149-150 by a non-empty Firefox AMO URL. components/seo/structured-data.tsx:70-80 relies on the stale comment's premise: its own comment says "Store URLs are empty on a fork that has not published one, so filter(Boolean) drops them cleanly", then builds `sameAs = [SEO_GITHUB_URL, DISCORD_INVITE_URL, CHROME_WEB_STORE_URL, FIREFOX_ADDON_URL].filter(Boolean)` and emits it in the JSON-LD Organization node at :95. filter(Boolean) drops nothing, because none of the four are empty. CONFIG_DISCORD_INVITE_URL at :143 is VulnRadar's own invite (discord.gg/...) and is rendered at components/landing/landing-open-source.tsx:59, components/profile/tabs/profile-social-tab.tsx:799 and app/llms.txt/route.ts:207. All three keys are `tier: "build"` in lib/config/registry.ts, so per hc-01 the admin panel cannot change them, and per AUDIT-014#host-05 the Docker path cannot rebuild to change them either.
findings.impact: A fork or self-hosted instance publishes structured data telling Google and every answer engine that its Organization's verified profiles include VulnRadar's Chrome Web Store listing, VulnRadar's Firefox add-on and VulnRadar's Discord server. That is a schema.org sameAs assertion of identity, not a link, so it actively merges the two entities in knowledge-graph terms, which is bad for both parties. The user-facing half is the same misdirection as hc-02: the fork's own footer and llms.txt point its users at a third party's community, and /docs/extension:113 and :139 send them to a store listing that only talks to vulnradar.dev.
findings.recommendation: Set CONFIG_CHROME_WEB_STORE_URL and CONFIG_FIREFOX_ADDON_URL to "" in lib/config/config-values.ts (making the comment at :144 true) and move the real hosted-instance values into NEXT_PUBLIC_CHROME_WEB_STORE_URL / NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREFOX_ADDON_URL env overrides read in lib/config/constants.ts:200-201, which is the pattern SEO_TWITTER_HANDLE and the verification tokens already use at :216-226. Do the same for CONFIG_DISCORD_INVITE_URL at :143. Then app/docs/extension/page.tsx should hide the store buttons when the URL is empty, and components/seo/structured-data.tsx's filter(Boolean) becomes the load-bearing guard its comment already claims it is.

findings.title: API_VERSION exists so "all API calls" can be switched between versions, but 60 fetch call sites across 28 files hardcode the /api/v3 path instead
findings.description: lib/config/client-constants.ts:80-83 declares `// API VERSION - Change this to switch all API calls between versions` followed by `export const API_VERSION = "v3"`, and :87 onwards builds the whole API route map from it as template literals. That map is used correctly 157 times across app/ and components/. It is also bypassed 60 times in 28 files by fetches that spell the version out: app/admin/page.tsx alone has five (:350, :447, :456, :468, :489), plus app/admin/ai-chats/[id]/page.tsx:73, app/checkout/browser-credits/page.tsx:35, app/checkout/credits/page.tsx:34, app/checkout/github-credits/page.tsx:36, app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx:55, app/dashboard/page.tsx:273 and app/unsubscribe/page.tsx:197 among others. lib/config/config-values.ts:659-660 additionally exports CONFIG_API_CURRENT_VERSION and CONFIG_API_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS as a second, unconnected copy of the same fact.
findings.impact: The stated purpose of the constant is not achievable: bumping API_VERSION to v4 leaves 60 client calls pointed at v3, so the app would half-migrate with no compile error and no test failure, and the breakage would surface as scattered 404s in admin, checkout, dashboard and unsubscribe. This is the reverse-check shape the section is about: the operator or maintainer believes they changed one value and changed 72 percent of the call sites. Not self-host-breaking today, since v3 is the only supported version, but it makes the one migration the constant exists for unsafe.
findings.recommendation: Add the missing routes to the API map in lib/config/client-constants.ts:87 onwards (admin teams, admin updater status, ai conversations, ai info, auth me is already there, account unsubscribe) and replace the 60 literals with the map entries. Then add an ESLint `no-restricted-syntax` rule scoped to app/ and components/ that flags any string literal matching `/api/v\d`, so the 61st cannot be added silently. Also collapse CONFIG_API_CURRENT_VERSION into API_VERSION so there is one source of truth rather than two.

findings.title: docker-compose.yml mounts no persistent volume for backups or uploads, and /app is root-owned while the process runs as uid 1001, so the app cannot even create the directories its own docs promise
findings.description: Static analysis. The production compose declares one volume, postgres_data (:114-116), and the app service (:52-112) mounts none. Two directories the app writes to are therefore on the container's throwaway writable layer: BACKUP_DIR, which defaults to join(process.cwd(), "backups") in both app/api/v3/admin/backup/route.ts:27 and scripts/backup-db.mjs:184, and the legacy avatar directory join(process.cwd(), "data", "avatars") in lib/uploads/avatar-migration.ts:48. Neither exists in the image, and neither can be created at runtime: the runner stage sets WORKDIR /app as root (Dockerfile:68) before switching to USER nextjs (:102), and the COPY --chown flags at :76-79 only chown the copied children, so /app itself stays root:root and a uid-1001 process cannot mkdir inside it. scripts/backup-db.mjs:200 calls mkdir(backupDir, { recursive: true }) and would fail with EACCES. .env.example:49-51 explicitly warns "On a container this MUST be a persistent/mounted volume, otherwise every backup is lost on the next rebuild/redeploy", and app/docs/setup/page.tsx:684 documents `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d` as the update command, which recreates the container. docker-compose.dev.yml:62-66 does mount avatar_data_dev and its comment says "See docker-compose.yml's avatar_data volume comment", a comment and volume that do not exist in docker-compose.yml.
findings.impact: Backups taken from the admin panel or by cron inside the container land nowhere durable, and would fail on the permission error before that. An operator who follows the .env.example advice has no volume to point BACKUP_DIR at, and BACKUP_DIR is not forwarded to the container anyway (host-03). The dev compose's cross-reference tells the next maintainer a comment exists that does not.
findings.recommendation: Add `backup_data:/app/backups` and `avatar_data:/app/data/avatars` volumes to the app service in docker-compose.yml with matching top-level volume entries, and add `RUN mkdir -p /app/backups /app/data/avatars && chown -R nextjs:nodejs /app/backups /app/data` to the Dockerfile runner stage before USER nextjs at :102. Fix the dangling cross-reference in docker-compose.dev.yml:63.

findings.title: The self-updater advertises itself as supported inside Docker but writes into a root-owned /app as uid 1001, runs a migrate script the image does not contain, and any success is discarded by the documented update command
findings.description: Static trace. isUpdaterSupported() (lib/updater/environment.ts:8-17) returns unsupported only when process.env.VERCEL is set; there is no container detection, so both app/api/v3/admin/updater/status/route.ts:37 and .../apply/route.ts:56 report the updater available inside the official image and the admin UI offers it. runUpdateJob then sets appRoot = process.cwd() (lib/updater/apply.ts:206), which is /app, and calls copyTreeOverlay(sourceRoot, appRoot) at :261 to write the release's full source tree there. /app is root:root because WORKDIR /app runs as root at Dockerfile:68 and the process runs as USER nextjs (uid 1001) from :102, so creating new top-level entries such as /app/lib or /app/app fails with EACCES, while pre-existing chowned files such as /app/package.json and /app/next.config.mjs would be overwritten in place first (overwriting an existing file needs write on the file, not the directory). The job then fails with a raw permission error after package.json has already been replaced with the new release's copy while node_modules and .next are still the old build. Even if the copy succeeded, the npm-ci step at :325 and the `npm run db:migrate -- --yes` step at :353 run against a tree with no scripts/ (host-02), and the final log line at :369 asks the admin to run `npm run build` and restart, which in a container means the next `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d` (app/docs/setup/page.tsx:684) throws the whole writable layer away. AUDIT-013#cov-06 recorded that this pipeline has 0% test coverage and AUDIT-013#migrate-01 that the migrate step it invokes stamps 3.0.0 on a schema missing 11 tables; this finding is about the updater being reachable at all in the deployment shape where it cannot work.
findings.impact: A self-hosting admin sees an in-app Update button, clicks it, and gets a half-applied file copy plus an opaque EACCES in the job log, with package.json now describing a version whose code is not installed. In the worst case they then follow the log's advice and restart, and the update silently disappears on the next image pull.
findings.recommendation: Extend isUpdaterSupported() in lib/updater/environment.ts to detect a container (existence of /.dockerenv, or an explicit CONTAINER/VULNRADAR_UPDATER_DISABLED env var set in the Dockerfile) and return supported: false with a reason pointing at `docker compose pull`. If in-container updating is wanted instead, chown /app to nextjs:nodejs in the runner stage and ship scripts/ (host-02).

findings.title: API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY is defaulted to an empty string in compose instead of being a required substitution, so a missing key produces a crash-looping container rather than a compose-time error naming the variable
findings.description: Static analysis. lib/config/env.ts:19-26 requires API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY to be exactly 64 characters, and instrumentation.ts:33-35 calls validateEnv() as the first thing register() does, so an empty value throws before anything else. docker-compose.yml:61 passes it as `${API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY:-}`, which substitutes the empty string when the variable is absent from .env. Compare docker-compose.yml:23, where POSTGRES_PASSWORD uses `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?Set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}` and compose refuses to start with a named error. The result of the inconsistency is that the one variable .env.example:27 ships blank by design (API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY= with no value) is also the one that fails latest and least legibly: `docker compose up -d` reports success, and the operator has to run `docker compose logs app` on a restart-looping container to find the zod message. The Dockerfile comment at :41-44 explains the deliberate decision not to set a build-time placeholder so operators must inject a real key, which is right, but the compose file then undoes the loud failure that decision was meant to produce.
findings.impact: The single most commonly missed self-host variable produces a container that reports as started and then crash-loops, indistinguishable at the `docker compose ps` level from the empty-database crash-loop in host-01. The operator has to correlate two different failures from the same symptom.
findings.recommendation: Change docker-compose.yml:61 and docker-compose.dev.yml:51 to `${API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY:?Set API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY in .env (64 hex chars: node -e \"console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('hex'))\")}` so the failure happens at compose parse time with the generation command in the message.

findings.title: The admin 'update password' action enforces a hardcoded 8-character minimum, bypassing the admin-configurable PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH (12) and the strength gate every user-facing path applies
findings.description: Every user-facing password path resolves the live setting and then runs the strength analyzer: app/api/v3/auth/signup/route.ts:68-:72 and :88-:89, app/api/v3/auth/reset-password/route.ts:36-:41 and :46-:47, app/api/v3/auth/update/route.ts:316 and :301-:302, app/api/v3/auth/staff-invite/[token]/route.ts:156 and :170-:171. All four call getSetting('PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH') (default CONFIG_PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH = 12, lib/config/config-values.ts:314, admin-editable at lib/config/registry.ts:2130) and reject analyzePassword(pw).score < 3. The admin case 'update_password' at app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:732-:753 does neither: it validates only `typeof newPassword !== 'string' || newPassword.length < 8`, hashes, writes, and revokes sessions. There is no getSetting call and no analyzePassword call anywhere in that branch.
findings.impact: On a deployment where the operator raised PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH to meet a policy, an admin resetting a user's password can still set an 8-character password, and 'Password123' passes because the analyzer never runs. The account then holds a credential the deployment's own configured policy forbids, and the audit log records it as a normal update_password action.
findings.recommendation: In app/api/v3/admin/route.ts's update_password case, replace the literal 8 with `await getSetting('PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH')` and add the same `analyzePassword(newPassword).score < 3` rejection the other four routes use, so all five password write paths share one policy.

findings.title: Three transactional emails hardcode the expiry number in their body copy while the actual expiry is read from an admin-editable setting
findings.description: email2FACodeEmail(code) at lib/email/email.ts:1167-:1181 writes 'It expires in 10 minutes' at :1170 and :1176. The row it describes is inserted with `NOW() + ($4 * INTERVAL '1 minute')` where $4 is getSetting('EMAIL_2FA_CODE_EXPIRY_MINUTES') (app/api/v3/auth/2fa/email-send/route.ts:72-:74, app/api/v3/auth/login/route.ts:227-:230, app/api/v3/auth/oauth/[provider]/callback/route.ts:419-:421). The default is 10 (lib/config/config-values.ts:273) and the key is admin-editable at lib/config/registry.ts:2200. billingVerificationCodeEmail(code) at :1183-:1200 does the same with 'It expires in 5 minutes' (:1186, :1192) against BILLING_VERIFY_CODE_EXPIRY_MINUTES (default 5, config-values.ts:1220, registry.ts:894, read at app/api/v3/billing/verify/send/route.ts:61). teamInviteEmail(teamName, inviteLink, invitedBy) at :586-:609 says 'The invite expires in 7 days' (:598, :604) against TEAM_INVITE_EXPIRY_DAYS (default 7, config-values.ts:1042, registry.ts:2715, read at app/api/v3/teams/members/route.ts:209). None of the three template functions accepts an expiry parameter, so the copy cannot follow the setting.
findings.impact: An operator who tightens the 2FA code window to 5 minutes for a compliance requirement ships an email that tells every user it lasts 10, and users report the code 'expiring early' as a bug. The team-invite case is worse in the other direction: lengthen it to 30 days and recipients still see 'expires in 7 days' and discard a live invite.
findings.recommendation: Give each of the three templates an expiry argument (email2FACodeEmail(code, expiryMinutes), billingVerificationCodeEmail(code, expiryMinutes), teamInviteEmail(teamName, inviteLink, invitedBy, expiryDays)) and pass the value the call site already resolved for the INSERT. The call sites all have it in scope one line above.

findings.title: The Discord sign-in path hardcodes the email 2FA code expiry as SQL INTERVAL '10 minutes' while the other three insert sites read the admin setting
findings.description: Four code paths insert into email_2fa_codes. Three parameterize the expiry from getSetting('EMAIL_2FA_CODE_EXPIRY_MINUTES'): app/api/v3/auth/2fa/email-send/route.ts:74, app/api/v3/auth/login/route.ts:230, app/api/v3/auth/oauth/[provider]/callback/route.ts:421, each using `NOW() + ($4 * INTERVAL '1 minute')`. The fourth, sendDiscordEmail2FACode in lib/discord/discord-utils.ts:28-:31, writes `NOW() + INTERVAL '10 minutes'` as a literal inside the SQL string with no getSetting call anywhere in the file. It is live, not dead: app/api/v3/auth/discord/callback/route.ts:314 invokes it on the real Discord sign-in flow for any account with email 2FA enabled.
findings.impact: The admin panel's 'Email 2FA code expiry' control silently applies to three of four sign-in flows. Set it to 3 minutes to harden the deployment and a Discord sign-in still issues a 10-minute code, which is exactly the window the operator tried to close. Set it to 15 and a Discord user's code dies at 10 with no explanation.
findings.recommendation: In lib/discord/discord-utils.ts, read `await getSetting('EMAIL_2FA_CODE_EXPIRY_MINUTES')` and use the same `NOW() + ($4 * INTERVAL '1 minute')` parameterized form the other three sites use.

findings.title: The admin content table buckets the 0-10 danger score at 4 and 7 while the engine's tiers and the two other renderers use 5 and 8, so a 'safe' host shows amber and a 'caution' host shows red
findings.description: lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts's getDangerScore anchors the score to the safety tier: tierBase safe 0 / caution 5 / unsafe 8 (:312-:316) and tierCap safe 4 / caution 7 / unsafe 10 (:317-:321). So the bands are safe 0-4, caution 5-7, unsafe 8-10. Two renderers encode exactly that: components/host/danger-score-trend-utils.ts:19-:23 (`score >= 8` critical, `score >= 5` medium, else success), covered by tests/components/host/danger-score-trend.test.ts:30-:41 which assert 4 is success and 7 is medium; and extension/src/lib/badge.ts:27, whose doc comment at :18-:24 records that an earlier extra yellow band at 3-4 was removed precisely because it disagreed with the tier. components/admin/features/content-manager.tsx:367-:371 reimplements the buckets inline as `danger_score >= 7` destructive, `danger_score >= 4` severity-medium, else muted. A score of 4 (top of the safe band) renders amber and a score of 7 (top of the caution band) renders red.
findings.impact: The admin Public Scans table disagrees with the host trend chart, the browser extension badge, and the engine's own verdict on the same number for the same host. An admin triaging the public-scan corpus by colour is looking at two off-by-one bands, and the regression the extension explicitly documented fixing is live again in the admin panel.
findings.recommendation: Promote tierColorForScore out of components/host/danger-score-trend-utils.ts into a shared module (it has no host-page dependency) and call it from components/admin/features/content-manager.tsx:367 instead of the inline ternary. Better still, export the two boundaries from lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts so the engine, the two web renderers and extension/src/lib/badge.ts all read one pair of numbers.

findings.title: Both user-visible scoring engines, the safety verdict and the SSL letter grade, are built entirely from unnamed literals with zero registry entries, so the false-positive rate is untunable
findings.description: getSafetyRating decides safe/caution/unsafe from four bare comparisons: criticalExploitWeight >= 1 (:260), highExploitWeight >= 2 (:264), mediumExploitWeight >= 3 (:276), highHardeningWeight >= 5 (:282). getDangerScore adds SEVERITY_WEIGHTS critical 4 / high 2 / medium 1 / low 0.3 / info 0.05 (:298-:304), the tierBase and tierCap tables (:312-:321), a fallback weight of 0.1 (:327), and the multipliers 1.5 exploitable / 0.15 hardening / 0.05 other (:335-:337). getEngineConfidence adds a base of 97, a 94 timed-out variant (:368), a per-severity averaging table (:373-:379), a default confidence of 85 for a finding that carries none (:385), and a 0.3/0.7 blend with a floor of 50 (:392-:394). lib/scanner/ssl-grade.ts is the same story: deductions of 55, 70, 40, 20, 10 and 5, bonuses of 3, and the letter cutoffs 95/80/65/50/35 at :231-:236. A grep of lib/config/registry.ts for 'safety', 'danger' or 'confidence' returns only the three ADAPTIVE_CONFIDENCE / ENGINE_FEEDBACK entries (registry.ts:2731-2751), none of which touch any of the numbers above. The per-check static confidence values are equally scattered as literals across roughly 40 files (lib/scanner/checks/page-checks/links.ts:124 confidence 45, disclosure.ts:135 confidence 55, framework-fingerprint.ts:111 confidence 92, and so on).
findings.impact: An operator running VulnRadar against a fleet where five missing hardening headers is normal has no way to stop every host being labelled 'caution'; the only lever the admin panel offers is turning adaptive confidence on or off. A security team that wants a stricter or looser bar has to fork lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts, which puts them off the upgrade path for a scanner whose whole value is the checks it ships.
findings.recommendation: Name and export the four getSafetyRating comparison thresholds and the two ssl-grade letter tables as CONFIG_ constants in lib/config/config-values.ts and register them in lib/config/registry.ts under the existing scanner section, the same way SCANNER_THREAT_INTEL_API_TIMEOUT_MS and ENGINE_FEEDBACK_NOISE_THRESHOLD_PERCENT already are. The scoring weights themselves can stay as named constants without registry entries; the tier boundaries are the ones an operator actually needs.

findings.title: Four security-relevant rate limits are inline numeric literals that never reach the admin registry, unlike the seventeen that do
findings.description: lib/rate-limiting/rate-limit.ts:247-:276 exposes seventeen named rate limits, each carrying a `limit` name so checkRateLimit resolves the live admin override (registry keys RATE_LIMIT_*_MAX_ATTEMPTS / _WINDOW_MINUTES). Four call sites bypass that entirely by passing raw numbers: app/api/v3/auth/forgot-password/route.ts:49-:53 (per-email reset cap, maxAttempts 3 / windowSeconds 60*60), app/api/v3/auth/signup/route.ts:130-:134 (per-email signup cap, 5 / 60*60), app/api/v3/domains/route.ts:69-:73 (domain add, 20 / 3600) and app/api/v3/domains/[id]/verify/route.ts:39-:42 (domain verify, 30 / 3600). None of the four has a registry key. This is distinct from AUDIT-009#dup-01, which was about routes importing the wrong RATE_LIMITS export; lib/config/constants.ts:352-:360 records that collision as resolved. These four never reference either export.
findings.impact: An operator responding to a signup-flood or reset-flood incident can tighten every limiter in the admin panel and still leave the two per-email counters, which are the ones that actually stop the attack described in each site's own comment, at their compiled values. The two domain limiters are the documented numbers in app/docs/api/page.tsx:843 and :876, so the docs also become uneditable truth.
findings.recommendation: Add four entries to RATE_LIMIT_DEFAULTS and RATE_LIMITS (forgotPasswordEmail, signupEmail, domainAdd, domainVerify) in lib/rate-limiting/rate-limit.ts with matching registry keys, then spread them at the four call sites the way every other limiter does.

findings.title: The CLI's default 300-second timeout is the single-scan budget, so `vulnradar scan --crawl` in CI exits 1 as 'Timed out' on a crawl the server still has 600 seconds left to finish
findings.description: cli/lib.mjs:5-:14 declares DEFAULTS with `timeout: 300` and `crawl: false`. cli/vulnradar.mjs:64 turns that into `const deadline = Date.now() + opts.timeout * 1000` and the poll loop at :65-:85 gives up at the deadline, printing 'Timed out after 300s waiting for scan ${scanId}.' at :88-:90 and calling process.exit(1) at :91. Server-side, 300 is exactly CONFIG_SCAN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (lib/config/config-values.ts:544) for a single-URL scan, but a crawl runs under CONFIG_CRAWL_SCAN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 900 (:551), enforced by the crawl watchdog at lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:361-:364. The CLI passes --crawl through but never adjusts its own deadline, and neither cli/lib.mjs:130 ('Give up waiting for the scan (default 300)') nor app/docs/cli/page.tsx:135 and :154 warns that --crawl needs a larger --timeout.
findings.impact: A CI job that runs `vulnradar scan --crawl` against a site of any size fails red on a scan that is still running and will complete successfully. The user sees a timeout error, the pipeline blocks the merge, and the scan quietly finishes and lands in history a few minutes later, which reads as the tool being unreliable rather than as a default being wrong.
