First, make the account reference a link everywhere it appears: support-inbox.tsx:253, audit-log.tsx:422-445 and :499-516 (keep the existing filter-by-target action as a secondary control and make the name itself the link), plus error-logs-manager and email-logs-manager once those rows carry a user id. Reuse the exact anchor pattern already at app/admin/page.tsx:1467-1482, href `/admin?tab=users&user={id}` with the ctrl/meta passthrough so middle-click opens a real tab. This requires the routes behind those panels to select the user id alongside the email; support-tickets already joins the owner.

Second, and better for the ticket case specifically, add an account slide-over rather than a navigation. Extract the Overview card from components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:513-700 (avatar, plan and role badges, the four quick stats, the security chips) into an `<AccountSummary userId>` component that fetches `GET /api/v3/admin?section=user-detail`, and mount it in a Sheet from the ticket header. The operator sees plan, quota, disabled state and recent scans without leaving the thread: task A drops from seven clicks to one.

findings.title: Sending a staff invite that grants the admin role takes one unconfirmed click, while resetting one settings value to its default opens a modal
findings.description:
handleSendInvite (components/admin/staff/staff-list.tsx:156-186) POSTs to /api/v3/admin/staff-invites straight from the Send invite button at :718-730. There is no confirmation dialog anywhere in that file: a grep for confirm in staff-list.tsx returns nothing. The role select at :702-711 is populated from INVITABLE_STAFF_ROLES (:79-83), which excludes only USER and SUPER_ADMIN, so `admin` is selectable. Server side, app/api/v3/admin/staff-invites/route.ts:49 calls requireAdmin() and nothing else: no password re-auth.

Compare the equivalent action through the other path. Granting a role via PATCH /api/v3/admin is in PASSWORD_GATED_ACTIONS (components/admin/config.ts:308-326, which lists set_role, make_admin and remove_admin), so the caller must re-enter their own password, and the client puts it behind AdminPasswordConfirmDialog (user-detail-panel.tsx:2804, :2852). Same privilege, two paths, opposite friction.

At the other end, routine reversible actions are gated. system-settings-manager.tsx:756-767 opens a full ConfirmDialog to delete one stored override so a setting falls back to its default. security-alerts-manager.tsx:399-442 opens a SaveConfirmationModal with a two-row change-diff table to mark an alert reviewed. backup-manager.tsx:121-137 starts a real pg_dump child process with no confirmation at all, which is the right call for a non-destructive but expensive job and shows the panel has no consistent rule.

Note AUDIT-012#auth-03 and #authz-10: the invite email links to /staff-invite/[token], a page that does not exist, so today no invite can actually be accepted. That caps the current exposure but does not change the interaction design, and the moment that page ships the gap is live.
findings.impact: The panel's confirmation weight does not track risk, which trains operators to click through dialogs. The one action that hands out administrative access to an arbitrary email address is the one with the least friction, and it bypasses the password re-auth that the codebase already built for exactly this privilege change.
findings.recommendation:
Set the rule by consequence, not by history.

Needs confirmation plus admin password re-auth (add `send_staff_invite` to PASSWORD_GATED_ACTIONS in components/admin/config.ts:308 and enforce it in app/api/v3/admin/staff-invites/route.ts alongside requireAdmin): sending a staff invite; every action already in that Set.

Needs confirmation, no password: delete team (already correct, teams-list.tsx:516-526), send or resend a broadcast (already correct, mass-email-manager.tsx:683), block a user from a security alert, purge a host, revoke a share, delete scans for a blocked value, clear the error or email log, import a settings file.

Does not need a modal: reset one setting to its default (system-settings-manager.tsx:756, make it an inline undo toast instead, the value is recoverable), mark a security alert reviewed (security-alerts-manager.tsx:399 when action is manual_review, drop the change-diff table and make Resolve immediate with an Undo in the toast), revoke a pending staff invite (staff-list.tsx:185, already unconfirmed and correctly so), start a backup (already unconfirmed and correctly so).

findings.title: The admin user detail page presents 21 support actions as identical icon-in-rounded-square cards in a three-column grid, so Delete Account is visually one peer of Clear Avatar
findings.description:
The Support Actions card (components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:1872) renders 21 ActionCard instances across four `grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-2` blocks headed Session and Security (:1891), Usage and Limits (:2017), Account Management (:2107) and Danger Zone (:2324). ActionCard itself (components/admin/shared/action-card.tsx:47-58) is an `h-9 w-9 rounded-lg` tinted square holding an `h-4 w-4` icon, then a label and a caption. That is the exact construction audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md tell-tale 5 marks as a fail, and CLAUDE.md's What to avoid list names twice (generic icon-in-rounded-square for every feature item, and grids of identical icon cards). The landing page, the yardstick, has zero instances of it across nine sections.

The only separation between the four groups is a `text-[10px] uppercase tracking-wider text-muted-foreground` line. Delete Account (:2460), Delete All Scans (:2407), Delete Webhooks (:2425) and Delete Schedules (:2442) sit in a grid of the same geometry as Clear Avatar (:2149) and Reset AI Usage (:2047); the only difference is a destructive border tint from the `variant` branch at action-card.tsx:38-40.

The page also names two different things the same. tocItems at :502-510 offers Account Management as one of five jump targets, pointing at the card with id account-management at :816 whose heading is Account Management (:821). Inside Support Actions, a different group is also headed Account Management (:2107). The jump list sends you to the wrong one.
findings.impact: The operator's eye has no ranking to follow, so finding one action out of 21 is a linear scan of a uniform grid rather than a glance. It also flattens risk: the most destructive action in the product renders at the same size, in the same grid, with the same affordance as clearing an avatar. And the page's own jump list points at the wrong Account Management.
findings.recommendation:
Rebuild Support Actions as a divided list, the pattern design-language.md D4 records as the house idiom, and split the destructive set out.

1. Replace the three non-destructive grids with one `divide-y divide-border/50` list. Each row is `flex items-center justify-between gap-3 py-3`: label and one-line description on the left in `text-sm` and `text-xs text-muted-foreground`, an `h-8` ghost button on the right. Drop the icon squares entirely. Keep the three group headings as `border-t` section rules.
2. Add a filter input above the list that matches on label, since 17 rows is past the point of scanning. This is what actually cuts task C's time-to-find.
3. Move Danger Zone (:2324-2470) out of the grid into a separate card below Support Actions with `border-destructive/20`, collapsed by default behind a Show destructive actions disclosure, rows rendered as `variant="destructive"` buttons rather than cards.
4. Rename the Support Actions subgroup at :2107 to Account State, so it stops colliding with the Account Management card at :821, and verify the tocItems entry at :504 still resolves to id account-management.

findings.title: The scan result view renders the findings list last, below the verdict summary and up to eight secondary panels including a screenshot, a DNS table and a notes editor
findings.description:
ScanResultDetail is the shared body for all four scan-result surfaces (dashboard, history, /shared/[token], /host/[hostname]). Its render order (components/scanner/scan-result-detail.tsx:118-237) is: redirect warning, ScanSummary (:142), afterSummary slot (:144, the host trend chart), CrawlPagesInfo (:146), then the More about this host block (:150-210) holding ScreenshotPanel, ResponseHeaders, DnsRecordsPanel, PortScanPanel, ThreatIntelPanel, SoftwareInventoryPanel, the subdomain slot and the panelFooter slot, and only then ResultsList at :220.

On the owner's own scan the panelFooter is HistoryTagsCard plus HistoryNotes (dashboard-results.tsx:251-267), and both are fully expanded cards, not collapsed rows, so the block between the summary and the first finding is up to six collapsed accordion headers plus a tags card plus a notes editor. The six panels are individually correct: each is collapsed by default (`useState(false)` in screenshot-panel.tsx:83, response-headers.tsx:32, dns-records-panel.tsx:106, port-scan-panel.tsx:64, threat-intel-panel.tsx:34, software-inventory-panel.tsx:33) and three of them return null when they have no data. The problem is the ordering, not the panels.
findings.impact: The report's primary artefact, the list of things to fix, is the last thing on the page on every surface the product has. A reader who scans top-down passes a screenshot, a header dump, a DNS table, a port list, a threat feed, a software inventory, a tag editor and a notes box before reaching a single finding. On the public /host report, which is the shareable link and the SEO surface, the same ordering means a first-time visitor sees infrastructure trivia before the security result.
findings.recommendation: Reorder scan-result-detail.tsx's fragment to summary, findings, then evidence panels: move the `ResultsList` block (:220-237) to sit directly after `{afterSummary}` at :144, and move the More about this host block (:150-210) below it. Keep CrawlPagesInfo above the findings, since it selects which page's findings you are reading. Split the panelFooter slot in two: leave tags with the header chrome next to the scanned URL in dashboard-results.tsx:158-207 where it is metadata about the scan, and move HistoryNotes to the very bottom below the panels, since writing a note is something you do after reading, not before. Give the More about this host heading (:153) a one-line subtitle stating what it is, for example `Infrastructure captured during this scan`, so a reader who has already read the findings knows whether the section is worth opening.

findings.title: The findings list orders on severity band alone, and the exploitability data the scanner already computes is either buried one click deep or never displayed at all
findings.description:
The list groups by severity, not by check category, and defaults to most-severe-first: `grouped` is true at components/scanner/results-list.tsx:119, `sortAsc` is false at :118, and the comparator at :335-337 reads only SEVERITY_PRIORITY. Within a band the order is the array order the scanner produced. So the answer to whether the report ranks by severity or by category is severity, which is right, but it stops there.

The scanner computes three exploitability signals that never reach the list. `inKev` (lib/scanner/types.ts:169), true when a CVE named in the finding is in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, is rendered in exactly one place: components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:748-755, inside an opened finding. `epssScore` (types.ts:162) is rendered at issue-detail.tsx:756-763, same place. `cvssScore` and `cvssVector` (types.ts:179-181) are, by their own doc comment, backfilled onto every finding in every completed scan by attachCvssScores, and a grep for cvssScore across all of app/ and components/ returns zero render sites. Three signals stored on every finding, one of which is never shown anywhere in the product.

Consequence: a high-severity finding that CISA has confirmed is being exploited in the wild right now sorts identically to a high-severity finding that is theoretical, and the reader cannot tell them apart without opening both.
findings.impact: The report cannot answer its own core question, what do I fix first, past the granularity of five severity buckets. On a scan with a dozen highs the user picks essentially at random. The product already paid for the KEV lookup and the EPSS call (AUDIT-011#scan-04 measured the EPSS call as an uncached blocking-path request) and then throws the answer away above the fold.
findings.recommendation:
Three changes, all in components/scanner/results-list.tsx.

1. Add exploitability as the secondary sort inside each severity group, at the comparator at :335-339: after the SEVERITY_PRIORITY comparison, order by `inKev` true first, then descending epssScore, then descending cvssScore. This is a five-line change and it makes the top of each group meaningful.
2. Surface the signal on the row. Add a small `text-[10px] font-semibold uppercase tracking-wide text-[hsl(var(--severity-critical))]` chip reading `Exploited` when `inKev` is true, next to the existing severity badge, and show `cvssScore` as `font-mono tabular-nums` at the row's right edge alongside the existing category label. Follow the pill idiom in design-language.md D3 and do not add a second colour vocabulary; KEV borrows the critical token, CVSS is plain muted numerals.
3. Add an `Exploited first` toggle beside the existing sort and group toggles at :401-435, using the same button geometry, so a reader can collapse straight to the actively exploited set.

While there, add `cvssScore` to the issue-detail header at issue-detail.tsx:729-763, next to the existing KEV and EPSS chips, so the number that is computed for every finding is visible somewhere.

findings.title: The dashboard's headline risk number is a lifetime sum across every scan, so fixing an issue and rescanning makes it go up
findings.description:
The dashboard's third stat cell is Critical and high (components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:274-279), computed at :240 as `sb.critical + sb.high` from the API's severityBreakdown. That breakdown is `SUM((summary->>'critical')::int)` over every row in scan_history for the user, with no dedupe by URL and no restriction to the latest scan per host (app/api/v3/dashboard/route.ts:46-54). The same applies to Findings by severity (dashboard.tsx:417-450) and to Most common findings, whose query counts every findings array element across every scan (route.ts:55-62).

Mechanically: a user with one host carrying two high findings scans it, fixes one, rescans. Scan 1 contributed 2, scan 2 contributes 1, the dashboard now reads 3. Fixing a finding and verifying the fix strictly increases the number the page presents as the account's risk. The same effect makes Most common findings a ranking of which host the user rescans most often, not which issue is most prevalent.

The rest of the page is the same shape: Scans run and Hosts covered are lifetime counters, Started from the API is a lifetime counter, and Findings by severity is the same lifetime sum drawn as a bar list. The only element that answers what changed since I was last here is the 14-day activity strip (:289-337), and it charts scan volume, not findings.
findings.impact: The most prominent number on the signed-in landing page moves the wrong way in response to the exact behaviour the product wants: fix, rescan, verify. A user cannot use the dashboard to tell whether their security posture improved this week, which is the only reason to open a dashboard rather than the history list.
findings.recommendation:
Change what the dashboard aggregates, not how it draws it; the drawing already follows the design language (one inline strip, one severity bar, no card grid).

1. In app/api/v3/dashboard/route.ts, replace the severityBreakdown query at :46-54 with a latest-scan-per-URL aggregate: `SELECT DISTINCT ON (url) summary FROM scan_history WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY url, scanned_at DESC` as a CTE, then sum over that. Now Critical and high means open critical and high across the hosts you track, and it falls when you fix something.
2. Apply the same CTE to the topVulnerabilities query at :55-62, so Most common findings ranks by how many distinct hosts have the issue.
3. Add a delta. Compute the same latest-per-URL sum as of seven days ago and return it as `severityBreakdownPrior`, then render the change beside the Critical and high cell using the TrendBadge component that already exists at dashboard.tsx:118. That is the what changed since I was last here answer, in the component the page already has.
4. Retitle the cell to `Open critical and high` so the semantics are stated, and keep Scans run and Hosts covered as lifetime counters since those are honest as totals.

findings.title: Four signed-in pages open with the same four-cell aggregate strip, and on /history three of its four cells are derivable from the other one and from the heading directly above it
findings.description:
The identical container `grid grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-4 gap-px bg-border overflow-hidden rounded-md border border-border` opens four pages: /dashboard (components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:148 and :261), /history (components/history/history-stats.tsx:66), /shares (components/shares/shares-stats.tsx:64) and /assets (components/assets/assets-stats.tsx:53). All four hold four cells built from a `Cell` or `StatCell` function with the same body: a StatIcon, a `text-2xl font-semibold tabular-nums` number and an `text-[11px] text-muted-foreground` label. Adjacent pages therefore open with an identical template, which is what CLAUDE.md's layout-patterns-to-avoid list and design-language.md tell-tale 6 call out.

On /history it is also redundant content. The h1 subtitle at app/history/page.tsx:579-585 already reads `{scans.length} scans on record`, and the very next element, HistoryStats at :588, opens with a Total scans cell holding the same `scans.length` (history-stats.tsx:55, :67-72). Of the remaining three cells, Came back clean (:56) and Had findings (:57) are complementary filters of the same array and sum back to the first cell, so three of the four numbers carry no information the reader did not already have. Only Findings total (:58-61) is new.
findings.impact: Every signed-in list page looks like every other signed-in list page above the fold, and the strip costs a screenful before the reader reaches the thing the page is for. On /history specifically the reader is shown the same number twice in adjacent elements.
findings.recommendation:
Keep the strip where it earns its place and vary the others, following the nine-different-layouts principle the landing page demonstrates.

- /history: delete HistoryStats entirely (remove the import and the call at app/history/page.tsx:588, delete components/history/history-stats.tsx and its skeleton branch). Fold the one number worth keeping into the existing subtitle at :579-585: `{n} scans on record, {m} findings across them, kept for {retention}`. That removes a component and a screenful and loses nothing.
- /shares: replace the four cells with the SeverityDistribution bar from components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:129-190, whose own docblock explains it reads as one bar rather than five cards. Clean, warnings and unsafe are proportions of one whole, which is exactly what that component is for.
- /assets: same substitution, the four cells are Hosts scanned plus a three-way safety split.
- /dashboard: keep the strip. It is the one page where four independent counters are the right shape, and it is already paired with the activity sparkline rather than standing alone.

findings.title: The domain portfolio UI renders at two URLs because the move to /attack-surface never removed the copy in the profile Developer tab
findings.description:
DomainsSection (components/profile/tabs/developer/domains-section.tsx:97, 515 lines) has two importers. app/attack-surface/page.tsx:54 renders it as a top-level page reached from the HistoryViewTabs strip, and that file's own doc comment at :12-14 states the reason: the domain-verification UI already existed but was buried in the profile Developer tab, so this surfaces it as its own tab. components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx still lists it as a fourth sub-tab at :82 and still renders it at :754, reachable at /profile?tab=developer&dtab=domains.

The two surfaces are the same component with different chrome: /attack-surface gives it an h1, an explanatory paragraph about what verifying a domain unlocks, and the History/Assets/Attack Surface/Public Scans tab strip; the profile copy gives it a sub-tab label and nothing else. Verifying a domain from one and then opening the other shows two independently fetched copies of the same list.
findings.impact: Two URLs for one feature, so a user who bookmarks or is linked to one never discovers the other, and the profile copy is the worse of the two because it has none of the explanatory framing that tells the user what domain verification is for. It also doubles the maintenance surface: any change to the surrounding affordances has to be made twice or the two drift.
findings.recommendation: Finish the move. Delete the `{ id: "domains", label: "Domains", icon: ShieldCheck }` entry from DEVELOPER_SECTIONS at components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:82 and the `{activeSection === "domains" && ...}` branch at :754, and drop domains from the DeveloperSection type. In its place put a one-line pointer in the Developer tab's header, `Verified domains moved to Attack surface`, linking to ROUTES.ATTACK_SURFACE, so anyone with the old deep link lands somewhere useful. Add a redirect from ?tab=developer&dtab=domains to /attack-surface in the dtab handling at app/profile/page.tsx:110-120 for the same reason.

findings.title: Scheduled scans and webhooks sit three levels deep under Account Settings while Badge, a one-time embed snippet, is a top-level nav item
findings.description:
The signed-in nav (components/scanner/header.tsx:26-33) has eight entries: Scanner, History, Repos, Compare, Shared, Teams, Badge, Profile. Badge is /badge, a page that generates an embeddable status badge snippet, which a user configures once and never returns to. It sits at the same level as History.

Scheduled Scans, the product's recurring-monitoring feature with its own documentation section at app/docs/scheduled-scans, is at /profile?tab=developer&dtab=schedules: Profile in the nav, then the Developer tab (app/profile/page.tsx:645-651), then the Scheduled Scans sub-tab (profile-developer-tab.tsx:81). Three levels, and the page it lives on is titled Account Settings (app/profile/page.tsx:679). Webhooks are in the same place (:80). Both are things a user returns to, filed under settings; the header's DEVELOPER_HREF constant at header.tsx:23 already acknowledges the depth problem by hard-coding a shortcut to the Developer tab, but that shortcut is not a nav item.

Meanwhile Assets, Attack Surface and Public Scans are sub-tabs of History via HistoryViewTabs (components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx:8-13), which is a sensible grouping and shows the pattern already exists.
findings.impact: The two features that create recurring engagement, scheduled scans and webhooks, are the hardest to find, and the one that creates none is the most prominent. A user setting up monitoring has to guess that a scheduling feature lives behind a tab called Developer inside a page called Account Settings.
findings.recommendation: Rebalance without adding nav width. Replace the Badge entry at components/scanner/header.tsx:32 with a Monitoring entry pointing at a new /monitoring route, and give that route the same HistoryViewTabs-style sub-strip holding Scheduled Scans, Webhooks and Alerts. Move SchedulesSection and WebhooksSection there by import, exactly as app/attack-surface/page.tsx:54 already does for DomainsSection, and remove their sub-tab entries from DEVELOPER_SECTIONS (profile-developer-tab.tsx:80-81) so the Developer tab is left with API Keys alone, at which point rename that tab to API. Move Badge to the profile Social tab, next to the other share and embed affordances, which is where a one-time embed snippet belongs.

findings.title: The finding detail puts two owner-workflow widgets above the evidence and the fix, so How to fix it, which its own comment calls the reason anyone opened this page, is the sixth block down
findings.description:
IssueDetail renders in this order (components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:701-948): Back to findings button (:703), the header with severity, category, KEV and EPSS chips, title and description (:719-787), the AI verdict banner when present (:789-813), FindingFeedback (:815-822), RemediationControl (:824-832), Evidence (:834), the What this means / If left unfixed pair (:837-859), and finally How to fix it at :862. The comment above that section, at :861, reads: Fix: the reason anyone opened this page.

FindingFeedback and RemediationControl are both always-expanded owner cards, not collapsed rows. RemediationControl (:265-530) is a five-option status picker plus assignee, due date and note fields with its own save button. FindingFeedback is an accuracy-reporting widget. Neither is what the reader came for on a first read; both are things you do after you have decided the finding is real, which requires reading the evidence and the fix that sit below them.
findings.impact: Every reader scrolls past a status picker and a feedback prompt to reach the fix. On a scan with a dozen findings that is a dozen scrolls past the same two widgets. It also inverts the workflow: the page asks you to triage the finding before it has shown you the evidence for it.
findings.recommendation: Reorder the fragment in components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx so it reads header, evidence, what it means, how to fix, working example, then triage. Concretely, move the FindingFeedback block (:815-822) and the RemediationControl block (:824-832) to sit after the Working example section at :888-926 and before the references footer at :928. Keep the AI verdict banner (:789-813) where it is, since it changes how you read the evidence. To keep triage one click away without keeping it at the top, add a compact status pill to the header row at :729-763 showing the current remediation status and scrolling to the control when clicked, using the pill idiom at design-language.md D3.

findings.title: The DNS and port panels are the only entry points to their own on-demand fetch endpoints, but both return null when the data is missing, so a scan run without the port-scan option can never have one added
findings.description:
Port scanning is opt-in at scan time: lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:330-333 only starts the sweep when the `portScan` flag is set, and :841 spreads `portScan` into the result only when a result exists. DNS is the same shape, :767-769 reads a per-host cache and :838 spreads `dnsRecords` only when it is populated, so a cold cache means no records on the scan.

Both panels bail out when the field is absent: components/scanner/port-scan-panel.tsx:104 is `if (!portScan) return null;` and components/scanner/dns-records-panel.tsx:187 is `if (!records || groups.length === 0) return null;`. The refresh control lives inside those panels (port-scan-panel.tsx:76-99, dns-records-panel.tsx:120-140), so it disappears with them.

The endpoints behind those controls have no such precondition. app/api/v3/history/[id]/ports/route.ts:87-104 checks ownership, resolves the hostname, runs the sweep and merges the result into result_meta whether or not one was there before; the DNS route at app/api/v3/history/[id]/dns/route.ts:72-74 does the same. The prop doc in scan-result-detail.tsx:62 even describes the intent as `Owner only: enables the DNS + port on-demand fetch/refresh controls`, but on-demand fetch is unreachable: the control can only ever refresh data that already exists.
findings.impact: A user who ran a scan without ticking the port-scan option, or whose DNS cache was cold, has no way to add that data to the saved scan. Their only recourse is running the whole scan again, which spends a daily quota slot and produces a second history row for the same host, polluting the aggregates described in qols-10. A working, owner-gated, rate-limited endpoint ships in the product and no user can reach it in the case it was built for.
findings.recommendation: Give both panels an empty state instead of returning null, on the owner's own surfaces only. In components/scanner/port-scan-panel.tsx, replace the `return null` at :104 with a guard that returns null only when `scanId` is undefined (the public /shared and /host views pass no refreshScanId), and otherwise renders the same collapsed header row with the headline `Not scanned` and the existing refresh button relabelled `Run port sweep`. Apply the identical change to components/scanner/dns-records-panel.tsx:187, labelled `Fetch DNS records`. Both reuse the existing premium gate and upgrade-modal branches unchanged. Update the prop doc at scan-result-detail.tsx:62 to match what the control then actually does.

findings.title: Nothing replaces the removed timer: the status endpoint returns progress but no findings, so the wait has no payoff until it ends
findings.category: scanning page: replacement for the timer
findings.description:
This is the replacement proposal AUDIT-011#scan-05 asked for and did not specify. It is scoped strictly to what the API produces today, verified by reading the endpoint and the producer.

WHAT EXISTS NOW. GET /api/v3/scan/status/[id] builds `responseBody` at app/api/v3/scan/status/[id]/route.ts:162-168 with exactly five keys while a scan is live: `status`, `currentCategory`, `categoriesCompleted`, `categoriesTotal`, `elapsedMs`. On `completed` it adds the whole `result`; on `failed` it adds `error`. The client reads three of them (app/dashboard/page.tsx:146-150) and drops `elapsedMs` on the floor. The producer is `createProgressTracker` in lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts:117-139, whose hook fires once per CATEGORY as `start` and once as `done`, writing `current_category` / `categories_completed` / `categories_total` to scan_history. The hook's type is `(category: string, phase) => void` (lib/scanner/types.ts:352-355): it carries no check count and no findings.

So of the three things the brief asked for, the API supports exactly one and a half today:
1. "Which check category is running" -- SUPPORTED. `currentCategory` is a real Category id, and lib/scanner/category-meta.ts already holds a client-safe label and one-line blurb for all 18, importing only a type.
2. "How many of the ~797 checks are done" -- NOT SUPPORTED as checks; supported as families. `categoriesCompleted / categoriesTotal` is real and exact (route.ts:332-339 derives the denominator from `getPlannedSyncCategories` plus `getPlannedAsyncBranches`, never estimated). Per-check counts are computed but only at the end: lib/scanner/engine.ts:206-211 returns `checksRun` and `checksSkipped` after the whole loop, and they reach the user only as the "Checks run" stat on the finished view (components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx:295-302).
3. "Findings streaming in as discovered" -- NOT SUPPORTED AT ALL. `runSyncChecks` accumulates into a local `findings` array (engine.ts:156) and nothing reads it until `dedupeFindings` at :205. scan_history.findings is written once, by `finalizeScanSuccess` (scan-jobs.ts:240-245), in the same UPDATE that flips status to `completed`. There is no partial-findings column and no partial-findings field on the poll response.
findings.impact: After scanui-01 the card would show a family name, a bar, and nothing else, which is less information than the clock it replaced. The scan is the product's whole value proposition and for its entire duration the user is shown zero of its output, then all of it at once, then (until AUDIT-011#scan-08 is fixed) a blur over the top of it. The visible work is a large part of a scanner's perceived worth and this page currently spends the wait proving nothing.
findings.recommendation:
Build it in three tiers, each independently shippable.

TIER 1, zero backend change, ship with scanui-01. Three real numbers in a mono definition list, all already on the wire:
  FAMILIES  12 / 18      (categoriesCompleted / categoriesTotal)
  RUNNING   DNS          (CATEGORY_META[currentCategory].label)
  NEXT      Email        (the next entry in the client's own planned family list)
plus the one-line `FAMILY_STEP` sentence for the running family, which is already written and is good copy ("Grepping responses for keys and tokens"). Keep those strings; they are the best thing in the current component.

TIER 2, one generated file, still no server change, gives a real check count. scripts/compile-checks-knowledge.mjs already iterates lib/scanner/checks-data/<category>.json per category (see its loop and the write at :283-286) and emits lib/config/check-stats.generated.ts, which is client-safe (`EXACT_CHECK_COUNT = 797`, `EXACT_CHECK_CATEGORY_COUNT = 18`, no runtime imports). Add one export: `export const EXACT_CHECKS_BY_CATEGORY: Record<string, number> = {...}`. The client then sums the counts of the families already marked done and renders `CHECKS 531 / 797` in `font-mono tabular-nums`, rising in real steps. Label it honestly: this counts the checks in the families that have reported, so it will slightly overstate against the final `checksRun` (page checks whose `requirementsMet` gate fails are counted as skipped at engine.ts:186-188). Either accept a final reconciliation to the real `checksRun`, or emit legacy-only counts and label the row `RULES`.

TIER 3, the real prize, and it needs a backend change. Stream findings as they are discovered:
  a) Widen `ScanProgressHook` (lib/scanner/types.ts:352-355) to `(category, phase, snapshot?: { found: number; newFindings: { severity: Severity; title: string }[] })`.
  b) In lib/scanner/engine.ts, at the `onProgress?.(category, "done")` call at :203, pass the findings pushed during that category's iteration (the loop already has them; slice `findings` from the index recorded before `onProgress?.(category, "start")` at :166).
  c) In `createProgressTracker` (lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts:117-139) append those into a new `scan_history.partial_findings JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'` column in the same fire-and-forget UPDATE that already runs there, keeping the existing `WHERE status IN ('pending','running')` guard so a late write after completion is a no-op. Add the column in instrumentation.ts beside the other scan_history additions, and to scripts/migrate (see AUDIT-013#migrate-01: this is exactly the kind of column that gets missed).
  d) In app/api/v3/scan/status/[id]/route.ts add `responseBody.partialFindings = row.partial_findings` in the live branch only (never in the `completed` branch, where `result.findings` is authoritative). Cap it server-side at ~40 entries and store only `{severity, title}`, never evidence or remediation, so a 2-second poll stays small.
  e) On completion, clear `partial_findings` in `finalizeScanSuccess`'s UPDATE so a re-poll of a finished scan does not carry two lists.
The one honesty trap: `dedupeFindings` (engine.ts:205) runs after the last category, so a streamed count can go DOWN at the end. Present the live list under the label "Found so far" and let the completed view's real summary replace it wholesale, rather than animating a number downward.

What NOT to do: do not synthesise a percentage from `elapsedMs`, and do not use `elapsedMs` at all on this screen. It is the same number scanui-01 removes, just served from the server.

findings.title: The scanning card is a boxed progress bar over a two-column grid of 20 identical status rows, which is the templated pattern the design language names, and its labels clip on a phone
findings.description:
Measured against audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md and its 14-point checklist. The scanning state is app/dashboard/page.tsx:910-922, a single centred `<div className="flex justify-center pt-10 sm:pt-16">` wrapping components/scanner/scanning-indicator.tsx.

DEVIATIONS, each verified at a line:

1. Tell-tale 5 and E1. scanning-indicator.tsx:307-344 is a `grid grid-cols-1 ... sm:grid-cols-2` of up to 20 rows, every row structurally identical: a 14px `rounded-full` glyph followed by a truncated label. That is the named anti-pattern in list form. The design language's alternatives for exactly this job are the divided list (`divide-y divide-border/50`), the mono-term `<dl>`, and the real table (D4). Four of the nine landing sections use no card grid at all.

2. Tell-tale 4, accent restraint. The doctrine is at most two accented elements per section, documented twice in code comments (landing-categories.tsx:6-11, landing-open-source.tsx:18-19). This card has: the mode pill (:262, `border-primary/20 bg-primary/10 text-primary`), the bar fill (:300, `bg-primary`), and one primary-tinted circle per completed row (:321, `border-primary/40 bg-primary/15 text-primary`) plus the running one (:322, `border-primary bg-primary`). By the last second of a full scan that is roughly 22 primary-tinted elements in one card.

3. Tell-tale 1 and C1. Section rhythm is `py-16 sm:py-20`. The scanning state uses `pt-10 sm:pt-16` with no bottom padding of its own (app/dashboard/page.tsx:911), a third value.

4. C5 radius ladder. `:259` is `rounded-md`, which resolves to `calc(var(--radius) - 2px)` via tailwind.config.mjs:75-79 and is the BUTTON radius. The spec's content card is `rounded-xl`. components/scanner/scan-form.tsx:562 and components/scanner/dashboard-error-state.tsx:182 make the same choice, so all three surfaces of this page are consistent with each other and none matches the spec.

5. C1 divider opacity. "`border-border/50` is the divider, not `border-border`. Full opacity is reserved for the footer's outer edge and card outlines." The internal dividers here are `border-b border-border` (:261) and `border-t border-border` (:307), both full opacity. The house content card (D1) uses `border-b border-border/60` internally.

6. D3 pill idiom. `:262` is `rounded border ... px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium`. The house pill is `rounded-full`, `text-[10px]`, mono or `uppercase tracking-wider`, border at /25 to /30. The severity badge is the one deliberate `rounded` exception and this is not it, so it is a third pill grammar.

7. B2 type scale, and it is also an a11y defect (filed separately as scanui-08): the card has no heading of any kind. `ScanHero` (the page's only `<h1>`) lives inside the `status === "idle"` branch at app/dashboard/page.tsx:887 and is unmounted the instant scanning starts.

8. MOBILE, the one measurable usability defect here. The row label at :331-338 is `min-w-0 truncate` inside a `grid-cols-1` column below the `sm` breakpoint, so it clips on one line with no wrap, no `title` attribute and no tooltip. The strings it clips are the longest ones in FAMILY_STEP: "Parsing page content for mixed content and inline script" (55 chars), "Probing forms & endpoints for XSS, SQLi, SSTI & more" (51), "Looking for leaked paths, versions and stack traces" (50). Derived from the class list rather than measured in a browser: at a 375px viewport the available text width is roughly 375 minus 32 (main `px-4`) minus 32 (card `px-4`) minus about 22 (glyph plus `gap-2`), so about 289px, against roughly 300 to 310px needed for 55 characters at `text-xs`. At 640px and up the same strings sit in a half-width column and clip harder. Also, at one column the list is 20 rows tall, so on a 667px phone the card runs past the fold for a state that lasts a few seconds.

9. Tell-tale 14, motion. globals.css:141-151 collapses CSS `animation-duration` and `transition-duration` under `prefers-reduced-motion`, so the bar's `transition-[width] duration-500` (:300) is covered. The `requestAnimationFrame` settle ramp at :227-248 is not: it writes `style={{ width }}` from JS over SETTLE_ANIMATION_MS and ignores the media query entirely.

10. Structural. The three states are three mutually exclusive full-page branches (app/dashboard/page.tsx:885-958). Submitting the form unmounts ScanHero, ScanForm and the whole Dashboard widget block and replaces them with one small centred card; completion unmounts that card and mounts DashboardResults. Nothing is shared between them, so the page's contents are wholly swapped twice per scan.
findings.impact: This is the highest-traffic transient surface in the product: every scan passes through it, and it is the surface the section brief singles out as reading AI-generated. The mobile clipping is a real loss of information, not a matter of taste: on a phone the user cannot read what is currently running. The three-way content swap means the page never feels like one thing filling in, which is what a scanner should feel like.
findings.recommendation:
Rebuild as one surface that transforms in place. Concretely, so a developer can build it without re-deciding anything. STRUCTURE. Keep the page container `w-full max-w-6xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6` (already `CONTAINER` at app/dashboard/page.tsx:61). Replace the `flex justify-center pt-10 sm:pt-16` wrapper with `py-16 sm:py-20` (C1 standard rhythm) and do not centre: left-align, like every other app surface. HEADING BLOCK, mirroring ScanHero's geometry so the swap from idle is a text change, not a layout change:

Scanning {hostname}

797 checks across 18 families. Findings appear here as each family reports, before the run finishes.

Pull 797 and 18 from lib/config/check-stats.generated.ts (`EXACT_CHECK_COUNT`, `EXACT_CHECK_CATEGORY_COUNT`), never hardcoded (tell-tale 8). BODY, 2-column asymmetric split (E2 idiom, mirrors the hero): `grid gap-8 lg:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_minmax(0,1.15fr)] lg:gap-12`. LEFT: the run readout, in the ResponseReadout grammar (components/shared/response-readout.tsx:161-216), which is the house signature and already renders "the literal shape of scanning". `overflow-hidden rounded-xl border border-border bg-card font-mono`. - Header, `flex items-baseline gap-2 border-b border-border/60 bg-muted/20 px-5 py-3`: `GET` in `shrink-0 font-semibold text-primary`, then `min-w-0 flex-1 truncate text-foreground` hostname, then the mode label as plain `text-xs text-muted-foreground` (drop the pill entirely; it is the least important thing on screen and it is costing an accent). - Body, `px-5 py-4`: one line of `text-sm text-foreground` carrying the current family's FAMILY_STEP sentence (keep those strings verbatim, they are the best copy in the file), then the bar, then a mono-term `
` (D4 pattern 2): `
` with rows FAMILIES `12 / 18`, CHECKS `531 / 797`, FOUND `7`, values in `font-mono tabular-nums text-foreground`. - Bar: `h-1.5 w-full overflow-hidden rounded-full bg-muted` with a `bg-primary transition-[width] duration-300 ease-out` fill. Reuse the geometry of `SeverityDistribution` (components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:129-190), which is already the canonical "one bar, not five cards" aggregate. - Family list, replacing the 20-cell grid: a `divide-y divide-border/50` list, each row `flex items-baseline justify-between gap-3 py-2`. Left is `CATEGORY_META[c].label` (lib/scanner/category-meta.ts, client-safe, 14 chars at most: "Info disclosure"), right is `font-mono text-xs tabular-nums` check count for that family. State encoded by weight, not by 20 tinted circles: pending `text-muted-foreground/50`, done `text-muted-foreground` with the count in `text-foreground`, running `text-foreground font-medium` on a row carrying `border-l-2 border-primary pl-3`. That single rail is the only accent in the list, which brings the card to three accented elements total (the `GET` word, the bar fill, the one rail). - Footer, `flex items-center justify-between gap-3 border-t border-border/60 bg-muted/20 px-5 py-2.5 text-xs`: cancel on the left as `

findings.title: The scan-failed card's primary button is labelled "Try again" but only returns to an emptied form, cancel silently drops you to idle after burning a daily scan, and authenticated scans cannot be cancelled at all
findings.category: scanning page: failure and cancel paths
findings.description:
Three separate defects on the same page's exit paths.

(a) "Try again" does not try again. app/dashboard/page.tsx:932 passes `onRetry={handleReset}` to DashboardErrorState. dashboard-error-state.tsx:279 wires the primary button to `onRetry`, and :283 wires the secondary "Back to scanner" button to the same `onRetry`. Both call `handleReset()` (page.tsx:851-872), which only resets state and clears `?scan=`. Neither re-runs anything. Worse, the form is unmounted while `status === "failed"` (it is inside the `status === "idle"` branch at page.tsx:885-907), and components/scanner/scan-form.tsx:315 initialises `const [url, setUrl] = useState("")` with no query-param seed, so remounting hands back an empty input. The error card literally displays the failed URL two elements above (dashboard-error-state.tsx:206) and the button underneath throws it away. The scanner selection survives, because `mode`, `screenshot`, `port_scan` and `active_probes` are seeded from the query string at scan-form.tsx:320-371 and are only cleared on the SUCCESS path (page.tsx:290-296).

(b) Cancel has no confirmation and no distinct state. `handleCancelScan` (page.tsx:802-808) fires the DELETE, sets `runningScanId` null and `setStatus("idle")`. The whole page snaps back to the scan form with nothing on screen saying the scan was cancelled. Meanwhile the server side is not a no-op: the DELETE handler (app/api/v3/scan/status/[id]/route.ts) calls `finalizeScanFailure(row.id, "Cancelled")`, which writes `status = 'failed'`, `error_message = 'Cancelled'` and a real `duration`, leaving the row permanently in scan_history with `findings_count = 0` and `summary = '{}'`. The daily quota was already charged at app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:394 (`incrementDailyCountCapped`) and there is no decrement anywhere in lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.ts or the scan routes. So cancelling costs one of the day's scans (25 on free) and leaves a phantom zero-finding row, and the UI tells the user neither fact.

(c) Cancel is unavailable exactly when it is most wanted. page.tsx:919 renders `onCancel={runningScanId ? handleCancelScan : undefined}`, and `setRunningScanId(scanId)` only happens at :594, after the POST round trip resolves. So for the first several hundred milliseconds of every scan there is no cancel control, and it then pops into existence, shifting the card's height by the `mt-3` plus button row at scanning-indicator.tsx:347-358. For the authenticated path the `if (!auth)` gate at :585 means `setRunningScanId` is never reached at all, so an authenticated scan, which is the slowest kind because it drives a real login first, has no cancel control for its entire run.
findings.impact: A failed scan makes the user retype the URL that is printed on screen in front of them, behind a button that promises otherwise. A cancelled scan gives no acknowledgement, silently spends one of a free account's 25 daily scans, and leaves a zero-finding row that is indistinguishable from a clean result in History (see scanui-06). An authenticated scan cannot be stopped once started.
findings.recommendation:
(a) Give DashboardErrorState a real retry. Add an `onRetry` that re-invokes `runScan` with the same `url`, `mode`, `categoryFilter`, `captureScreenshot` and `portScan` (all still held in `scanningUrl`, `scanningMode`, `scanningCategories`, `pendingScreenshot`, `pendingPortScan` at page.tsx:229-253) and keep `handleReset` on a separate `onBack` prop for the secondary button. Two buttons that call the same handler with different labels is the actual bug; one of them has to change. Do not offer retry for `kind === "rate_limit"` or `kind === "validation"`, where retrying identically cannot help; show "Back to scanner" alone there.

(b) Add a `cancelled` value to `ScanStatus` and have `handleCancelScan` set it instead of `"idle"`. Render the cancelled state per scanui-03: the readout stays, the body line becomes "Cancelled after 6 of 18 families. The partial run is in your history.", and the footer action is "Run it again". If the product intends cancelling not to cost quota, that is a separate change in `finalizeScanFailure`'s caller, but the copy must match whichever is true: if it does cost, say "This still counted against today's scans."

(c) Render the cancel control from the moment `status === "scanning"`, `disabled` with `aria-disabled="true"` until `runningScanId` is set, so its box never appears or disappears. Set `runningScanId` for the authenticated path too, or, if that endpoint genuinely cannot be cancelled, render the control with a tooltip saying so rather than omitting it.

findings.title: The status poll's fetch has no timeout or abort signal, so one stalled request leaves the scanning page frozen past its own six-minute ceiling with a bar that never moves
findings.description:
`pollScanStatus` (app/dashboard/page.tsx:128-165) loops `while (Date.now() - startedAt < maxWaitMs)` and calls `const res = await fetch(API.SCAN_STATUS(scanId));` at :142 with no second argument: no `AbortSignal`, no `AbortSignal.timeout`, no racing timer. The give-up ceiling (`SCAN_MAX_WAIT_MS = 6 * 60 * 1000` at :87, `CRAWL_MAX_WAIT_MS = 16 minutes` at :88) is only evaluated between iterations, so a single request that stalls without erroring never reaches it. The retry budget does not help either: `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_POLL_FAILURES = 3` at :126 counts thrown requests, and a hanging request never throws.

What the user sees while that happens is the worst pairing of the two signals on the card. `hasRealProgress` is already true from the last successful poll, so components/scanner/scanning-indicator.tsx:170-188 pins `targetStep` at the last reported family and the bar stops moving, while the independent 500ms interval at :148-151 keeps the elapsed clock climbing. A frozen bar next to a rising clock.

The inverse case is also mis-tuned. With `CONFIG_SCAN_STATUS_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 2000` (lib/config/config-values.ts:555) and a three-strike budget, roughly six seconds of flaky connectivity is enough to abandon a scan that is still running perfectly well server-side, and the message it throws at :157 ("Lost track of the scan while it was running.") does not mention that the scan continues and its result will appear in History. The sibling timeout message at :162-164 does say exactly that, so the good wording already exists in the same function.
findings.impact: On a train, a hotel wifi, or a phone handing off between cells, the scanning page either hangs indefinitely on a spinner-equivalent, or gives up after about six seconds and tells the user the scan was lost when it was not. Both outcomes strand a scan that the user has already been charged a daily quota unit for.
findings.recommendation: In `pollScanStatus`, pass a per-request deadline: `fetch(API.SCAN_STATUS(scanId), { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(pollIntervalMs * 4) })`. An aborted fetch throws, so it feeds the existing `consecutiveFailures` path with no other change. Raise `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_POLL_FAILURES` from 3 to about 6 (roughly 12 to 20 seconds of tolerance) and reuse the timeout branch's wording for the give-up message: "Lost the connection to this scan. It is still running, and the result will be in your history in a few minutes." Also thread an `AbortController` from the caller and abort it on unmount, which is the fix AUDIT-012#fe-09 already asked for (polling continues for up to 16 minutes after the user navigates away); one controller solves both.

findings.title: Leaving the scanning page abandons the scan with no way back, and the in-flight row then renders in Recent scans and History as a finished scan with 0 findings in 0ms
findings.category: scanning page: navigate away and back
findings.description:
The scan's entire progress state lives in the DashboardContent component: `status`, `runningScanId` and `scanProgress` are all `useState` (app/dashboard/page.tsx:204, 219, 234) and the poll loop is a local `async` function. There is no persistence, no `sessionStorage`, and nothing that queries for the user's own in-flight scans. So a soft navigation, a refresh, or a phone backgrounding the tab long enough to be evicted drops the whole thing: coming back to /dashboard shows `status === "idle"`, the empty scan form, and no indication that a scan of theirs is still running server-side. It does keep running (that is the point of the background-job design, see app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:405-419) and it does eventually complete, so the user has no way to watch it and no signal that watching would even be possible.

What they see instead is worse than nothing. The row is INSERTed as `pending` before any work starts (app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:365-379) and `scan_history.scanned_at` defaults to `NOW()` (instrumentation.ts:428), so it exists immediately and sorts to the top of every list ordered by `scanned_at DESC`. Neither list filters on status:
  - app/api/v3/dashboard/route.ts:41-44 selects `public_id AS id, url, summary, findings_count, duration, scanned_at, source FROM scan_history WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY scanned_at DESC LIMIT $2`, with no `status` predicate. This feeds the "Recent scans" widget on the very page the user just came back to (components/scanner/dashboard.tsx).
  - app/api/v3/history/route.ts:120-139 has the same shape and the same omission (`WHERE sh.user_id = $1 AND (sh.scan_type IS NULL OR sh.scan_type != 'github')`).
The column defaults at instrumentation.ts:420-423 are `summary '{}'`, `findings_count 0`, `duration 0`, and `finalizeScanSuccess` (lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts:244-248) is the only thing that fills them. So a running scan, a cancelled scan (`finalizeScanFailure` at :363-381 sets `status='failed'` but never touches `summary` or `findings_count`) and a watchdog-killed scan all render identically to a genuinely clean result: the site's name, "0 findings", "0.0s".
findings.impact: The most natural recovery action, going back to the scanner, is punished twice: the user loses the scan they were watching, and the page they land on tells them that scan found nothing. On a phone, where the browser evicting a background tab is routine, this is the normal path rather than the edge case. A cancelled scan leaves the same false clean-bill-of-health row permanently.
findings.recommendation:
Two changes, independently useful.

1. Make the lists honest. Add `status` to both SELECTs (app/api/v3/dashboard/route.ts:41 and app/api/v3/history/route.ts:120 and :129) and render non-completed rows distinctly rather than as zero-finding results: `running` and `pending` get a muted "Running" chip in place of the findings summary, `failed` gets a `text-[hsl(var(--severity-medium))]` "Did not finish" chip. Do not filter them out, because a user needs to see that a scan happened; just stop them wearing a clean result's clothes. Check whether the aggregate queries in the same file (the severity roll-up at :46-54 and the top-findings query at :55-63) should also exclude non-completed rows; they sum over `summary` and `findings`, which are `'{}'`/`'[]'` for those rows, so they are currently harmless but will silently break if partial findings are ever stored (see scanui-02 tier 3).

2. Let the user rejoin a running scan. `GET /api/v3/scan/status/[id]` already returns everything needed and is already owner-scoped (`getOwnedScan`). Either (a) write the in-flight `scanId` to `sessionStorage` in `runScan` right after `setRunningScanId(scanId)` (page.tsx:594), clear it in the `finally` at :620-622, and on mount resume `pollScanStatus` against it if the row is still `pending`/`running`, or (b) add a `?scan_job=<publicId>` param that the existing `syncFromUrl` effect (page.tsx:302-342) recognises as a third meaning alongside target and history-id. Option (a) is smaller and survives a plain refresh; option (b) additionally makes the running scan linkable. Either way the recovered state should render the same readout scanui-03 specifies, so nothing new has to be designed for it.

findings.title: The scanning state has no heading anywhere in the document, no aria-busy, and announces up to twenty polite live-region updates in two seconds while never announcing that the scan finished
findings.category: scanning page: accessibility of the transient states
findings.description:
Verified structurally by reading every component mounted during `status === "scanning"`.

1. NO HEADING. The page's only `<h1>` is in ScanHero (components/scanner/scan-hero.tsx:7), which is inside the `status === "idle"` branch (app/dashboard/page.tsx:887) and is unmounted the moment scanning begins. ScanningIndicator contains no heading element. Header (components/scanner/header.tsx) contains none. app/dashboard/layout.tsx is a passthrough. The only headings left in the document are three `<h3>` in the footer (components/scanner/footer.tsx:63, 114, 163). So while a scan runs, `<main id="main-content" tabIndex={-1}>` (page.tsx:879-883), which is the skip-link's own target, contains zero headings, and the document outline starts at h3 in the footer. The `failed` state is the same: DashboardErrorState's title is an `<h2>` (dashboard-error-state.tsx:194) with no h1 above it.

2. LIVE-REGION SPAM. scanning-indicator.tsx:279-286 puts `aria-live="polite"` on the current-step paragraph, whose text changes every time `displayStep` advances. `displayStep` is ratcheted by a `setInterval` at `MIN_STEP_DISPLAY_MS = 120` (:58, :205-212). For a scan that completes between two polls, which the component's own comment at :46-57 says is the common case, `targetStep` jumps to the end and the ratchet then fires up to 20 announcements in about 2.4 seconds. Polite announcements queue rather than interrupt, so a screen reader user hears family names still being read out after the results have already rendered.

3. NO COMPLETION ANNOUNCEMENT. Grepping components/scanner/dashboard-results.tsx and components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx finds no `aria-live`, no `role="status"` and no `sr-only` announcement. The indicator unmounts, DashboardResults mounts, and nothing tells a non-sighted user the scan is over or what it found. Focus is not moved either, so the keyboard user's focus is wherever it was, on a control that no longer exists.

4. `role="progressbar"` (:291-298) declares `aria-valuemax={steps.length}` and `aria-valuenow={displayStep + 1}`, but the visible fill is `displayPercent`, which is `(displayStep + 1) / steps.length * 92` (:219-222). At step 10 of 20 the announced value is 50 percent and the rendered bar is 46 percent. There is no `aria-busy` on the container and no `aria-valuetext` giving the family name.
findings.impact: The core flow of the product is announced as an unstructured page with no headings, then narrated as a burst of twenty queued strings, then goes silent at exactly the moment there is something to say. A screen reader user gets the least useful part of the experience loudly and the most useful part not at all. The published accessibility statement is already contradicted elsewhere (AUDIT-011#docs-07); this is the same claim failing on the highest-traffic surface.
findings.recommendation:
1. Give every state a heading, per scanui-03's heading block: `

Scanning {hostname}

` for scanning, "Scan of {hostname}" for the result, "{hostname} did not finish" for the failure, with DashboardErrorState's current `

` kept as the sub-heading beneath it. 2. Move `aria-live` off the per-step paragraph. Mark the step text `aria-hidden` and add one `

` that is throttled to the FAMILY level, not the ratchet, and reads "12 of 18 families done. Running DNS." Update it only when `categoriesCompleted` actually changes, so a fast scan produces two or three announcements instead of twenty. Put `aria-busy="true"` on the readout container while scanning. 3. Announce completion. On the `status` transition to `done`, render a `role="status"` `sr-only` region with "Scan complete. 7 findings: 1 high, 4 medium, 2 low." built from `result.summary`, and move focus to the results heading with a `ref` plus `focus()`. Do the same for `failed` with `role="alert"`. 4. Either drop `role="progressbar"` in favour of the `role="status"` text (the numbers are already on screen in a `

` after the rebuild), or make the two agree: keep `aria-valuemin=0 aria-valuemax=100`, set `aria-valuenow` to the same rounded percent the fill uses, and add `aria-valuetext={"12 of 18 families"}`.

findings.title: The scanning page, its progress component and its poll loop have no tests at all: tests/components/scanner contains exactly one file, for an unrelated helper
findings.description:
Grepping the whole tests/ tree for `ScanningIndicator`, `scanning-indicator`, `pollScanStatus` and `dashboard/page` returns nothing. `tests/components/scanner/` contains a single file, `ai-review-gate.test.ts`, which covers lib/scanner/ai-review-gate.ts and nothing on this page. So none of the following is covered anywhere: the real-progress branch versus the simulated-progress branch at scanning-indicator.tsx:170-193, the `displayStep` ratchet at :205-212, the settle ramp at :227-248, `pollScanStatus`'s consecutive-failure budget at app/dashboard/page.tsx:154-159, its max-wait ceiling at :140, the `cancelledRef` race handling at :603-629, or any of the four status branches at :885-958.

This matters specifically because scanui-01, scanui-02 and scanui-03 propose rewriting all of it. The repo has 362 test files and 89,192 test lines, so the tooling and the habit exist; this surface is simply a hole in it.
findings.impact: The highest-traffic transient surface in the product can be rewritten with no regression signal. The subtle parts, the ratchet and the two progress branches, are exactly the kind of logic that looks right and behaves wrong, and their existing behaviour is only documented in code comments.
findings.recommendation:
Write the tests before the rebuild, so they pin the behaviour worth keeping. Minimum set, all pure and fast:
  - `pollScanStatus`: returns on `completed`; returns on `failed`; throws the correct message after N consecutive rejections; throws the max-wait message when the clock passes `maxWaitMs`; calls `onProgress` with the exact fields for every successful poll. Use a fake timer plus a stubbed `fetch`; no database, per the project rule.
  - Add a case for the scanui-05 fix: a fetch that never settles must abort and count as a failure rather than hanging the loop.
  - `ScanningIndicator` render tests with `@testing-library/react`: with `categoriesTotal > 0` the family count matches the props exactly; with `categoriesTotal === 0` the indeterminate state renders (after scanui-01, no simulated step counter); the cancel control is present and disabled before `onCancel` is supplied; the live region announces once per family change and not once per ratchet tick.
  - One test asserting a heading exists in every state, which is the scanui-08 regression guard.

findings.title: A shared scan report has no per-report metadata or image: every share link is titled "Shared Scan Report", described with the site-wide app description, and carries the generic marketing OG card
findings.description: app/shared/[token]/layout.tsx:7 is the only metadata source for the route and it calls privatePageMetadata("Shared Scan Report", "/shared"). lib/seo/metadata.ts:130 expands that to pageMetadata with description = APP_DESCRIPTION (the generic site description), image = SEO_OG_IMAGE ("/og-image.png", the static marketing card), and canonical/og:url = APP_URL + "/shared", a path that has no route at all (there is no app/shared/page.tsx). app/host/[hostname]/layout.tsx:8 does the same with "Host Report" and "/host". Nothing per-report reaches the head. There is no opengraph-image.tsx anywhere in the repo and no use of next/og or ImageResponse (grepped across app/, components/, lib/, scripts/): zero dynamic social images exist. The data needed is already available server side by token: app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.ts:30 selects sh.url, sh.summary, sh.findings_count and sh.scanned_at from scan_history by SHA-256 token hash, with the expiry and revocation gates already written. The page itself cannot supply it (app/shared/[token]/page.tsx:1 is "use client" and fetches in useEffect), but the layout is a server component and can export generateMetadata({ params }). The rendering toolchain also already exists: public/og-image.svg is a 1200x630 template whose right-hand card is literally a mock scan result ("your-domain.com / RISK SCORE 2 of 10 / TOP FINDINGS"), and scripts/build-og-image.mjs rasterizes it with sharp.
findings.impact: The strongest visual asset the project owns (AUDIT-011 names the OG image one of its three best artifacts) is spent showing a fake domain and fake findings, while the real ones are one query away. A share of a genuine report previews identically to a share of the homepage, so nothing in the unfurl tells a reader that someone scanned a specific site and found specific problems. That is the entire viral mechanic of this product category, unused. Note the privacy math is favourable: whoever the unfurler is already holds the token, which grants the full report, so putting the hostname and severity counts in the head leaks nothing the link does not already grant.
findings.recommendation: Add `export async function generateMetadata({ params })` to app/shared/[token]/layout.tsx that hashes the token the same way app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.ts:24 does, selects url, summary and scanned_at, and returns pageMetadata({ noIndex: true, title: `Security scan of ${hostname}`, description: `${critical} critical, ${high} high and ${medium} medium findings on ${hostname}, scanned ${date} by VulnRadar. Open the full report.`, image: `/shared/${token}/opengraph-image` }). Fall back to the current generic strings when the token misses, is expired, or is revoked, so an invalid link leaks nothing. Then add app/shared/[token]/opengraph-image.tsx using ImageResponse from next/og (bundled with next 15.5.23, no new dependency) at size 1200x630, laid out as the right-hand card of public/og-image.svg: hostname, risk score out of 10, and the top five finding titles with severity dots in the --severity-* colours. Do the same for app/host/[hostname]/. twitter.card is already "summary_large_image" via lib/seo/metadata.ts:116, so nothing else changes.

findings.title: The 36-character title clamp on /checks pages collapses 22 distinct check pages onto 8 identical titles, and puts an ellipsis in the title of 348 of the 749
findings.description: app/checks/[id]/page.tsx:69 builds the metadata title as `How to fix: ${clamp(check.title, 36)}`, using the local clamp() at line 38 which cuts at a word boundary and appends "...". The root template then appends " | VulnRadar". I ran the exact same clamp over all 749 non-disabled entries in lib/scanner/checks-data/*.json (the set getAllChecks() returns, lib/seo/checks-content.ts:127): 348 of 749 titles come out truncated with an ellipsis, and 8 title strings are produced by more than one check, covering 22 pages. The worst is "How to fix: Permissions-Policy... | VulnRadar", which is the title of five different pages: /checks/permissions-policy-publickey-credentials-get-blocked, -ambient-light-sensor-blocked, -picture-in-picture-blocked, -window-management-blocked and -attribution-reporting-blocked. "How to fix: Missing..." is the title of three (cross-origin-resource-policy-report-only-missing, coep-missing, xpcdp-missing). "How to fix: Hard-coded secret in source..." is the title of three. "How to fix: document.cookie write missing..." is the title of three. The same string is also the og:title and twitter:title (lib/seo/metadata.ts:73, 98, 117). 84 titles still exceed 60 characters after the clamp, so the clamp does not even achieve its stated goal on those.
findings.impact: Five URLs competing for the same title on a distinct long-tail query is the classic keyword-cannibalisation shape: Search Console reports them as duplicate titles, Google picks one and demotes or omits the rest, and the five specific Permissions-Policy directives a searcher typed are invisible. Beyond the collisions, an ellipsis in the title of 46 percent of the organic surface reads as broken to a human scanning results, and the part cut off is always the part that distinguishes the page ("ambient-light-sensor", "picture-in-picture") because the shared prefix comes first.
findings.recommendation: Replace the fixed 36-character head clamp at app/checks/[id]/page.tsx:69 with a tail-preserving builder. Drop the redundant local clamp() at lines 38-43 (it is a buggier copy of clampText in lib/seo/metadata.ts:19: it omits the `lastSpace > 0` guard, so a title with no space in the first N characters loses its last character instead of being hard-cut) and import clampText. Build the title as `${check.title} fix` and clamp the whole string to 48 so the suffix fits in 60, but when the clamped result is not unique across getAllChecks(), fall back to `${check.title}` truncated from the distinguishing end, or append the category label: "Permissions-Policy ambient-light-sensor allowed" is 47 characters and needs no truncation at all. A one-time uniqueness assertion in a test over getAllChecks() (there is no test for this today) stops the collision class from coming back when checks are added.

findings.title: 682 of the 749 /checks meta descriptions end mid-sentence in an ellipsis, because the template concatenates description plus riskImpact and then hard-clamps the result to 155 characters
findings.description: app/checks/[id]/page.tsx:72 builds the description as clamp(`${check.title} is a ${severity}-severity ${label} finding. ${check.description}${check.riskImpact}`), where the comment at lines 70-71 says riskImpact is appended so terse descriptions still fill the 150-character window. Running the same construction over all 749 checks: the median length is 153 and the maximum is 157, both effectively at the cap, and 682 of 749 end with "..." because the appended riskImpact almost always overflows. No two descriptions are identical (I checked: zero duplicate groups across all 749, and zero duplicates in the raw `description` field itself), so the thin-content risk the brief asks about is not duplication here. It is that nearly every snippet Google can show is a sentence cut in half. Example shape: "<title> is a high-severity content finding. <full description>. <first two thirds of the risk sentence>...".
findings.impact: Google shows the meta description verbatim when it matches the query. 91 percent of the organic surface therefore presents a snippet that stops mid-clause, which reads as a scraped or broken page and costs click-through on the pages the whole /checks investment exists to win. The information that was cut is the risk consequence, which is the part that would make someone click.
findings.recommendation: Change app/checks/[id]/page.tsx:72 to append riskImpact only when it fits whole. Compute `const base = `${check.title} is a ${check.severity}-severity ${label.toLowerCase()} finding. ${check.description}`;` then `const desc = check.riskImpact && (base.length + 1 + check.riskImpact.length) <= 155 ? `${base} ${check.riskImpact}` : base;` and pass clampText(desc) as a final safety net. Because the raw description field is already unique for all 749 checks, most pages will then end on a complete sentence with no ellipsis at all. For the checks whose base is itself over 155 (measure after the change), shorten the boilerplate lead-in from "X is a high-severity content finding." to "High-severity content finding." which buys back the title length.

findings.title: Nine of the twenty docs pages are fully indexable with their own metadata and JSON-LD but are missing from sitemap.xml, because the sitemap hand-lists docs routes while components/docs/docs-nav.ts is the real source of truth
findings.description: lib/seo/routes.ts:25 declares STATIC_PUBLIC_ROUTES, whose header comment claims a new public page "only has to be added once and cannot end up in the sitemap while being disallowed in robots.txt". It hand-lists 11 docs routes: /docs, /docs/api, /docs/api/playground, /docs/setup, /docs/extension, /docs/self-hosting, /docs/developers, /docs/architecture, /docs/webhooks, /docs/rate-limits, /docs/config. components/docs/docs-nav.ts:13 declares DOCS_NAV, which drives the sidebar, mobile drawer, breadcrumb and pager and contains 20 entries. The nine in DOCS_NAV but not in the sitemap are: /docs/scheduled-scans, /docs/triage, /docs/teams, /docs/sharing, /docs/account-security, /docs/github, /docs/ai, /docs/reports and /docs/cli. All nine have their own layout.tsx with pageMetadata (index:true, a real canonical, keywords) plus BreadcrumbList and TechArticle JSON-LD, so they are built to rank and then left out of the discovery file. Everything else that is indexable is present: I diffed the 45 pageMetadata routes against PUBLIC_ROUTES and the docs nine are the entire gap. The generated surfaces do not have this problem because CHECK_ROUTES (line 80), CATEGORY_ROUTES (line 64) and ALTERNATIVE_ROUTES (line 72) derive from the same loaders the pages use.
findings.impact: Nine documentation pages, including /docs/cli (the page AUDIT-013#subdeps-01 flags for advertising `npx vulnradar`), /docs/github, /docs/teams and /docs/triage, are absent from the file search engines use to prioritise crawling, and carry no lastmod or priority signal. They are reachable by internal link so they will eventually be found, but they are crawled last and refreshed slowest, which is exactly backwards for the pages that answer high-intent product questions. The stated invariant of the file is also false, which means the next docs page added will silently repeat this.
findings.recommendation: In lib/seo/routes.ts, delete the eleven hand-typed `/docs*` entries and derive them: `import { DOCS_PAGES } from "@/components/docs/docs-nav";` then `const DOCS_ROUTES: readonly PublicRoute[] = DOCS_PAGES.map((p) => ({ path: p.href, priority: p.href === "/docs" ? 0.8 : 0.7, changeFrequency: "monthly" as const }));` and spread DOCS_ROUTES into PUBLIC_ROUTES alongside CHECK_ROUTES. That makes the docs sitemap entries as drift-proof as the check ones and matches the file's own stated design. docs-nav.ts is a plain data module with no client-only imports, so importing it from lib/seo/routes.ts is safe.

findings.title: Every docs child page emits two conflicting TechArticle blocks and two conflicting BreadcrumbList blocks, one pair from the parent layout describing /docs instead of the current page
findings.description: app/docs/layout.tsx renders BreadcrumbStructuredData with items [{ name: "Docs", path: "/docs" }] at line 32 and TechArticleStructuredData with title "Documentation" and path "/docs" at line 36, both outside DocsShell and therefore on every route beneath /docs. Each of the 19 child sections then renders its own pair: app/docs/cli/layout.tsx:28 emits BreadcrumbList [Docs, CLI] and line 35 emits TechArticle with url /docs/cli. So the HTML for /docs/cli carries two `application/ld+json` BreadcrumbList blocks (one a single-item trail pointing at the wrong page) and two TechArticle blocks whose `url` and `headline` disagree. The same shape exists under legal: app/legal/layout.tsx:28 emits BreadcrumbList [Legal] on every legal route, and app/legal/terms/layout.tsx:24 emits [Legal, Terms of Service] on top of it. That is 19 docs pages plus 6 legal pages carrying contradictory structured data. Separately, the child breadcrumbs start at "Docs" or "Legal" with no "Home" position 1, while the /checks pages correctly start at Home (app/checks/[id]/page.tsx:146).
findings.impact: When a page publishes two BreadcrumbList items Google treats them as alternative trails and may render either, so a docs result can show the trail "Docs" with no leaf, or nothing. Two TechArticle blocks with different `url` values on one page is the malformed case: the parent block asserts that this page is the /docs index, which contradicts the canonical the same page sets. It is exactly the sort of inconsistency that makes a validator flag the page and makes Google discard the markup rather than pick a winner, so all 25 pages lose the rich-result eligibility the markup was added for.
findings.recommendation: Move both JSON-LD blocks out of app/docs/layout.tsx into app/docs/page.tsx, so the /docs index describes itself and no child inherits them. Do the same for app/legal/layout.tsx into app/legal/page.tsx. Then prepend `{ name: "Home", path: "/landing" }` to the items array in all 19 docs child layouts and all 6 legal child layouts so the trail matches the /checks convention at app/checks/[id]/page.tsx:145-150. If the shared trail is worth keeping DRY, add a `docsBreadcrumb(leafLabel, leafPath)` helper next to DOCS_NAV that returns [Home, Docs, leaf] and call it from each child.

findings.title: The check-count sentence appended to every /checks category description is silently deleted again by the clamp on 17 of the 18 categories, so the one number that differentiates those pages never reaches the meta description
findings.description: app/checks/category/[category]/page.tsx:64 sets description = clampText(`${seo.intro} ${count} checks, each with fix steps and code.`). The comment above it (lines 59-61) says the clamp exists because "several category intros are long enough that appending the count sentence pushed them past 160". I ran clampText (lib/seo/metadata.ts:19) over all 18 CATEGORY_SEO intros in lib/seo/checks-content.ts:188: 17 of the 18 lose the appended sentence completely, and 17 of the 18 end in "...". Only `reputation` (a 139-character intro) survives, and it is the only one that keeps "3 checks, each with fix steps and code." The concatenation order guarantees this: the intros are 130 to 160 characters on their own, so a 39-character suffix appended before a 155-character clamp can never survive.
findings.impact: The eighteen category pages are the mid-tier of the SEO surface, sitting between /checks and the 749 leaves, and the only thing that differentiates their snippet from the on-page intro copy is the check count. Every one of those snippets is instead a truncated version of the intro, ending in an ellipsis. Google may then substitute its own snippet from the body, which defeats the point of writing intros tuned for the meta window at all.
findings.recommendation: Reorder the concatenation at app/checks/category/[category]/page.tsx:62-65 so the differentiator survives: `description: clampText(`${count} ${label.toLowerCase()} checks, each with fix steps and code. ${seo.intro}`)`. That leads with the number, keeps the whole count clause, and lets the intro be the part that clamps. Alternatively clamp the intro to `155 - suffix.length` first and then append. Assert in a test that all 18 rendered descriptions contain the digit count, so the regression cannot recur.

findings.title: The security badge is the product's only backlink loop and every badge points at a /shared/ URL that is Disallowed in robots.txt and served noindex, nofollow, so the inbound links are thrown away
findings.description: app/docs/sharing/page.tsx:386 publishes the embed snippet users paste onto their own sites: ``. Both halves of that snippet point at paths that robots.txt forbids: `/shared/` via lib/seo/routes.ts:121 and `/api/` via line 108, both spread into the wildcard Disallow at app/robots.ts:60. On top of that the link target itself serves `noindex, nofollow` (app/shared/[token]/layout.tsx:7 via privatePageMetadata, lib/seo/metadata.ts:85).
