More importantly, concurrent scans queue on four OS threads: with a resolver that takes 100ms, eight simultaneous scans serialize their SSRF checks and also stall unrelated filesystem and crypto work in the same process. VulnRadar runs as one persistent Node process, so this is process-wide back-pressure, not per-request.
findings.recommendation: Add a short-TTL (5-15s) in-process memo in front of `validateScanTarget` in lib/scanner/safe-fetch.ts keyed on hostname, returning the cached `SafetyCheckResult`. The TTL must stay short so the DNS-rebinding protection the function exists for is preserved -- a 10s window is still far tighter than a scan's own lifetime. Separately, set `UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE` in the Dockerfile/start script to something matched to the box (16 is a common default for I/O-heavy Node services).

findings.title: GET /api/v3/auth/me issues seven queries per call, reading the same users row three times and gifted_subscriptions twice, and it runs on every page load
findings.category: redundant queries on the hottest authenticated route
findings.description: `getSession()` at app/api/v3/auth/me/route.ts:61 already runs `SELECT ... FROM sessions s JOIN users u ON s.user_id = u.id WHERE s.id = $1` (lib/auth/auth.ts:98-104). The route then runs a six-way `Promise.all` at line 79 which reads the same users row again (lines 80-88), reads `gifted_subscriptions` (lines 96-99), and calls `getUserPlanLimits(session.userId)` (line 110) which calls `getUserPlan` (lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.ts:75) -- a third read of the users row joined against gifted_subscriptions a second time. Net: 7 queries, 6 of them concurrent out of a pool whose max is 10 (lib/config/config-values.ts:393), for data that is one users row, one badges join, and one discord row.
findings.impact: This is the endpoint `AuthProvider` calls on every page navigation, so it is the highest-frequency authenticated query in the product. Every page view costs 7 database round trips instead of 3, and two simultaneous page loads from different users take 12-14 of the 10 available pool connections, forcing everything else in the process to queue.
findings.recommendation: Have `getSession` return (or a request-scoped cache hold) the users row so lines 80-88 do not re-read it, and pass the already-fetched plan into `getUserPlanLimits` instead of letting it call `getUserPlan` again. Fold the `gifted_subscriptions` lookup into the single users query with a LEFT JOIN, exactly as `getUserPlan` already does. That takes the route from 7 queries to 3.

findings.title: The scan progress tracker writes two UPDATEs to scan_history per category, so a single scan does about 40 row rewrites of the widest table in the schema
findings.description: `createProgressTracker`'s `onProgress` hook fires an `UPDATE scan_history SET current_category = $1, categories_total = $2 WHERE id = $3` on every "start" event (lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts:120-127) and an `UPDATE scan_history SET categories_completed = $1, categories_total = $2 ...` on every "done" event (lines 131-138). The hook is invoked twice per category by `runSyncChecks` (lib/scanner/engine.ts:166 and :203) and twice per branch by `runAsyncChecksDetailed` (lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:4642 and :4644). `categoriesTotal` is `plannedSync.length + plannedAsync.length` (app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:339), which for a default full scan is roughly 16 sync categories plus 4-5 async branches -- about 40 UPDATEs per scan. Because Postgres is MVCC, each one writes a new version of a `scan_history` row that carries the `findings`, `summary`, `response_headers` and `result_meta` JSONB columns.
findings.impact: About 40 dead tuples per scan on the largest table in the schema, plus 40 write round trips competing for the same 10-connection pool the scan's own reads use. On a crawl this is 40 x page count. It also inflates autovacuum work on the one table every list, dashboard and public page reads from.
findings.recommendation: Coalesce progress writes in lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts:113: keep the counters in memory and flush at most once every ~500ms (or only when `current_category` actually changes) with a single UPDATE, dropping the separate start/done writes. The status poll already runs on a 2s interval (AUDIT-011 scan-03), so sub-second progress precision buys nothing.

findings.title: GET /api/v3/ai/context reads up to 998KB from disk with readFileSync on every request, uncached, and resolves the session twice
findings.category: uncached synchronous file I/O on a request path
findings.description: `readKnowledgeFile` does `existsSync` then `readFileSync(p, 'utf8')` (app/api/v3/ai/context/route.ts:20-22) with no memoization. The files it serves are lib/ai/checks-knowledge.md at 998,790 bytes, lib/ai/changelog-knowledge.md at 250,398 bytes, lib/ai/docs-knowledge.md at 99,069 bytes, lib/ai/checks-index.md at 71,804 bytes and lib/ai/legal-knowledge.md at 34,746 bytes. They are build artifacts (generated by scripts/compile-*-knowledge.mjs) and never change at runtime. The `/finding` command additionally reads the full 998KB file at line 284 and then runs a regex with a lazy `[\s\S]*?` and a lookahead across the whole string (lines 302-306). Separately, `GET` already calls `getSession()` at line 29, and the `history`, `me` and `stats` branches call it again at lines 115, 230 and 327 -- two session queries per request on those paths.
findings.impact: `readFileSync` blocks the event loop for the whole read, so every /checks or /finding slash command in the AI chat stalls the single Node process serving all users for the duration of a 1MB synchronous read plus a 1MB UTF-8 decode plus a 1MB regex scan. Nothing about these files justifies re-reading them; they are identical between every request until the next deploy.
findings.recommendation: Load each knowledge file once into a module-level `Map<string, string>` on first use in app/api/v3/ai/context/route.ts and serve from memory thereafter (the process restarts on deploy, so staleness is impossible). For `/finding`, build an id -> section index once at first load instead of regex-scanning the full document per request. Pass the already-resolved `session` from `GET` into `handleContext` instead of calling `getSession()` a second time at lines 115, 230 and 327.

findings.title: An invalid API key falls through to a full scan of the legacy key rows and a bcryptjs comparison per row, on the main thread
findings.category: unbounded work on an unauthenticated failure path
findings.description: `validateApiKey` tries the O(1) locator lookup first (lib/api/api-keys.ts:336), but when it matches nothing it does not return. It then runs `SELECT ... WHERE ak.key_locator IS NULL AND ak.key_encrypted IS NOT NULL` (line 362) and AES-decrypts every returned row, and then `SELECT ... WHERE ak.key_hash IS NOT NULL AND ak.key_locator IS NULL AND ak.key_encrypted IS NULL` (line 392) and calls `verifyKey(key, row.key_hash)` for every row in a `for` loop (line 404). `verifyKey` is `bcrypt.compare` from `bcryptjs` (lines 2 and 126) -- the pure-JavaScript implementation, which does its work on the main thread rather than the libuv pool -- against hashes generated at cost 12 (`const saltRounds = 12`, line 120). Only on a match is the locator backfilled (line 376), so a legacy key that is never used again keeps its row in the scanned set forever.
findings.impact: Every request with a wrong, revoked or stale Bearer token costs three extra queries and one main-thread bcrypt-12 comparison per un-backfilled legacy row. bcryptjs at cost 12 is on the order of 200-400ms of JavaScript CPU per comparison, so a handful of legacy rows turns each bad token into a second or more of event-loop time in a single-process deployment -- and POST /api/v3/scan reaches this before any rate limiting applies (app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:65).
findings.recommendation: In lib/api/api-keys.ts:326, return `null` immediately after the locator lookup misses unless a one-time startup check confirms un-backfilled rows still exist (`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM api_keys WHERE key_locator IS NULL)`, cached in module scope and cleared on key creation). Run the backfill as a migration in instrumentation.ts rather than lazily on match, then delete the two fallback scans entirely.

findings.title: Nine missing indexes: four force full table scans inside the single long cleanup transaction, two make per-scan triage lookups degrade with total history
findings.description: Cross-checking every index in instrumentation.ts against the WHERE/JOIN/ORDER BY columns in app/ and lib/ leaves these gaps. (1) `rate_limits.window_start` has no index -- `UNIQUE(key, window_start)` (instrumentation.ts:842) leads on `key` -- so `DELETE FROM rate_limits WHERE window_start < NOW() - INTERVAL '1 day'` (lib/database/cleanup.ts:211) seq-scans the fastest-growing table in the schema. (2)(3)(4) The same shape on `scan_finding_feedback.created_at` (cleanup.ts:380), `user_notifications.created_at` (cleanup.ts:389) and `github_review_usage.updated_at` (cleanup.ts:401): each table's only timestamp index is a composite led by `user_id` (instrumentation.ts:1471, 1672, 2047), unusable as a timestamp-only scan key -- while admin_audit_log, email_logs, system_error_logs and api_usage all do have the plain index their identical prune uses. (5) `ai_conversations.last_message_at` has no index; the table has `idx_ai_conversations_created_at` (instrumentation.ts:1191) on the wrong column, and both real consumers use `last_message_at` (cleanup.ts:353 and app/api/v3/ai/conversations/route.ts:171-175, which also sorts by it). (6)(7) `finding_remediation(user_id, finding_url)` and `scan_finding_feedback(user_id, finding_url)`: both tables have `UNIQUE (user_id, finding_id, finding_url)` (instrumentation.ts:1516, 1467), with `finding_id` sitting between the two columns the hot queries actually filter on (lib/scanner/remediation-store.ts:41-44, lib/scanner/regression-alert.ts:47-49), so only `user_id` is usable as a key. (8) `broadcast_recipients(message_id, user_id)` -- see perf-07. (9) the public-shares partial index -- see perf-04.
findings.impact: The cleanup pass (lib/database/cleanup.ts) performs four full table scans on the largest, fastest-growing tables, all inside one transaction (see perf-22). `getRemediationMap` runs on every scan-result render and `regression-alert` after every completed scan; both currently cost O(that user's entire triage history) instead of O(findings for this URL), so a heavy user's scans get slower the more findings they have ever triaged. The admin AI-conversations page seq-scans and externally sorts a table of JSONB message arrays on every load.
findings.recommendation: Add to the performance-index block in instrumentation.ts (around line 1587): `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_rate_limits_window_start ON rate_limits(window_start); CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_ai_conversations_last_msg ON ai_conversations(last_message_at DESC); CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_user_notifications_created ON user_notifications(created_at); CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_sff_created ON scan_finding_feedback(created_at); CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_gru_updated ON github_review_usage(updated_at); CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_finding_remediation_user_url ON finding_remediation(user_id, finding_url); CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_sff_user_url ON scan_finding_feedback(user_id, finding_url);` Keep the existing three-column UNIQUEs -- they back the `ON CONFLICT` clauses in app/api/v3/scan/remediation/route.ts:93 and app/api/v3/scan/feedback/route.ts:60. `idx_ai_conversations_created_at` has no reader and can be dropped.

findings.title: Four hot queries wrap an indexed column in a function or regex, so the index that exists for them can never be used
findings.description: (a) app/api/v3/host/[hostname]/trend/route.ts:77-82 filters `WHERE is_public = true AND status = 'completed' AND url ~* $1`, with `$1` built as `^https?://(www\.)?<host>([:/?]|$)` at line 70. `~*` is not a b-tree-indexable operator, so `idx_scan_history_url_public_completed` (instrumentation.ts:2359) degrades to a full scan applying a case-insensitive regex to every row, then a sort, and only then `LIMIT 30`. The query also selects the full `findings` JSONB for those 30 rows. This is a public unauthenticated page. (b) app/api/v3/dashboard/route.ts:75 joins on `DATE(sh.scanned_at) = days.day` (see perf-06). (c) lib/domains/scope.ts:47-53 filters `($1 = domain OR $1 LIKE '%.' || domain)` -- the LIKE pattern is built from the column with the parameter on the left, which no b-tree can serve, so `idx_domains_domain_verified` (instrumentation.ts:3189) is unusable and every scan authorization check scans all verified domains across all tenants. (d) app/api/v3/admin/blocked-data/route.ts:60-83 and its DELETE twin at :124-135 apply `LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(sh.url, ...))` per row over all of scan_history before the `LIMIT 100`.
findings.impact: Each of these reads the whole table where an index exists specifically to prevent that. (a) and (c) are the ones that matter operationally: (a) is on an unauthenticated route whose cost grows with total public scan volume, and (c) runs on the authorization gate for every active-probe or port-scan request.
findings.recommendation: For (a), store the normalized host at scan time (a `host` column populated from lib/scanner/root-domain.ts, indexed) and filter `WHERE host = $1` instead of regexing the URL; also stop selecting `findings` there and project only title/severity. For (b), rewrite as a range predicate. For (c), store the registrable domain and each of its parent suffixes so the lookup becomes `domain = ANY($1::text[])`, which is indexable. For (d), the same normalized `host` column removes the REGEXP_REPLACE.

findings.title: The root layout reads headers() for a CSP nonce, which forces all ~790 public SEO pages to be server-rendered per request with no static or ISR output
findings.category: no static rendering anywhere in the app
findings.description: `RootLayout` does `const nonce = (await headers()).get('x-nonce') ?? undefined` at app/layout.tsx:146. The comment above it (lines 139-145) states the consequence outright: this "forces this layout (and everything under it) into per-request dynamic rendering". app/checks/[id]/page.tsx repeats it at lines 29-31 -- `generateStaticParams` still enumerates the id space (line 34) but the pages are never actually prerendered. `getAllChecks()` returns the full check inventory (lib/seo/checks-content.ts:142), which is the ~754-page /checks tree, plus /checks/category/*, /docs, /finding-types, /host/* and the legal pages -- roughly 790 public routes, every one of which runs the full React server render on every single hit.
findings.impact: Googlebot crawling the /checks tree, or any traffic to the SEO surface the project deliberately built for discovery, costs a full server render per page view with zero cache. The same CPU is shared with the scan engine's synchronous check loop (AUDIT-011 scan-06) in one Node process, so crawler traffic directly slows scans. It also means `next build` produces no static output for content that never changes between deploys.
findings.recommendation: Move the nonce out of the layout's render. Either (a) have middleware.ts inject the nonce into the response HTML stream so the layout stays static, or (b) switch the CSP for the static content routes to a hash-based or `strict-dynamic`-with-no-nonce policy, and drop the `headers()` read from app/layout.tsx so /checks, /docs and the legal pages can be prerendered and revalidated on a long interval. Keep the nonce path for the authenticated app routes that genuinely need per-request rendering.

findings.title: POST /api/v3/scan/bulk does roughly nine sequential database round trips per URL, up to 900-1000 in one request, and takes a row lock on the API key each time
findings.description: The bulk route loops `for (let i = 0; i < urlsToScan.length; i++)` at app/api/v3/scan/bulk/route.ts:622 with every step awaited in order. Per iteration: `checkAndRecordRequest` (line 637) costs `getDailyLimit` -> `getUserPlan` plus an UPSERT and possibly a re-read (lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.ts:309/330/361/378) = 2-3 queries; `checkApiKeyRateLimit` (line 668) runs `pool.connect` + BEGIN + `SELECT id FROM api_keys WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE` (lib/api/api-keys.ts:489) + a 24h `COUNT(*)` over api_usage (line 505) + an INSERT (line 514) + COMMIT + an `UPDATE api_keys SET last_used_at` (line 528) + a `SELECT used_at ... LIMIT 1` (line 543) = 7 round trips holding a row lock; `runSingleScan` (line 688) adds `checkAccessRules` (2 queries) and an `INSERT INTO scan_history`. `MAX_URLS_BULK` defaults to 100 (lib/config/config-values.ts:543).
findings.impact: A 100-URL bulk request performs on the order of 900-1000 serialized database round trips inside one HTTP handler, acquiring and releasing a `FOR UPDATE` lock on the same api_keys row 100 times, while holding pool connections throughout. Even at 2ms RTT that is two seconds of pure database latency layered on top of 100 sequential network scans.
findings.recommendation: Hoist the per-user work out of the loop in app/api/v3/scan/bulk/route.ts:622: resolve the plan and daily limit once, charge quota for the whole batch in one capped statement, and record API usage once per batch (or as a single multi-row INSERT at the end) rather than per URL. Cache the access-rules result per host for the duration of the request.

findings.title: Four routes select the full findings JSONB for an unbounded row set, including a GDPR export that buffers the entire admin audit log into memory twice
findings.description: (a) app/api/v3/shares/route.ts:15-30 selects `summary, findings` for every share a user owns with no LIMIT, then JSON.parses each blob in JS at lines 32-36 -- and the only derived value is `findingsCount: findings.length` (line 50), which the `findings_count` column already stores. (b) app/api/v3/admin/audit-log/export/route.ts:79-88 runs `SELECT ... FROM admin_audit_log al LEFT JOIN users au ... LEFT JOIN users tu ... ORDER BY al.created_at DESC` with no WHERE and no LIMIT, buffers all rows into a JS array (line 81) and then `JSON.stringify(result.rows, null, 2)` (line 104) -- the entire audit table held in the Node heap twice. (c) lib/notifications/posture-digest.ts:80-93 runs `SELECT DISTINCT ON (url) url, findings FROM scan_history WHERE user_id = $1 AND status = 'completed' ORDER BY url, scanned_at DESC` with no LIMIT and no time bound, and it is called twice per user at lines 113-117. (d) app/api/v3/data-request/route.ts:167-174 selects `findings` for every scan the user ever ran.
findings.impact: (b) is the sharpest: an admin clicking Export on a mature instance OOM-kills the single Node process that also runs every in-flight scan, since `admin_audit_log` grows on every staff action and there is no bound at all. (a) and (d) ship tens of megabytes per request for users with many scans. (c) makes the digest worker's cost scale with total history rather than with what the digest actually reports.
findings.recommendation: Add `findings_count` to (a) and drop `findings` from the projection entirely. Stream (b) with a keyset-paged cursor and write CSV/NDJSON incrementally instead of building one string, and bound it with the same retention window lib/database/audit-log-archive.ts:80 uses. Give (c) a `LIMIT` and a `scanned_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '...'` bound, and project only the finding fields the digest renders. Page (d) or stream it to a file.

findings.title: Single requests fan out more concurrent queries than the entire connection pool holds: 25 from the data-export route against a pool max of 10
findings.description: `CONFIG_DB_POOL_MAX` is 10 (lib/config/config-values.ts:393), wired into the Pool at lib/database/db.ts:58. app/api/v3/data-request/route.ts:97-122 destructures 25 results from a single `Promise.all` at line 123, each of them a `pool.query` -- so one request asks for 25 connections at once and queues on itself for 15 of them, several of which are unbounded (sessions at :137-143, api_usage joined to api_keys at :155-164, all of scan_history with findings at :167-174, scan_tags at :178-183). app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:146 fans out exactly 10 in the `user-detail` branch, monopolizing the pool. app/api/v3/dashboard/route.ts:33 fans out 7 (perf-06), and app/api/v3/admin/billing-overview/route.ts:103 fans out 7 including three full `users` counts. Separately, lib/database/cleanup.ts:481-498 fires `2 x N` unawaited `.catch()`ed writes for expired browser sessions with no cap.
findings.impact: Any one of these requests can starve every other request in the process -- including `getSession`, so an admin opening a user detail page can make other users' logins hang until `connectionTimeoutMillis` fires. The pool is a process-wide resource and nothing in the codebase budgets it per request.
findings.recommendation: Cap fan-out per request. Either raise `CONFIG_DB_POOL_MAX` well above the largest fan-out and size Postgres accordingly, or (better) batch: the data-export route's 25 queries are mostly `WHERE user_id = $1` on different tables and can run in chunks of 4-5, and the admin user-detail branch can be consolidated into 2-3 joined queries. Add an explicit concurrency limiter to the cleanup fan-out at lib/database/cleanup.ts:481.

findings.title: checkExposedFiles fires 23 unthrottled parallel requests at the scan target, and checkLiveFetch adds three more branches on top
findings.description: `checkExposedFiles` builds a 23-entry probe list (paths /.git/config, /.git/HEAD, /.env, /.env.local, /.htpasswd, /phpinfo.php, /info.php, /docker-compose.yml, /phpmyadmin/, /adminer.php, /backup.sql, /terraform.tfstate, /wp-json/wp/v2/users, /metrics, /.npmrc, /.env.production, /web.config, /debug.log, /package-lock.json, /jenkins/, /consul/, /minio/, /rabbitmq/) and dispatches all of them at once with `Promise.allSettled(probes.map(async (probe) => ...))` at lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:3500, each with a 5s timeout. Its caller `checkLiveFetch` runs it concurrently with `checkRobotsTxt`, `checkSecurityTxt` and `checkBucketListing` (lines 4399-4404), and `runAsyncChecksDetailed` runs that branch concurrently with the DNS, TLS, reputation and OSV branches. There is no per-target concurrency cap anywhere in the async layer.
findings.impact: Every scan opens 25+ simultaneous connections to the target within a few hundred milliseconds. Rate-limited targets and WAFs respond by 429ing or blocking, which silently turns real findings into non-findings, and it makes VulnRadar look like an attacker to the site it was asked to assess. On a crawl this repeats per page (perf-03), so a 25-page crawl fetches /.git/config 25 times.
findings.recommendation: Add a small concurrency limiter (4-6 in flight) around the probe dispatch at lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:3500 and share one limiter across every branch that talks to the same origin, so the whole scan presents a bounded, polite request rate. Cache the exposed-files result per origin so a crawl probes each path once.

findings.title: The nightly cleanup runs about thirty DELETEs, four of them full table scans, inside one 350-line transaction holding a pooled connection
findings.description: `lib/database/cleanup.ts` opens `BEGIN` at line 114 and does not `COMMIT` until line 464, wrapping roughly thirty DELETE statements across sessions, rate_limits, tokens, scan_history, scan_finding_feedback, user_notifications, github_review_usage, ai_conversations and more in a single transaction on one pooled client. Four of those DELETEs cannot use an index and seq-scan their table (see perf-15): rate_limits (line 211), scan_finding_feedback (line 380), user_notifications (line 389), github_review_usage (line 401). None of the work is transactionally coupled -- these are independent retention prunes on unrelated tables.
findings.impact: One of the 10 pool connections is held for the entire pass, and every row deleted stays locked for its duration, so any concurrent write touching those rows blocks. The four full scans make the pass length grow with total table size rather than with the number of rows actually being deleted. A failure at line 480 rolls back thirty prunes that had nothing to do with each other.
findings.recommendation: Split the pass in lib/database/cleanup.ts:114-464 into one autocommitted statement per table (or small groups), with the batching pattern `DELETE ... WHERE ctid IN (SELECT ctid ... LIMIT 5000)` in a loop for the large tables, so no single statement holds locks for long. Add the four missing indexes from perf-15 first.

findings.title: checkAccessRules runs two uncached sequential-scan queries on every scan, and once per URL on every bulk or crawl request
findings.description: `checkAccessRules` always issues a blacklist query (lib/scanner/access-rules.ts:56-73) and, when that misses, a `SELECT COUNT(*)::int AS count FROM access_rules WHERE rule_type = 'whitelist' AND is_active = true ...` (lines 100-104) -- two sequential round trips, with no caching anywhere. Both predicates are non-sargable: `LOWER($1) = LOWER(value) OR LOWER($1) LIKE '%.' || LOWER(value)` builds the LIKE pattern from the column, and the IP branch casts `value::inet` (line 51), so neither `idx_access_rules_value` (instrumentation.ts:1022) nor `idx_access_rules_type` (:1023) can be used. It is called on every scan (app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:285), once per URL in `checkAccessRulesBatch`'s sequential loop (lib/scanner/access-rules.ts:160-161), and once per crawl page before the crawl starts (lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:423-428).
findings.impact: Two extra serialized round trips on the front of every scan, and `2 x N` for a 100-URL bulk request or a 250-page crawl selection -- up to 500 round trips just to check an admin blocklist that changes maybe once a month.
findings.recommendation: Cache the `access_rules` table in process with a short TTL and an explicit invalidation from the admin write path, exactly as lib/config/runtime-config.ts:63 and lib/tags/auto-tags.ts:702 already do for their tables, and evaluate the match in JavaScript. That turns `checkAccessRulesBatch` and the crawl pre-check into zero queries.

findings.title: Nine admin and public list routes pair a full COUNT(*) with the paged SELECT, most of them running the two back to back instead of in parallel
findings.category: unbounded COUNT on every page load
findings.description: `COUNT(*)` in Postgres always scans the full matching set; a LIMIT on the sibling query does not bound it. Confirmed instances, all on growing tables: app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:269-271 counts all of `admin_audit_log`, awaited AFTER the paged select at :257-268 rather than alongside it, and that paged select uses `LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2` (line 266) so deep pages re-scan and discard every preceding row; :329-338 runs ten scalar sub-selects on the default admin dashboard including two full `scan_history` counts and a full `users` count; :344/:359 add a correlated `(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM scan_history sh WHERE sh.user_id = u.id)` per listed user; :371-375 counts `users` behind a leading-wildcard ILIKE; :300-321 runs three `admin_audit_log` counts per staff row in the polled active-admins section. Same sequential COUNT-then-page shape in app/api/v3/admin/error-logs/route.ts:66 (over an unindexable `message ILIKE '%..%'`), app/api/v3/admin/email-logs/route.ts:81, app/api/v3/admin/content/route.ts:56 and :76, app/api/v3/admin/support-tickets/route.ts:61 (a `GROUP BY status` with no WHERE at all), and app/api/v3/public-scans/route.ts:77 (perf-04).
findings.impact: Opening the admin panel triggers several full-table counts, and the audit-log and email-log searches scan their whole table twice per keystroke-driven page load. The public-scans one is unauthenticated. As the instance ages every one of these gets linearly slower with no upper bound.
findings.recommendation: For the admin routes, drop the exact total: use keyset pagination with a `hasMore` flag from `LIMIT n+1`, or an approximate count from `pg_class.reltuples` where a number must be shown. Where a real count is required, at minimum run it inside the same `Promise.all` as the page query instead of sequentially (app/api/v3/ai/conversations/route.ts:167-178 already does this correctly and is the pattern to copy).

findings.title: HTTPS targets are validated by DNS lookup and then re-resolved by undici at connect time, leaving the DNS-rebinding window the guard exists to close
findings.description: validateScanTarget (lib/scanner/safe-fetch.ts:430-494) calls `lookup(hostname, {all:true})` and rejects the target if any returned address is private, then hands back `resolvedIp = addresses[0].address`. safeFetch pins that IP into the request URL only when the scheme is NOT https/wss (lib/scanner/safe-fetch.ts:601-620). For HTTPS, the `else if (isSecureProtocol && safety.resolvedIp)` branch at lib/scanner/safe-fetch.ts:621-624 does nothing but set a Host header; the URL keeps the hostname, so undici calls `dns.lookup` again at connect time. Node has no process-level DNS cache, so an attacker serving a TTL-0 A record from their own authoritative nameserver returns a public IP to validateScanTarget's query and 127.0.0.1 / 169.254.169.254 / an RFC1918 address to undici's query. This is deterministic, not a race. The same limitation is repeated verbatim in applyPinnedTarget (lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:2747-2759, `if (parsed.protocol !== "http:") return {url, init}`) and in pinToResolvedIp (lib/scanner/safe-fetch.ts:285), so every HTTPS probe in the scanner shares it. Both places document it as accepted ("for HTTPS the protection is the DNS re-resolution happening immediately before the request"), which is not a protection at all. Note that the TLS-specific checks got this right: lib/scanner/checks/tls.ts:261-267 and lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:2268-2278 both `tls.connect({host: safeIp, servername: hostname})`, pinning the IP while keeping SNI, which is exactly the pattern the fetch layer is missing.
findings.impact: An attacker who controls a nameserver can make every HTTPS request the scanner issues land on an internal address of their choosing. Certificate validation stops them reading a response body (the cert will not match their hostname), but the TCP connect and TLS ClientHello still happen, and the difference between an immediate RST, a TLS alert, and a full timeout is a working blind port/service scanner for the network VulnRadar runs in, driven from an unauthenticated /api/v3/demo-scan request. It also means the entire private-IP block list is advisory on the HTTPS path, so any future change that relaxes cert checking (the scanner already uses rejectUnauthorized:false elsewhere) turns this into a full read primitive.
findings.recommendation: Pin the connect address without breaking SNI. In lib/scanner/safe-fetch.ts, build a per-request undici `Agent` whose `connect.lookup` returns the already-validated `safety.resolvedIp` (`new Agent({ connect: { lookup: (host, opts, cb) => cb(null, [{address: resolvedIp, family: isIP(resolvedIp)}]) } })`) and pass it as `dispatcher` in the fetch init, for https and http alike. That preserves the hostname for SNI and certificate validation while guaranteeing the socket goes to the address that was checked. Then delete the http-only branch at :601-624, apply the same dispatcher in applyPinnedTarget (lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:2747) and pinToResolvedIp (lib/scanner/safe-fetch.ts:273), and drop the "HTTPS relies on the immediate re-resolution" comments they all copy.

findings.title: The private-IPv4 block list omits 100.64.0.0/10, so Alibaba Cloud's metadata endpoint 100.100.100.200 and all CGNAT/pod-network space is reachable, along with 198.18/15 and 192.0.0.0/24
findings.description:
PRIVATE_IPV4_PATTERNS (lib/scanner/safe-fetch.ts:62-71) is the single source of truth for IPv4 filtering: isPrivateIP (:111-132) tests it directly for v4, extracts the embedded v4 out of IPv4-mapped/NAT64 IPv6 and tests it again (:123-127), and validateScanTarget (:441, :462) and port-scan's resolveSafePublicIp (lib/scanner/port-scan.ts:281-296) both delegate to it. The list is:

  /^127\./, /^10\./, /^172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[0-1])\./, /^192\.168\./,
  /^169\.254\./, /^0\./, /^2(2[4-9]|3[0-9])\./, /^(24[0-9]|25[0-5])\./

Missing, verifiable by inspection against those eight regexes:
- 100.64.0.0/10 (RFC 6598 shared address space). `100.100.100.200`, Alibaba Cloud's instance metadata endpoint, the direct analogue of 169.254.169.254 which IS blocked on line 67, matches none of them. Neither do Alibaba's 100.100.2.136/100.100.2.138 internal DNS resolvers. The same /10 is what AWS EKS and GKE hand to pods and what carrier-grade NAT uses, so on those platforms it is live internal space.
- 198.18.0.0/15 (RFC 2544 benchmarking), routed internally on plenty of networks.
- 192.0.0.0/24 (IETF protocol assignments).
- The TEST-NET blocks 192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24.

Because isPrivateIP is also what the IPv4-mapped-IPv6 path feeds (lib/scanner/safe-fetch.ts:125), `http://[::ffff:100.100.100.200]/` is unblocked for the same reason, and so is `http://[64:ff9b::100.100.100.200]/`. Encoding variants are not a separate hole: the hostname `1684366792` (decimal for 100.100.100.200) is rejected earlier by assertSafePublicHttpUrl's `hostname.includes(".")` requirement (:529), and dotted octal/hex forms go through getaddrinfo, which normalises them before isPrivateIP sees them, but they normalise to 100.100.100.200, which is then allowed.
findings.impact: On any Alibaba Cloud deployment (VulnRadar is self-hostable and advertises exactly that), scanning `http://100.100.100.200/latest/meta-data/ram/security-credentials/` returns the instance's temporary RAM credentials in the scan result body, an unauthenticated full compromise of the host role via /api/v3/demo-scan. On AWS EKS or GKE the same /10 reaches sibling pods and node-local services. Even on a deployment where none of this is routable it is a hole in a control the rest of the product leans on: port-scan.ts, banner.ts, tls.ts and every probe in async-checks.ts all defer to isPrivateIP for their internal-range gate.
findings.recommendation: Add to PRIVATE_IPV4_PATTERNS in lib/scanner/safe-fetch.ts:62: `/^100\.(6[4-9]|[7-9][0-9]|1[01][0-9]|12[0-7])\./` (100.64.0.0/10), `/^198\.1[89]\./` (198.18.0.0/15), `/^192\.0\.0\./`, and the three TEST-NET blocks. Better still, replace the regex list with numeric CIDR containment (parse to a uint32 once and test against a table of [network, prefixLen] pairs) so a range can be stated as a CIDR and reviewed against IANA's special-purpose registry instead of being hand-encoded as a prefix regex; that also removes the class of bug in ssrf-05. Add a test to tests/lib/scanner/safe-fetch.test.ts asserting isPrivateIP("100.100.100.200") is true.

findings.title: The authenticated-scan endpoint will POST caller-supplied credentials to any public host, so it works as a credential-validation proxy against sites the caller does not own
findings.description:
POST /api/v3/scan/authenticated accepts a target `url` plus an `auth` object carrying a username and password (app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts:298-303) and hands both to establishScanSession at :334. That walks to lib/scanner/auth/browser-login.ts:456-489, which builds `username=<caller value>&password=<caller value>` plus the target's own hidden fields and POSTs it to the discovered form action via safeFetch with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `Referer`, `Origin` and an `X-CSRF-Token` scraped from the page. The only host restriction is `allowedHostnames: [hostnameOf(origin)]`: the caller's own chosen origin.

The domain-ownership gate at app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts:312-330 fires only when `requestsActiveProbing(scanners)` is true. A plain authenticated scan of a domain the caller has never verified is explicitly allowed. The outcome is reported back distinguishably: lib/scanner/auth/browser-login.ts:496-498 returns "The target rejected the login request with 401", :505-509 returns "The login did not set or change any cookie", :511-515 returns "still showed a login form", and success returns a completed scan: the route surfaces the reason verbatim at app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts:341-346. That is a clean three-way oracle for whether a credential pair is valid on a third-party site.

The only limits are checkGlobalRateLimit on `scan-authenticated:<userId>` (:200-207) and the per-account daily scan quota (:189, :208-215). Signup is free and open, so both scale with the number of accounts an attacker creates.
findings.impact: VulnRadar's server IP becomes the origin of credential-stuffing attempts against arbitrary third-party login forms, with a built-in success oracle and CSRF-token handling already done for the attacker. The victim site's logs, lockouts and abuse reports point at VulnRadar, which for a service with a public reputation and a shared egress IP means blocklisting and abuse complaints. It also puts the operator in the position of having proxied unauthorised authentication attempts.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same ownership gate to the credential-submitting path that active-probes already has. In app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts, move the `isUrlOwnedByUser(url, authedUserId)` check at :312-330 out of the `requestsActiveProbing(scanners)` condition and require it whenever `parsed.data.auth` carries a username/password (form or basic auth); a cookie-only session (`auth.cookies`, lib/scanner/auth/login.ts:86) is the caller supplying their own already-established session and can stay ungated. Keep a per-target-host failure counter so repeated 401s against one host stop the feature for that account regardless of quota.

findings.title: All ten admin sticky table headers are inert because a second scroll container sits between the header and the height cap
findings.description: components/admin/shared/data-table.tsx:130 applies maxHeight to an outer `overflow-auto` div, but components/ui/table.tsx:9 wraps the table in its own `relative w-full overflow-auto` div with no height cap. position: sticky binds to the nearest scrolling ancestor, which is the inner uncapped div whose scrollTop is permanently 0, so sticky top-0 on TableHeader never engages while the outer container does the actual scrolling.
findings.impact: Column headers scroll away on all ten admin tables. Worst on the eight-column Engine Feedback table, where the meaning of each column is lost after one scroll.
findings.recommendation: Move the maxHeight onto the components/ui/table.tsx wrapper, or have TableScrollArea render a bare <table> without the extra div.

findings.title: Five admin panels render confident wrong values when their fetch fails, including a settings page showing false defaults
findings.description: Each renders a plausible but incorrect state instead of an error: components/admin/features/backup-manager.tsx:81 shows 'Last backup: Never'; components/admin/features/updater-manager.tsx:116 shows 'cosign: Not installed'; components/admin/features/system-settings-manager.tsx:108 shows every setting at its shipped default with no Customized badges; components/admin/features/queue-status-manager.tsx:136 shows skeletons forever; components/admin/features/billing-overview-manager.tsx:238 shows header-only tables.
findings.impact: The system-settings case is the dangerous one: an admin edits from a false baseline and can silently revert real configuration across the whole product. The backup case tells an operator they have no backups when they may have many.
findings.recommendation: Check res.ok in each and render a distinct error state. Prioritise system-settings-manager, where the failure mode causes data loss rather than confusion.

findings.title: Every system-settings tab shares one id, and that id is the React key, so the mobile drawer jumps to the wrong tab
findings.description: components/admin/features/system-settings-manager.tsx:92 gives every tab entry id: "settings-panel", and that id is used as the React key at components/admin/shared/admin-mobile-toc.tsx:200.
findings.impact: Tapping one tab in the mobile drawer can switch to a different one.
findings.recommendation: Give each tab a unique id.

findings.title: The admin toast has no width cap, so server error strings clip off-screen on mobile
findings.description: components/admin/shared/toast.tsx:24 is fixed bottom-4 right-4 z-50 with no max-w constraint.
findings.impact: The error message an admin needs to read is the part that runs off the edge of the screen.
findings.recommendation: Add max-w-[calc(100vw-2rem)] sm:max-w-sm.

findings.title: The impersonation banner overflows on mobile, causing horizontal scroll on every page while impersonating
findings.description: components/admin/impersonation-banner.tsx:85-88 is a centred flex row with no truncate, no min-w-0 and no flex-wrap anywhere in the file. At 375px the content measures roughly 380px against 343px available, before the optional error span at :101 adds about 150px more. With justify-center the overflow splits both sides. It is mounted in app/layout.tsx:181, so it affects every page.
findings.impact: Horizontal page scroll across the entire app while impersonating, with the 'Stop impersonating' button pushed partly off the right edge - the one control the admin most needs.
findings.recommendation: Add flex-wrap, min-w-0 on the span, truncate max-w-[45vw] on the email, and shrink-0 on the button.

findings.title: The audit-log filter strip hides seven of ten filters on mobile with no scrollbar
findings.description: components/admin/audit/audit-log.tsx:283 is `flex gap-2 overflow-x-auto pb-2 sm:pb-0 sm:flex-wrap scrollbar-hide`, the last remaining overflow-x-auto scrollbar-hide strip in admin. components/admin/features/email-logs-manager.tsx:284 wraps instead of scrolling.
findings.impact: Seven of ten audit filters are invisible on a phone, with scrollbar-hide removing the only cue that more exist.
findings.recommendation: Bring in line with components/admin/features/email-logs-manager.tsx:284 and wrap rather than scroll.

findings.title: Four sticky sidebars ignore the banner offset variables the nav uses, so the nav paints over them
findings.description: app/admin/page.tsx:1052 is `sticky top-20`, and components/docs/docs-sidebar.tsx:27 and components/docs/docs-toc.tsx:17 are `sticky top-16`. components/scanner/header.tsx:120 shifts by calc(var(--vr-banner-h,0px) + var(--vr-imp-banner-h,0px)) and components/landing/landing-nav.tsx:49 shifts by top-(--vr-banner-h,0px) at z-50. components/shared/site-notifications.tsx:586 sets --vr-banner-h live and components/admin/impersonation-banner.tsx:41-53 sets --vr-imp-banner-h. app/profile/page.tsx:746 is the correct pattern, though even it omits --vr-imp-banner-h. Since impersonation is an admin feature, app/admin/page.tsx:1052 is guaranteed to fail during impersonation.
findings.impact: With a banner showing, the nav slides down over the top rows of these sidebars and they stop being clickable. The docs pair additionally has a 7px dead band even with no banner, since top-16 is 64px against a 57px nav.
findings.recommendation: Use top-[calc(5rem+var(--vr-banner-h,0px)+var(--vr-imp-banner-h,0px))] transition-[top] duration-300 on all four, following app/profile/page.tsx:746.

findings.title: The ToS gate blocks the unsubscribe link in every marketing email
findings.description: components/auth/tos-gate.tsx:9 sets SKIP_TOS_PATHS to ["/login", "/signup", "/legal"]. The logged-out path is fine because :28-31 sets status skip when /api/v3/auth/me is not ok. The exposure is a signed-in user with pending or needs_reaccept status, for whom the page renders at opacity-20 blur-xs pointer-events-none behind TosModal (:77-91). /unsubscribe, /verify-email and /reset-password are not in the skip list.
findings.impact: The unsubscribe link in every marketing email is gated behind accepting updated terms. Coupled with auth-05, the unsubscribe flow is compromised at both ends.
findings.recommendation: Add "/unsubscribe", "/verify-email", "/reset-password" and "/forgot-password" to SKIP_TOS_PATHS.

findings.title: Auth pages prerender a null Suspense fallback, so first paint is empty and the indexable /login is one empty div
findings.description: app/reset-password/page.tsx:41 uses Suspense fallback={null}, prerendered into the static HTML, while the pitch column is hidden lg:block. First paint on a phone is wordmark, empty band, footer. The same shape at app/login/page.tsx:12 and app/signup/page.tsx:12 replaces the entire page.
findings.impact: A blank first paint on the three highest-intent pages in the product, and the HTML a crawler receives for the indexable /login is a single empty div.
findings.recommendation: Give each Suspense a real skeleton fallback.

findings.title: The unsubscribe page prints an email address with no break-all and scrolls the page sideways
findings.description: app/unsubscribe/page.tsx:293 and :324 render redactEmail() output with no break-all, while three sibling components have it.
findings.impact: A long address scrolls the whole page horizontally.
findings.recommendation: Add break-all.

findings.title: Unsubscribe toggles are 24px tall and the destructive action is a 16px target at 60% opacity
findings.description: The 19 Switch toggles are 24x44px with the row's py-3 outside the hit area. The destructive 'unsubscribe from all' at app/unsubscribe/page.tsx:378 is a roughly 16px target at text-xs and 60% opacity.
findings.impact: A compliance-relevant preference screen is hard to operate accurately on a phone, and the most consequential control on it is the hardest to hit.
findings.recommendation: Make the whole row the label and hit area; promote the destructive action to h-11.

findings.title: The unsubscribe page crushes 19 preference rows into max-w-sm while an unused wide variant exists for exactly this screen
findings.description: app/unsubscribe/page.tsx:393 renders a 19-row preference list inside max-w-sm, leaving about 1050px empty on either side at 1440px. components/auth/auth-layout.tsx:9-11 documents an unused width="wide" prop with a docstring saying it is 'for the one screen that is a list rather than a form', which is this screen.
findings.impact: The page is needlessly cramped, and the fix already exists in the codebase unused.
findings.recommendation: Pass width="wide".

findings.title: The browser session viewer renders raw runtime error strings to the user
findings.description: app/browser/[id]/page.tsx:153-155 sets `e instanceof Error ? e.message : ...` and renders it at :546. A stale-deploy HTML response therefore surfaces `Unexpected token '<', "<!DOCTYPE "... is not valid JSON` to the user. The same shape at :319-323 renders {logsError} raw at :670-672, which can be literally 'HTTP 502'. For contrast components/scanner/dashboard-error-state.tsx:257-275 deliberately shows the scanner's message, and that is safe because app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:288-292 sets details to a fixed string.
findings.impact: Users see JSON parser internals. Given the known stale-deploy chunk-404 failure mode in this project, this is the error they are most likely to hit.
findings.recommendation: Keep the raw text in console.error and render a fixed sentence.

findings.title: The bulk remediation endpoint fans out 200 unbatched queries with no transaction, making its error message dishonest
findings.description: app/api/v3/scan/remediation/bulk/route.ts:83-119 issues Promise.all over up to 200 independent pool.query calls with no transaction. Partial failure leaves partial state while the UI shows a generic 'Couldn't apply. Try again.' Separately lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:366 declares security: [{ apiKey: [] }] for this route (and :337 for the single route) but neither handler has a Bearer path, so an API-key client following the published spec gets a 401.
findings.impact: A user who retries after a partial failure re-applies to findings already changed, and cannot tell which ones took. The endpoint has zero external consumers because the published spec is wrong about its auth.
findings.recommendation: Replace the fan-out with one INSERT ... SELECT ... FROM unnest(...) inside a transaction, then the all-or-nothing error copy becomes true. Correct or remove the apiKey security declaration in the OpenAPI spec. Note this is a prerequisite for the undo described in bulk-01.

findings.title: The subscription is created before card validation, leaving an orphan incomplete subscription on every typo
findings.description: components/billing/stripe-checkout.tsx:210 creates the Stripe subscription before calling elements.submit(). The other three billing components validate first and carry a comment explaining why.
findings.impact: Every mistyped card leaves an orphan incomplete subscription on the customer record, polluting billing data and potentially triggering dunning.
findings.recommendation: Call elements.submit() first, matching components/billing/ai-credit-checkout.tsx.

findings.title: The checkout success page only understands subscriptions, so credit top-ups warn about a payment that succeeded
findings.description: app/checkout/success/checkout-success-content.tsx:13 is the return_url for all four checkout flows but only polls verify-subscription. A redirect-method credit top-up polls for about 22.5 seconds and then warns the payment could not be confirmed. redirect_status=failed is ignored entirely, so a genuinely failed payment also lands on a page implying success is pending.
findings.impact: A successful purchase is reported as possibly failed, and a failed purchase is reported as probably fine. Both directions are wrong on the money path.
findings.recommendation: Branch on the product type in the return URL and read redirect_status.

findings.title: The support tickets section renders nothing while loading, so /contact looks like the feature is missing
findings.description: components/contact/support-tickets.tsx:174 is `if (isLoading) return null`, under the first and most prominent category on /contact.
findings.impact: On a cold load the page appears not to have a ticket feature at all.
findings.recommendation: Render a skeleton instead of null.

findings.title: /donate removes its own fallback link at the moment it is needed and traps the back button in a redirect loop
findings.description: app/donate/page.tsx:14-22 redirects via window.location.href after 100ms and sets redirected true. At :51-60 the manual 'Continue to Stripe' button renders only when !redirected, and a thank-you message replaces it when redirected. Three defects compound: the fallback disappears exactly when the automatic redirect has failed; location.href rather than location.replace() leaves /donate in history, so Back from Stripe returns here and re-fires after 100ms; and the page has no nav, no <main> and no footer, so a stranded user has no way off it.
findings.impact: A user whose redirect fails is shown a thank-you for a donation that never happened, with no link to complete it and no navigation. Pressing Back from Stripe creates an inescapable loop.
findings.recommendation: Use location.replace(), keep the fallback link rendered unconditionally, drop the premature thank-you, and wrap the page in PublicPageShell.

findings.title: Checkout columns are misaligned between 768px and 1024px by a hardcoded top padding
findings.description: app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx:306 uses a magic md:pt-[120px] to align the second column.
findings.impact: The two columns visibly misalign across the whole tablet band on the payment page.
findings.recommendation: Align with a grid row rather than a hardcoded pixel offset.

findings.title: Dashboard analytics renders nothing on a failed fetch and throws on a partial payload
findings.description: components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:211-230 sets data only if d && d.severityBreakdown, catches by setting loading false, then returns null at :229. Only severityBreakdown is checked, but the render accesses data.sourceBreakdown.find (:242), data.dailyActivity.map (:244), data.topVulnerabilities.map (:255) and data.recentScans (:348) unguarded, so a partial response throws into app/dashboard/error.tsx.
findings.impact: A failing /api/v3/dashboard leaves the scan form followed by blank space with no message and no retry. A partial response takes out the whole route.
findings.recommendation: Render a distinct error state instead of null, and guard every field the render touches rather than only severityBreakdown.

findings.title: The activity tooltip prints '0 issues' for every day because the API hardcodes the field
findings.description: app/api/v3/dashboard/route.ts:102 returns issues: 0 for all 14 days; the SQL at :65-79 counts scans only. components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:325 renders `· ${d.issues} issues` whenever d.scans > 0.
findings.impact: Every activity bar tooltip reads 'N scans · 0 issues', which is visibly and confidently wrong on the main dashboard.
findings.recommendation: Either compute the real per-day issue count in the SQL or remove the clause from the tooltip. Do not ship a zero that looks like data.

findings.title: The docs mobile drawer declares modality it does not enforce and its close button scrolls out of reach
findings.description: components/docs/docs-mobile-nav.tsx:65-84 declares role="dialog" aria-modal="true" at :70-71 but has no focus trap, so Tab walks straight out into the fully focusable page behind. There is no body scroll lock, so the page behind scroll-chains at the drawer's ends. The close X is absolute right-3 top-3 at :81, positioned against the padding box of the fixed element that is itself the scroll container (overflow-y-auto at :73); the drawer holds 19 two-line nav links plus the full page TOC, easily 1200px against a 667px phone, so the X scrolls out of reach within one swipe. It does get Escape (:57-59) and initial focus (:55) right.
findings.impact: A screen-reader user is told the drawer is modal and then tabs into hidden content behind it. Any user who scrolls loses the close button.
findings.recommendation: Move the content into an inner overflow-y-auto div and keep the close button a direct child of the fixed element (or sticky top-3); add body scroll lock to the existing open effect with cleanup; add a Tab-cycling branch to the existing keydown handler.

findings.title: Docs prose runs about 124 characters per line at 1440px on eight of twenty pages
findings.description: At 1440px the docs article column is 880px. Ten pages cap prose at max-w-[68ch] (about 483px); eight cap only the first paragraph and let the rest run the full 880px, roughly double the readable measure. Drifted: cli, architecture, rate-limits, webhooks, setup, self-hosting, developers, extension. Correct: github, sharing, account-security, triage, scheduled-scans, ai, api, reports. Representative offender app/docs/cli/page.tsx:59 constrained versus :74, 86, 93, 108, 174, 183, 194 unconstrained.
findings.impact: Half the documentation is materially harder to read on a desktop, and the inconsistency between adjacent pages is visible.
findings.recommendation: Put max-w-[68ch] once on the DocsSection body wrapper at components/docs/docs-section.tsx:55 so no page can drift again. The class is already the house standard (components/docs/docs-callout.tsx:83).

findings.title: The docs shell is 144px wider per side than its own nav above 1440px
findings.description: components/docs/docs-shell.tsx:60 is max-w-360 (1440px) while components/landing/landing-nav.tsx:53 is max-w-6xl (1152px). Docs is the only section wider than the nav above it. At 1920px the logo sits at x about 384 while the docs sidebar's left edge sits at x about 240.
findings.impact: The logo visibly floats inward from the content beneath it on every docs page at large widths.
findings.recommendation: Cap the docs shell at max-w-[calc(72rem+30rem)], or give LandingNav a containerClass prop. Capping is the smaller change.

findings.title: /checks ships roughly 754 list items and 190KB of HTML that never paints
findings.description: app/checks/page.tsx:147-188 renders an <li> for every one of roughly 754 checks across 18 categories, each with a SeverityPill carrying three inline style properties and a Link, all inside collapsed <details> elements.
findings.impact: Slow first paint on a phone, on the page whose entire purpose is to rank in search and be read by mobile arrivals.
findings.recommendation: Inline only the first N categories and link the rest to the existing /checks/category/[category] pages, or move the full index behind a crawlable ?all=1. The 754 individual check pages are intentional SEO surface and stay.

findings.title: API playground form inputs have no associated labels, contradicting the published accessibility statement
findings.description: app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx:511-518 renders a <label> with no htmlFor beside an <Input> with no id, repeated per expanded endpoint card. Same at :403-412 for the request-body textarea. The API-key field 300 lines earlier does it correctly with htmlFor="api-key" and id="api-key" at :202-211, so this is inconsistency rather than ignorance. app/legal/accessibility/page.tsx:89-90 claims 'All form inputs have associated labels for clarity.'
findings.impact: An expanded POST /scan card stacks four or five unlabeled text boxes; a screen-reader user hears five identical unnamed inputs. It also makes a published legal claim false.
findings.recommendation: Thread useId() through ParamField: const id = useId(), then htmlFor={id} and id={id}. Same for the body textarea.

findings.title: Route error and loading boundaries exist for five routes and are missing on the other eight core routes plus all public content
findings.description: error.tsx exists for /dashboard, /history, /shares, /assets, /teams, /admin, /profile, /compare only. Missing on /repos, /badge, /public-scans, /attack-surface, /host/[hostname], /shared/[token], /browser/[id], /demo, /changelog, /checks, /alternatives, /tools, /docs, /legal, /contact, /pricing, /donate, /security and all of /checkout. loading.tsx has the same gaps, and /checkout has none despite components/billing/checkout-skeleton.tsx existing. app/dashboard/error.tsx:9-16 states the intent: it keeps the surrounding chrome intact. Additionally app/admin/error.tsx lacks the role="alert" and icon aria-hidden that app/profile/error.tsx:20,26 has.
findings.impact: A thrown error on any of those routes falls through to the root boundary, losing the page chrome and dropping the user onto a bare error screen. That covers roughly 790 public pages, since only /compare has its own boundary.
findings.recommendation: Add error.tsx to the eight missing core routes and to the public content sections, following app/dashboard/error.tsx. Add loading.tsx to /checkout wrapping the existing CheckoutSkeleton. Bring app/admin/error.tsx in line with app/profile/error.tsx.

findings.title: The root 404 has no public chrome and its primary button sends logged-out visitors to the dashboard
findings.description: No in-scope content route has its own not-found.tsx, so all three dynamic content routes fall through to the root one, which renders no LandingNav, no Footer, and a primary button linking to ROUTES.DASHBOARD. The same shape applies to app/error.tsx:103.
findings.impact: A logged-out visitor landing on a stale /checks/some-renamed-id from a search result gets a chrome-less 404 whose main button bounces them through middleware to /login. The likeliest visitor to a dead check URL is exactly the person with no account.
findings.recommendation: Add app/checks/not-found.tsx and app/alternatives/not-found.tsx wrapping SeoPageShell, or make the root 404's primary button conditional on auth and default it to ROUTES.LANDING.

findings.title: publiclyListed on the share POST is silently ignored for an existing live share
findings.description: app/api/v3/history/[id]/share/route.ts:65-77 validates publiclyListed, but the early return at :109-122 for a live non-expired token skips share_publicly_listed entirely; it is only applied at :134-139 when creating a genuinely new share. Latent today because both UI toggles use the dedicated PUT .../share/publicly-listed.
findings.impact: Harmless now, but it will silently drop the value for whoever adds the expiry control from drift-02 to the same request.
findings.recommendation: Apply publiclyListed in the existing-share branch as well, or reject the field there explicitly rather than ignoring it.

findings.title: /public-scans shows three private tabs to anonymous visitors, all of which bounce to login
findings.description: app/public-scans/page.tsx:114 renders HistoryViewTabs unconditionally on a page anonymous visitors can reach. 'My History', 'Assets' and 'Attack Surface' all redirect a guest to /login.
findings.impact: Three of four tabs on a public page are traps for the exact audience the page exists to serve.
findings.recommendation: Gate the three private tabs behind useAuth() inside components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx:8-13.

findings.title: Twelve schema columns are written and never read, or defined and never written
findings.description: Verified dead, each with the grep that found no live reference: users.beta_access (:303) hardcoded false in every INSERT (lib/auth/auth.ts:282,361,382; staff-invite/[token]/route.ts:199), no UPDATE, no gate; users.email_session_revoked (:317) a legacy duplicate whose nine live references all resolve to notification_preferences; users.daily_scan_limit (:304) see drift-05; broadcast_recipients.opened_at and .clicked_at (:1155-1156) DDL only; broadcast_messages.scheduled_at (:1137) inserted but no worker consumes it and status is hardcoded 'draft' then 'sent', so the CHECK values 'scheduled' and 'cancelled' are unwritable; broadcast_messages.message_type (:1135) hardcoded "email" by the UI and never read by the send path (:504); data_requests.completed_at (:876) DDL only, the route uses downloaded_at; system_settings.setting_type (:1121) DDL only; gifted_subscriptions.reason (:950) selected in the GDPR export but the only INSERT (admin/route.ts:1671) omits it and the gift dialog has no field; badges.is_limited (:496) only ever inserted as false with no UPDATE anywhere; api_keys.team_id (:931) no reference in lib/api/api-keys.ts or app/api/v3/keys; scan_screenshots.width and .height (:1381-1382) written at lib/scanner/page-screenshot.ts:295, never selected, consumers read the result_meta copy.
findings.impact: Schema noise that misleads anyone reading the model, plus three cases (beta_access, message_type, scheduled_at) that look like shipped features and are not.
findings.recommendation: Decide per column: wire it or drop it. Deletions need owner sign-off. beta_access, broadcast scheduling and broadcast message_type are the three worth a product decision rather than a silent drop.

findings.title: Fifteen permission constants gate nothing, including two for a reports feature that does not exist
findings.description: Dead constants in lib/auth/permissions-client.ts: VIEW_USER_API_KEYS (:29), DELETE_ANY_TEAM (:76), VIEW_REPORTS (:80) and RESOLVE_REPORTS (:81) - there is no reports feature or table at all - VIEW_DEBUG_INFO (:92), CLEAR_CACHE (:94), SEND_USER_EMAILS (:85), ACCESS_ADMIN_PANEL (:11), ACCESS_STAFF_PAGE (:12) granted to six roles while app/staff does not exist, VIEW_USER_SESSIONS (:27), VIEW_BADGES (:34), VIEW_ALL_SCANS (:41), VIEW_SCAN_STATS (:43), VIEW_SUBSCRIPTIONS (:47), MANAGE_SUBSCRIPTIONS (:48). requireModerator() at lib/auth/authorization.ts:102-122 has zero call sites. Separately, several cards render ungated where a permission exists for them: the API Keys card at user-detail-panel.tsx:2561, sessions at :2667, all-scans at :2507, and badges at admin/route.ts:281-286 which has no permission call unlike its neighbours at :249 and :294.
findings.impact: An operator granting or withholding these permissions changes nothing, which is a security-adjacent false assurance. The ungated cards are the mirror image: data visible to staff roles that were never granted access to it.
findings.recommendation: Split into two passes: wire the four ungated cards to their existing permissions first, since that is a real access-control gap; then delete or implement the fifteen dead constants.

findings.title: Eight admin permission and UI gate mismatches, including one that exposes every AI conversation to any staff role
findings.description: The ai-chats tab requires MODERATE_CONTENT at app/admin/page.tsx:756 while its API only calls requireStaff() (app/api/v3/ai/conversations/route.ts:99), so any staff role can read every AI conversation by calling the endpoint directly. The 'Active Staff' tab at :705 has no gate but its API requires VIEW_AUDIT_LOG (admin/route.ts:294), guaranteeing a 403 for billing, content_manager and ops. EDIT_USER_EMAIL and EDIT_USER_PLAN gate nothing because the editors use canManageStaff (user-detail-panel.tsx:878,894,968,1019). The Staff Role card is gated on DELETE_USER (:1106) rather than EDIT_USER_ROLE. send_email has a permission (:85), a role grant (:178) and a success toast (app/admin/page.tsx:557) but no backend case, so it would 400; the repo's own test flags this at tests/lib/auth/permissions-client.test.ts:323-327.
findings.impact: One genuine authorization gap (AI conversations readable by any staff role via the API), one guaranteed-broken tab, and several controls whose permission labels do not describe what they actually check.
findings.recommendation: Fix the ai-chats API gate first: add the MODERATE_CONTENT check to app/api/v3/ai/conversations/route.ts so it matches its tab. Then align the remaining gates with the permissions their labels claim, and either implement or remove send_email.

findings.title: Seven runtime-tier settings have no reader or are read via the compiled constant
findings.description: The runtime tier promises effect within the 30 second TTL, so there is no 'next build' excuse. Dead: ENTERPRISE_EMAIL (registry.ts:456, never rendered), BILLING_HISTORY_PAGE_SIZE (:904, zero readers and no invoice route exists to consume it), SITE_NOTIFICATION_DEFAULT_DISMISS_DAYS (:2595, zero readers while components/shared/site-notifications.tsx:58-59 hardcodes 30 days - exactly the drift the constant was meant to prevent), MAX_EMAIL_LENGTH (:2655, reached only through the dead DATABASE object at lib/config/constants.ts:478-484). Read from the constant instead of the setting: POSTURE_DIGEST_MAX_FINDINGS_LISTED (:775 vs lib/notifications/posture-digest.ts:46,155), DOMAIN_REVERIFY_TICK_INTERVAL_MS (:737 vs lib/scanner/reverify-worker.ts:28,117,125), PAGINATION_MAX_PAGE_SIZE (:2763 vs four routes importing the constant). Also CONFIG_BACKGROUND_COLOR_LIGHT (config-values.ts:190, registry.ts:505) is admin-editable with no corresponding export, so it changes nothing.
findings.impact: Eight more admin controls that appear to work and do not, on top of the 28 build-tier ones in drift-07.
findings.recommendation: Wire the readers or remove the keys. SITE_NOTIFICATION_DEFAULT_DISMISS_DAYS is the clearest single fix: point site-notifications.tsx:58-59 at the setting.

findings.title: Nineteen API capabilities exist with no UI control, each with a specific screen it belongs on
findings.description: Verified by reading each handler. POST /api/v3/scan/import-spec (parses OpenAPI 3, Swagger 2 and Postman, returns targets) has no UI caller; API.SCAN_IMPORT_SPEC exists at lib/config/client-constants.ts:145 referenced only by the changelog - belongs on the bulk tab of components/scanner/scan-form.tsx. Authenticated crawl is unreachable: app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:216,300-337 accepts the same auth block, but app/dashboard/page.tsx:415-449 routes any request carrying auth to the single-page endpoint, so deep plus a login silently downgrades. PATCH /api/v3/teams/members (role change, with ceiling and self-demotion guards) has no caller; the only way to change a teammate's role is remove and re-invite - belongs on components/teams/team-members-list.tsx:160. PATCH /api/v3/account/discord (syncAvatar, syncName) unreachable while components/modals/discord-profile-modal.tsx:27-28 has exactly those checkboxes but POSTs OAuth query-string values to /api/v3/auth/update, so it only works in the seconds after connecting. Badge revoke (DELETE /api/v3/badge/site?scanId=N, sets revoked_at) has no caller, so a badge pasted into a public README cannot be killed - belongs under the ScopeToggle at components/badge/badge-preview.tsx:261. Support tickets cannot be reopened: the route permits it at app/api/v3/support-tickets/[id]/route.ts:321-328 but both UIs only send resolved and closed, and replying to a closed ticket 409s. The updater can only install the newest release (app/api/v3/admin/updater/apply/route.ts:94,120-123 accepts any targetVersion; components/admin/features/updater-manager.tsx:185 always sends status.latest) so there is no rollback or pin. /api/v3/health returns schema_version vs schema_required, missing_tables, latency and pool stats and has no consumer, so a self-hoster needing a migration has no in-app signal. Stripe setup is curl-only, and both routes gate on role !== ADMIN exactly (setup-products/route.ts:31, setup-webhook/route.ts:36) which locks out super_admin unlike every other admin route. Also: teamId on schedules and webhooks, webhook type pinning (both UI paths hardcode "auto"), GitHub repo scan branch/ref, per-finding feedback notes, browser session viewport and ttlSeconds (the latter hardcoded to 360 at scan-actions-menu.tsx:384, defeating the admin setting), security alerts limit/offset/severity/user_id (hardcoded to 100 so alert 101 is unreachable), admin AI-conversations userId filter, admin notification email tone (hardcoded "info"), history rescan dropping all original scan options, scan source 'scheduled' rendering as "Web", admin content and public directory page sizes, and markAllRead on the notification bell.
findings.impact: Nineteen shipped backend capabilities that no user can reach. Several are not conveniences: badge revoke has no alternative, authenticated crawl silently does something other than what was asked, and the health endpoint is the only signal a self-hoster has that their schema is behind.
findings.recommendation: Triage by user harm rather than effort. Highest first: authenticated crawl (silent wrong behaviour), badge revoke (no alternative exists), team member role change (workaround is destructive), support ticket reopen (dead end), health panel (self-host blocker). The rest are ordinary missing controls.

findings.title: Four backend capabilities are gated behind conditions nothing can satisfy
findings.description: domains.team_id (instrumentation.ts:3176) is read for team access at app/api/v3/domains/route.ts:33, but the INSERT at :120 omits it, no PATCH exists anywhere under app/api/v3/domains/ (exports are GET, POST, DELETE plus verify POST), all four UPDATE/INSERT statements skip it, and components/profile/tabs/domains-section.tsx:147 hardcodes team_id: null - yet app/docs/teams/page.tsx:425 documents it as a feature. DEFAULT_API_KEY_DAILY_LIMIT (registry.ts:1527-1536) is admin-editable and read at lib/api/api-keys.ts:70 via `dailyLimit ?? await getSetting(...)`, but generateApiKey has exactly one production caller (app/api/v3/keys/route.ts:95) which always passes an explicit number, so the branch is dead; compounding, app/docs/api/page.tsx:738 and app/docs/rate-limits/page.tsx:173 tell users the default is 50 while the real value is the plan's apiRequestsPerDay, 25 on Free. access_rules.is_active = false is writable via the API but the list query filters WHERE is_active = true (admin/features/route.ts:168), so a deactivated rule vanishes and can never be reactivated. The empty-string state of CHROME_WEB_STORE_URL and FIREFOX_ADDON_URL (registry.ts:397-412) is documented as falling back to a packaged release, but the admin write goes through z.url() which rejects "", the env path skips empty overrides (runtime-config.ts:89), and reset restores a non-empty default - and the fallback UI does not exist either, since app/docs/extension/page.tsx:113,139 link unconditionally under a hardcoded 'Live' badge.
findings.impact: Four documented behaviours that cannot occur. The API key limit case additionally publishes a wrong number to users in two docs pages.
findings.recommendation: Correct the two docs pages about the API key default immediately, since that is user-facing misinformation. Then either implement domains.team_id (a PATCH route plus a selector) or remove it and its docs claim.

findings.title: Two entitlements are enforced but never advertised, and one has no admin setting at all
findings.description: The crawl page-selection limit is hardcoded at lib/billing/crawl-page-limits.ts:18-23 (25/50/100/250) and enforced at app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:258, but a grep for CRAWL_PAGES in lib/config/registry.ts returns zero. It is the only per-plan entitlement with no registry key, so it is absent from Admin > Settings > Billing and from components/pricing/pricing-features.tsx, surfacing only at point of use (components/scanner/crawl-url-selector.tsx:50). githubReviewTokensPerWindow is enforced per plan but no plan's features array mentions GitHub review (only AI review tokens at lib/billing/catalog.ts:141,174,205), so a Free user hits a hard 403 with no prior signal. Separately, lib/billing/github-review-usage.ts:365-372 implements a free-plan trial whose own comment reads 'Hidden trial, never advertised on the pricing page', while Free's githubReviewTokensPerWindow of 0 makes components/pricing/pricing-features.tsx:85-89 render a cross for Free.
findings.impact: Two invisible paywalls that users meet as a 403 rather than as a plan comparison, and a genuine free-tier benefit that the pricing page actively denies exists.
findings.recommendation: Add BILLING_*_CRAWL_PAGES registry keys and a Scanning row on /pricing. Add a GitHub review row to the plan comparison. Decide whether the hidden trial should be advertised; if it stays hidden, stop rendering a cross for a capability Free actually has.

findings.title: Five destructive or persisting actions fail silently across history, shares and teams
findings.description: components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:505-515 catches a failed Delete scan with only setDeleting(false), leaving the confirm dialog open and the spinner stopped with no explanation. app/shares/page.tsx:123-144 (revokeShare) and :100-121 (togglePubliclyListed) do nothing on a non-ok response, so the dialog closes or the toggle silently reverts. app/teams/page.tsx:428-457 (handleRename) is the only action on that page that does not set actionError. app/history/page.tsx:389-397 with components/history/history-notes.tsx:22-27 always exits edit mode, so on a failed PATCH the note stays on screen from local state while nothing was persisted; app/dashboard/page.tsx:375-387 catches and discards outright.
findings.impact: A user revokes a share and believes it is revoked. A user edits scan notes and believes they are saved. Neither happened. For share revocation specifically this is a security-relevant false confirmation.
findings.recommendation: Surface an error in every one of the five handlers, and for the notes case keep the editor open with the unsaved text rather than exiting on failure.

findings.title: The history view tabs wrap to two lines on mobile, breaking the underline baseline across four pages
findings.description: components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx:29 is `flex gap-1 border-b border-border/50` with links at `px-3 py-2` (:37). Four tabs need about 409px against 343px available. They do not overflow because min-width:auto floors them at about 294px; instead every multi-word label wraps ('Attack / Surface'), producing ragged tab heights and a broken border-b baseline. Affects /history, /assets, /attack-surface and /public-scans.
findings.impact: The primary navigation for four pages looks broken on every phone.
findings.recommendation: Add overflow-x-auto to line 29 and shrink-0 whitespace-nowrap to the Link at line 37.

findings.title: An invisible tag button sits under every history row's URL and steals the tap
findings.description: components/history/scan-tags.tsx:178-182 applies opacity-0 with group-hover and group-focus-within reveals. revealOnHover defaults to true and components/history/history-scan-row.tsx:134 uses the default. opacity-0 does not disable pointer events, and phones never hover, so a roughly 24x18px invisible button sits under every row's URL.
findings.impact: Tapping a scan row near the URL opens a tag input instead of the scan.
findings.recommendation: Add pointer-events-none with group-hover:pointer-events-auto and group-focus-within:pointer-events-auto, or use opacity-100 sm:opacity-0.

findings.title: The software inventory header clips its own count and chevron on mobile because the card is overflow-hidden
findings.description: components/scanner/software-inventory-panel.tsx:195-221. When vulnerableCount > 0 the header row measures about 363px against 343px at 375px and 358px at 390px. The card is overflow-hidden at :189, so the count and chevron are clipped rather than scrollable.
findings.impact: The component count and the expand affordance are invisible on a phone whenever the panel has something worth expanding for.
findings.recommendation: Line 198: add min-w-0 flex-1 truncate. Line 211: add hidden sm:inline.

findings.title: The host page CTA says 'Scan example.com now' and scans vulnradar.dev instead
findings.description: app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:170-175 renders a button linking to ROUTES.DEMO with the label `Scan {data.host} now`. /demo has exactly one action, handleSelfScan, which hardcodes the target at app/demo/page.tsx:38 as `const siteUrl = window.location.origin;`. There is no target parameter.
findings.impact: The call to action on a public SEO landing page promises to scan the host the visitor came to see and scans the vendor's own site instead. This is the conversion path for organic traffic.
findings.recommendation: Link to `${ROUTES.DASHBOARD}?scan=${encodeURIComponent(data.host)}` - the dashboard already treats a dotted ?scan= value as a target (app/dashboard/page.tsx:70-72, 784-793) - or relabel the button to 'Try the scanner'.

findings.title: activeTab is never reset between findings, so opening a finding with fewer code examples throws
findings.description: components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:662 is useState(0) while :922-923 reads issue.codeExamples[activeTab].code. The component explicitly supports issue changing while mounted (useEffect keyed on issue.id at :675), and the sibling RemediationControl was given key={issue.id} at :826 for exactly this reason; activeTab was missed.
findings.impact: Going from a finding with three code examples (tab 2 open) to one with a single example throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading code)' and takes out the view.
findings.recommendation: Add key={issue.id} at the IssueDetail call sites, or clamp the index against codeExamples.length.

findings.title: The pagination control overflows the viewport once a user passes 50 scans
findings.description: components/ui/pagination-control.tsx:118-208 is flex items-center gap-1 with no wrap: four arrow buttons at h-8 w-8 plus up to seven number or ellipsis slots at min-w-8 (:151-177), about 388px against 343px. Reached on /history and /assets at page size 10 once a user has more than 50 scans.
findings.impact: Horizontal page scroll appears on the two most-used list pages as soon as a user has real data.
