The endpoint also allows disabling security notification emails (password-changed, 2fa-changed, new-device alerts), which violates the principle that security-critical alerts should be non-disableable. Additionally the route calls migrate() DDL on every request.
findings.recommendation: Remove email from GET response; block disabling of security notification categories; remove migrate() call (run migration once at startup or via migration script).
findings.fixedIn: security(AUDIT-004): rate limiting, 2FA gate, LIKE escaping, DKIM timeout, CSP, unsubscribe hardening
findings.fixSummary: unsubscribe/route.ts rewritten: email removed from GET response, security category forced to true in all reads/writes (NON_DISABLEABLE set), unsubscribe_all sets security=true, migrate() DDL removed.

findings.title: LIKE metacharacter injection in admin user/team search
findings.description: Admin user and team listing routes used raw search terms in LIKE queries without escaping % and _ metacharacters. A malicious admin could trigger unintended broad matches.
findings.recommendation: Escape % and _ in the search string before using it in LIKE patterns; add ESCAPE '\' clause to queries.
findings.fixedIn: security(AUDIT-004): rate limiting, 2FA gate, LIKE escaping, DKIM timeout, CSP, unsubscribe hardening
findings.fixSummary: Both admin routes now do search.replace(/[\\%_]/g, '\\$&') before inserting into LIKE patterns, and both queries include ESCAPE '\\'.

findings.title: DKIM DNS queries have no per-query timeout
findings.description: checkDKIM in async-checks.ts probes multiple DKIM selectors via dns.resolveTxt with no per-query AbortSignal or timeout. A slow or unresponsive DNS resolver can stall the entire async-checks pipeline for an unbounded duration.
findings.recommendation: Wrap each dns.resolveTxt call in a Promise.race with a short timeout (e.g. 3s) to bound the total DKIM probe time.
findings.fixedIn: security(AUDIT-004): rate limiting, 2FA gate, LIKE escaping, DKIM timeout, CSP, unsubscribe hardening
findings.fixSummary: async-checks.ts adds resolveTxtWithTimeout() and resolveCnameWithTimeout() helpers that race the DNS promise against a 3s timer. All DKIM selector lookups use these wrappers.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options set to SAMEORIGIN in COMMON_HEADERS but DENY in deployed middleware
findings.description: lib/config/constants.ts COMMON_HEADERS had X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN while middleware.ts applied DENY. The mismatch meant routes using COMMON_HEADERS (rather than the middleware header) allowed same-origin framing, weakening clickjacking protection.
findings.recommendation: Changed COMMON_HEADERS X-Frame-Options to DENY.

findings.title: Stripe API missing from CSP connect-src
findings.description: middleware.ts CSP did not include https://api.stripe.com in connect-src, blocking Stripe Embedded Checkout fetch calls and causing silent checkout failures in browsers with strict CSP enforcement.
findings.recommendation: Added https://api.stripe.com to connect-src.

findings.title: ProviderInfo.url leaked internal AI provider URL via X-AI-Provider-Url response header
findings.description: chat-widget.tsx read the X-AI-Provider-Url header from AI chat responses and stored it in ProviderInfo.url, then rendered it as a link in the chat footer. This exposed the internal provider endpoint (Ollama URL, custom endpoint, etc.) to end users.
findings.recommendation: Removed url from ProviderInfo type. Removed X-AI-Provider-Url header reading. Changed Powered by link to plain text.

findings.title: CSP connect-src has trailing https: wss: wildcards
findings.description: CSP connect-src 'self' https://challenges.cloudflare.com ... https://www.browserbase.com wss://*.browserbase.com https: wss: ends with the scheme-only wildcards https: wss:, which permits fetch/XHR/WS to any HTTPS origin.
findings.recommendation: Drop the trailing 'https:' 'wss:' scheme wildcards; allowlist specific API hosts.

findings.title: docker-publish.yml dual-tags :latest in GHCR
findings.description: Every tagged release also pushes :latest. Anyone running :latest (despite compose using :3.0.0) gets an unreviewed mutable reference.
findings.recommendation: Drop the second -t $IMAGE:latest + matching docker push $IMAGE:latest.

findings.title: docker-compose app port binds to 0.0.0.0
findings.description: Short-form binding defaults to 0.0.0.0:3000. Self-hosters fronted by nginx expose Node directly on the LAN.

findings.title: package.json engines allows Node 20 (EOL)
findings.description: engines allows Node 20 which reached EOL on 2026-04-30 per the Dockerfile comment. Yet package.json still accepts Node 20 dev environments.
findings.recommendation: Drop the '<21.0.0' branch from engines.node.

findings.title: Email regex duplicated with character-class overlap
findings.description: The same email regex appears in content.ts, information-disclosure.ts, secrets-extended.ts (3x). [a-zA-Z0-9.-]+ is greedy and overlaps with the trailing \.[a-zA-Z]{2,}.
findings.recommendation: Hoist a single EMAIL_RE constant in lib/scanner/_helpers.ts; replace with anchored pattern.

findings.title: Reset/verify tokens use raw SHA-256, not HMAC
findings.description: Token hashes use sha256(token). Token entropy is sufficient but HMAC-SHA256 is the canonical pattern.
findings.recommendation: Use createHmac('sha256', secret).update(token).digest('hex') with a server secret.

findings.title: discover route skips validateScanTarget on the user-supplied root URL
findings.description: scan/discover parses the user URL into a hostname, then fires DNS queries to ~140 prefix names and crt.sh / hackertarget / subdomain.center / rapiddns BEFORE validateScanTarget is ever called.
findings.recommendation: Call validateScanTarget(url) on the user-supplied URL first; reject before any external lookup.

findings.title: Webhook registration uses hand-rolled partial private-IP blocklist
findings.description: Replaces the canonical isPrivateIP check from safe-fetch.ts. Misses 127.0.0.2, 169.254.0.1, IPv6 ULA, IPv4-mapped IPv6, NAT64.
findings.recommendation: Replace the manual list with validateScanTarget(url).

findings.title: Verified correct: no icon-only button without an accessible name, no onClick on a bare div, no positive tabIndex, every image has alt, and prefers-reduced-motion is honoured globally
findings.description: Recorded so the next audit does not redo the work. (1) Icon-only buttons: a script walked every `
findings.impact: None. Documented to narrow the search area for the next accessibility pass: the risk in this codebase is concentrated in the colour tokens (a11y-01 through a11y-03, a11y-05, a11y-10, a11y-18) and in the small set of hand-rolled components that bypass the shadcn/Radix primitives, not in the general component library.
findings.recommendation: No action. When re-auditing, start from app/globals.css and from the files that do not import from components/ui/, since Radix already covers dialogs, sheets, dropdowns, selects, tooltips, toasts and tabs correctly wherever they are used.

findings.title: Verified correct: the compiled AI knowledge is byte-identical to a fresh compile, and the CLI, plan quotas, active-probe ids, crawl quota semantics, reports and triage pages all match the code
findings.description: Recorded so the next audit does not redo the work. (1) lib/ai/docs-knowledge.md is in sync: re-running a redirected copy of scripts/compile-docs-knowledge.mjs against the current app/docs tree produced a file differing only in the `_Auto-compiled ... on <date>_` line, so no docs page has been edited without a recompile. (2) app/docs/cli matches cli/lib.mjs exactly: all ten flags, their defaults (apiBase, crawl false, maxCritical 0, maxHigh 0, maxMedium -1, timeout 300, pollInterval 5, json false at cli/lib.mjs:5-14) and the 0/1 exit-code contract. (3) The daily quota table on app/docs/rate-limits (25/100/150/500 scans, 25/100/5000/unlimited API) matches lib/billing/catalog.ts:116-213. (4) The nine active-probe scoped tokens listed at app/docs/api/page.tsx:55 match lib/scanner/active-probe-catalog.ts:48-96 exactly, and the 18 scanner categories at :53 match lib/scanner/types.ts:23-41. (5) The crawl quota semantics (per-page on session auth, one unit on Bearer) match lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:445-497. (6) The scan time budgets 300/900/1800 match lib/config/config-values.ts:544-551. (7) app/docs/reports matches app/api/v3/history/[id]/report/route.ts including the markdown alias, case-insensitivity, the json default, and every Content-Type/Content-Disposition pair. (8) app/docs/triage's remediation and support-ticket endpoint tables match the exported handlers exactly. (9) app/docs/teams' 13 endpoint rows all resolve to real routes and methods. (10) The GitHub token budgets 0/200k/1M/5M and the 300,000-token per-run 413 ceiling match lib/billing/catalog.ts and lib/config/config-values.ts:878. (11) All 28 endpoint cards on app/docs/api resolve to a route file that exports the documented method, and every `/api/v3/...` path string across all 20 docs pages resolves to a real route.
findings.impact: None. Documents what was checked and found correct so a later audit can skip it.
findings.recommendation: No action. Re-verify item (1) whenever an app/docs/*/page.tsx changes without a build, since the script's own staleness warning is dead (see apidoc-29).

findings.title: Negative results: pipeline secrets handling is clean, every action is SHA-pinned, and the release artifact chain works end to end
findings.description: Verified so the next audit does not repeat it. (1) No workflow uses `pull_request_target`, `secrets: inherit`, or `workflow_call`; grep across .github/ returns nothing for all three. (2) The only secret referenced anywhere in .github/ is `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` (7 references across 5 files); no third-party credential is present in the pipeline. (3) No secret is passed as a Docker build arg or baked into an image ENV: Dockerfile:16 declares only `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` as an ARG and lines 37-40 set placeholder values, with the comment at 41-44 explaining that API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY is deliberately left unset so it fails closed. (4) No untrusted `github.event.*` field is interpolated into a `run:` body; release.yml routes `release.tag_name` and `workflow_run.head_branch` through `env:` at lines 86-88 with a comment naming the CodeQL rule, and docker-publish.yml:40 and 43 use the `GITHUB_REF_NAME` and `GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER` shell variables rather than expressions. (5) All 23 `uses:` lines across the seven workflows are pinned to a 40-character commit SHA with a version comment (23 of 23 match `@[0-9a-f]{40}`). (6) Permissions are scoped per workflow or per job everywhere except label.yml (see ci-05); ci.yml is `contents: read`, docker-publish.yml scopes `packages: write` and `id-token: write` to the one job that needs them, release.yml scopes `contents: write` and `id-token: write` to its one job. (7) `continue-on-error` appears exactly once (release.yml:168, see ci-12) and there is no `|| true` anywhere. (8) `npm audit --audit-level=high --omit=dev` currently reports 0 vulnerabilities, so the gate at ci.yml:71 is passing rather than being routed around. (9) next.config.mjs sets no `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors`; `eslint.ignoreDuringBuilds: true` at line 23 is compensated by the standalone `npm run lint` step at ci.yml:40. `output: "standalone"` is deliberately absent and consistent with Dockerfile:75-79 copying `.next` and `node_modules` (line 4-8 comment). (10) The CI knowledge-drift gate works: I confirmed empirically that `git diff --exit-code --ignore-matching-lines='compiled from'` ignores a date-only change and still exits 1 on a real content change, and the date lines in all five generated files contain the string "compiled from". (11) The release artifact chain is live and correct: I fetched the releases API and v3.6.0 through v3.7.2 each carry the tarball, the `.tar.gz.cert` cosign bundle, `sha256sums.txt`, both extension zips, and the CycloneDX SBOM, and the asset names match exactly what lib/updater/apply.ts:85-88 looks for. (12) Nothing can publish an image from a branch push: docker-publish.yml triggers only on `push: tags: v*`.
findings.impact: None. This records what was checked and found correct.
findings.recommendation: No action. Re-verify items 5, 6 and 8 if new workflows are added.

findings.title: Container, IaC, cloud and SCA scanning and an IAST agent are real competitor features that this product should deliberately never build, and saying so is part of the answer
findings.category: list (a) ranks 16 to 18: the deliberate do-not-build list
findings.description: Three capabilities appear in the peer set and belong at the bottom of the ranking with a stated reason rather than in a backlog. (1) Container, IaC, cloud and SCA scanning: Snyk is the only vendor of the eight spanning SAST, SCA, container, IaC, secrets, DAST and SBOM, and the best tool in that space is Trivy, which is free, Apache-2.0, 37,679 stars, emits SARIF 2.1.0 and CycloneDX/SPDX, and would take years to match. VulnRadar's nearest existing capability is deliberately narrow and correct: lib/scanner/github-repo-scan.ts:1 reuses the secrets-extended detectors verbatim against repo file contents, and lib/scanner/software-inventory.ts plus osv-check.ts correlate detected libraries against OSV for the live URL. (2) An IAST agent: only Acunetix ships one (AcuSensor, for PHP, ASP.NET, Java and Node.js), and none of the other seven has a comparable server-side sensor. It would require a per-runtime agent, an installation story, and version support forever, and it directly contradicts the product's own repeated promise that there is nothing to deploy alongside your application (components/landing/landing-features.tsx:4, app/checks/page.tsx's "0 agents to install"). (3) An internal or behind-the-firewall scanning agent, which Snyk and Intruder both ship as a Docker or Kubernetes workload: for this product the self-host path is the answer to that requirement and is strictly better, since the whole scanner runs inside the network rather than a relay.
findings.impact: None if left alone. The risk this finding addresses is the opposite one: each of these is impressive on a competitor's feature matrix, and a small team that chases them spends quarters reaching parity in a market it is not in, while the cheap items in comp-02, comp-03, comp-04, comp-06 and comp-07 stay unbuilt.
findings.recommendation: Record all three as permanent non-goals in AGENTS.md or a short ROADMAP note so they stop reappearing. For (1), do the interop instead of the feature: document the pairing in app/docs ("Trivy for images and dependencies, VulnRadar for the deployed URL"), and since both emit SARIF 2.1.0, both already land in the same GitHub Security tab with no work. For (3), make the self-host answer explicit on the relevant /alternatives rows rather than building an agent: "They give you a relay container. This runs the whole scanner inside your network." That claim depends on comp-01 being fixed first.

findings.title: Position on the 2026 agentic-pentest shift: VulnRadar should deliberately not compete, and should use its determinism as the counter-position
findings.description: Every major vendor launched an agentic AI pentest product this year: Invicti Agentic Pentest (announced 29 to 30 July 2026, parallel specialised agents for SQLi, RCE, XSS, SSRF, XXE, insecure deserialization, path traversal and NoSQLi, max $500 per pentest, 24-hour turnaround), Intruder AI Pentesting from $3,500 per test, Astra autonomous agents, and Snyk Evo Continuous Offensive Security. All are aimed at the buyer who needs a pentest report for an auditor, and all are priced 10x to 100x below a human pentest (audits/AUDIT-014/research-competitors-commercial.md, "The 2026 industry shift"). Three facts from this codebase determine the right answer. First, the product's headline promise is the opposite claim: components/landing/landing-features.tsx:26 to :32 is titled "Run it twice, get the same answer twice" and states "There is no model in the detection path deciding today that something is medium when yesterday it was low", which is what makes lib/scanner/regression-alert.ts's diff and the CI gate in .github/actions/scan-gate/action.yml meaningful at all. Second, an agentic pentest requires unattended exploitation against a live target, which this product has structurally refused: the nine active probes are opt-in and gated behind verified domain ownership (lib/scanner/active-probe-catalog.ts:117), and there is no out-of-band channel (comp-11). Third, AI is already used here on the correct side of that line, for triage rather than detection: lib/ai/verify-findings.ts attaches aiVerdict and aiConfidence that re-weight the safety rating (lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts:27 to :40) without changing what the deterministic engine found.
findings.impact: Entering this market would cost the product the one claim it currently wins on, and it would compete on turnaround and exploitation depth against vendors with dedicated infrastructure, insurance and legal cover. Ignoring it silently is also a cost: "why not just buy a $500 agentic pentest" is now a live objection at every price point above free, and there is no answer to it on the site.
findings.recommendation: Do not compete on agentic pentesting. Take the counter-position explicitly, because determinism is a differentiator only if someone states what it is against. Add an FAQ entry to app/landing/page.tsx's buildFaq array, in the existing blunt voice, along these lines: "Do you do AI pentesting? No. The detection engine is deterministic: the same URL produces the same finding IDs every run, which is what lets you fail a build on a specific ID and diff Tuesday against Friday. We use a model to triage and explain findings, never to decide whether one exists." Keep the AI confined to lib/ai/verify-findings.ts's triage role and to the assistant, and never let a model reach the detection path. If a pentest-report artifact is ever wanted, build the attestation page described in comp-14, which is the deliverable that buyer actually needs, rather than the exploitation engine.

findings.title: Verified negative results: five capabilities the prior competitor hypothesis listed as gaps already exist and are complete, so the next audit does not need to re-check them
findings.description: The prior session's candidate list (compliance reports, Jira integration, proof-based exploit evidence, CVE and port scanning, SSO/auth-flow scanning, cloud and container scanning, IAST agent) was a hypothesis. Five items are wrong or substantially wrong and are closed here. (1) Compliance reports EXIST and are complete: lib/reports/compliance-mappings.ts:43 covers PCI DSS 4.0, SOC 2 TSC, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A, OWASP ASVS 4.0, HIPAA and GDPR, with a documented OWASP-Top-10 backbone and an honest unmapped-findings path, rendered by lib/reports/compliance-report.ts and exported at app/api/v3/history/[id]/report/route.ts. (2) SARIF EXISTS and is complete: lib/reports/sarif-report.ts:1 to :253 emits SARIF 2.1.0 with rule descriptors, security-severity and tags, wired to both the export menu (components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:556) and the API. (3) CVE and port scanning EXIST: lib/scanner/port-scan.ts (749 lines), lib/scanner/protocols/banner.ts, lib/scanner/software-inventory.ts (1,202 lines), lib/scanner/osv-check.ts and lib/scanner/cve-enrichment.ts. (4) Authenticated scanning EXISTS in three modes with a real browser-rendered login path; see comp-05 for what is actually missing. (5) A GitHub Action EXISTS at .github/actions/scan-gate/action.yml (195 lines, complete poll-and-gate); see comp-02 for what it does not do. Also verified and worth recording: the SSL letter grade is computed in-house from a live handshake (lib/scanner/ssl-grade.ts:1 to :30) and is NOT derived from the SSL Labs API, so the SSL Labs v4 prohibition on commercial use does not apply to this product, a risk the research explicitly flagged for checking.
findings.impact: None directly. Recording it prevents the next audit or roadmap session from re-filing five gaps that are already shipped, which is the failure mode that turns a competitive review into busywork.
findings.recommendation: Supersede the earlier seven-item competitor-gap list with this section's ranked list. Of the original seven, only proof-based exploit evidence (comp-11) and Jira (comp-08, and reframed toward closing the GitHub loop first) survive as real gaps, cloud/container and IAST move to the permanent non-goal list (comp-16), and the other three are done. Separately, one item outside section 20's scope but adjacent to it: AUDIT-013#subdeps-01 found the npm name `vulnradar` is unclaimed while /docs/cli advertises `npx vulnradar`, which is a distribution gap of the same kind as comp-02's missing Marketplace listing and should be fixed in the same pass.

findings.title: Negative results: every documented npm command exists, all 25 docs anchors resolve, the CLI help matches its implementation, and every SECURITY-POSTURE part A control is really in middleware
findings.description: Checked mechanically and found correct, recorded so the next audit does not repeat it. (1) Commands: every `npm run <script>` and every `node scripts/*.mjs` appearing in README, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, AGENTS, CLAUDE, SUPPORT, scripts/README, cli/README, extension/README, tests/README and all 20 docs pages resolves to a real entry in the matching package.json or a real file, 24 distinct scripts across three package manifests, zero misses. (2) Links: across the same set plus app/legal, only five internal href targets do not resolve to a route in app/ or a file in public/, and four of those are API base paths or wildcards; the only genuine dead one is /bimi-logo.svg in SECURITY-POSTURE.md:56, for a record marked optional. (3) Anchors: all 25 in-page and cross-page `#id` links in app/docs, app/legal and components/docs resolve to a real id, including the six cross-page ones. (4) CLI: cli/README.md's ten flags and all seven defaults match cli/lib.mjs:5-14 and :124-133 exactly, and cli/package.json's `engines: >=18` is consistent with the README's Node 18+ note. (5) Extension: '18 check families + 6 service probes' matches extension/src/lib/categories.ts exactly. (6) SECURITY-POSTURE part A: every control in the table is really set in middleware.ts (HSTS max-age=63072000 with includeSubDomains and preload at :160, strict-dynamic CSP at :62, Report-Only Trusted-Types at :136, X-Frame-Options DENY at :137, nosniff at :138, Referrer-Policy at :139, COOP and CORP same-origin at :146-147, COEP unsafe-none as documented at :158) plus httpOnly + production-gated secure + SameSite=Lax cookies at lib/auth/auth.ts:63-65; security.txt's Expires is in the future and mta-sts.txt is in the documented `mode: testing`. (7) CONTRIBUTING.md's 'all commits to main must be GPG-signed' holds: the last twelve commits all report %G? = G. (8) CLAUDE.md's file-map table resolves for all 15 paths, and its browser-session note (1 minute start, +1 minute, 5 minute max) matches app/browser/[id]/page.tsx:126, :196 and :287. (9) README's factual claims that are checkable are right: 18 categories matches EXACT_CHECK_CATEGORY_COUNT, 25 free scans a day matches lib/billing/catalog.ts:116, all five export formats exist under lib/reports/, and the PostgreSQL 14+ floor holds (the newest server feature used is GENERATED ALWAYS AS STORED, which is PG12).
findings.impact: None. Recorded to save the next audit the work and to bound where the real problems are: the failures in this section are concentrated in stale architecture prose and in operator recovery procedures, not in command names or links.
findings.recommendation: No action. If a link or command checker is ever wanted in CI, the three throwaway scripts used here (command extraction against package.json, internal href resolution against app/ page.tsx and route.ts, anchor resolution against id= attributes) are each about 60 lines and run in under a second on this repo.

findings.title: Negative result: the theme system, motion policy, focus policy and copy discipline are genuinely sound, and the auth flow and the scan result view are the internal reference examples to copy
findings.description: Recorded so a future audit does not redo this. (a) Theming is real, not aspirational: across all of app/ and components/ there are exactly three `dark:` class overrides (components/landing/landing-hero.tsx, components/profile/tabs/developer/schedules-section.tsx, and the shadow on the hero readout). Everything else switches via the CSS variables, which is why dsn-01's contrast fix can be made in one place. (b) Motion: app/globals.css:141-152 sets a global prefers-reduced-motion block that caps animation-duration and iteration-count, so tell-tale 14 passes product-wide even where a component uses animate-pulse. (c) Focus: app/globals.css:370-372 sets a global :focus-visible ring with a documented exclusion for Radix collection items, so tell-tale 13's focus half holds even on the elements that do not opt in locally. (d) Copy: the only em dashes in app/ and components/ are inside code comments and one empty-cell placeholder at components/admin/features/content-manager.tsx:451, so the CLAUDE.md ban is genuinely honoured; "Everything you need" survives only as mid-sentence prose at app/docs/architecture/page.tsx:77 (already AUDIT-011#design F2). (e) The auth flow is the strongest in-app work and should be the model: components/auth/auth-split-layout.tsx:77-146 is a one-canvas asymmetric layout with a real ResponseReadout, a hard-broken two-line headline and a border-l definition list, and components/auth/auth-shell.tsx:22-90 centralises the field class, focus ring, step indicator and heading so every screen in the flow is identical by construction. (f) The scan result view is the strongest data surface: components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx is a genuine single source of truth, SeverityDistribution at :129-190 is one bar with a legend rather than five stat cards exactly as its docblock claims, and components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx carries zero raw palette colours across 300-odd lines. (g) The joined stat strip idiom (`grid grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-4 gap-px bg-border`) is the correct anti-pattern-avoidant shape and is used consistently on /dashboard, /history, /assets and /shares; only its implementation is duplicated (dsn-06), not its design.
findings.impact: None. This is a record of what was checked and found correct.
findings.recommendation: No action. When building a new in-app flow, copy components/auth/auth-shell.tsx's shape: put the shared field class, focus ring and heading component in one module per flow so the screens cannot drift. When building a new data panel, copy components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx. Point new contributors at those two files rather than at the landing page, which is a marketing surface and does not answer in-app questions.

findings.title: Verified clean: the docs surface, the email layout, and the Markdown and SARIF severity vocabulary are all consistent systems, and the AUDIT-013 label inconsistency does not reach any export
findings.description: Recording what was checked and found correct, so the next audit does not repeat it. (1) DOCS ARE ONE SYSTEM. All 19 docs pages plus app/docs/page.tsx use DocsHero and DocsSection; the chrome (breadcrumb, prev/next pager, table of contents, sidebar, mobile nav) lives once in components/docs/docs-shell.tsx:60-90 and is applied by app/docs/layout.tsx to every page, so no page can forget it. Hand-rolled cards outside the primitives total 7 across 12,000 lines of docs pages (2 in api, 3 in setup, 1 each in developers and rate-limits) and there are zero hand-rolled `<table>` elements. DocsCallout (components/docs/docs-callout.tsx:12-18) draws its four variants from semantic tokens with a left rule and an explicit docblock rejecting the icon-in-a-rounded-square. The open docs issues remain AUDIT-011#docs-03 (124-character measure), #docs-04 (shell wider than its nav), #docs-07 (unlabelled playground inputs) and #docs-11 (tablist without tabpanel); nothing new was found. (2) EMAIL HAS THE SHARED LAYOUT IT NEEDS. lib/email/email.ts:107-180 is a single layout() used by every template through sendEmail:431, with seven composition helpers (:193-332), an escapeHtml applied at every interpolation, a plain-text alternative on every template (47 `text:` keys against 46 `html:`), zero emoji, zero em dashes in user-facing strings, a 600px table with a max-width:600px media query and mobile padding overrides (:138-141), `color-scheme` and `supported-color-schemes` meta (:133-134) which is the correct guard against forced dark-mode inversion, and colours sourced from lib/config/brand.ts rather than hardcoded (:19-46). Copy voice follows the rules: mechanism-first, specific, no platitudes. The open items are dsnx-05, dsnx-06 and dsnx-11 only. (3) SEVERITY VOCABULARY IN EXPORTS IS CONSISTENT. AUDIT-013#dup-02 found `/checks` labelling info as "Informational" (lib/seo/seo-ui.tsx:30) against "Info" elsewhere. That inconsistency does NOT reach any export: markdown-report.ts:31-37 and compliance-report.ts:29-34 both use "Info", pdf-report.ts:273 prints `sev.toUpperCase()`, sarif-report.ts maps to SARIF's own three levels, and CSV uses `f.severity.toUpperCase()`. Ordering is critical-to-info in all five, and findings arrive pre-sorted from lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:711. "Informational" appears in only three places repo-wide and none of them is an export. (4) THE EXTENSION POPUP DOES MATCH ITS STORE ART. store_1.png's product panel shows a risk score with a label, a severity chip row, findings with coloured left rails, and a footer with a finding count and a "Full report" link; extension/src/popup/popup.ts:331-430 renders exactly that structure, including the 3px severity rail at :508. The store screenshots are honest about the shipped UI. (5) NO HTML REPORT RENDERER EXISTS. The export set is JSON, CSV, PDF, SARIF, Markdown and the compliance crosswalk; the shared scan page at /shared/[token] is the de facto HTML report and belongs to the in-app review.
findings.impact: None. This is a record of coverage. It matters mainly for the two surfaces auditors most expect to be broken and which are not: the email system already has the shared layout that usually needs to be proposed, and the docs already read as one manual rather than twenty pages.
findings.recommendation: No action. When re-auditing section 5, start from the report renderers and the extension, which is where the real drift is, and treat lib/email/email.ts and components/docs/ as reference implementations of what a shared abstraction should look like on the other surfaces.

findings.title: Negative results: reports, scanner user-agents, sitemap, robots, security.txt, badge snippets, CI integrations, third-party credentials and filesystem paths are all correctly config-derived
findings.description: Recorded so the next audit does not repeat the sweep. (1) Report exports: lib/reports/pdf-report.ts, markdown-report.ts, sarif-report.ts and compliance-report.ts all use APP_NAME, APP_URL and APP_VERSION for every attribution string, including the SARIF driver informationUri at sarif-report.ts:245. (2) Scanner identity: every outbound User-Agent is built from APP_NAME (nine sites, listed in hc-14). (3) SEO plumbing: app/sitemap.ts:16, app/robots.ts:88-89 and app/layout.tsx:122 (metadataBase) all derive from APP_URL, and app/robots.ts:79 uses APP_NAME as the self-referential crawler token. (4) app/api/security-txt/route.ts:19 correctly resolves SECURITY_EMAIL through getSetting, and LEGAL_EMAIL/SECURITY_EMAIL/ENTERPRISE_EMAIL reach the /legal/* pages the same way. (5) Badge and share embed snippets at app/docs/sharing/page.tsx:386 and :391 are built from APP_URL. (6) The GitHub Action (.github/actions/scan-gate/action.yml:15-18) and the GitLab template (public/gitlab/vulnradar-scan.gitlab-ci.yml:31) both expose the API base as a documented input for self-hosted use. (7) The self-updater derives its release source from APP_REPO (lib/updater/github-release.ts:28, lib/updater/cosign.ts:22). (8) No hardcoded third-party credentials or object IDs anywhere: no Stripe price_/prod_ literals, Browserbase project id and API key are env-only (lib/browserbase/client.ts:94-139), Turnstile and Google Web Risk likewise, and there is no analytics ID in the app at all. (9) Filesystem paths: no absolute or Windows-shaped path in any runtime module; the four writable locations all derive from process.cwd() or an env override (app/api/v3/admin/backup/route.ts:27 BACKUP_DIR, lib/uploads/avatar-migration.ts:49, lib/backup/run-backup.ts:30, lib/updater/apply.ts:130 which correctly uses os.tmpdir()). (10) The two DoH resolvers at lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:843-849 and :1758-1762 (dns.google, cloudflare-dns.com) are hardcoded but redundant with each other and are a scanner dependency rather than a deployment-identity value, so they are noted here rather than filed.
findings.impact: None. This is the verified-correct half of the deployment-identity sweep, recorded to bound the problem: the hardcoding in this codebase is concentrated in the config-resolution layer (hc-01, hc-03, hc-06, hc-07), the extension (hc-02) and the Docker image contents (hc-04), not spread through the application code.
findings.recommendation: No action. If a future audit re-runs this section, start from lib/config/registry.ts's tier field and the getSetting call graph rather than from a grep for the domain: the grep is clean and the defects are all in whether a resolved value is actually read.

findings.title: Negative results for the next audit: root .env.local is correctly excluded from the image, the container runs non-root with a real healthcheck and shutdown handlers, and Stripe, AI, Turnstile and Browserbase all degrade gracefully when unset
findings.description: Recorded so the next audit does not re-derive them. All static, nothing executed. (1) Secret leak into the image: root .env.local IS matched by both `.env.*` and `.env*.local` at .dockerignore:5-6 and never enters the context; `!.env.example` at :7 correctly re-includes only the template. The nested caveat is host-11. (2) The `*.md` exclusion at .dockerignore:9 is root-anchored and therefore does not strip the five generated AI knowledge files under lib/ai/, and the prebuild compilers (package.json:13) read .ts sources (scripts/compile-changelog-knowledge.mjs:26 reads lib/changelog/data.ts), so the build is not broken by it. (3) Non-root: Dockerfile:71-72 creates uid/gid 1001 and :102 switches to it before EXPOSE. (4) HEALTHCHECK at Dockerfile:99-100 and docker-compose.yml:87-99 both target /api/v3/health, which does a real pool.connect plus a schema-version and required-tables probe (app/api/v3/health/route.ts:88-116) rather than the GitHub-only /api/version, and the path is in lib/config/public-paths.ts:109 so middleware does not block the probe. (5) Compose ordering is correct: the app depends_on postgres with condition: service_healthy (docker-compose.yml:79-81) against a pg_isready healthcheck (:26-30), so there is no startup race. postgres_data (:115) persists across `docker compose down`, and app/docs/setup/page.tsx:679-680 correctly flags `down -v` as the destructive variant. (6) Postgres 16.4-alpine (:18) satisfies the documented 14+ floor in README.md:124. (7) Graceful shutdown: SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers close the pool at the end of instrumentation.ts's register(), and tini is PID 1 (Dockerfile:114). (8) Optional integrations fail soft, not hard: Turnstile is gated behind TURNSTILE_ENABLED at app/api/v3/auth/signup/route.ts:41 so signup works with no keys; the AI provider, Stripe and Browserbase are all optional in the lib/config/env.ts OptionalSchema and none is read at boot. (9) There is no seeded account and no default password anywhere in the fresh-install path: scripts/create-fresh-db/create-fresh-db.mjs seeds only default badges, and the first admin is made by hand via SQL per app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:276-284.
findings.impact: None. This records the parts of the self-host surface that are correct so a future audit can spend its time on host-01 through host-08 instead.
findings.recommendation: No action. Keep the .dockerignore `!.env.example` ordering, the service_healthy dependency and the /api/v3/health healthcheck target as they are if any of these files are refactored.

findings.title: Negative result: the support-ticket module is the pattern the rest of the codebase should copy for shared limits, and adaptive confidence already reads its thresholds from settings
findings.description: Recorded so the next audit does not re-derive it. lib/support/ticket-constants.ts:48-:49 exports TICKET_SUBJECT_MAX = 200 and TICKET_MESSAGE_MAX = 5000; the same two constants drive the client maxLength attributes (components/contact/support-tickets.tsx:362, :388, :611 and components/admin/features/support-inbox.tsx:346), the server validation (app/api/v3/support-tickets/route.ts:117, :129) and the error copy, which interpolates the constant rather than restating the number (:119). That is the shape every finding above is asking for. Two other areas check out clean: lib/scanner/adaptive-confidence.ts:82-:96 resolves both of its thresholds (ENGINE_FEEDBACK_MIN_SAMPLE_SIZE, ENGINE_FEEDBACK_NOISE_THRESHOLD_PERCENT) through getSetting and reuses the exact pair the admin panel already displays; and lib/billing/plan-limits.ts:129-:139 correctly guards the -1 unlimited sentinel in withinPlanLimit before planLimitMessage can ever interpolate it, with every caller re-checking `!== -1` as well (app/api/v3/scan/bulk/route.ts:527), so the '-1 days' class of bug fixed in commit 30c278bf is not present on the plan-limit message path. components/pricing/pricing-features.tsx:11-:14 and :35-:40 also guard it. The one place a raw plan limit still reaches the DOM unguarded is app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx:204, :223, :294 and app/pricing/page.tsx:120 rendering dailyScans directly, which is latent only because no shipped plan sets dailyScans to -1 (lib/billing/catalog.ts:116, :148, :180, :211 are 25/100/150/500).
findings.impact: None. This records verified-correct ground so a later audit spends its time elsewhere, and names the one latent -1 render site worth a guard if plan limits ever become fully admin-editable.
findings.recommendation: No action required. When fixing magic-04, magic-15 or magic-16, model the fix on lib/support/ticket-constants.ts: one exported constant, imported by the client input, the server validator and the error string.

findings.title: AI answer engines cannot reach any of this because Cloudflare AI Crawl Control blocks them at the edge, which is a dashboard toggle and not a code change
findings.description: Recorded so nobody spends a day on it in code. The app does its part: app/robots.ts and app/llms.txt/route.ts exist, lib/config/public-paths.ts explicitly allowlists /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt, /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml for session-less crawlers with a comment explaining that AI crawlers carry no cookie, and components/seo/structured-data.tsx emits SoftwareApplication and FAQPage JSON-LD on the landing page including both extension store URLs. None of that reaches an AI crawler, because Cloudflare's Managed robots.txt / AI Crawl Control feature overrides the application's own robots.txt at the edge and disallows GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot and Google-Extended. This was confirmed in prior work as the reason AI assistants do not know the product exists. It is fixed by turning the feature off in the Cloudflare dashboard. Related and separately filed: AUDIT-012#fe-01 found the root layout's await headers() forces all 311 routes dynamic so Cloudflare caches no HTML, which affects crawl budget for the roughly 780 SEO pages, and AUDIT-013#subdeps-01 found the npm name vulnradar is unclaimed while /docs/cli advertises npx vulnradar.
findings.impact: None directly. It explains why the marketing surface described in the other findings does not appear in AI answers, and it prevents a future auditor from proposing code fixes for an edge configuration problem.
findings.recommendation: No code change. The owner toggles Managed robots.txt / AI Crawl Control off in the Cloudflare dashboard for vulnradar.dev. Once that is done, the llms.txt and JSON-LD work already in the repo starts being read, and mkt-07's APP_DESCRIPTION rewrite becomes the sentence AI answers actually quote, which is a reason to do mkt-07 before or alongside the toggle.

findings.title: Negative results: the nine landing sections, the demo copy and the pricing hero already meet the voice standard, so a future audit should not re-review them
findings.description: Read line by line against the CLAUDE.md voice rules and audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md section F. Zero em dashes in any user-facing string across components/landing/, app/landing/page.tsx, components/demo/ and components/pricing/. Zero adjective-only benefit claims of the Lightning Fast / Deep Analysis / Developer First class. Numbers are pulled live from the registry rather than hardcoded: app/landing/page.tsx:102-104 computes checkCount and categoryCount from getCategoryCounts(), landing-categories.tsx:16 recomputes the total, and landing-hero.tsx:14 carries the comment "Real count from the scanner registry, not a marketing label." Section headings are declarative sentences, not noun-phrase labels. The strongest copy in the repo is components/demo/demo-info.tsx:12-23 ("A security tool that will not run its own checks on itself is asking you to take a lot on faith"), components/landing/landing-how-it-works.tsx:14-19 and :32-35, components/landing/landing-features.tsx:7-8, and components/pricing/pricing-hero.tsx:18-24 ("Free until the free tier runs out" plus "Nothing is held back behind a tier"). components/pricing/pricing-features.tsx:186-188 states that the comparison table reads its numbers straight out of the billing config so it cannot drift, and that is true of the table itself. BILLING_ENABLED gating is handled correctly for self-hosters at three checked points: components/landing/landing-nav.tsx:22 drops the Pricing nav link, components/scanner/footer.tsx:94-103 drops the footer Pricing link, and app/pricing/page.tsx:68-146 renders a purpose-written page ("There is nothing to pay for here") rather than a broken pricing grid, with app/landing/page.tsx:65-67 and components/landing/landing-cta.tsx:46-49 both branching their copy on the same flag. The -1 unlimited sentinel is guarded in all three places it is rendered (app/landing/page.tsx:41-47, components/pricing/pricing-faq.tsx, app/pricing/page.tsx:26-31). The findings in this file are about what is missing or what is now false, not about the standard of the prose.
findings.impact: None. Records the parts of the selling surface that are correct so the next audit spends its time on mkt-01 through mkt-04 rather than re-reading nine sections of good copy.
findings.recommendation: No action. When acting on the other findings in this file, preserve these strings verbatim rather than rewriting around them, in particular components/demo/demo-info.tsx, which mkt-01 keeps and only retitles.

findings.title: Verified correct on the scanning page, recorded so the next audit does not re-derive it
findings.description:
Things I checked on this surface and found sound, so they need no work.

1. The progress denominator is genuinely real, not estimated. app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:332-339 derives `categoriesTotal` from `getPlannedSyncCategories` plus `getPlannedAsyncBranches` against the actual selected scanners, and explicitly zeroes the sync side for raw-IP targets to match executeScan's own gating. lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts:117-139 persists only events the engine actually emits. Tell-tale 8 (numbers real, not hardcoded) passes on the counter, even though the bar around it does not.

2. The component's ratchet is not a stall. `MIN_STEP_DISPLAY_MS` paces the display only; the parent's `status` flip unmounts the indicator immediately on completion regardless of where the ratchet has got to. The docblock at :46-57 says so and the code matches. No artificial minimum display time exists, confirming AUDIT-011#scan-05's own negative finding still holds.

3. Colour discipline is clean. No `bg-gray-*`, `text-slate-*`, `bg-[#hex]` or raw brand constant appears in scanning-indicator.tsx, dashboard-error-state.tsx or the scanning branch of app/dashboard/page.tsx. Severity in the error card goes through `hsl(var(--severity-medium))` and `bg-destructive` (dashboard-error-state.tsx:98, 106, 216), which is the correct encoding. Tell-tale 3 passes.

4. No em dashes in any user-facing string on this page. Every `--` in these files is inside a code comment.

5. Focus rings are present on both interactive controls: the cancel button (scanning-indicator.tsx:352) and the copy button plus support link in the error card (dashboard-error-state.tsx:241, 294) all carry `focus-visible:outline-hidden focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring`. No `onClick` on a bare div anywhere on this surface. Tell-tale 13 passes on focus, fails only on semantics (scanui-08).

6. `app/dashboard/` has both `loading.tsx` and `error.tsx`, so it is not part of AUDIT-011#drift-13's missing-boundary set.

7. The per-family copy in `FAMILY_STEP` (scanning-indicator.tsx:16-36) is good, specific, mechanism-first writing that matches the voice rules: "Grepping responses for keys and tokens", "Negotiating TLS versions and ciphers", "Looking for leaked paths, versions and stack traces". The rebuild should keep these strings; the problem is the container, not the words. The only nit is the two ampersands at :35.
findings.impact: None. Recorded so a future audit of this surface starts from the open items rather than re-deriving the settled ones.
findings.recommendation: No action. When scanui-03 is built, carry points 3, 4, 5 and 7 forward rather than rewriting them.

findings.title: Verified correct: all 71 pages have page-specific metadata, all 749 check descriptions are unique, the OG image is a correct 1200x630, and there is no indexable duplicate of a scan result
findings.description: Recording what I verified as correct so the next audit does not re-derive it. (1) Metadata coverage is complete: I walked all 71 page.tsx files and resolved each to the nearest metadata source. Zero fall back to the root default. 45 use pageMetadata (indexable, canonical, OG, Twitter, googleBot directives), 25 use privatePageMetadata (noindex, nofollow, nocache), and the only inline case is app/page.tsx, which is a bare `redirect("/landing")` with no content of its own. (2) Hand-written copy is in range: across all 44 description strings and 61 title strings in app/**, zero titles exceed 60 characters with the " | VulnRadar" suffix, zero descriptions exceed 160 except one 163-character TechArticle description const at app/docs/api/playground/layout.tsx:11 (the meta description in the same file is 154), and no two pages share a description. (3) All 749 generated check descriptions are unique, and so are all 749 raw `description` fields in the checks-data JSON. (4) public/og-image.png is exactly 1200x630 at 107.6 KB, twitter.card is "summary_large_image" everywhere (lib/seo/metadata.ts:116), and metadataBase is set (app/layout.tsx:118) so relative image and canonical paths resolve absolute. (5) No indexable duplicate of a scan result exists: there is no /history/[id] page, and /shared/[token] and /host/[hostname] are both noindex, so the same report is never indexable at two URLs. (6) trailingSlash is not set in next.config.js, so Next 308-redirects /path/ to /path and there are no trailing-slash duplicates; the only query-parameter surface on an indexable page is /public-scans?page=N, which canonicalises to /public-scans. (7) The sitemap is 805 URLs (33 hand-listed, 18 categories, 5 alternatives, 749 checks), far under the 50,000-URL and 50 MB limits, so no sitemap index is needed yet. (8) /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt both exist as real routes (app/llms.txt/route.ts, app/llms-full.txt/route.ts) and are among the only 5 prerendered routes in the build. (9) Alt text is a non-issue for discoverability: there are 7 `` elements in all of app/ and components/, and the only one on an indexable page is inside a code sample in app/docs/sharing/page.tsx:386 which already carries an alt. (10) app/layout.tsx:177 renders SiteStructuredData without a nonce while every other JSON-LD call site passes one; this is cosmetic, since a `script type="application/ld+json"` is a data block that the HTML spec returns from before the CSP inline check, so it is not blocked.
findings.impact: None. These are the checks a discoverability audit would otherwise repeat, and the SEO foundation here is genuinely above average for a project this size: a single pageMetadata helper, a routes.ts that derives the generated surfaces from the same loaders the pages use, real JSON-LD across six types, and llms.txt.
findings.recommendation: No action. Use this as the baseline: the defects filed in seo-01 through seo-21 are the delta from an otherwise sound implementation, not a missing foundation.

findings.title: AI crawler access is blocked by Cloudflare's Managed robots.txt at the edge, not by app/robots.ts, so this is a dashboard toggle and no code change will fix it
findings.description: Recording this so nobody spends a day on the wrong file. app/robots.ts:19-43 already declares an explicit AI_CRAWLERS group naming GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-Web, anthropic-ai, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Google-Extended, Googlebot, Applebot-Extended, CCBot, cohere-ai, Bytespider, Amazonbot and Meta-ExternalAgent, and grants them `Allow: /` with only the same private paths everyone else is denied. The application code is correct and needs no change. Cloudflare's Managed robots.txt (AI Crawl Control) overrides the origin's robots.txt at the edge and Disallows GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot and Google-Extended, which is the confirmed reason AI assistants do not know this product. That is a Cloudflare dashboard setting on the zone, not anything reachable from this repo.
findings.impact: The product publishes /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt and 749 per-check remediation guides specifically so answer engines can cite them, and the edge blocks the crawlers that would read them. Fixing the app's robots.txt would change nothing, because the origin file never reaches those crawlers.
findings.recommendation: The owner toggles Managed robots.txt / AI Crawl Control off in the Cloudflare dashboard for the zone. Verify afterwards by fetching https://vulnradar.dev/robots.txt with `User-Agent: GPTBot` and confirming the response matches what app/robots.ts generates. Do not modify app/robots.ts for this.

findings.title: Route-level loading and error boundaries are missing on 61 of 71 pages, but almost every gap is already covered by an in-page state ladder, so the real exposure is narrower than the raw count suggests
findings.description: Measured for this audit, extending AUDIT-011#drift-13 rather than re-filing it. loading.tsx exists for /admin, /assets, /compare, /dashboard, /history, /pricing, /profile, /repos, /shares, /teams (10). error.tsx exists for the same set minus /pricing and /repos (8, plus app/error.tsx and app/global-error.tsx). not-found.tsx exists once, at the root. Of the 61 pages without a route-level loading.tsx, the ones that actually block on data almost all carry their own in-page gate: /shared/[token] and /host/[hostname] render SharedScanSkeleton (app/shared/[token]/page.tsx:137, app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:135), /public-scans renders PublicScansTableSkeleton (:134), /badge renders BadgeSkeleton (:88), /browser/[id] gates at :519, all three /checkout/* pages render CheckoutSkeleton (for example app/checkout/credits/page.tsx:65-67), and /dashboard wraps its own content in Suspense with a real skeleton fallback (app/dashboard/page.tsx:169). The 17 pages that are async server components (all of /legal, /tools, /alternatives, /checks, /security, /landing) resolve from the local registry and config rather than the database, so a missing loading.tsx there costs a paint, not a hang. The genuinely uncovered blocking surfaces are the ones filed separately above and in AUDIT-011#auth-08 (/login, /signup, /reset-password prerender `Suspense fallback={null}`) and #ck-06 (/contact's ticket list returns null while loading). Recorded so the next audit does not re-derive the 61-page number as if it were 61 blank screens.
findings.impact: None directly. This is a negative result: the loading.tsx count understates the product's actual coverage, and prioritising by that count alone would spend effort on static pages while the real blank-screen and never-resolving cases (state-04, state-06, state-08) sit elsewhere.
findings.recommendation: When acting on AUDIT-011#drift-13, prioritise error.tsx over loading.tsx: the segments that most need a boundary are /host/[hostname], /shared/[token] and /browser/[id], where a render-time throw on untrusted server data currently escapes to the full-screen app/error.tsx and destroys the public page chrome. loading.tsx can be skipped entirely for the 17 async server pages.

findings.title: Positive result: DashboardErrorState, the results-list filtered-empty block, /public-scans, /demo, /browser/[id] and repo-detail are the correct in-repo models for these states and should be reused rather than reinvented
findings.description: Recorded so the fixes above have something concrete to copy and so the next audit does not re-derive it. components/scanner/dashboard-error-state.tsx:43-76 classifies a scan failure into seven kinds (blocked, network, rate_limit, validation, server, auth_failed, generic) from the message and status, and :78-onward gives each one a title, an icon, a severity-toned rail and a description that states what happened and then what to do about it, plus a retry. It is the best error component in the product and the only one that distinguishes retryable from permanent. components/scanner/results-list.tsx:597-621 is the model empty state: it says why the list is empty ("N findings are hidden"), what to do, and offers a one-click Reset filters. app/public-scans/page.tsx:134-145 is the model three-way ladder (skeleton, then error, then empty, then data) in a single page. components/repos/repo-detail.tsx:242-255 is the model four-way ladder, spoiled only by the missing finally described in state-04. app/demo/page.tsx:68-92 and app/browser/[id]/page.tsx:519-546 both carry designed error branches. app/shared/[token]/page.tsx:139-158 is the model "this thing does not exist" state, with a specific explanation and a conversion CTA rather than a bare 404. All of them use the established design language: dashed border-border on bg-card/50 for empty, destructive or severity tones for error, and no shadow beyond the shadow-xs baseline.
findings.impact: None. This is coverage of what is already right, so remediation does not invent a seventh visual grammar for an error block.
findings.recommendation: When fixing state-05, state-07, state-10, state-11 and state-16, reuse these: the classified-kind approach from dashboard-error-state.tsx for anything that needs to distinguish retryable from permanent, the dashed empty block (`rounded-md border border-dashed border-border bg-card/50 px-4 py-12 text-center`) with a title, a why line and an action for anything genuinely empty, and a destructive-toned inline band for a load failure inside an otherwise working page. Do not introduce a new shell.

findings.title: Measured coverage baseline for AUDIT-013: 79.35% statements over 412 files, with 44 files at zero and 419 React files outside the denominator entirely
findings.category: baseline reference for the next audit
findings.description: Recorded so the next audit has a real number to compare against rather than the stale 2026-08-13 coverage/ directory. I ran `npx vitest run --coverage` on the current tree on 2026-08-28: 356 test files, 10,158 tests, 0 failures, 89.21s wall. Coverage over the 412 files matched by coverage.include: statements 79.35% (20,623/25,987), branches 71.24% (12,701/17,826), functions 82.04% (2,994/3,649), lines 81.02% (19,152/23,638). 44 files measure 0%, totalling 1,054 statements; the largest are lib/updater/apply.ts (134), lib/ai/review-source.ts (101), app/llms.txt/route.ts (62), app/api/v3/admin/content/route.ts (61), lib/hooks/use-modal-a11y.ts (59), lib/auth/security-migration.ts (54), lib/reports/markdown-report.ts (53). Source-to-test mapping by path: 176 of 251 lib files and 142 of 157 API routes have a same-path test; 8 of 313 component files do (2.6%). Outside the denominator: 313 components files (65,147 lines), 152 app/*.tsx (30,147 lines), middleware.ts (546 lines), instrumentation.ts (3,639 lines), scripts/ (13,161 lines), extension/src (7,048 lines), cli/ (254 lines). The threshold check currently fails with eight errors (see cov-08), so `npm run test:coverage` exits non-zero even though every test passes.
findings.impact: None directly. The purpose is to make the next audit's comparison meaningful and to make the gap between the headline 81% and the true whole-repo figure explicit: the measured denominator excludes roughly 119,000 lines of the repository.
findings.recommendation: No action required for this finding on its own. If cov-09 and cov-07 are implemented, re-run the baseline afterwards and record the new, larger-denominator number in the next audit so the drop is understood as a measurement fix rather than a regression.

findings.title: There are no actionable TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX markers and no commented-out code blocks anywhere in the source: all 14 marker matches are scanner detection patterns or display placeholders
findings.category: verified clean: deferred-work markers and commented-out code
findings.description: Item 6 of the scope expected 14 TODO-family markers across app, lib, components, extension/src, cli and scripts. All 14 matches exist, and none is a deferred-work marker. Seven are the scanner's own detection logic, which looks for these strings in the sites it scans: lib/scanner/checks/content.ts:841 (comment naming the keyword set), :1899 (the regex /(?:TODO|FIXME|XXX|HACK|console\.log|debugger)/i) and :1902 (its finding message); lib/scanner/checks/information-disclosure.ts:456-457 (a comment recording that this keyword family was deliberately REMOVED from that check because it fires on nearly every real site); lib/scanner/checks/vibe-code.ts:91 and :93 (a regex for a TODO comment naming an unimplemented security control, and its message). The other seven are the literal string 'XXXX' used as a formatting placeholder or a fake key: lib/scanner/checks/content.ts:1641, lib/scanner/checks/secrets-extended.ts:24, lib/ai/verify-context.ts:93, app/api/v3/auth/me/route.ts:122, app/api/v3/auth/2fa/setup/route.ts:31, app/api/v3/auth/2fa/backup-codes/route.ts:18 and components/auth/login-2fa-form.tsx:143 (the backup-code input placeholder 'XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX'). Nothing in extension/src, cli/ or scripts/ matches at all. Separately, item 5: I scanned every .ts/.tsx/.mjs file outside node_modules for runs of three or more consecutive // lines whose content parses as code, and then for any single line matching ^\s*//\s*(const|let|var|import|export|return|await|function|class|if \(|for \(|console\.log). Both produced only prose. There is no commented-out code in this repository.
findings.impact: None: this is a clean result. It is recorded so a later audit does not spend the same effort re-deriving it, and so the 14 raw grep hits are not mistaken for a backlog. The one thing worth knowing is that a real TODO added to this codebase today would be the only one, so a lint rule that forbids them would pass immediately.
findings.recommendation: No action required. If the owner wants to keep it that way, add 'no-warning-comments' at warn level for terms TODO/FIXME/HACK to eslint.config.mjs, scoped to app/, lib/, components/ and hooks/, and exclude lib/scanner/checks/ where those strings are detection data rather than notes.

findings.title: npm audit is clean, every package resolves from the public registry, and the lockfile's Linux native bindings are intact
findings.description: Recording the negative results so the next audit does not redo them. `npm audit --json` on the full tree reports 0 vulnerabilities across 813 packages (369 prod, 363 dev, 137 optional, 1 peer) at every severity including info, so there is no reachability analysis to do: nothing is reported. `npm view <pkg> deprecated` across all 86 direct dependencies returns nothing, and no lockfile entry carries a `deprecated` field. Scanning all 814 lockfile entries, every single `resolved` URL points at https://registry.npmjs.org: there are no git URLs, no tarball URLs, no alternate registries and no `file:` links. Exactly three entries have `hasInstallScript: true` (core-js 3.49.0, fsevents 2.3.3 which is macOS-only and optional, and unrs-resolver 1.12.2 which is dev-only), and Dockerfile:24 runs with `--ignore-scripts` anyway (see deps-05). Most importantly given this repo's history: the committed lockfile still contains the full set of Linux native bindings that a Windows regeneration strips. Verified present: @next/swc-linux-x64-gnu, -x64-musl, -arm64-gnu and -arm64-musl all at 15.5.23; @img/sharp-linux-x64, @img/sharp-linuxmusl-x64 and @img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64; @tailwindcss/oxide-linux-x64-gnu and -musl at 4.3.3; @unrs/resolver-binding-linux-x64-gnu and -musl at 1.12.2; lightningcss-linux-x64-gnu and -musl at both 1.33.0 and 1.32.0. package-lock.json is tracked by git and .gitignore has no lock entry. The Node version story is consistent everywhere it is stated: .nvmrc `22`, .node-version `22`, all five ci.yml jobs `node-version: "22"`, Dockerfile:11 and :62 node:22.11.0-alpine, package.json:8 `>=22.0.0` (see deps-07 on tightening that upper bound).
findings.impact: No action required. Two things here are worth an operator knowing: the lockfile is currently healthy on the exact axis that has broken this repo before, so whoever applies deps-01, deps-02 or deps-08 needs to regenerate it on Linux or graft entries by hand rather than running npm install on Windows; and `npm audit` being clean means the CI gate at ci.yml (`npm audit --audit-level=high --omit=dev`) is currently passing on merit rather than on a suppression.
findings.recommendation: No change. When applying any of the package.json edits in this section, re-run the Linux-binding check afterwards: the thirteen entries listed above must still be present in package-lock.json before the change is committed.

findings.title: Sixteen packages are behind, and only next and typescript are majors: both are deliberately held, and the rest are minor or patch drift with no security content
findings.description: `npm outdated --json` lists sixteen entries. Two are majors and both are held on purpose, documented in .github/dependabot.yml:73-81. (a) `next` 15.5.23 vs 16.3.3 (package.json:95), with `update-types: ["version-update:semver-major"]` ignored so the Next 16 jump arrives as a manual decision rather than an automated PR. Next 15.5.23 is well past the 15.2.3 that fixed the middleware-bypass advisory and npm audit reports nothing against it, so this is a planning item, not a security one, though see deps-13 for the eslint-config-next half of it having already moved. (b) `typescript` 6.0.3 vs 7.0.2 (package.json:135), held because `@typescript-eslint/*` 8.67.0 declares `typescript: ">=4.8.4 <6.1.0"`, so TS 7 would break both the lint and typecheck CI jobs; dependabot.yml:78-81 states exactly this. The other fourteen are minors and patches with no advisory content: @ai-sdk/anthropic and @ai-sdk/openai and `ai` (all unused, see deps-01), @types/node 26.2.0 vs 26.4.0, @types/react-dom, @typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin and parser 8.67.0 vs 8.68.0, eslint-config-next 16.3.2 vs 16.3.3, lucide-react 1.34.0 vs 1.35.0, nodemailer 9.0.5 vs 9.0.6, stripe 22.5.0 vs 22.6.0, and zod 4.4.3 vs 4.5.2. Note that `npm outdated`'s `current` column here reflects a workspace whose node_modules has drifted below the lockfile in three places (eslint 10.8.1 installed against 10.9.0 locked, @ai-sdk/anthropic 4.0.40 against a `^4.0.41` floor, react-hook-form 7.85.0 against an exact 7.86.0 pin), which is a local-install artifact, not a repo state: `npm ci` on CI resolves the locked versions and the CI run on main is green.
findings.impact: None urgent. The one thing worth tracking is the typescript hold: it is correctly reasoned and correctly documented today, but it couples the TypeScript version the whole codebase compiles against to a single lint plugin's peer range, so it needs revisiting when typescript-eslint ships TS 7 support rather than being left to drift.
findings.recommendation: No action needed on the fourteen minors beyond letting dependabot's weekly PRs land. Add a dated note to the typescript ignore rule at .github/dependabot.yml:78-81 so the hold is revisited rather than becoming permanent, and treat the Next 16 upgrade as its own scheduled piece of work given deps-13 shows the lint half already moved ahead of it.

findings.title: A full Radix toast stack is mounted on every page for exactly one consumer while 50 components hand-roll their own error and success banner state
findings.category: two mechanisms for the same job
findings.description:
components/ui/use-toast.ts (191 lines), components/ui/toast.tsx and components/ui/toaster.tsx implement a Radix-backed toast queue, and app/layout.tsx:195 mounts <Toaster /> inside the root layout so it renders on every route. components/ui/toaster.tsx:13-18 records that this mounting was itself a fix: "Mounted once in app/layout.tsx: without it the toast state updated but nothing ever drew it, so every toast() call (e.g. the billing-verification modal's error/success feedback) was silent."

That billing-verification modal is still the only consumer. components/profile/modals/billing-verification-modal.tsx:138 is the single `useToast()` call site outside components/ui/ itself; it fires nine toasts. Every other surface in the app reports success and failure one of two other ways: a locally held `useState<string | null>(null)` banner pair (50 files) or a setError/setSuccess pair prop-drilled down from the page (the profile tab tree, typed at components/profile/types.ts and threaded through profile-social-tab.tsx, profile-notifications-tab.tsx and developer/domains-section.tsx). A third mechanism, the admin-authored site notification with `type: "toast"`, is rendered by components/shared/site-notifications.tsx and shares nothing with the Radix stack.
findings.impact: No user-visible bug: the modal's toasts work and the banners work. The cost is that feedback looks and behaves differently depending on which of three mechanisms a screen happened to use, that a Radix provider and its dependency ship on every page load for one modal, and that a new contributor picking a pattern has no signal about which one is intended. This is the reason a fix like "errors should auto-dismiss" or "errors should be announced to screen readers" cannot be made once.
findings.recommendation: Decide which one wins and write it in CLAUDE.md. If toasts win, migrate the 50 local-banner components in batches and delete the prop-drilled setError/setSuccess from components/profile/types.ts. If banners win, delete components/ui/toaster.tsx, components/ui/toast.tsx and components/ui/use-toast.ts, drop <Toaster /> from app/layout.tsx:195, and convert components/profile/modals/billing-verification-modal.tsx's nine calls to the banner pattern its parent already uses. Either way this is not urgent; it is worth deciding before the next batch of forms is written.

findings.title: Negative result for the next audit: the four config surfaces share no duplicated export, all 271 registry defaults derive from CONFIG_ constants, and all seven paginated routes use the same page/limit convention
findings.description:
I checked the specific split-brain shape AUDIT-009#dup-01 found (RATE_LIMITS defined in two places so 11 routes bypassed the admin-configured values) against the current tree and it has not recurred.

Extracting every `export const` and `export function` from lib/config/constants.ts (788 lines), lib/config/client-constants.ts (378), lib/config/config-values.ts (1,368), lib/config/registry.ts, lib/config/brand.ts and lib/config/env.ts gives zero names exported from more than one of them. The layering holds in the direction it is documented: config-values.ts holds the literals, constants.ts imports and re-exports them (RATE_LIMITS at constants.ts:360-470 is built entirely from CONFIG_RATE_LIMIT_* imports, with no second literal anywhere), and client-constants.ts is re-exported through constants.ts rather than redefined.

lib/config/registry.ts contains 272 `default:` entries and every one of them is a CONFIG_ constant imported from config-values.ts, not a literal, so an admin-editable setting cannot fall back to a value that disagrees with the compiled one. The comment at registry.ts:1-11 describes that rule and the code follows it.

Separately, every paginated endpoint uses the same query convention: `page` and `limit` in all seven (app/api/v3/admin/route.ts, admin/content, admin/email-logs, admin/error-logs, admin/teams, ai/conversations, public-scans). Nothing uses offset or a cursor. The response-side key drift is filed as dup-08; the request side is consistent.

The brand palette is likewise consolidated: lib/config/brand.ts is the single source and lib/email/email.ts:19-47 aliases it rather than holding its own hexes, which is what the comment at brand.ts:1-13 claims.
findings.impact: None. Recorded so the next audit does not spend time re-deriving these four surfaces or re-checking pagination conventions.
findings.recommendation: No action. Keep the registry.ts:1-11 rule ("Adding a configurable value means adding an entry here, not a bare constant") enforced in review; it is the thing preventing the AUDIT-009 shape from returning.

findings.title: Rollback coverage is complete at the version level but the 11 boot-only tables have no down step, so a downgrade leaves them behind as orphans
findings.description: Answering the rollback question directly: every registered transition does have a down step. scripts/migrate/_registry.mjs:573 composes transitions pairwise across the three registry versions, findVersionFile (line 609) resolves 3.0.0 to 2.0.0 to 2.0.0-to-3.0.0.mjs (which exports `downgrade` at line 1169) and 2.0.0 to 1.0.0 to 2.0.0-to-1.0.0.mjs, so there is no missing rollback path. The gap is the same one as migrate-01 seen from the other direction: because the 11 boot-only tables are created by no upgrade step, the downgrade's dropTables list (line 1204-1230) does not include them either, so a 3.0.0 to 2.0.0 downgrade leaves browserbase_credit_purchases, browserbase_usage, domains, email_logs, github_credit_purchases, scan_screenshots, support_tickets, support_ticket_messages, support_ticket_shares, user_avatars and worker_failure_state in place. All 11 have FKs to users or scan_history with ON DELETE CASCADE or SET NULL, so the downgrade's `DELETE FROM users WHERE password_hash IS NULL` (line 1293) does not error on them, and a subsequent 2.0.0 to 1.0.0 downgrade does not error either.
findings.impact: No failure and no data loss, but a downgraded database ends up as a mixture: it fingerprints as 2.0.0 (fingerprintDetect only requires the fingerprint's tables to be present, scripts/migrate/_detect.mjs:33) while carrying 11 v3.7-era tables full of live data that the v2 app cannot read and that nothing will clean up. Also worth recording that the destructive-step counter shown before an upgrade (migrate.mjs:479) is driven only by dropTable and dropColumn kinds, so on the 2.0.0 to 3.0.0 upgrade it reports exactly one destructive step (the year_month DROP COLUMN at line 1134) and the upgrade path therefore never prompts for anything meaningful.
findings.recommendation: Fold into migrate-01's fix: when the 11 tables are added to addTables, add the same names to dropTables in the downgrade, ordered so children (support_ticket_messages, support_ticket_shares) precede parents (support_tickets). The DROP TABLE ... CASCADE that _planner.mjs:92 already emits handles the rest.

findings.title: Column types are inconsistent for the same kind of value across tables: IP addresses in three different types, and two JSON payloads stored as TEXT
findings.description: The schema stores an IP address three different ways: `INET` in security_alerts.ip_address (instrumentation.ts:1100), `VARCHAR(45)` in sessions (:336), sessions.ipv4_address (:352), api_keys.bound_ip (:382), admin_audit_log (:574), device_trust (:856) and access_rules (implicitly, in the TEXT `value` column at :1009), and plain `TEXT` in staff_activity.ip_address (:736). Only the INET column can be compared with a subnet operator or validated by the database; the VARCHAR ones silently accept anything up to 45 characters, which matters for api_keys.bound_ip because lib/api/api-keys.ts's passesApiKeyIpBinding compares it as a string. Two JSON payloads are stored as TEXT while everything else in the schema uses JSONB: `users.backup_codes TEXT` (:316), which is written with JSON.stringify (app/api/v3/auth/2fa/backup-codes/route.ts:110) and read with JSON.parse (:49), and which app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:156 probes with the string comparison `u.backup_codes IS NOT NULL AND u.backup_codes != '[]'` to compute has_backup_codes, so any serialization that emits `[ ]` or `null` instead of exactly `[]` flips that flag; and `data_requests.data TEXT` (:874), which holds the whole GDPR export document. Positives worth recording, since they are the things that usually go wrong: money is integer cents everywhere (billing_history.amount_cents INTEGER at :525, all three credit ledgers use BIGINT token counts), there is no float anywhere in the schema, and every timestamp is TIMESTAMPTZ or TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE with no naked `timestamp` column, so there is no time-zone ambiguity to fix.
findings.impact: No current failure. The cost is that a query cannot mix these columns (you cannot join or compare security_alerts.ip_address against sessions.ip_address without a cast), no CIDR or subnet analysis is possible over the VARCHAR ones, and the has_backup_codes flag in the admin user detail view depends on exact string equality with '[]' rather than on a structural check the database could do.
findings.recommendation: Low priority, but when any of these tables is next touched: migrate staff_activity.ip_address to VARCHAR(45) to match its six siblings (or migrate all seven to INET, which is the better target and lets the admin panel do subnet queries), and convert users.backup_codes and data_requests.data to JSONB so app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:156 can use `jsonb_array_length(backup_codes) > 0` instead of comparing text to '[]'. Both conversions are `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE jsonb USING col::jsonb`, safe on existing rows since both already contain valid JSON.

findings.title: Cross-manifest version table and measured fresh-clone cost for the four package.json files
findings.category: cross-manifest inventory, root + extension + cli + marketing
findings.description: Measured 2026-08-29 from the three lockfiles and from disk. Shared-package table (package | root | extension | marketing | verdict): typescript | 6.0.3 | 5.9.3 | 5.9.3 | MAJOR drift, see subdeps-09. eslint | 10.9.0 | none declared | 9.19.0 | major drift, and the extension has no linter of its own (root `eslint .` covers extension/src by omission, verified). @types/node | 26.2.0 | 22.20.1 | 26.4.0 transitive | major drift; the root declares Node >=22 but types Node 26 APIs. vite | 8.2.2 transitive via vitest | 6.4.3 direct | none | two majors apart, see subdeps-06. esbuild | none | 0.25.12 | 0.28.1 | three minors apart. prettier | 3.9.6 | 3.9.6 | 3.8.1 | aligned except marketing. react / react-dom | 19.2.8 | none | 19.2.3 | patch drift, isolated trees. @types/react | 19.2.18 | none | 19.2.7 | same. postcss | 8.5.26 (root override) | 8.5.23 | 8.5.26 | root pin does not cross, see subdeps-05. brace-expansion | 1.1.18 + 5.0.9 | 2.1.4 | 1.1.18 + 2.1.4 | all past their advisories today. sharp | 0.35.3 | 0.35.3 | none | aligned. zod | 4.4.3 | none | 4.4.3 | aligned. nanoid | 3.3.18 | 3.3.18 | 3.3.18 | aligned. cross-spawn | 7.0.6 everywhere | aligned. Node engines: root >=22, extension >=22, cli >=18, marketing none (subdeps-08). Fresh-clone cost, measured with du on this machine: root node_modules 789 MB across 813 lockfile entries; extension node_modules 107 MB across 194 entries (28 MB of that is @img, the sharp native binaries, pulled in only to run `npm run icons`, and 23 MB is a second copy of TypeScript); marketing node_modules 648 MB across 401 entries, including a 270 MB chrome-headless-shell that is fetched over the network on first `remotion render` rather than at install time; cli 0 MB, zero dependencies. Total on disk right now: about 1.54 GB across 1,408 lockfile entries. The number that matters for a new contributor is smaller than that: marketing/ is gitignored and cli/ has no dependencies, so a fresh clone plus `npm ci` at the root and `npm ci` in extension/ costs about 896 MB across 1,007 packages and two separate installs. I could not measure wall-clock install time because every writing npm command is forbidden in this repo.
findings.impact: No failure today. This is the reference table for subdeps-05, subdeps-06, subdeps-08 and subdeps-09, and it answers the fresh-clone question: the 648 MB Remotion tree is not part of a clone at all, so onboarding cost is the root plus the extension, not the sum of all four.
findings.recommendation: No action required for this entry on its own. Use it when acting on subdeps-05 (mirror the overrides), subdeps-06 (vite), subdeps-08 (engines) and subdeps-09 (typescript). If extension install size becomes a concern, `sharp` at `extension/package.json:35` is 28 MB of native binaries used by exactly one script, `extension/scripts/generate-icons.mjs:11`, and could be moved behind an optional install or replaced with a committed set of pre-rendered PNGs.

findings.title: .gitignore line 56 is a typo, `nscripts/storage/`, which matches no path and duplicates the correct `scripts/storage/` three lines below
findings.description: `.gitignore:56` contains `nscripts/storage/`, sitting at the end of the "Dependency directories" block after the four `.yarn/*` entries. There is no `nscripts` directory in the repo (`ls -d nscripts` returns nothing), so the pattern matches nothing. The intended pattern is present and correct three lines later at `.gitignore:59`, `scripts/storage/`, under its own "FP audit temporary scan storage" comment. The likely cause is a stray `n` from a keystroke landing at the start of a duplicated line. Note also that this is the only defect I found in gitignore coverage for the sub-projects: `git ls-files | grep node_modules` returns nothing, no `dist-chrome`, `dist-firefox` or `.zip` artifact is tracked, `extension/.gitignore` correctly covers `node_modules/`, `dist-chrome/`, `dist-firefox/`, `dist-build/`, `dist-tsc/`, `out/`, `*.tsbuildinfo` and `vulnradar-*.zip`, and the comment at `.gitignore:66` explaining why the root must not add `extension/*` is accurate.
